It is hoped that God, exalted be His glory, will manifest its recompense and assist them in that which is the cause and means of everlasting remembrance, as well as the cause of eternal blessing.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thereafter, the servant hath attained to that which flowed from your pen that moved in praise and glorification of God and in describing His attributes and names. When I opened it and read it and became aware of its contents, I turned toward the heaven of the Cause and presented what was presented before the Throne.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thereafter, the letter of that spiritual beloved arrived. In truth, it was like a warbling nightingale and a melodious verse. The servant testifieth that it was as a dove cooing upon the branch of divine knowledge. The fragrance of the love of God and steadfastness was diffused and evident throughout the entire letter.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: We have heard that wherewith thou didst commune with God and We answer thee with that which diffuseth the fragrance of eternity through the duration of My most excellent Names. We have found from thy words the fragrance of My love. We have turned toward thee from this station and revealed unto thee this wondrous Tablet.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Indeed, what can I say, for I have witnessed the Sun of Favor rising and manifest in regard to you. This much I submit, that in all conditions the glances of unfailing grace have been and, God willing, will continue to be directed toward you, and you have been and will be mentioned with wondrous and sublime remembrance.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thereafter, the letter of that beloved of the heart arrived, which was a perfect remedy for the poison of separation and estrangement and the chronic ailments of remoteness in the days of divorce. It accomplished its purpose, and indeed achieved its healing, for it burned away grief and increased the light of joy and gladness.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thy letter hath come, and the Most Great Branch, who was present before the Throne, read it. We have answered thee with verses that God hath made as an ocean of light for His loved ones, as a globe of fire for His enemies, as the Most Exalted Paradise for His chosen ones, and as the Supreme Paradise for those who circle round the Throne.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter of the Afnan, upon him be my Baha and my loving-kindness, which was sent to this servant was presented before the Face of the Wronged One and was perused. Praise be to God, the entire letter was illumined with the light of divine love and aflame with the fire of godly attraction, speaking and testifying of the ocean of sincerity.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The greatest glad-tidings of all is that the wish and request of the spiritual friend, J.B., upon him be the Glory of God, has been granted acceptance. One coat from the blessed attire has been bestowed. Whosoever is ready to depart, it shall be sent, God willing. This robe and mention of it will endure forever in the book of the world of the Kingdom.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The esteemed Observer, upon him be 966 [Baha'u'llah], has described Aqa Mirza Husayn Beg who resides in that land, and truly he has acted with the utmost love and affection towards travelers and emigrants. Previously too his mention was made in the Most Holy Court, and the Observer, upon him be the bounty of God, had requested that the Most Great Branch write something to him.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As to what you wrote regarding the trees, fruits and seeds, after presenting it He said: God willing, may the trees and seeds that the honored Afnan has obtained be planted like the trees planted in the Most Holy Place in the Most Great Name, and may they appear with new and distinguished fruits, and may their mention remain eternal and everlasting until the end that has no end.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Send the carpets that are ready for the Most Exalted Shrine, and have one large carpet woven with the words "Most Exalted Shrine" inscribed on it, then send it. However, let there be no red or yellow colors in it, and whatever design you deem appropriate. And Jinab-i-Mir Taju'd-Din ?abbagh and his two descendants are permitted to send one piece of carpet for the Most Exalted Shrine.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The box of entrusted provisions and plums, a trust from His Holiness A and H, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, and likewise the trust from Haji Ali Asghar, upon him be the Glory of God, and the trust from Aqa Mir Ali Akbar, upon him be the Glory of God, and the trust from Aqa Ali, upon him be the Glory of God - all were received through His Holiness Ism-i-Jud, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: a letter from the beloved of hearts, Jinab-i-Mulla 'Ali-Akbar, upon him be the Glory of God and His favors, arrived. Praise be to God, it brought joy and gladness. Likewise, two letters from the beloved of hearts, Jinab-i-Aqa Mirza Asadu'llah, upon him be the Glory of God, arrived on this same day. Similarly, a letter arrived from the beloved of hearts, Jinab-i-Ibn-i-Abhar, upon both of them be the Glory of God and His mercy.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Four plain cloaks sent by his honor M.N., and one cloak sent by his honor Zayn, and 10 pairs of socks sent by his honor Abu'l-Hasan who visited the House, one box of rosewater and one plain agate ring and socks sent by his honor Ghulam-Husayn, and socks sent by his honor Abu'l-Qasim, upon them be the Glory of God, through his honor Shaykh, upon him be the Glory of God, were received by this servant in the month of Rabi'u'th-Thani 1298.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The samovar and items that were with Jinab-i-Haji Ahmad arrived, and specifically they commanded that the samovar be kept for the days of the Festival so that all may drink tea from it in remembrance of the Beloved. Likewise, the rice that Jinab-i-Shaykh, upon him be the Glory of God, sent arrived without defect. The rosewater too was specifically preserved for the Festivals as commanded, and upon its arrival, after one day the Blessed Beauty made use of it.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The grape vines and trees they sent before and after arrived, and due to the abundance of rain and severity of winds, were placed in the soil. During these two or three days they were taken out and planting began in their name, as the true Planter and Cultivator. This year the intensity of rain disrupted the order and work of tree planting. Such is the decree of our Lord, the Mighty, the All-Knowing. For instance, the olive trees were cut two months from their location and it was not possible to place them in the ground due to the mud.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The offerings of that beloved one, which in truth were each like a cutting sword for the day of mourning, like a rain-bearing cloud for the day of thirst, and like a brilliant light for the day of eclipse and night of darkness, arrived and at that very moment were graced with the gaze, and this is a true testimony to the sincerity, sanctity and purity of that beloved's deeds. At this time mention was made of the sugar that was sent, although it has not yet arrived. Nevertheless, God is witness and testimony that the palate of the soul has been sweetened by it.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Blessed are they who succeeded in paying the debts of the Leaf of Paradise. The names mentioned who have been blessed with this supreme gift are each remembered before the Wronged One and honored with incomparable verses. O My loved ones in that place! By the life of God, ye have ever been and continue to be remembered. Know ye the value of this most exalted station and supreme rank. That which hath reached the honored Leaf is acceptable before the Wronged One. We beseech God to send down upon those who have expended, from the heaven of His bounty, the rain of His mercy.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: A hundred liras reached the servant in the prison

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: To his Excellency Nuri Sadik Efendi, employee of the Ottoman Bank

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: A small amount of money and medicine was sent for Jinab-i-Tamaddun.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your letter was received. I have accepted the invitation of Unity Church

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The sum of two hundred and fifty francs which thou hadst sent was received

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: His Honor the Trustee, in all his letters, like a clear messenger gives news

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: This letter acknowledges receipt of news and communication from the recipient.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The friends arranged a magnificent gathering and showed the utmost consideration

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Mention of giving gifts and honors to officers and police to allow secret visits

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter references receipt and handling of communications regarding contributions

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thy recent letter was received which, praise be to God, was evidence of great success.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The honored Haji Ghulam-'Ali, upon him be My Baha, arrived and the Huquq was received.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Everyone who passes through that region praises you greatly and is grateful and pleased.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Several letters have arrived from you, and this is the second letter being sent in reply.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: References to efforts being made by various individuals to resolve financial/legal matters

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thou art among the earliest of the believers and hast rendered service to the Cause of God.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: "all the letters from your honor to Minshadi...were examined word by word with utmost care"

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The amount of one hundred and forty-five tumans was received through His Holiness Ismu'llah

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The detailed answer to thy letter was written before, and now a new letter from thee has arrived.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: One hundred tumans from the funds of the land of Kha to be sent as a gift from one of the friends

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Wilhelm's donation;  deliver Mr. Wilhelm's donation in Port Sa'id to Siyyid Javad or Aqa Ahmad Yazdi

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The entire text is an acknowledgment of contribution to the ?a?iratu'l-Quds and installation of doors

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Each month, if five tumans from the Huquq are received, give it to him with utmost humility and apology.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: At the beginning of the letter there is a list of names from Stuttgart who apparently sent a contribution

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The sum of twenty-five French liras has been sent by post. Please write to confirm receipt of the letter.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your letter dated 13 Rajab 1338 arrived. The papers which you had submitted with your letter were received.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The tea money of his honor Master Muhammad Husayn, upon him be 966 [Baha'u'llah], was received and accepted.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: I am well pleased with thee, and I pray at all times for confirmations of thy steadfastness in this service.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thy services on the Spiritual Assembly are acceptable at the Divine Threshold and well-known among the friends.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Please send word about how much was submitted to you at the time of departure for household and other expenses.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: This donation of thine will have a profound effect in America, and thus did Abdul-Baha become immensely delighted.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: I hope the believers of God will become able to pay the $200,000.00 which they have pledged themselves to contribute.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: This servant has undertaken to write this letter with the utmost embarrassment, for the reply to your letter was delayed.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: the letter which you had sent with the travelers was received and the letter of Aqa Mirza Yuhanna David was also reviewed.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: That picture thou hadst enclosed of the souls - from all their faces the light of the love of God is manifest and visible.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: That which you forwarded through Jinab-i-Aqa Abu'l-Qasim was accepted and was expended on repairs to the Garden of Ridvan.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Aqa Mirza Muhsin will provide up to five liras per month, and whenever more becomes possible there shall be no shortcoming.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your blessed letter was noted. Its meanings were a clear proof of sincere intentions, therefore I became happy and grateful.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As for what thou didst write regarding the Unity Company, the Most Great Branch presented it and it was graciously accepted.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Whatever assistance and offerings Karbila'i Husayn and Shah Khalilu'llah have made were accepted at the threshold of the One.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: If the means were available, I would certainly have had her come to Beirut for a change of air, but the means are not at hand.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: And if contributions are collected for the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, send those contributions now to the House of Blessing in Ishqabad

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As to the rental of the meeting-place of the Baha'is of which thou hast written, it was most opportune that thou didst remit it.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: You are mentioned in this divine gathering and renowned at the Threshold of the All-Glorious. 'Abdu'l-Baha is constantly mindful of you.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter acknowledges receipt of funds: "Haji Yusuf sent 500 pounds sterling via Baghdad in one transaction and 300 pounds in another."

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: fifty tumans from Shaykh Salman and some from another source... if any funds have arrived or will arrive from Abadih, they should be paid

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thy letter was received. Thou hadst written about the receipt of letters, and likewise a letter arrived from Jinab-i-Aqa Mirza Ahmad Khan.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: From every direction money has come to him and out of pure avarice he has wrongfully appropriated people's property and denied their rights.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: the hundred and fifty pounds which you sent on 20 Rabi'u'th-Thani 1331 arrived at an opportune time. May God reward you with the best of rewards.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding the salary of the late ?akim Musa, upon him be God's mercy and forgiveness, assuredly what his honor the Afnan hath written is correct.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your endeavors in the path of Truth are known and praiseworthy... Give thanks to God that your deeds are accepted and praised at the Divine Threshold

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: At this feast elaborate arrangements are not necessary - the purpose is gathering together. If possible, let the food also be Persian and of one kind.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your letter was received and contained good news, namely that you have recently guided someone. Praise be to God that you have been successful in this.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: I was made very happy of your endeavor and I will never forget this kindness of yours. I ask for you the Divine blessings and I have accepted this sum.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your services at the threshold of the Divine Unity are accepted and beloved. The maidens of Paradise in the sacred chambers are engaged in praising you.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: His honor, the Name of Beauty, upon him be My Baha and loving-kindness, has previously submitted that the sum of twenty tumans is with him for the Huquq.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: After presenting a small sum that was received in those parts, they were instructed to deliver it to them and likewise to others whatever may be received.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: I told Aqa Siyyid Yahya to remain in Akka. [...] Should major incidental expenses occur, you may every month obtain up to five Liras from Aqa Mirza Muhsin.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: According to what they have written, the Trustee himself will arrive in these days. Regarding the funds mentioned, whatever thou decidest to do is approved.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The Afnan and the friends must show kindness and bestow bounty, according to their means, upon the families and dependents of the martyrs in the path of God.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: two payments of thirty-eight tumans each were received by this servant through His Honor the Trustee, upon him be the Glory and Grace of God, in the year 1305

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Through the instrumentality of His Honor the Trustee - upon him be the Glory of God, the Most Glorious - to the Sayyids of the Land of Ta concerning the Huquq

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The matter of the Huququ'llah is momentous in the sight of God, and if they succeed in carrying out what has been ordained, surely divine favor will encompass them.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your Huquq that was collected in the year 1326 was accepted at the Threshold of Unity, and it has surely been spent in necessary places through the sincere friends.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter of his honor Aqa Mirza Musa, upon him be the Glory of God, together with the sum of ten tumans, was received by this servant through his honor the Trustee

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your labors have been many... Rest assured that the good reward for these services at the Threshold of the Blessed Beauty is greater than the sovereignty of the world

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: His honor Mirza Muhammad Shafi' has given me a detailed register containing all your blessed names, and has also delivered your letters requesting a response for all.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your household has many expenses, therefore whatever rights arrive henceforth should be counted against the household debt, and you should also attend to your own affairs.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Concerning what you had written about "Hokook", in case any is at hand, send it care of the Anglo-Egyptian Bank in Haifa that it may be expended in the interest of the poor.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: If there has been any delay in sending letters, it is due to the press of occupations and intensity of sorrows, not due to forgetfulness. You have been and are always in mind.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As to the two drafts of 1000 dollars each, they have been received. The sum of 32/10/0 English pounds, which thou hadst sent through the Anglo-Egyptian Bank, has been received.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Concerning what was written about settling the debt of Haji Mirza Husayn-'Ali (upon him be Baha'u'llah), this was a source of joy and gladness, and a means of bounty and blessing.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The sum which the beloved in Yazd endeavored to raise and sent for the assistance of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar has reached Port Said. God willing, it will soon be forwarded to America.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The contribution that the friends of Furugh have made for the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, especially the proceeds from the belongings of that soul who has ascended to God, was most acceptable.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The drafts that you had sent from Ishqabad and Baku both arrived and were sent to Afnan Aqa Mirza Muhsin so that he might write out the receipts and send them to be sealed and forwarded.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: And concerning what you wrote about Ismu'llah having given some funds to the people of the honored Amin - let him record it in his accounting ledger. His share shall reach him from before.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Twenty-three tumans were received by the servant in the prison through his honor the Afnan, Haji Siyyid Ali, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, in the month of Rabi'u'th-Thani 1302

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: [Note regarding remittance of 100 tumans from Mirza Q.L., upon him be the glory of God, through Afnan Aghayi Aqa Siyyid A.H., upon him be all the Most Glorious Glory, in Rabi'u'l-Avval 1300]

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding what was written about the quorum, whether permission is granted to the poor or not, when this was submitted, they said: We give you permission, but it is not generally permissible.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thy letter from Dublin was received like the highest paradise. Its contents were soul-stirring, from beginning to end filled with supplication, entreaty and attraction to the Kingdom of Glory.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The payment of the Right of God is conditional upon one's financial ability. If a person is unable to meet his obligation, God will verily excuse him. He is the All-Forgiving, the All-Generous.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: However, they must pay the Rights of God, and this servant mentions this out of sincerity, for this practice has been and is the cause of the purification of wealth and the descent of blessing.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The services you rendered at the time of the ascension of His Holiness the Afnan of the Blessed Tree, Jinab-i-Aqa Mirza Aqa, were accepted and beloved at the Sacred Threshold of the Abha Beauty.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letters you requested were written and sent despite lack of time. Observe how, despite the lack of opportunity and abundance of occupations, multiple letters were written out of love for you.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The thirty-five tumans which thou didst present to his honor Aqa Siyyid Abdullah, most of which was from the charitable fund's assets - I hope it will be accepted at the Threshold of Divine Unity.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The Trustee (Jinab-i-Amin), upon him be My glory, hath mentioned thee, and in his letters hath repeatedly sought mercy and bounty for the friends, and this hath been accepted before the Wronged One.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Among the proofs of this is that his honor has shown kindness and rendered service to His Honor Furughi, having extended him a loan. This act of kindness has been accepted in the Most Glorious Kingdom.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: And likewise you had mentioned the matter of Jinab-i-Aqa 'Abdu'l-Husayn, upon him be the Glory of God, through whom the aforementioned sum was sent from the Land of Peace and the Land of Ha and Mim to ?adba.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The matter of the translation office is still without foundation, rather it is imaginary, and if such a thing were to take root, God forbid, again Khan should rest assured that it will be properly arranged.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding what you wrote about the distribution of funds after the telegraphic news - this was accepted, and it should also reach those souls who left ?adba (Mosul) whose names you had mentioned in this letter.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Reference to funds for the American Mashriqu'l-Adhkar: "give Qa'im-Maqami's draft, of which approximately fifty Ottoman liras belonged to the Holy Threshold, to Aqa Ahmad to send for the American Mashriqu'l-Adhkar"

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: O Na?ir! The Greater Branch was present and made mention of thee. Praise be to God that for years thou hast dwelt beneath the shade of the Divine Lote-Tree, and this Wronged One hath been with thee in all conditions.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Through Jinab-i-Amin to the Dawlatabadis - Jinab-i-Aqa Nasru'llah, Jinab-i-Aqa Fathu'llah, Jinab-i-Aqa Abdu'llah, Jinab-i-Aqa Asadu'llah, Jinab-i-Aqa Abdu'l-Husayn, Jinab-i-Aqa Muhammad Kazim and other friends of God

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: We have heard thy call time and again, and this servant present has offered thy prayers and supplications unto God, thy Lord and the Lord of thy forefathers. All have attained the honor of being heard by the Wronged One.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The services ye are rendering in support of the Ta'yid School merit the highest praise...these friends have pledged themselves to make sacrifices in this connection, and are contributing to the support of the Ta'yid School

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Jinab-i-Aqa Rida-Quli, upon him be the Glory of God, has requested, on behalf of himself, his wife, his sons 'Ali, Lu?fu'llah and ?abibu'llah, and his daughter Bahiyyih, the bestowal of bounties and descent of divine gifts

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Through Jinab-i-Adib, upon him be the Glory of God - to Jinab-i-Khalil ibn Ibrahim, Jinab-i-Rahim, Jinab-i-Ibrahim, Jinab-i-Masih, Jinab-i-Jalal, Jinab-i-Kishvar and the handmaiden of God Tuba, upon them be the Glory of God

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: His honor Zain, upon him be the Glory of God, hath made mention of thee and the other loved ones in his letters which he hath sent to the Most Holy Court. Know ye his worth, for he is among the successful, the sincere ones.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The service of him who was named Ashraf is mentioned, and likewise the sum which was to be spent on blessed garments and for the Branches of the blessed Tree and the dwellers of the pavilion of infallibility. This was accepted.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The remittance of Ustad Muhammad, upon him be the Glory of God, in the amount of thirty-eight (38) tumans, was received by this servant through His Honor the Trustee, upon him be the Glory of God and His favor, in the year 1305.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: We have mentioned every name that was in thy letter and have answered every petitioner whose letter reached the Wronged One in this noble station. All this is from My favor upon thee - know thou this and be of the thankful ones.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The missive of Jinab-i-Karbila'i Isma'il Beg, upon him be the Glory of God, in the amount of twelve manats, was received by the servant through His Holiness the Trustee, upon him be the Glory of God and His grace, in the year 1304.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: You have shown great effort and extended a helping hand in supporting the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar. You have again contributed to its construction. Through Sheikh and Khan, dedicate the pledged fifty tumans to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar as well.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As regards what was written concerning Haji Ali, upon him be the Glory of God, and the Huquq, this too hath been accepted, though one portion was bestowed upon him directly while another portion was, according to His command, divided.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Reference to financial arrangements and acknowledgment of funds: "though this servant has one hundred tumans with him. It is hoped that affairs there will proceed with truthfulness, sincerity and uprightness, and that debts will be paid."

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As to what thou didst write concerning the debt, take counsel in all matters, then act according to what consultation decideth. Be not grieved, for perchance worldly means may become available and thou mayest be honored to discharge the debt.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Your letter dated the 23rd of Rajab of the current year arrived. The drafts that you sent from 'Ishqabad and Baku both arrived and were sent to Afnan Aqa Mirza Muhsin so that he could write up the receipts and send them to be sealed and forwarded.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: And regarding what was given in the lands of ?a and Kaf, if it has been sent, the matter is concluded; if not, let it remain with His Excellency and let him send the names of those souls to the Most Holy Court. Verily, He is the Ruler over what He willeth.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Some receipts were previously sent. It appears some may have been sent repeatedly. Please review and inform which ones have arrived. [...] The point is that receipts for these three items have been given twice, and that beloved one should be informed of this.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As to what his honor the Trustee, upon him be the Glory of God, the Most Glorious, has written regarding this matter - that his honor Ustad, upon him be the Glory of God, the Most Glorious, has sent two payments and this servant has requested and sent receipts.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The contribution of the two brother cotton-carders, upon them be the glory of the All-Merciful, in the amount of eighty-six tumans, was received by the servant in the prison through His Honor the Trustee, upon him be the glory of God, in the month of Safar 1305.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: O my beloved, some have acted contrary to what is befitting towards him, and this matter has caused grief to this evanescent one. We beseech God to adorn all with the ornament of justice and confirm them in what is befitting. Verily He has power over all things.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Mr. Amin has repeatedly offered the utmost praise for your attraction and love, that truly you are firm in faith and steadfast in the Covenant and servants of the Threshold, and whatever was entrusted to them was fully delivered after the flight of the late Khan

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter of Haji Ali, upon him be the Glory of God, containing three tumans, four thousand two hundred and fifty dinars, was received by this servant in the prison through Jenab-i-Amin, upon him be the Glory of God, in the month of Dhi'l-Qa'dih of the year 1303.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter of his honor Aqa Mirza Muhammad-Baqir and the leaf his wife, upon them both be the Glory of God, together with nineteen (19) tumans through his honor the Trustee, upon him be the Glory of God and His loving-kindness, reached the servant in the year 1305

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding what thou didst write about Rama?an-'Ali Big, his deed is accepted and hath attained the honor of divine acceptance. We beseech God to assist him and enable him to do that which He loveth and is pleased with, and to serve His mighty and impregnable Cause.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: O Khalil! Verily the All-Glorious hath heard thy call time and again, and hath answered thee through this Tablet, wondrous and sublime, We were seated upon the throne of utterance when the servant in attendance entered with thy letter and presented it before Our face.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter of his honor Afnan, Aqa Mirza Muhammad-Baqir, upon him be the Glory of God, the Most Glorious, containing seventy-six tumans was received by this servant in the prison through his honor the Trustee, upon him be the Glory of God and His favor, in the year 1305.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The deed of Afnan, upon him be My glory and My loving-kindness and My mercy, was observed and was illumined by the lights of the Sun of acceptance. Blessed is he, then blessed is he, for he saved others. He is the sign of divine assistance, having aided one of the friends of God.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: I apologize for any shortcoming, hoping that in future I may overcome this embarrassment and prove that in all conditions I share and participate with friends. I have written briefly; if I were to elaborate, it would become clear how disordered this wanderer's affairs are at present.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Praise be to God that joy was obtained from Abdu'l-Baha's letter which contained some admonition, and this became the cause of success. Praise be to God, five hundred pounds and three hundred pounds arrived from Baghdad and were immediately sent to Baghdad for the repair of the House.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Concerning what was written about the favors of His Excellency, the exalted Ambassador - may God, the Blessed and Most High, assist him - there is no doubt that, praise be to God, it has come from the world of potentiality into action, and from the realm of concealment into manifestation.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The contribution of his honor Ali-Muhammad ibn H-S, upon him be the Glory of God, in the amount of seven tumans, was received by this servant in the prison through the beloved of hearts, his honor the Trustee, upon him be the Glory of God, in the month of Dhi'l-Qa'dah the Sacred in the year 1303.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The honored beloved of the heart, Haji Siyyid Javad (upon him be 966 [Baha'u'llah]), when he came, sent funds to the Presence. He said the command was that they should first attend to the payment of external debts, and then to others. Therefore the loved ones must look to and act upon the command.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: His honor Shaykhu'r-Ra'is has, on certain occasions, taught the Faith from the pulpit through allusion, hint and indirect reference. Therefore, 'Abdu'l-Baha will never forget this service of his, and surely the friends must speak only well of him and must show consideration and respect toward him.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: They said one must move with great patience and calm in that land; teaching is not permitted. And They said: Do not believe every speaker and do not trust every visitor. People are mostly weak in reality; one must act with perfect consideration. Some mentions have become causes of hindrance and prevention.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As to what you wrote regarding the sum sent by Aqa Muhammad-Husayn, brother of him who circumambulated the House - upon them both be the glory of God - the aforementioned person sent word from the great city and wrote that after the bill's term expires it will be sent. Whatever reaches them, they will forward

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The missive of Mulla 'Abdu'r-Razzaq and his sister...was received by this servant through the beloved of hearts, His Holiness the Trustee...And yet, when an offering was adorned with the glory of His acceptance and reported by Jinab-i-Amin, twice that amount was ordered to be paid out to the poor and the needy.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Payment of the Rights of God is obligatory upon all and its benefit returns to the servants themselves. However, its acceptance depends upon spirit and fragrance and the good pleasure of just and active souls. In this case acceptance is permitted, otherwise not. Verily thy Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the All-Praised.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: His honor Mirza Ahmad has sent two thousand dollars so far - it was immediately returned so that he could return it to the contributors with utmost gratitude and appreciation. I became very pleased with the friends for showing such resolve, and I accepted, but since travel provisions are ready and nothing is needed...

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thanks be to God [they] gave the amount for the House in Iraq, and likewise what they gave according to the assignment to the family of his honor the Nazir, upon him be 96 [Baha'u'llah]. The purpose is that the account should be settled and completed with justice. Whatever else Amin does or arranges will be acceptable.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: It is most evident and clear that payment of the Rights of God has been and will always be the cause of bounty, blessing, honor and protection. Blessed is he who has recognized and acknowledged, and woe unto the deniers. This applies when one acts with complete joy and fragrance and desire to fulfill the laws of the Book.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thereafter, twelve pieces of cloth and two bundles of silk have arrived, as well as fifteen tumans from Master Muhammad the brazier, and a ring which Mir Muhammad Bey has sent. His honor Afnan, upon him be all the most glorious glory of God, has sent some funds from the Land of Ha, and has written that details will follow.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding the ten thousand tumans of debt you wrote about - this debt is a heavy burden. Henceforth, do not send a single penny until this debt is paid off...As for Siyavash's forty-seven pounds, your letter was opened at sea and Jinab-i-Siyavash has returned to the Holy Land. It was written to Aqa Mirza Muhsin to pay this amount

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Another submission is that eighteen tumans have been transferred for the honored Samandar, upon him be 669 [Baha'u'llah], to deliver to your honor to give to Ha before Sin from the people of Ta and Fa. The details are that the honored 'Azim, upon him be 669 [Baha'u'llah] and His favors, has ascended, and this amount remained from his estate.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Through Haji Yusuf Muttahidih from Baghdad, fifty thousand (50,000) rupees were received. Henceforth, whatever is sent should be sent according to the instructions given, or through a specially designated trustworthy person. Receipts are not possible at present. Your receipt is my receipt, and what is recorded in your ledger is confirmed with God.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The funds which Jinab-i-Haji Mirza Abu'l-Hasan, upon him be the Glory of God, remitted from cash and the value of silk through Jinab-i-Samiyy-i-Hadrat-i-Maq?ud (?a before Sin and Lam after 'Ayn) and Jinab-i-Aqa Muhammad ?adiq, upon them both be the Glory of God, reached this evanescent servant in the month of Dhi'l-?ijjih al-?aram in the year 1298.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The ring-watch that you had sent to the Most Holy Court was forwarded so that you might sell it and distribute its proceeds among certain handmaidens of God there. One third should be given to ?ayfu'llah, that is, the Guest of Baha'u'llah, and the remaining two thirds should be divided between their two sisters and the sisters of Aqa Muhammad-Rida.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Autobiographical account/narrative of Abdu'l-Baha describing being overwhelmed with correspondence and duties: "'Abdu'l-Baha acknowledges shortcomings in sending successive replies to the Hands of the Cause of God, but at every moment is exposed to attacks from every fierce claw of beasts and birds, and the sea of tribulation is a tumultuous ocean..."

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The sum of seventy tumans has been received by this evanescent servant through his honor Afnan Aqa'i, his honor A. and H.A., may the most glorious Glory of God rest upon him, for the Huququ'llah. This matter was written and recorded on behalf of his honor Name 66 [Allah] J.M., may the Most Glorious Glory of God rest upon him, and his honor Abu'l-Hasan.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Through Jinab-i-Shaykh and Khan to Jinab-i-Aqa Khuda-Bakhsh, upon him be greetings and praise. O Gift of God! Thou art mentioned at the Threshold of Oneness and renowned in the gathering of the All-Merciful. Thou didst make a noble effort and didst show forth a shining hand in contributing to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar. Once again thou hast assisted in its repair.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding what you wrote about Gholam - upon him be the glory of the All-Merciful - having allocated funds to be delivered over four months by him who serveth the Cause - upon him be the glory of God and His loving-kindness - they commanded that two months thereof be [delivered] to the teachers - upon them be the glory of God, His loving-kindness and His mercy.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: deliver from the land of Kha the sum of fifty tumans to the honoured Zabih of the land of K... Likewise, send the sum of one hundred and thirty-three tumans and eight thousand to His Holiness Ismu'llah Jamal...to be delivered to the heirs of the late Ustad Ahmad who ascended to the Most Exalted Horizon while in prison. Obtain a receipt and forward it to the Most Holy Court.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Another matter: As some funds were needed, twenty tumans were borrowed from the spiritual friend Mr. Muhammad Ibrahim - upon him be the peace of God - which your honor should convey to him. Although at first he was unwilling to accept it, they specifically stated it must reach him and he accepted. Your honor must pay it. And what the friends brought of gaz and other items was received.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Thus there is no doubt that whoever contributes financially in this regard will be accepted at the threshold of the Divine Unity and receive praise and glorification from the Concourse on High. Since you have exerted great effort in this mighty endeavor, it is hoped that you will receive recompense from the Lord of Clear Signs and be encompassed by the glances of the Eye of Divine Mercy.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: And regarding what His Honor Sheikh has mentioned about the designation - that beloved one knows that sometimes it is present and sometimes absent, at times the sun of wealth is visible and at times poverty. However, concerning His Honor Sheikh, upon him be the Glory of God, He commanded that it be transferred through His Honor Aqa Ali-Haydar, upon him be the Glory of God, to be delivered.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Some of them are ministers who are in the utmost justice and benevolence, and with heart and soul desire comfort and tranquility for humankind, and are kind to all subjects. Though I do not mention their names openly, in my heart and soul I beseech divine grace and protection for them, and I hope that each may become a unique well-wisher of the world and distinguished in the arena of bounty.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: According to the command, that sum should reach the Siyyid in full. This evanescent servant beseecheth the eternal Truth to confirm all the friends in service to the Cause. Once these exalted words were heard from the Lord of all beings, Who said that Siyyid Mu??afa, upon him be My glory, hath served according to his capacity. We beseech God to open before his face the gates of His grace and bounty.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The most beloved of things in My sight is justice. Can you imagine how many pages arrive? By God, reading them requires a hundred assistants, let alone responding to all. Moreover, travelers arrive daily, each wanting a hundred letters in return. Moreover, the sorrows and grief of this wronged one. Moreover, attending to all affairs both internal and external. Moreover, and moreover, and moreover...

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The law of Huquq is most great; it hath ever been and shall continue to be the cause of blessing, bounty, exaltation and glory. Although your departed father - who, as attested by the Supreme Pen, hath ascended to the highest heights - held an exalted station and continues to do so, yet this matter shall add to the brilliance of his station and likewise to the wealth and prosperity of his descendants.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding what was written about the honored Afnan - upon them be the most glorious of all glory - having hosted a feast, after it was mentioned in the Most Holy Court the Tongue of Grandeur spoke this most exalted word: Verily it was mentioned before Our face. We have veiled its mention lest every corrupt deceiver become aware of it. There is recorded for him from the Supreme Pen the good of this world and the next.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As regards Mr. Mulla Muhammad-'Ali (Tafti), upon him be the Glory of God [Baha'u'llah], after presentation They stated that upon his arrival in prison he sent whatever he had, and permission was given to accept it, but until now We have not used it. And now, considering that he has again intended to send an amount, We will accept this sum provided that he also accepts this second amount from Us. This is a bounty from Us.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding the sum that the late Aqa Rahmatullah had entrusted to 'Abdu'l-Baha, of which nineteen tumans were designated for the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, and all of which this servant had returned to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, and fifty tumans of which Aqa Hasan had given for trading, and now 'Abbas-'Ali wishes to pay the principal amount to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar - very well, let him deliver the principal sum to the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: The letter of Jinab-i-Khalil, upon him be the Glory of God and His loving-kindness, together with thirty-five Ottoman liras and two majidis, was received by this servant in the prison, through the transfer order of Haji Shaykh, upon him be the Glory of God and His favors, by way of His Holiness, the beloved Name of Generosity, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, in the month of Dhi'l-Qa'dih al-Haram in the year 1303.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: And regarding what was written about the Huquq, the sale of properties is not permitted according to the Command. Those souls upon whom Huquq has become incumbent should, if they are able, be blessed to pay it. They said: We have left the properties to those souls themselves - they may dispose of them as they wish. The benefit of good deeds returns to the souls performing them, especially for one who is enabled to pay the Right of God.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: These are honored servants and devoted handmaidens who have hastened to the fountain of Thy mercy and rushed to the shelter of Thy protection. They have forsaken their rest and bid farewell to their wealth, turning to the Kingdom of Beauty and supplicating to the Realm of Glory. O Lord! They have spent their wealth in building the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, that they may remember Thee at dawn and at daybreak, and worship Thee by night and by day.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Through Mr. Za'ir Shahvir Bahram, Mr. Khusraw Mihrban, Mr. Bahram Bahman, Mr. Nushirvan Mihrban, Mr. Siyavash Mihrgan, Mr. Rustam Surush, Mr. Ardishir Bahram, Mr. Rustam Pulad, Mr. Firaydun Khudadad, Mr. Rustam Bahram, Mr. Nushirvan Bahram, Mr. Nushirvan Khudabakhsh, Mr. Mihrban Kayqubad, Mr. Hurmuzdyar Khudabakhsh, Mr. Khudamurad Bahram, Mr. Jamshid Bahram, Mr. Mihrban Bahram, Mr. Shahriyar Bahram, Mr. Rustam Khudadad, upon them be the Glory of God, the Most Glorious

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: ?abibu'llah - upon him be My glory and loving-kindness - after his return to the horizon of manifestation attained unto the presence and was sustained by the cup of reunion. He dispatched to the Most Holy Court a leaf adorned with the names of the loved ones, seeking the expression of bounty for each one, and each was blessed with that for which he was brought from nothingness into being, and there was sent down for each that which the treasures of earth cannot equal.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: According to what was written concerning some being informed or uninformed of certain matters, it is clear and evident to your honor that most matters do not occur without his knowledge, as most write to him with details of affairs. For example, Aqa Muhammad-Rida did not write anything to this servant but had written the details of their affairs to him, and he conveyed it to this servant in whatever way possible, as in these days no one is able to correspond directly.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding what was written about the funds, some time ago this servant, as commanded, wrote to Jinab-i-Haji Mirza Abu'l-Hassan (upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God) and emphasized that if they had any of the Right of God with them and if sending it would be accomplished with joy and fragrance, they should send it, otherwise not. Later Jinab-i-Amin forwarded some funds, and they were repeatedly written to, asking them to consult with him in all matters and act according to his judgment.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Previously, one mithqal of gold was set as an offering for this circle, but His Holiness the Exalted - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him - granted a reduction. The purpose of the offering is for the person who receives the circle. The Manifestations of Truth have never had, nor will ever have, any attachment to this world and what it contains. Whoever received it would spend it, on behalf of the Truth, either for those they knew to be deserving or for other beneficial purposes they deemed appropriate.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: And as to their intention to pay the Huquq, excellent is what they have intended thereby. Their station shall be exalted and blessings shall descend upon them. Verily their Lord, the All-Merciful, is the All-Bountiful, the Generous. They are adorned and illumined with the lights of the Sun of grace and favor. A door hath been opened unto them which all the powers and forces of the world are powerless to shut. This is from God's grace, which He bestoweth upon whomsoever He willeth. Verily, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Regarding your mention of Aqa Muhammad-'Ali from [location] and his intention to pay the Huquq several months ago, this servant also wrote about this matter and it was presented at the Most Holy Court. No response emerged from the Source of the Cause until these days when this supreme word shone forth from the Lord of Names - He says, exalted be His glory: "O servant in attendance, write to the Afnan, upon him be Baha, if the mentioned person has truly intended to pay the divine Huquq, let it be delivered to the mentioned souls."

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Concerning what thou didst mention about the four units of Huquq being assigned to Haji Nabil - upon him be Baha'u'llah's glory - to be forwarded, which apparently has been delayed, and the servant did not inquire [...] After this matter was presented before the Most Holy and Most Exalted Presence, these sublime words were revealed - exalted be His utterance: Well done in what thou hast done, for the matter of Huquq dependeth upon the acceptance of the souls themselves. Should any soul, with the utmost joy and fragrance, of his own free will, desire to pay the Right of God, it is acceptable; otherwise, no.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: As regards the Huquq, it was never mentioned in the Most Holy Presence. That beloved of the heart is well aware that some years ago the King of Martyrs, may our souls be sacrificed for him, supposed that in the Land of Purpose the means of livelihood were straitened. For this reason he instructed the revered beloved, His Holiness the Name of God, Jamal, upon him be the Most Glorious Beauty of God, to proceed specifically to the Land of Kha to collect Huquq. When this news reached the Most Holy Presence, He immediately summoned this servant and revealed a wondrous and most mighty Tablet forbidding that matter.

Subject: acknowledgment of gift; of monetary contribution
Quotation: Take twenty-six pounds from Haji Siyyid Javad and distribute them thus: three pounds to the wife of Mishkin-Qalam, two pounds to his bride, two pounds to the wife of Aqa Faraj, two pounds to the wife of Mirza Husayn, two pounds to the wife of Ustad Abdul-Karim, two pounds to the wife of Ustad Muhammad-Ali, three pounds to the sister of Aqa Husayn, two pounds to the wife of Jinab-i-Zayn, two pounds to the wife of the physician, two pounds to the wife of Aqa Abul-Qasim the coppersmith, two pounds to the wife of Aqa Muhammad-Ali Afnan, two pounds to Khatun-Jan to give to her daughter, and separately two pounds should be taken by Aqa Mirza Muhsin and given to Khalid Effendi to give to that builder who fell from the wall of the mansion.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: I hope that you will always be confirmed in contentment and service to the Greatest Name.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Be adorned at all times with the raiment of patience and contentment, and be expectant of the favors of your Lord.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: "Be content with what We have ordained and be of those who rejoice. It behooveth every soul to be content with the decree of his Lord"

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: "Do thou likewise neither lament nor grieve, but be content with the divine decrees and whatsoever hath been ordained by Him...Be not disheartened - be content with the good-pleasure of the Friend."

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Let me quaff in Thy Cause, O my God, whatsoever Thou didst desire, and send down upon me in Thy love all Thou didst ordain. By Thy glory! I wish only what Thou wishest, and cherish what Thou cherishest.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Therefore, ye must needs be in the utmost state of resignation and contentment, and in adversity and tribulation be moved to forbearance and patience, that all may follow your example and be immersed in the ocean of acquiescence.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Although I am far from attaining the honor of Thy presence, yet for several reasons, since my nearness would cause afflictions to arise, I am content with whatever comes to pass, in submission to God's decree and in surrender to His command.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Nevertheless, man's inner being will be so revived by the breeze of divinely-ordained woes and trials that the dust of wailing and lamentation will entirely subside and the light of submissive resignation unto His Will shall shine forth like unto a radiant morn.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: In any case, one such as yourself must submit to God's decree and remain firm and steadfast in surrender. In the fire of tests one must be refined and, like pure gold, shine forth radiantly, teaching others the way of patience, forbearance, submission and contentment.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Today one like you should educate the people of the earth that all may drink from the ocean of contentment and fix their gaze upon the Will and Purpose of God. Take what thy Lord hath commanded thee and set aside all else. He, verily, is the All-Explaining, the All-Commanding, the All-Knowing.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Praise be to God that thou art content in name [called "Rida"] and content at heart with His decree. The station of contentment is among the most exalted of stations, and the state of submission is among the best of states. As much as thou art able, be thou content and submissive and resigned.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: I hope, through the grace and bounty of my Lord, that you will keep bright the lamp of that forgiven one and water the garden of hopes and wishes of that accepted one at the Threshold of Oneness, so that his pure soul may find spirit and fragrance in the Abha Kingdom and attain the utmost joy and gladness.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: In this Day it is incumbent upon all to evince true resignation. The Primal Point Himself hath informed every soul and summoned them to this loftiest and sublime station, that all may attain unto the good pleasure of God, may forsake their own desires, of whose ultimate consequence they remain ignorant, and may fix their gaze upon the will of God.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Man must live in contentment with the conditions of his time. Contentment is real wealth. If one develops within himself the quality of contentment he will become independent. Contentment is the creator of happiness. When one is contented he does not care either for riches or poverty. He lives above the influence of them and is indifferent to them.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: When a person is content, they are content with everything. When a person is not content, even if they possess sovereignty, they remain discontent. There were loved ones in Baghdad who were in the utmost joy and delight, despite spending their nights with only plain bread. From early evening until morning they would chant prayers in the utmost joy.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: We have no pleasure save the pleasure of God. And creation, like unto them, doth proclaim: We have no pleasure save the pleasure of God. This is what satisfieth My soul on this Day, and on the Day when God shall cause Me to return, that My heart should harbor no aversion to anything. This is the pleasure of God and verily it is the most great contentment, did ye but know.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: One who is the embodiment of self-surrender and acquiescence... They are so content with the divine decree that they drink from the cup of tribulation as though it were honeyed ambrosia and recognise in poisonous afflictions the sweetness of immortality... My point is that bitterness and venom in this life can be transformed to the sweetest honey if accepted with the spirit of acquiescence.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: We are submissive. If one is not submissive, then one falls into trials. Submissiveness brings great comfort to a person. One does not fall short in what is necessary and proper, whether in treatment or in vigilance. But one is submissive, otherwise how can a person find peace in this abode of accidents? One would always remain anxious. It is impossible for a day to pass without some incident. There is no peace for man except through submission.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: But if he letteth him go, and interfereth not with him, let him say, "Praise be unto Thee, O Lord of all the worlds! Verily, I am content with Thy good pleasure and what Thou hast predestined unto me in Thy path, even though I did desire that the earth might be dyed with my blood for Thy love. But what Thou willest is best for me: verily, Thou knowest what is in myself, while I know not what is in Thy Self; and Thou art the All-Knowing, the All-Informed."

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: Contentment is the antidote for all the social diseases. It is a divine virtue to be satisfied with very few things. Contentment is the master-key to all success. If the members of my family starve I will not ask money from the people. It is more kingly to be satisfied with a crust of stale bread than to enjoy a good dinner composed of many delicious dishes the money for which comes out of the pocket of others. A Bahai must be satisfied. There was a time that I lived on five cents a day and I was then much happier than I am now.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: One of the companions of the Messenger of God, peace be upon Him, whose prayers were answered, developed severe eye ailment in his final days. Someone asked why he would not pray for himself that God, exalted be His glory, might grant healing. He replied: 'God's decree is dearer to me than my eye.' If one attains to the sweetness of these words - that is, comprehends them - boundless joy will take hold of him. Praise be to God that that honored one was confirmed in submission, contentment and gratitude at the appearance of the divine decree.

Subject: acquiescence and resignation; contentment
Quotation: By Thy might, O Thou the Lord of manifest signs, hadst Thou accepted a sacrifice for these great calamities, we would have offered up our hearts and souls for them. But Thy inscrutable decree and irrevocable ordinance in all matters is not kept back by sacrifices, and the powers of earth and heaven are not able to resist them and this, verily, is by virtue of Thy profound wisdom invested within the realities of all things. Thou doest as Thou willest and rulest as Thou pleasest. There is no recourse for us but resignation and utter submission to Thy command, and patience and serenity at the manifestation of Thy decree, and deference to Thy will at the raging of fierce tribulations.

Quotation: As to what thou hast asked concerning the noble stone - whether it be copper or lead or something else - know thou that it hath been called by all names, but most people understand not. The people's intention regarding copper was not the copper of the common folk, nor their lead, nor their gold. Thy Lord is verily the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. We have sent down concerning this knowledge diverse epistles in an eloquent Arabic tongue and a lucid Persian language, and We have sent thee that which will make thee independent of every possessor of knowledge and wisdom. Read it and ponder upon it, that thou mayest find the knowledge of thy Lord encompassing those who are in the heavens and on earth. We do not desire that any of the loved ones occupy themselves with it. Rather, it behooveth thee and those who have believed to make your chief concern in these days the remembrance of God and the promotion of His decisive and wise Cause. With thy Lord is the knowledge of all things, and in His grasp are the keys to the treasuries of all things....

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: As regards what was asked concerning the mixture of the four elements, it is known to thee that the combination of separated, external, and opposing elements is not possible. Indeed, the masters of the craft consider four elements necessary in their work, for they regard all things as subsisting through the four elements. In truth, all four are necessary to earth, for it is the seat of manifestation. Verily earth cannot bring forth vegetation without water, as is evident, hence water is necessary - "and from water We made all things living." And earth deprived thereof brings forth neither herbage nor fruit. Fire too is necessary, for motion arises from heat and ever has, and in its absence no motion can occur, hence fire is necessary. And air, which is the cause of mixture and the source of colors, is assuredly necessary, and therein is ordained what is not ordained elsewhere, though people know it not. Indeed it is fire through its heat and water through its moisture, thus the work is perfected therein, were ye of those who know. And therein is combined what is not combined elsewhere - thus hath it been ordained by One mighty and powerful. The four elements - namely fire, air, water and earth - after combination and coalescence manifest two qualities each: in fire there is heat and dryness, in air moisture and heat, in water cold and moisture, and in earth dryness and cold. Therefore in the hidden work some have been content with two elements, calling them male and female, spirit and body, for in two elements the four are manifest. This station they have expounded in detail and called by all names. Were the details of these degrees to be mentioned, the discourse would surely grow lengthy. Therefore it is briefly stated that in the aforementioned work one must search and find something from which these four elements themselves become manifest. For if they emerge from different things, their mixture is very difficult, just as water never has and never will mix with oil, unless there be found a water in whose depths oil is concealed, and through alchemical processes the inner oil overcomes the outer form - then that water, which is in reality oil, can mix and unite with oil. In brief, what is intended by the hidden craft is that thou shouldst separate the four elements from a single thing, and after purifying each element from incidental impurities through dissolution and coagulation, unite these elements. The purpose of purification is that they be cleansed of impurities that prevent and obstruct, that they may become capable of true mixture. Now consider what thing is that stone from which the four elements are separated. Beware lest thou engage in practice before knowledge, for knowledge precedeth practice. Therefore strive to attain knowledge, then undertake the work. The stone exists in one of the three kingdoms and is visible in the streets and markets. Reflect that thou mayest know. And if thou findest it and separate it, then ask God to teach thee what He hath ordained therein, for with Him is the knowledge of all things, and the knowledge of the heavens and earth, and knowledge of what was and what shall be.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: When thou considerest the science of elixir, thou wilt discover conditions beyond counting save by God, and all manifest according to the measure of effect that God hath created therein. On this account have the philosophers differed, each following their own path, and likewise have the seekers differed in their knowledge and deeds, each following their own way. The science of elixir, like the creation of all things, hath neither beginning nor end - a knowledge that God hath concealed behind holy veils, and when He bestoweth it upon any of His servants, they act by God's command. And what the seekers of guidance say manifesteth no effect until the Effector permitteth it from Our presence. Say: Glory be to God! At the time of effect, God hath already permitted it - do ye not see? Do ye witness anything separated from its effect? That is what God hath created therein, and all stand firm by God's command. Yea, when God willeth, He can separate between a thing and its effect as He pleaseth - verily He hath power over all things. But according to how He hath created the causes, each thing manifesteth according to what was created in it, even as ye observe and witness. When thou hast understood this, know that there are no limits to this knowledge, and whosoever clingeth unto any aspect thereof will manifest something through it. Do ye not observe those who have been given a portion of this knowledge? Do ye not reflect upon those who have received a share of this knowledge yet walk not according to God's good-pleasure? This is because God withholdeth not the effect of that which He hath created therein, and this is by God's command that ye may be thankful. That which God hath concealed of this knowledge is not of that which was given to creation, for that which was given hath no station with God. All in the kingdom move by His command and then become still. Like unto those who were given this knowledge are those who were given knowledge of aught else; all manifest according to the measure they have received. God hath created naught except that He hath created therein something of the elixir, yet not all are able to manifest it, for the elixir was created to indicate God's testimony that there is no God but I, the Mighty, the Beloved. There is naught but beareth witness unto this, yet none can bear witness unto it save those endowed with insight. Consider, for example, clay, the lowest form of created things in the realm of solidity. When days pass over it, God transformeth it and maketh it stone, even as ye observe. And when that stone is taken by one endowed with knowledge of crystal-making, he extracteth from it its essence, even as ye witness that crystal from that stone. Then essence is extracted from essence until the crystal reacheth a degree beyond which there is no higher, and this is the limit of its existence wherewith ye delight yourselves. Thus hath God commanded in the Bayan that there should be manifested in all things whatsoever can be manifested of refinement, that ye may enter into and be grateful for the precincts wherein manifestations have been ordained, the means whereof have been created from all things having no equal in your lives. Those who have been given an oil whose name equateth with "the Sustainer," when they apply it to that crystal, transform it into oil, and this is a wondrous creation, for God hath created within it such effect that when it falleth upon this, it maketh it water, and this is of God's handiwork, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting. Thereafter, if there be added to that water the equivalent of eight portions here equating to the name of the Revealer, and the sun's ocean nourisheth it for numbered days, it will affect that very crystal, and less than that, being transformed by what equateth to the number of "the Sovereign" in what ye mention in the foreign tongue, into gold from which not a thing diminisheth in the melting. This is of God's handiwork, the Subtle, the Beloved. This is the most perfect expression of that knowledge, but as for the lower degrees, all have been given a portion and all rejoice in what they have been given. This pertaineth to the knowledge of those who desire the knowledge of the sun in  he creation of gold. Say: Glory be to God, the Most High! All stand firm by His command. As for what thou hast mentioned concerning the knowledge of the moon - verily, when it descends upon the fugitive as an oil in yellow sulfur, it solidifies more swiftly than the twinkling of an eye when the fugitive touches the fire that does not flee. This is from the craftsmanship of God, the Ordainer, the Beloved. However, in spirit and various lunar aspects there hath not appeared what appeared before. But the extraction of the oil is difficult, then more difficult, as the sulfur burns when touched by fire. And what the first who answered God taught thee is difficult upon difficult. Yet those who were given that knowledge have all mentioned wisdom and devised matters, and all they were given was the perfection thereof in what God created therein. All rejoice in what they have been given. Whatever knowledge thou possessest of this, that which thou hast not yet become certain of is nearer than what thou art certain of within thyself. God will manifest it when He willeth - verily He is the All-Knowing, the Powerful. And that whose name equals the name of the Honored One, when diminished by the number of alif and ba, when equated with sulfur, prevents fire from burning it. This confirmeth that should We explain the keys of this knowledge concerning gold and silver, they could not be counted. God hath created through numbers, and the knowledge of everything is in everything, and God hath ever been powerful and mighty over this. But We have referred to gold with one mention and to silver with another mention. Let this suffice both the solar and lunar practitioners if they understand. They shall understand what they understand, and shall conceal what they understand, and shall hide what they witness. This is what We have bestowed upon thee, and all that shall be understood until the Day of Resurrection. This is God's gift unto thee - verily there is no God but He, the All-Bountiful, the Supreme, the Beloved. Hadst thou asked God how He sendeth down these verses unto thee, say: All rejoice in what God hath revealed. How many servants spend their wealth in this yet understand not, and how many servants spend and do understand! Say: All are from God - these and those are nurtured by what God hath revealed. But bear witness, O My Name, that God loveth not to command His creation save with what all are capable of understanding. Consider from the first One unto this time - hath there appeared a Manifestation who educated people thus? Nay, they conceal themselves from those who desire this, and forbid it, for that whereby God's Manifestation appeareth is that all in every Revelation seek shelter in God's shadow, and all are exalted by what He willeth. Consider how God hath created gold and silver upon the earth - all belong to God, and in every Revelation none should possess them save God. And when established in the Manifestation of God's Revelation, then all become possessors like what God manifested in the days of Solomon, when a hundred leagues were paved with gold whereon God's hosts stood firm. And if it appear not, thou hast heard how Muhammad, the Messenger of God, placed a stone upon his belly that those who had naught might find solace, and they are patient. Yet God, the Most High, transcends all that hath been created and shall be created, and all stand firm by His command. Consider the movements of the exalted ones and the ways of the noble, and thou shalt surely find sufficiency in what God hath ordained for those who have been given the Book, for this is nearer in the Book of God for the God-fearing. And should that knowledge be disclosed such that all would exchange whatsoever they possess for gold and silver - yet God hath created gold and silver in the earth many times over that amount. In every Dispensation ye strive to establish proofs upon proofs, for all good lieth in the shadow of this all from God, whereby all are enriched. Verily God hath fixed the sun and moon and made them means whereby ye are elevated in the kingdom. Otherwise, with God, gold is like that which is not gold, and God maketh that which is not gold to be gold, according to how ye conduct yourselves in the kingdom. Consider: were God to transform every stone into ruby, wherein would ye glory?
