For God hath already created mountains of ruby in the sea - when thou enterest the sea thou seest the water reddened from the hue of those mountains. Yet God permitteth none to possess these save whom He willeth, for He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. If everything possessed them as they possess other things, how then would ye glory in them? God setteth forth these similitudes regarding the creation of your essence. Observe what sustaineth the kingdom, for everything within its limits hath a sign like unto all things - will ye not then be thankful? Consider the place of ink: if thou were to make it of red ruby, would it suffice thee? Nay, everything in the measure of its existence benefiteth all things as all things benefit each other, but most men do not reflect. Look at the fruit of that knowledge: is it aught but that thou shouldst possess gold and silver and thereby suffice thyself and the believers? Yet before thou possessed that knowledge, God had already sufficed thy needs and the needs of whomsoever He willeth, for He is gracious and kind. What fruit is there whether thou possess it or possess it not, save that thou weary thine essence, when God loveth not that thou shouldst experience any measure of sorrow? Be thou clear-sighted until God gathereth for thee the means, and if thou desirest to witness this, God's sincere servants shall work for thee. Say: Verily God loveth that all who make mention of aught that hath been or shall be created should dwell in glory and wealth, in joy and delight, for God is bountiful and kind. Say: God is well-pleased with those who desire that knowledge which yieldeth fruit from their deeds, as they expend in the path of God. Do ye desire that knowledge only that ye might possess its working and then expend in God's path that your Lord might be pleased with you? Yet God was pleased with you before ye possessed or labored. How then do ye still desire to possess? Say: Yea, by my Lord! My heart loveth to possess it, and were God to send down all the pages, still my heart would not be emptied of the love of That One and all that pleases God, my Lord. Indeed, My heart is consumed with love for That One, and all that God sends down of His good-pleasure shall find ardent love, and this shall never end, for that which pleases God is endless, and We are all journeying in the infinite oceans.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: Know thou that the principal aim in expounding this noble science is the knowledge of the honored Stone and the knowledge of its substance and origin from which it is derived, and thereafter the stages of its separation, purification and union. The divine philosophers have, in one sense, applied the term 'Stone' to the substance and origin from which the Stone is derived, and some have interpreted it as referring to the enduring earth which, after the separation of the Stone, is called the white magnet.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: Concerning what you wrote about the hidden operation, after separation two of its components are and will be dispensed with, as was alluded to in the blessed Persian Tablets of the Supreme Pen. I swear by the life of that Beloved One that this is among the mysteries of the Cause that has never before been mentioned, and until now everyone who has entered into this matter - that is, who has detailed this special substance - has desired that those separated components become one thing, which has been and is impossible. Beyond this no one's intellect has comprehended, and the thoughts of the servants have not advanced a step further, even though it has flowed from the Supreme Pen that like and similar substances should be taken. Nevertheless, they have taken pure water with viscous black oil and that earth which tells of the people of hell, desiring to unite them together. Alas, alas! For between water and oil complete opposition is evident - they have never been and never will be capable of mixing and uniting. And the earth too, when its essence is taken and reaches the state of ash, certainly has not been and will not be capable of life.  Some philosophers have mentioned ash, but what is meant by ash is the body (jasad) not the form (jism), for when the spirit of the form is taken, its life afterward is impossible. In the body there remains a vestige of spirit, though hidden; after treatment it is observed living and animate.  What is meant by water is volatile water, that is, similar to volatile; you must obtain it, and likewise some oil before its solidification, and nurture that water in it until it solidifies. These two components and two elements possess four natures, for in water there is cold and moisture, and in oil there is dryness and heat. This same water solidifies in the oil and is called the noble stone. This is why the philosophers have said "that which is not seen and that which is not found in what is not seen and is not found."  Now observe that some people suppose that the stone exists and countless differences appear concerning it - each group considers some thing to be the stone and busies itself with treating it, wasting their lives. This is why they have said "Work comes after knowledge." In any case, the stone has been and will be hidden, stored, and concealed.  After nurturing it in the eye of the sun which is oil - that is, the heat of the oil draws out its excess moisture - in this case it solidifies and appears like marble. It must be freed from the oil, and after being freed and washed, some of that same water from which this stone was produced must be made to prevail over it, and gradually with a fire like the heat of the sun it must be nurtured until whatever it has taken from the essence of oil is dissolved by this water which is the key, and this operation must be repeated until that which is the essence within this Stone is entirely extracted - and this essence is known as the Red Sulfur, the Philosophers' Gold, and the Two-Winged Gold. Often this essence appears white upon the surface of the water, and sometimes it appears as a most beautiful red. That which is white can, with some cultivation, be observed to turn red. Verily, this is the Red Sulfur, of which none is aware save God, the Possessor of Destiny, Who speaks from the Most Great Scene. Verily, there is no God but He, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. As to what you have written regarding similarity, the purpose is the oiliness of water - that is, water must be cultivated until its inner oiliness becomes manifest. In this state, its mixture with other oils becomes easy, but as long as its watery form remains, it is not and will not be capable of mixture. This water is that which has been called the volatile, the water of air, the fire of air, and by other names. It is the Divine Water. In any case, as mentioned, the acquisition of two elements which possess the four elements is necessary. In this state they are called the Mercury of the East and West. If you wish to dissolve all of that Stone, some of which has been dissolved and united with the Divine Water, it is possible - you must extract that water from it and gradually return a portion to it until all is dissolved. This matter must be completed with very gentle fire or gentle vapor. Then, when all - meaning the Stone and what has appeared from it - manifests in the form of water, gradually through heat its moisture is completely removed. After completion it congeals, and this dissolution and congealment may be completed in one operation, or in three or more times. Often, that very essence which was obtained from the noble Stone produces the work and hope, and is completed - this is Mercury alone. Some have also ground and pulverized the earth of the Stone with that water until they completed the work, then added the tincture, which is that same essence that appeared on the surface of the water, and completed the work. From these explanations, knowledge of the Salt is also obtained.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: Similarly, for the Stone and that which is derived from it, according to the stations and conditions manifested therein and the reflective qualities it assumes, they have found outward examples and similitudes, designating each by a name befitting its station. For instance, before separation it is called by one name, and after separation by other names, just as they have mentioned three stations for the stages of separation: spirit, soul and body - and some have termed these water, fire and earth. Likewise, before purification it bears one name and after purification another, and at each stage of solution, coagulation and sublimation, it takes on a name corresponding to and resembling that station. Thus it has been termed the resplendent water, the sulphuric water, the aerial water, the aerial fire, the volatile, gold, silver, sun, moon, and other names beyond counting save by God alone.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: As to what you wrote concerning the Stone, this station has been mentioned in every tongue, whether Persian or Arabic. However, in one Tablet concerning Mariyah the Copt, this station is mentioned in detail. This evanescent servant, from the first day he attained this Cause and was occupied with transcription, had never heard the Beloved mention anything in this regard. However, some petitions from before and after arrived from various directions inquiring about this matter. Therefore, in response to each one, as was befitting, drops from the ocean of knowledge were manifested, and whenever anyone wished to engage in this pursuit, they were forbidden and told that the time had not yet come - wait until God brings it forth in His Own time. For today all must be focused on another matter, which is teaching the souls with wisdom and utterance, so that the copper of the existence of the servants might be transformed into pure gold through the elixir of the divine Word and that they turn toward the supreme horizon....  In truth, nothing can be clearer than what was mentioned in the Persian treatise; everything was explained in detail in that treatise. As to what you wrote about returning water to the body, if there is a reduction in the repetition of water, and what should be done - the question was submitted, and He said: First, you must know that the water which is intended is the divine water, and that water is characterized by oiliness, for oiliness is concealed within it. For if the water were pure water, meaning plain water, it would never be capable of extracting the hidden oil in the earth which is called the gold of the sages and the essence of essences. Moreover, mixture would be impossible, for the hidden oil in the earth has been called fire and red sulfur in one station, and there can be no mixture between oil, which is the essence of fire, and water. This matter is clear and evident to every discerning one. Anyone who becomes cognizant of the water, if there is reduction in the process and it diminishes, can take its equivalent.... Know thou that God hath appointed a time for every matter, and verily it hath not come to pass, but when it doth come to pass it shall appear through the power of truth. He, verily, is the True Informer, the Trustworthy. We have not given leave to anyone to occupy himself with this matter. To this testifieth My tongue and My pen and beyond them thy Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: As to the questions mentioned by that honored one: First, you had written that when we observe the world of creation, we notice that gold and ruby may become corrupted before reaching their state of perfection, but after reaching maturity this is not possible. Yes, such questions have been asked and answers have descended from the Most Exalted Pen - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for it. Search and perhaps you will find it, for it suffices for all the world. In any case, it should be known to that honored one that regarding the nature of gold and ruby, who has not had knowledge of it, and the essential nature of gold is not known. Even if we accept this, first we say that this inability exists in contingent beings, but God has power over all things. He transforms whatever He wills - if He wishes to turn all the gold of the world into copper, He is able and empowered. And if He wills, He creates the possibility of change in all things by His command, then changes it by His sovereignty, for He is the Omnipotent, the Powerful. Moreover, gold does turn into copper, as the Pen of God has written, and they have said that whoever denies this should come into the presence and observe it. Beyond this, philosophers have stated that when gold remains in soil for a time, it turns to soil. And even without the words of philosophers, there is the Word of God which states "I created all from dust and to dust shall I return them." Therefore it is established that gold turns to dust, and dust is clearly baser than copper. Likewise ruby, when placed in fire, becomes like ashes. Consider the heart of the believer like a ruby - this ruby-like quality holds true for it as long as the fire of rejection does not touch it, but after encountering that fire it surely turns to ashes. This is clear to anyone with vision. Furthermore, no one is aware of divine wisdom to understand what it requires or does not require. Whatever matter appears from His sacred presence is itself the decree that required it to appear. If it was not required, it would not have appeared. Therefore look to the decree itself that has become manifest, rather than imagining in vain that such-and-such does not accord with wisdom....  Regarding what was previously mentioned about the ruby, it has become necessary to explain it in detail. In rubies various types and different colors are observed. All of its colors are altered in fire and its freshness and delicacy are lost, except for the pomegranate-colored and the crimson types - these two, if they encounter mild fire from behind a veil, their color somewhat increases. But if it encounters the fire that is known among the philosophers, it will certainly change, and if it touches the fire known in natural craft as red sulfur, it will immediately calcify just as gold, silver, copper and other metallic bodies are calcified through various medicines.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: As to what was written concerning the elixir, this Most Exalted Word was repeatedly heard from the tongue of the Lord of Names - exalted be His utterance and mighty His proof: "O servant in attendance! Whatever hath been revealed concerning the elixir from the heaven of divine Will was in response to the questions of the servants. They repeatedly asked until that which was revealed was revealed. Otherwise, the Most Exalted Pen would not have addressed it and hath not had, nor hath, any inclination to mention such matters. The Prophets have made mention of it, and likewise the philosophers have had countless discussions about the existence or non-existence of this art. Some have said that bodies other than gold are prevented from attaining to this station due to ailments, and that the power and balance of the elixir removes this and reveals their original color and essence. Others have deemed this impossible, saying that these metals are each composed of different elements and that the elixir is incapable of acting upon different contradictory things. Many philosophers have considered the transformation of essence impossible. The books of the people are filled with such mentions, objections, and differences among philosophers and others. However, if one possessed of insight and vision were to reflect upon the utterances that have flowed from the Most Exalted Pen, the matter of its existence or non-existence would become evident and manifest unto him." Time and again this servant has presented the petitions of the friends of God who have inquired about this matter, and some have shown utmost insistence in their questioning. Therefore there flowed from the Most Exalted Pen that which exists. Once this Most Exalted Word was heard, He said: "O servant in attendance! If no answer were to be revealed, there would be fear that they might attribute it to a lack of divine knowledge." And to each person an answer was revealed containing within it a prohibition, save for one or two. The prohibition against engaging in this work has been repeatedly revealed. The wisdom of the past has entirely differed from the wisdom of the present. In the elements, in the planets, and likewise in movements, spirits and bodies, fundamental differences have appeared, both in effects and in numbers, and assuredly in future years that which is now hidden from eyes shall be revealed. This Most Great Revelation is the cause and reason for the opening of the gates of sciences and wisdom. No one hath yet fully enumerated the sciences and hosts of Truth. How many manifest suns have not been seen, and how many moons remain hidden from sight! If all the world were to gather and attempt to enumerate the creation of but one of the fixed stars and the planets revolving around it, they would surely find themselves powerless and would utter the blessed words "None knoweth the hosts of thy Lord save Him."

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: Among the doubts which some of the polytheists have cast in this land is this: can gold become copper? Say: Yea, by my Lord! But with Us is its knowledge; We teach it to whomsoever We wish with knowledge from Our presence. And whoso is in doubt, let him ask God his Lord that He may show him, that he may become of the certain ones. And in copper attaining to the station of gold there is clear proof of gold returning to its original state, were they to perceive. All metals attain to each other's weight, form and substance, but its knowledge is with Us in a hidden Book. We say the knowledge of the deniers hath not ascended to this station that they might understand gold becometh copper. They have not even understood so much as that it becometh dust - this station which hath been evident to every person of insight, that all appeareth from dust and returneth to dust. And dust in worth and value is lesser than copper, for it is counted among bodies while copper is among metals, and this is most obvious and evident. And were people found worthy and mature, assuredly some of the hidden divine sciences would be mentioned at this point. But what is decreed is decreed.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: Thou hast asked God thy Lord to grant thee power over mercury, which ye call quicksilver. Yea, We have power over all things. This is a sign of truth concerning minerals - touch them not except in truth, then put thy trust in God, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting. Say: None hath been granted knowledge of this living thing save the Point, as ye observe in the beginning of the matter. Thus take the sign of the Point and place it upon the living thing, and thou shalt find it submissive unto God, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of all worlds. This is a mystery in the Mother Book among those who draw nigh. It behooveth not to reveal more than this, and verily We are the preservers of God's Cause. Should thou take its essence, this is nearer - verily We are All-Knowing. By the life of Him Whom God shall make manifest, if thou placest the mercury in a crystal vessel and setteth it upon a gentle fire, then addeth some of this essence unto it, thou shalt find it all become one piece, and when thou removest it, it shall be a mighty ingot. Say: Blessed be God, the Lord of the worlds! We have seen this from one who fashioned it - this is of God's handiwork, the One, the Inaccessible. But I counsel thee not to attach thy heart to this, for the Cause of God transcendeth it.... As to what thou hast mentioned regarding thy taking water from that tree without having been commanded beforehand - this profiteth thee not. Draw not nigh save unto that which benefiteth thee - a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. If thou art able to take water from the leaves which We indeed witnessed upon that land, growing from that which its inhabitants from those regions have not... this would be better for thee and nearer unto the worlds. We know not upon what remembrance these people make mention, but it is a rustling tree with small leaves emerging from the earth without its tree having grown. When touched by yellowness its color changes, yet taking its water leaveth no trace therein. Those who engage in this craft have veiled themselves from it and from its effects, yet still they persist therein. The essence of the matter is that thou shouldst be content with what God hath ordained for thee. And if thou desirest to see something, then create from what thou hast mentioned regarding half the amount, for this is nearer in the Book among the believers. Beyond this I know not what thou intendest, but God thy Lord will inform thee when He seeth it is best for thee. He is indeed the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. What I have written: Glory be unto Thee! There is no God but Thee. Verily Thou art the Ever-Living Who dieth not. This fleeing mercury will never remain stable upon that which God, the Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting, hath created.

Subject: alchemy; the elixir
Quotation: In regard to what thou hast asked about the craft, this Wronged One hath not, of His own accord, set forth anything on this subject.  However, certain individuals have asked questions, and, in response, the Pen of the Most High set down the explanations that are found in the Tablets.  There can be no doubt that what hath been revealed is, and shall ever be, the indisputable truth.  Wert thou to reflect, thou wouldst bear witness, ere the initiation of this work, to the fact that the Pen of the All-Knowing hath revealed the utter truth.  Nevertheless, its appearance hath been made one of the signs of the coming of age of the human race, and the time when this shall happen hath been fixed.  As yet it hath not come, but when it cometh it shall be manifested through the power of Him Who is the Sovereign Truth.  He, verily, is the All-Informed, the All-Knowing.  For this reason all have been prohibited from becoming engaged with it.  None hath the right to busy himself therewith.  This is what hath been decreed by the Beloved of the worlds in His perspicuous Book. Strive in this Day to attain the Elixir of the Divine Word.  It is the effective agent, the protector, the conqueror, the divine water, and the crown of victory within the Primal Reality.  Indeed, it is the matchless essence, the secret of the Concealer, and the secret of secrets.

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: Regarding the matter of hashish, you wrote that some Iranians are afflicted with its consumption. Glory be to God! This intoxicant is worse than all intoxicants and its prohibition is explicit. It causes confusion of thoughts and deadening of the human spirit in all conditions. How can people become familiar with this fruit of the Zaqqum tree and become afflicted with a state that makes them truly subhuman? How can they use this prohibited thing and become deprived of the favors of the All-Merciful Lord? Most assuredly, absolutely, you must counsel people as much as you can to become averse to this opium and hashish of Zaqqum and to repent before the Divine Threshold. Wine causes the mind to become oblivious and leads to ignorant behavior, but this filthy opium and vile hashish eliminate reason, deaden the soul, freeze the spirit, weaken the body, and render one completely frustrated and lost. Despite this, how can one dare to use it? Observe how the people of India and China, being addicted to smoking this plant of the depths of hell, are deadened, stupefied, downtrodden, abject and degraded. A thousand of them cannot resist one person. Eight hundred million Chinese people could not stand against a few regiments of Europeans, because cowardice, fear and dread have been kneaded into their nature due to smoking opium. Glory be to God! Why do others not learn from this? And according to reports this abominable practice has spread to the realm of Iran as well. May God protect us and you from this abominable prohibited thing, this filthy smoke and Zaqqum of hell, as God, blessed and exalted be He, has said: "It will boil in their bellies like scalding water."

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: But they must on no account allow their children to drink wine or alcoholic drinks. Abdul-Baha spoke of the Druzes who never drank wine or smoked, and in consequence of this, many diseases were quite unknown to them.

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: Regarding what you wrote about opium, although it has had some benefit at times, its harm has been and continues to be considerable. This blessed word was heard from the Master's tongue - this year they prohibited it.

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: In reality wine or spirits taken even in moderate quantities does not permanent good. It is like urging a horse to full speed by whipping him. The whip represents the effect of wine on man's body. Wine taken as a medicine for weak people, who have all their lives been used to it, is permitted. But they must on account allow their children to drink wine or alcoholic drinks.

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: Gambling and the use of opium have been forbidden unto you. Eschew them both, O people, and be not of those who transgress. Beware of using any substance that induceth sluggishness and torpor in the human temple and inflicteth harm upon the body. We, verily, desire for you naught save what shall profit you, and to this bear witness all created things, had ye but ears to hear.... It hath been forbidden you to smoke opium. We, truly, have prohibited this practice through a most binding interdiction in the Book. Should anyone partake thereof, assuredly he is not of Me. Fear God, O ye endued with understanding!

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: It is said that at one time a King went out travelling incognito. He put on a humble suite of cloth[es] and started on his way. After a few days journey he lost his way in the scorching desert and finally reached at the door of an Arab tent. The Arab finding the man exhausted from heat and hunger dragged him under the shade. When the King was revived he asked the Arab what he had to eat and drink. "I have a goat-skin of wine and a little goat" the Arab answered. "Very well. Bring the wine and kill the goat to be cooked." he said. The wine was brought. When the King drank one cup he looked at the Arab and said: "Do you know who I am?" "No." "Then you must know that I am a soldier in the King's Army." The Arab was glad to entertain a brave man.  He drank another cup. "Do you know who I am?" "Who are you?" "I am a Minster in the King's Council Chamber." "I am delighted to receive such a distinguished statesman."  A third cup was taken. "Do you know who I am?" "Well?" "I am the King himself." The Arab could not stand it any longer. He arose from his place and took from him the goat-skin of wine. "Why do you do this for?" the guest asked astonished. "Because I believe if you drink another cup you will declare yourself to be the prophet of God and a fifth cup may raise you to the station of God, so it is better for you to cool down a little, to cool down a little."

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: One meaning of "the accursed tree" is tobacco, which is detestable, condemned, harmful and poisonous. It wastes wealth and brings illness and melancholy. As for wine, by the explicit text of the Most Holy Book, its consumption is forbidden, for its drinking causes chronic diseases, weakens the nerves and impairs reason. But hashish is worse than all, and opium destroys the very foundation of faith, certitude and the human race.

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: The judge was accustomed to inject opium in his system, a very bad evil. The Master made him give it up; his family were most thankful and pleased. The judge would say that when the time of injection arrives and I do not get it I feel as dead, weak and impotent. "He was a drunkard before he said but if he did not drink for a day or two he would feel the longing for it as the injection of opium." Finally he had a hard fight but he gave it up at last.

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: Another subject which was discussed was 'smoking' and 'drinking' because the Druises as a rule are addicted to neither of these two evil habits. Mohamadan history contains many references to these subjects and the Master pointed out that there were in the past ages many temperance Societies and as a result of their activities teetotalers became very numerous. There were many men and women who abstained totally from all intoxicating drinks and especially from smoking tobacco.

Subject: alcohol and drugs; tobacco; opium
Quotation: Concerning opium which you wrote about - the user, buyer and seller are all deprived of divine grace and bounty, and by explicit divine text it is forbidden. The wine drinker is a hundred thousand degrees better than the opium user. It was extremely condemned in the Holy Presence, such that whenever opium use was mentioned, the Blessed Face would change. It is forbidden to this degree, unless someone buys and sells it for medical treatment, as used in pharmacies solely for treating illnesses. My wish is that, God willing, the friends will gradually abstain even from smoking tobacco, let alone opium.

Subject: all things are in motion; kinds of motion
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/all things are in motion; kinds of motion.txt
Quotation: As long as the birds are soaring aloft they are, moment by moment, rising in station but as soon as they stand still, their fall begins.

Subject: all things are in motion; kinds of motion
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/all things are in motion; kinds of motion.txt
Quotation: Now it is known that all motions are forced motions. This sun is compelled to move, even these other spheres are compelled to move. All are forced, not volitional.

Subject: all things are in motion; kinds of motion
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/all things are in motion; kinds of motion.txt
Quotation: Motion is the sign of life. If there be no wind, no motion the air becomes impure. When water is stagnant it also becomes impure. The point is this, that all existing things are in motion, that motion is the cause of life and lack of motion is the cause of death.

Subject: all things are in motion; kinds of motion
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/all things are in motion; kinds of motion.txt
Quotation: All things in creation require motion for their existence, from smallest particles to largest bodies. Motion brings universal benefits. Without motion there is nonexistence. Water becomes altered when still, air corrupts when stagnant, bodies become ill when motionless.

Subject: all things are in motion; kinds of motion
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/all things are in motion; kinds of motion.txt
Quotation: There is motion in everything, all the plants are moving. All bodies whether large or small are moving. There is no globe which is absolutely stationary. Motion is the sign of life. If there be no wind, no motion the air becomes impure. When water is stagnant it also becomes impure. The point is this, that all existing things are in motion, that motion is the cause of life and lack of motion is the cause of death.

Subject: all things are in motion; kinds of motion
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/all things are in motion; kinds of motion.txt
Quotation: For example, [he says] motion is of two kinds: forced motion and circular motion. Circular motion is evidence of will. Since we observe circular motion in these spheres, they possess will, and therefore in these spheres there exists an intellectual force which is the governing force of that sphere. Now it is known that all motion is forced motion. This sun is compelled to move, even these other spheres are compelled to move. All motion is forced, not volitional. There is no circular motion; that connecting force that exists between all created things is one single motion.

Subject: alteration of the divine will [bada]
Quotation: For the Truth sometimes jests and makes light - He promised punishment would descend upon the people of Jonah, but then due to their pleading and supplication, the sea of His mercy was stirred and He changed His decree, casting Jonah into the whale's mouth.

Subject: alteration of the divine will [bada]
Quotation: Concerning their Qa'imiyyat and Bada', it is related in Biharu'l-Anvar from 'Uthman Thuri that the Sadiq said: "This matter was concerning me, meaning it was the divine Will that I should arise and fill the earth with justice and equity, but Bada' occurred." Likewise, Majlisi relates in Bihar from the Sadiq who said: "The time for this matter was in the year 140, but when you were informed of it, you disclosed it; therefore God delayed that time." He also relates that the Sadiq, peace be upon him, said: "O Aba Ishaq, this matter was concerning me, but its time was delayed."

Subject: angels
Quotation: "By God the Truth, the angels of the Paradise of Holiness welcomed them with radiant faces"

Subject: angels
Quotation: The clamor of the heedless has become the cause of a great celebration in the Supreme Concourse - the tribes of angels and the Spirit give each other glad tidings and prepare to welcome, for verily the blessed spirit of Mahdi has intended the Supreme Companion.

Subject: angels
Quotation: Verily those who say 'Our Lord is God' and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them.

Subject: angels
Quotation: By God the Truth, verily the angels of the Supreme Assembly pray for thee every morn and eve and announce to thee glad-tidings!

Subject: angels
Quotation: And the angels of the Supreme Concourse have called out with a great and resonant voice in the ears of the people of earth and heaven

Subject: angels
Quotation: in the lower realm, angels from Kingdom of Glory have arisen to pray and supplicate and to intone the verses of Divine Unity in a holy gathering.

Subject: angels
Quotation: This is a prayer to the crimson light whose bearer was Israfil, peace be upon him... Bless, O God, the bearer of Thy crimson light, Israfil, peace be upon him, morning and evening.

Subject: angels
Quotation: And as for what you asked about God's word (mighty and glorious is He) regarding the command for the angels to prostrate and Iblis's pride...And all the angels prostrated to Adam except Iblis, who alone transgressed

Subject: angels
Quotation: and whatsoever God hath created in the Garden of Refuge of angels who glorify God by night and by day and never cease, and the angels who praise God by night and by day and never tire, and the angels who proclaim the unity of God and never falter, and the angels who magnify God and never wax proud, and whatsoever angel God hath created in the heavens but that He hath created in Paradise a celestial maiden.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: This is that whereby the heavens are nearly rent asunder, and the earth is cleft, and the mountains crumble

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: The All-Bountiful hath come, riding upon the clouds...and the Hour appeared with its signs, and the Resurrection with its mysteries.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: on a Day when the pillars of all created things were shaken, and the hearts of all beings were set ablaze, and every pregnant one cast her burden, and every nursing mother became heedless of the infant she was nursing

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: The heaven hath come with its smoke, and the matter hath been decreed by God, the Almighty, the Self-Subsisting. The heaven hath been cleft asunder with clouds, and the Youth hath come upon the clouds, yet ye know Him not.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: The Hour hath come and the moon of reckoning hath been cleft, and trembling hath seized the polytheists. The palm trees have been uprooted and souls have been thunderstruck, and the houses lie desolate upon their trellises.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: The Hour hath come, and the Trumpet hath been sounded, and the Balance proclaimeth... This is the day wherein the Trump resoundeth and the Bell ringeth out and the Trumpet proclaimeth: 'The Kingdom is God's, the Possessor of this wondrous Day.'

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: When that time comes, turn to the Holy Land from whence God's breath passes. When that time comes, approach Carmel (a mountain near Akka) even if crawling, then turn to the Holy Valley (the Syrian wilderness), the gathering place, the white spot.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: These are the verses of God sent down in truth, and none remember them except those possessed of understanding... through Whose will the suns of names were eclipsed and the moon was cleft in the heaven of destiny and the mountains passed away as passing clouds

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: And on that Day, the faces of the polytheists shall be in veils of fire, hidden around the fire. God has ordained no food for them save from a boiling spring that neither nourishes nor avails them aught, and God has prepared for them a painful chastisement in justice upon the truth.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: The foundations of the Concourse on High were shaken when the Call was raised from the Supreme Horizon, and thou seest the people stunned by the thunderous blast that hath caused all the powers of the earth to tremble, and it shall be followed by another blast, even more grievous and terrible.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: By God the Truth, verily the suns have been folded up, and the stars have been scattered, and the heaven has been cleft asunder, and the earth has been shaken with convulsions, and the mountains have been scattered as dust, and the palm trunks have been uprooted, and the seas have overflowed on the day when the earth shone with the light of its Lord

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: The Inevitable has come to pass...The earthquakes have come and the tribes have wailed out of fear of God...The Deafening Blast has cried out...Has the Great Catastrophe been fulfilled?...Have the stars fallen?...mountains have been scattered...Paradise has been adorned with the roses of inner meanings, and Hell has been kindled with the fire of the wicked

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: wherein the Trump would be sounded and the call of the Bugle would be raised, the Bridge would be set up and the Balance would be established...wherein the Trump was sounded and all who are in Thy heaven and earth were thunderstruck, save those whom the hand of Thy power did rescue. And I testify that the Bridge hath been set up and the Balance hath been established

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: And after three days and a half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them. Three days and a half, as we explained earlier, is 1,260 years. These two Persons whose bodies were lying soulless-that is, the teachings and the religion that Muhammad had established and that 'Ali had promoted, whose reality had vanished, and of which only an empty form had remained-were again endowed with spirit; that is to say, those teachings were established anew.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: Then there shall be another blast, and lo! they shall rise and gaze around them: And the earth shall shine with the light of her Lord. And from the second blast, spiritual realities and celestial essences shall find life and shall be set in motion by the dawning of the Sun of Truth. This second blast is the appearance of the Ancient Beauty, Him Whom God shall make manifest. This is the day when the heavens were folded up. This is the day when the sun was wound up. This is the day when the moon was cleft asunder. This is the day when the stars were scattered. This is the day when the mountains were set in motion. This is the day when the dead came forth from their graves.

Subject: apocalyptic imagery
Quotation: The Trumpet hath been blown, and lo, all eyes have stared up with terror, and the hearts of all who are in the heavens and on the earth have trembled, except them whom the breath of the verses of God hath quickened, and who have detached themselves from all things. This is the Day whereon the earth shall tell out her tidings. The workers of iniquity are her burdens, could ye but perceive it. The moon of idle fancy hath been cleft, and the heaven hath given out a palpable smoke. The earth hath been shaken, and the mountains have passed away, and the angels have appeared, rank on rank, before Us. Say: The heavens have been folded together, and the earth is held within His grasp, and the corrupt doers have been held by their forelock, and still they understand not.

Subject: apostles; early disciples of Christ
Quotation: They gathered on top of a mountain, and made a pact whereby they would consent to bear tribulations, renounce their comfort, and spread guidance. When they came down from the mountain, each of them went in a different direction and never returned.

Subject: apostles; early disciples of Christ
Quotation: Consider ye that after His Holiness the Spirit (Christ), the disciples did not stop for a moment nor did they choose rest for themselves. If the disciples had not been firm, after the departure of His Holiness the Christ, his Cause would have been utterly effaced and made non-existent.

Subject: apostles; early disciples of Christ
Quotation: The disciples who had followed His teachings met together in consultation upon the summit of a mountain near Jaffa... Then they took an oath and covenant among themselves, embraced each other and descended from the mountain, some going to the Eastward, some to the West, North and South.

Subject: apostles; early disciples of Christ
Quotation: After His Holiness Christ His apostles did not rest for one moment and devoted all their energies to the promotion of the Gospel of Salvation. If the Apostles did not manifest that Superhuman steadfastness the Cause of Christ would have been disappeared entirely from the face of the earth in its beginning.

Subject: apostles; early disciples of Christ
Quotation: Consider ye that after His Holiness the Spirit (Christ), the disciples did not stop for a moment nor did they choose rest for themselves. They strove night and day. If the disciples had not been firm, after the departure of His Holiness the Christ, his Cause would have been utterly effaced and made non-existent.

Subject: apostles; early disciples of Christ
Quotation: On the other hand, consider the Apostles of Christ! Although outwardly they were fishermen, yet because they renounced this world, opened their eyes to the Divine Universe, forgot entirely their personal selves, dedicated their lives to the Light of the world and became self-sacrificing in the path of His Holiness Christ â€" may my life be a ransom to Him!

Subject: arcs of ascent and descent
Quotation: "In the Koran there is a verse which speaks of the "lowest point of the low" as being the station of man. If we represent creation by a circle, at the top of it is God the creator, from His left descends the mineral creation, beginning first with the mineral kingdom, next below that is the vegetable kingdom, below that again is the animal kingdom, and at the bottom of the circle is man... But though this station is the "lowest of the low", it is also the dawning point of the new life, and the spiritual ascent to God!"

Subject: arcs of ascent and descent
Quotation: This is God's design for man - first descent through matter and then ascent through spirit, to teach him and develop him. A child must learn the alphabet before it can read, and the soul must gain self-consciousness through matter before it can know God.

Subject: arcs of ascent and descent
Quotation: For human reality is the dividing line between light and shadow, the confluence of the two seas, and the ultimate point in the arc of descent. Therefore it hath the capacity for all stations: through education it acquireth virtues, and without education it remaineth in the lowest depths of deficiency. Every child may become either a source of illumination for the world or a cause of darkness throughout the horizons.

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation: Help and assist others in need. The poor are the trust of God.

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation: Never talk to God to a man with an empty stomach. Feed him first.

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation: Beware lest ye withhold the surplus of your means from them that are near of kin unto you, and from the poor and the needy.

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation: O concourse of rulers! Turn ye unto the poor. God hath created you and them from one thing. Make ye in your possessions a portion for them. This will profit you throughout ages and centuries.

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation: become a treasury of riches for the poor and a shelter and asylum for the fugitive, bring joy and radiance to the destitute, and aid the needy through the strengthening grace of the All-Merciful

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation: In treating the poor, the weak, the needy and the strangers, provide blessed healing and guide them to health and wellbeing... Give great importance to the matter of the poor - be a refuge and shelter to every poor one, and a protector and helper to every sick one.

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation: It was a good gathering. I saw that the poor were very glad. Truly, the hearts of the poor are very tender; they are easily affected.  The hearts of the poor are easily broken. Thus, whenever a person can bring gladness to them, it is the right thing to do. When I was in 'Akka, I constantly extended invitations to the poor. You are, however, unaware of the dire straits in which the poor ones of the East live.

Subject: assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/assistance to the poor and lowly; the orphan; the sick.txt
Quotation:
"Should I also tend to the non-Baha'is?" I asked. "Yes, indeed," 'Abdu'l-Baha remarked, "We too are devoted to the poor. By all means, attend to all, particularly the needy."  ABU2343
The weak and the poor must be cared for.

Subject: astrology and numerology
Quotation: These rules of the stars are from the ancient astronomers. They used to take the sun coming out of the Zodiac and from that they would take out other things, but they had no true ambition... In ancient times the king had a man who used to make these calculations especially for him. If the Shah wanted to make a journey, this man might say, 'Don't go. If you do it will be dangerous.'

Subject: attaining good pleasure of God
Quotation: For the good-pleasure of God and that of His servants are the greatest of divine favours, nay His good-pleasure resideth in our being pleased with His servants.

Subject: attaining good pleasure of God
Quotation: Nothing has been or will be sweeter to the taste of lovers than the good-pleasure of God. Blessed is the servant who has attained, and the maidservant who has attained unto this exalted station.

Subject: attaining good pleasure of God
Quotation: What befitteth the friend is submission to, and contentment with, the good-pleasure of the Friend. Therefore, be thou content with the good-pleasure of the Friend and with whatsoever proceedeth from Him.

Subject: attaining good pleasure of God
Quotation: Forever supplicate and entreat at the court of Majesty and beg confirmation and assistance. Make ye an effort that you may win the good pleasure of Baha'o'llah. All the natural and supernatural advancements in the human world revolve around this one problem.

Subject: attaining good pleasure of God
Quotation: All my petition, O my God, is that Thou ordain for me Thy good-pleasure, even were it less than nine times nine-tenths of a mustard seed at the moment when my spirit departeth. For should my spirit leave me while Thou art not pleased with me, though I should have acquired all good things, they would profit me not, or though I should have attained all glory, it would not exalt me.

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: Serve God day and night and seek happiness from His name...thou mayest seek absolute spirituality

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: Find the life of the heart and spiritual joy; seek mighty gladness and wondrous spirit and fragrance; find repose of soul and peace of conscience; become of the divine hosts and of the celestial angels.

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: The reality of that world is the world of holiness and radiance, pure and sanctified above all imagination and thought. That immaculate world is so established and enduring that no tongue can describe it.

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: Spiritual transformation comes through self-effacement: "Be lowly, that you may become noble. Be humble, that you may become as a rising star. Become effaced and evanescent, that you may find the ecstasy of the eternal wine."

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: Attachment to the hem of the Spiritual Lord of Hosts and divine power will rescue man from the abyss of ignorance and raise him to the zenith of perfection, will call him to virtuous qualities and deliver him from base characteristics

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: The human temple is like unto a niche, and the heart is like unto a glass globe, and the love of God is like unto the light within that glass. When that lamp is lit, the globe becomes illumined and the physical niche likewise becomes bright and radiant.

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: You have lit a lamp in the heart whose radiance is heavenly; you have planted a tree in the garden of being whose fruit is divine; you have donned a garment whose adornment is eternal splendor; and you have drunk a cup whose intoxication is everlasting felicity.

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: The Prophets have been sent down in order to quicken the soul of man with the spirit of the Kingdom. This spirit is the cause of eternal life. This spirit is the cause everlasting felicity. This spirit is the cause of entrance into the Kingdom of God. This is the spirit which makes the worldly individual heavenly, and causes the darkened to become radiant.

Subject: attaining the life of the spirit
Quotation: They who are intoxicated with the divine chalice must needs experience ecstasy and joy, and they who receive glad-tidings of the gifts of the Kingdom must needs attain to delight. The cries and sighs of those intoxicated ones are essential, and the surge and tumult of the lovers are necessary - otherwise hard stone is better than a dead heart and a frozen existence.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Q: Will the Tablets and Utterances of Baha'u'llah be added to our Bible? A: No, they are a distinct Revelation of God and will form a Book larger than our Bible.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: In those days, all Tablets were revealed and sent down in the blessed handwriting, or He would be engaged in writing

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: The passage that was written in the letter of Andalib is correct. Do not change the passage, for there is wisdom in it.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Oral accounts cannot be authoritative; perhaps the listener did not properly understand. Reliance must be placed on the written word.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: We commanded the servant present before Us, and he heard and wrote down what the Tongue of Grandeur spoke forth in his luminous station

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: These three passages were on one yellow page in the blessed handwriting of the Ancient Beauty, may His Most Great Remembrance be glorified.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: We did indeed change the Book of Joseph before, and We sent down the Book of Justice thereafter, and verily therein are clear verses for people who believe

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: We gathered them from the Books, Scriptures and Tablets and compiled them in one Tablet that all might attain unto God's special favors and be freed and delivered from all else.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: This Tablet was written during childhood (in Adrianople). At certain times, some expressions have been mentioned according to the disposition of some. The true intention must be observed

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: "Baha'o'llah dictated the Book of Ighan to me 1275 A.H. (1858-1859 A.D.) in less than twenty-four hours." "Sometimes Baha'o'llah the Blessed Perfection dictated simultaneously to two or three scribes."

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Any one quoting me must have authority written either with my own hand, or Tablets signed with my seal. Otherwise these statements do not belong to me. Every instruction, every teaching that I desire to spread I will write with my own hand. You must know this generally. Never accept any statement without my writing which is signed and sealed -- any statement.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Some Tablets in the script of revelation were sent from this servant present before the Throne, as there was no time for signing. Several unsigned Tablets were sent - give these to whomever they deem appropriate.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: As commanded, this Tablet was revealed from the heaven of the Divine Will and transcribed from the original revelation and dispatched, along with Tablets numbering the Greatest Name which thou hadst previously requested

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: The Covenant-breakers produced a tablet, which they attributed it to the Ancient Beauty. Therein it was clearly stated that the numerical value of Kull u Shay (all things = 36 indicated the time limit when the Cause of Baha'u'llah would, God forbid, be disbanded or dispersed. Somehow the friends managed to obtain a copy of this tablet and sent it to the presence of 'Abdu'l-Baha, Who said there were numerous tablets corrupted like this one and that it was unimportant. "The House of Justice will put things right," He said. "It will gather together all the Sacred Writings, scrutinized them carefully, and pronounce its conclusive findings, and should any make contradictory remarks, he would be severely dealt with." Then He gave an explanation about how such a tablet never existed and was not from the Ancient Beauty and was not in His blessed idiom.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: And regarding the Book of Iqan, its correct version was bestowed upon His Honor Ali-Qabel-Akbar, upon him be Baha - the existing copies must either be made to conform with it or be rewritten anew from it, this latter being preferable and more fitting.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: I have written these letters in the most beauteous form, and fashioned them in the Book, in a Book mighty and sublime, in the most graceful calligraphy, on the finest of paper, with the most excellent refinement, in the most wondrous and original manner.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: And send thou likewise this Book unto the King of that region with golden ink that thou mayest be numbered among the helpers of that which is written. We have indeed conveyed thy Lord's decree in the Mother City and its environs in three Books of truthful verses.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: they have intended to steal the Book of God - that is, the Persian Bayan and Ahsanul-Qisas... It is obligatory and incumbent upon all the friends of Truth that whosoever possesses them should preserve them and guard them from this rebellious and transgressing band.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding what was written about honoring the Sacred Writings, whatever is beloved should be written. One must act in such a way that the Tablets remain in their original delicacy. They should be placed on separate sheets, read, and then preserved in a special place.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: At the time of the ascension of Baha'u'llah, as we were otherwise occupied, I gave him two boxes containing divine Writings. He has concealed them. He has kept them so that after my passing he might bring them out and use them in accord with his personal inclination.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Concerning what thou didst write about the translation of the Most Holy Book made by one of the loved ones of God - although the intentions of the translator were good, yet since such matters in these days become a cause of differences, therefore it is not permissible.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: It is submitted to Samandar that previously a packet of sublime and inaccessible Holy Tablets was sent addressed to His Honor Ibn-i-Abhar. Due to wisdom, some Tablets that should have been sent in that same packet were delayed at that time. They are being sent this time.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: A few days before the Ascension of the Blessed Beauty, He commanded 'Abdu'l-Baha to gather the papers in His blessed chamber and put them in a bag. According to His blessed command, the papers were collected and placed in two bags. He said "These papers are entrusted to you."

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding what was mentioned about the blessed verse, that the person in question said they had changed the verses and had written "yati'llah" instead of "ya'tihumu'llah" - it is very clear and evident that no change was intended, rather it was a reference to the meaning of the verse.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Whosoever quotes a statement from my tongue, ask from him the authority of the same, either in my handwriting or with my signature. If he has such an authority in his hand, all right; if he has no such authority, do not give any importance to tradition. Keep this criterion always before your view.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: The writings of the Point, exalted be His glory, the Bayan, were revealed in the manner of verses and in portions from the Book of God, exalted be His glory. Therefore, let these portions be bound into another volume, and if God willeth, all that hath been revealed in the Book shall be gathered for us.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: That which thou hadst written concerning the distribution of verses and their dispatch to the known place is understood. The Book of Laws was revealed in the language of verses in this land, and likewise some were revealed in Persian in the Land of Mystery. However, permission for their dissemination has not yet dawned.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding what was written about the omission of the word la from the revealed verse in the Tablet to Ismu'llah Ha, on whom be the Glory of God - often there is no opportunity for this servant to review again, hence in some Tablets it may be observed that one or two letters have been omitted. This blessed word is exactly as you have written it.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: A further submission is that several months ago, a sacred Tablet known as the Proclamation, as well as the Glad-Tidings, were dispatched according to the command of the Lord of the Unseen and the Seen. This Tablet contains laws that were scattered throughout the Most Holy Book and other Tablets, which the Blessed Being Himself gathered together.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: According to the explicit Text, this servant is the Interpreter of the Holy Writ, and whatsoever of the writings is not confirmed by Him cannot be trusted, save for that which is in the hand of Baha'u'llah Himself, and even that must be examined with the utmost care and attention to ensure that not an iota hath been added, subtracted or changed.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: The number of revealed Tablets sent is twenty-one. God willing, may all attain unto them. Tablets have been revealed to such an extent that it is impossible to enumerate them. From the Persian and Arabic, whatever is suitable for these days should be gathered and the divine words should be imparted according to the requirements of the station and the souls.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding what you wrote about not having received the Tablets revealed from the heaven of the Divine Will, and your request for copies of those exalted Tablets - a special volume hath been revealed from the Divine heaven of authority specifically for you, and the answer to the questions of the Afnan, upon them be the Most Glorious Glory of God, hath also been revealed therein.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Thereafter, one envelope containing sacred, glorious and blessed Tablets was sent last week, and now another envelope previously described in detail is being sent. At this moment while engaged in this writing, another envelope arrived containing fresh and flowing verses which, like a newly arrived flower, diffused such a fragrance of praise for the Beloved of all worlds that it gave strength to the heart and keenness to sight.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: I counsel thee by the Most Great Truth, and unto those who gaze upon this leaf: Write not with black ink a single letter of what God hath caused to flow from the Pen of the Bab. Write the Book with yellow water of red gold, for all that hath proceeded from the Bab, if ye are able. And if ye are unable, then write with white, or yellow, or green, or red ink. For God hath forbidden unto the believers black ink in this Most Great Gate.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: This evanescent one requests of your honor to arrange, as far as possible, that since each of the friends who has been seized had writings in their possession, which has caused great regret, they should exercise the utmost effort in preserving the divine verses and heavenly words. They should designate a specific place for safeguarding the trust of God, exalted be His glory, that perchance they may not fall into the hands of the heedless and remain preserved.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Furthermore, a matter whose declaration is among the most momentous and important of affairs is that this servant [Mirza Aqa Jan] heard a word that some of the friends in outlying regions have imagined that the letters sent in the name of this servant to them and other friends were - God forbid - jointly authored, meaning that what was written from the tongue of Truth, exalted be His glory, was from Truth, while the letter's address from the Point of "In the Name of our Lord" and the opening passages and prayers, up to a certain point, were directed to the Supreme Horizon and Most Exalted Summit, attaining the honor of being heard before the countenance of the Lord of Names, and in response to these exalted words there was revealed from the Source of verses - exalted be His glory and universal be His favors - that these passages were from this servant. I seek God's forgiveness from this great polytheism! How could one who is mute speak before the Kingdom of Utterance? Glory be to my Lord that I should be among the polytheists! Likewise, after the word "end", the passages that were recorded were all from the True One, exalted be His glory. I briefly submit that not a single word was from this servant - all were revealed from the Kingdom of God, my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of all who are in the heavens and earths. At all times, letters that were in this servant's name were, after permission, read in the Most Holy and Most Exalted Presence, and He would command "Take up the pen," and all responses from beginning to end would be revealed from the blessed mouth and recorded. And this was not specific to this servant; rather, repeatedly there was revealed from the Tongue of Grandeur, addressing those circling round and in the regions, that which was a clear book for all the worlds. Now we must all have mercy upon ourselves and the Cause of God, lest any word be uttered that might again lay the foundation of a new polytheism in the earth. May God protect us and you, O community of monotheists, from such thoughts and imaginings. I am naught but a recording servant before Him, and the Speaker is God, my Lord, the Utterer, the Revealer, the All-Knowing, the Ancient of Days.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: They were at a certain place with Aqa Mirza Javad-i-Khurasani and Mirza Aqa Jan. Aqa Mirza Javad, though hot-tempered, was a steadfast and devoted believer. At the direction of the Master, he transcribed a complete set of the writings of the Bab, mostly from the handwriting of Aqa Siyyid Husayn, and all were corrected and collated. The Master had obtained these with great difficulty and ultimately brought these writings to 'Akka, but it remains unknown what Mirza Muhammad-'Ali did with them. The loss of such Tablets causes harm to the Cause. After the Ascension, a committee was formed under the leadership of Mirza Muhammad-'Ali to collect and authenticate the Sacred Tablets, but most of their writings were altered. These people established a very poor foundation and defiled this pure and holy Cause. The harm from this does not affect me personally, but rather affects the Cause itself. Just as Azal stole the writings and seal of the Bab from the Blessed Beauty, these people did the same. They tampered with the writings of the Blessed Beauty and are determined to have me killed. Who would pay attention to him or follow him after such actions?

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Now for two months the commentary on the Surih of Joseph hath been among the people, yet none hath properly copied even a single manuscript. Fie upon them! Again fie upon them! Some portions that were sent from Shiraz arrived in one day, mostly with errors and in some places altered. Inform Mulla Sadiq that since some verses have been altered without true knowledge, they hold no authority with me, though for the people even one correct verse sufficeth. The manuscripts of verses in my possession are authoritative.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding the laws of marriage and divorce which you had requested - that which was revealed in the Kitab-i-Aqdas was sent previously. Likewise, in these days a marriage sermon has been revealed from the heaven of unity... You should write and send a copy of what was previously sent, together with the sermon and the two verses, and write to the aforementioned Haji that he should guard them carefully so they do not spread among the adversaries, for the protection of those who are there. Its dissemination in that city is not permitted.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: As for the scribes and the differences between the manuscripts they prepared, this is what has shown forth from the horizon of elucidation in answer (to your question): O Zayn!  The verses of God were revealed in such manner that no one was able verify them at the time of their revelation and those that were revealed in Iraq and Adrianople were never reviewed.  The servant attending the throne [Khadimullah] is often able to look them over, according to his capacity.  Nevertheless, he has been absentminded in some places, and what the scribes copy is frequently contradictory.  The people's condition is such that they do not know if those things that contradict (their grammatical rules) were revealed by the holy court or were a result of the inattention of the scribes. It is known that what is revealed by the Truth is the truth, of which there is no doubt.  However, since Jinab-i Nazir, upon him be the glory of God, wanted to publish some of (our) books, we commanded the Greater Branch [Muhammad `Ali] and the servant in attendance [Khadimullah] to compare them and to report those things that contradicted (the grammatical rules of) the people since most humans have not and do not understand and are unaware of the process of revelation.  On account of this review, souls did not perish, although "oppressors only increase in loss."

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: A letter has arrived from Abdul-Jalil Effendi concerning the treatise He Who Hath Attained the Most Exalted Companion in the Seat of Truth with an All-Powerful Sovereign by Abu'l-Fadl--may the spirit of those near to God be a sacrifice for him--namely The Brilliant Proofs. The intention is that this treatise should be newly published, but it does not match the original copy. You must exercise great care in this matter and obtain the original copy so that not a single word differs, that his blessed spirit may find joy and delight in the Abha Kingdom. You must verify in the Spiritual Assembly that this matches the original copy and then publish it.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: All of those Tablets were revealed by the lips of the Blessed Beauty. During the final blessed days [of Baha'u'llah], one of the friends asked [the same question] of Mirza Aqa Jan, but did not receive an affirmative response. For this reason, a number of the friends rose against him. Then the mother of Mirza Muhammad-'Ali came and said, Mirza Aqa Jan has become presumptuous before His Blessed Person and has said, 'I have labored more for You than His Holiness the Exalted One [the Bab], and You do not appreciate my labors.' At last, he wrote in his own hand to Iran, 'Whatever I have written in Tablets are utterances of the Blessed Beauty.'

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: And verily has been detailed in that Book all that has issued from my hands from the year 1260 to [...] In the year 1262, after half its months had passed, there were four consummate books and ten perfect scrolls, each one of which would suffice as proof of servitude for all who dwell in the heavens and the earth.... All these comprise fourteen blessed copies existing in that Book, along with the Scroll of Mashhudiyyih at its end in fourteen books from the friends of the servants. All this is written in this Book. As for what left my hands and was stolen on the pilgrimage path, its details are mentioned in the Scroll of Ridawiyyih. Whoever finds any of these is obliged to preserve it.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: These were the matters about which His Holiness inquired, and they have been answered point by point. As for this servant's submission, it was previously submitted that this servant would point out certain copying errors, including in the epistle of the maternal uncle. In these days it happened that I was blessed to read it until I reached a passage where the scribe had written khasif for sakhif, though khasif also has meaning, but sakhif was what was revealed. Likewise in the passage that states His glory be exalted until where it mentions that Sun of the heaven of meaning being brought before the assembly of Pilate and Caiaphas, who were the greatest scholars of that age - but in that copy the word Caiaphas was omitted, making it appear as though Pilate was among the greatest scholars of that age, whereas Pilate was governor on behalf of Caesar and Caiaphas was among the scholars and chief judge that year, as has been revealed in detail from the heaven of divine will in other passages.

Subject: authentication; disposition of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: At the time of emergence from between Gog and Magog, who were two polytheists, I sent a box containing blessed writings of the Exalted One and Aqa Siyyid Husayn, along with His seal, to that one who turned away from God [Yahya]. And in the early years of the new Cause, for four years We commanded him to copy from the writings of His Holiness, such that now writings of that apostate in the style of His Holiness exist. In these days he hath begun using those same writings and writing whatever Satan inspires in him, sealing it with His Holiness's seal and showing it to vile souls like himself. The deceit hath reached such a degree that it cannot be described.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Once when I lived in Baghdad I was invited to the home of a poor thorn-picker. In Baghdad the heat is even more intense that in Syria and it was a very hot day. But I walked twelve miles to the thorn-picker's hut. Then his wife made a little cake out of some meal for me, and burnt it in cooking it. Still that was the best reception I ever attended.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: We have an artist in New York. Her name is Miss Juliet Thompson. At first she said if I give one or two sittings she will paint my picture. I consented, but the one or two sittings became many. I wonder whether after all she got all the sittings she wanted" (here the Master laughed).  Then the daughter of the Consul asked whether she would be permitted to paint the Master.  "All right" the resigned answer came with a twinkling smile in his eyes. "How many hours do you require?"  "About three hours."  "This is too much; fifteen minutes will do?"  "Oh no! it is not enough."  "Will half an hour do?"  At last it was arranged for Monday that the Frauline may paint the Master.  "I hope you will not walk in Miss Thompson's footsteps." (He told her laughingly)

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Letters pour in from all directions like rain. Not even one in a hundred receives a reply, and that too brief. There is absolutely no time for detailed responses.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I remember when I was a child in Nur, the late Mirza Khudavirdi would weep bitterly saying "I served this family for fifty years - was it right that at Mirza Yahya's instigation, Gul-Baba should beat me publicly, insult me and drive me away?" In any case, due to that person's evil deeds, Nur became darkness and Miyan-Rud was extinguished. In Darkila one day in the presence of the Blessed Beauty, He spoke in such a way and spread such proofs and arguments that when He arose, four mujtahids, two of whom - Mulla 'Abbas and Mulla Abu'l-Qasim - were sons-in-law of Mirza Muhammad-Taqi the mujtahid, ran to arrange His shoes. That is how it was then, and this is how it became afterwards. In any case, praise be to God that you have been guided. When I was there your father was called 'Amu 'Ali and I loved him very much, and likewise the late Mirza Khudavirdi.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I am writing the answer to your letter in the Atlantic Ocean...I am writing this letter to you now in this great ocean in a state of weakness and feebleness and seasickness

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I spent the first years of my childhood in Mazandran. At the time the Blessed Perfection was in Teheran. After a while he sent for us to go to him. I started with one of my uncles. On the way, one day, we reached at a village and thought to alight from our animals and refresh ourselves for a few hours. Having entered the hamlet we heard a great deal of noises, cries and confusion. We approached and inquired about all these lamentations. The village chief came forward and said: Your honors! We are all very poor farmers and for the last few years we have been oppressed and heavily taxed. Last night ten tax-gatherers entered our village with the hope of exacting from us a heavy fine. We told them we have nothing. They started to abuse and beat us. They forced themselves into our homes and threatened us on the penalty of death that we should prepare for them a royal dinner. We did not murmur. We cooked for every two persons a plate of rice and a roast chicken with its "four legs" shooting upward. When we placed the trays before them and they looked at the plates they arose in their wrath and flagged us mercilessly with their whips. We started to cry: 'Why do you beat us? What have we done?' They answered: 'How did you dare to bring for us these dishes of rice with only "four legs"? Every dish must have "eight legs", otherwise we will burn your homes and drive away your cattle.' We pleaded and supplicated for their mercy but they hardened their hearts against us and would listen to no excuses till we have roasted for them more chickens. Now this morning we have heard that the Shah is dead and knowing well the disturbed condition of the country, we have arrested these men, placed halters around their necks, have led them into the stable, tied them before the manger filled with fodder and have been beating them with their own whips to eat the straw and barley. I asked them to take me to the stable to see these miserable fellows. It was a very ludicrous and laughable sight! They started to cry to us to rescue them from their plight.
