I mediated before the chief but he wanted them to swear on the Koran that they would leave the vicinity of his village immediately which they were most glad to do, considering their experience. Whenever I think of their horror-stricken faces standing before that manger, surrounded by all the villagers who whipped them to eat straw, I cannot help laughing heartily.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Because I longed to see you, I have shortened my visit to the country, and here am I. At Pleasanton the air is very good, very pleasant, elevated and beautiful surroundings. The views are delightful.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: This morning all the trunks were sent to Abou-Senan. The Master was out in the street till the camels started on their way. In the evening he had many guests from the officers set of Acca. Part of the day he was out calling...

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Before the Most Great Calamity, the only son of Abdu'l-Baha ascended to the Abha Kingdom. This servant did not become affected, saddened, or disturbed in any way, even though all the relatives were delighted by his sweetness and charm.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: in three and a half years I went through deserts, mountains, valleys, cities and countries, raising my voice and crying out... I went to those regions and saw that I was moving alone among their temples, gatherings, assemblies and churches

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I have done all that could be done. I have served the Cause of Baha'u'llah to the utmost of My ability. I have labored night and day all the years of My life. To the extent of my powers I have served the Cause of God. Night and day I found no rest.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Although My birthplace is Tehran and for successive years I was a wanderer in Iraq and for a time exiled to the lands of Rumelia and for forty years imprisoned in 'Akka, despite this My homeland is Mazandaran, that is, Mianrud in the district of Nur.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: From morning until now, despite this grief and anguish and sorrow, I have been occupied on one hand with writing, on another with arranging affairs and visiting the Holy Threshold, on another receiving American pilgrims, and on yet another responding to letters from the friends.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: These days, I do not feel very well. I am now growing old. O, very old! All through my life I have carried on my back, gladly, the burdens of the believers; but now I ever anticipate hearing the good news of service actually accomplished by them. Save this, I have no other joy in the world.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: There are certain urgent expenses at hand, including the living expenses of your companion and others, and various other endless expenditures, and I am perplexed as to what should be done. However, this amount is a debt upon me. God willing, it will be repaid in summer when it is building season

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: By chance, on this day my birth took place as well, but all must celebrate the day as the Anniversary of the Declaration of the Bab, and although my birth also happened to come on this day, they must not consider this of any import. Let the meaning of this day be the Declaration of the Bab, and not my birth.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: When we were travelling from Bagdad toward Constantinople, one day, we thought [to] go ahead of the family, pitch the tent and prepare everything till Baha'u'llah and the rest of the party arrive. There were twenty three of us, all on horses... Experience teaches us many lessons that we are not apt to forget.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: This evening I shall relate to you the story of the sojourn of Baha'o'llah during the two years of his solitude on the mountain of Sarkalu...Here ends the account of the sojourn of Baha'o'llah in the cave of Sarkalu. This I have told in order that you may be informed. It has never before been given in such detail.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: For the sake of the Blessed Beauty, I had it repaired. But after leaving the barracks, the simple matter of bathing became increasingly difficult for the Blessed Beauty until I borrowed a sum of money and repaired the bath in the House of 'Abbud. By some means, I was able to repay the money I had borrowed within four months.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: By God the Truth, through it my face becomes radiant, my breast is dilated, and my spirit is refreshed. For pure and sincere servitude to it, free from all interpretation and allusion, is the crown of my head, the diadem of my brow, the light of my countenance, the joy of my heart, the tranquility of my soul, and the assurance of my mind.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: "I went to Baha'u'llah and asked permission to build one. The more I begged the stronger was his refusal. I said only with fifty pounds a little, comfortable bath can be build but he did not give his consent. Finally a month passed and I was quite worried. At last I went to an Arab friend of mine and borrowed from him Â£2[0] at 2 per cent."

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I have no time to speak or sleep or write, and I pen these few words as though they were but a light refreshment, for I am occupied with work and heavily burdened. The night is an arena of divine address, the day immersed in replies. The morning brings tumult, the evening brings clamor, noon brings uproar, midnight brings murmuring, and dawn brings commotion.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Praise be to God, through the assistance and grace of the Divine Unity, I am spending my time in perfect health on Mount Carmel in the home of Aqa 'Abbas-Quli. Since communications were cut off, solely to inquire after the friends and get news of their wellbeing, Haji Rama?an is being sent here, as apart from him no one is able to travel this road in these days.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: When I returned home from a medical visit on the Carmel towards noon on 6 August 1910...The Master had me tell Him about the finger of the little girl, and whether the danger of blood poisoning was now gone...When I was leaving I saw the Master standing in the garden, where He was apparently engrossed in profound thought, looking at a fig-tree laden with fruit.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: When I was a very little child in Teheran it became necessary and urgent that I should carry a message of great importance to the General of the army garrisoned about 30 miles away from the Capital. I was so small that it precluded of course my riding alone. Therefore Abdul Vahhab Bay, our servant placed me before himself on the saddle of the horse and started out.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: For some time, due to the hardships of travel in the West and enduring trying conditions, the body was in danger, but now praise be to God, through the grace and favor of the Blessed Beauty, may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones, comfort and healing were immediately obtained. One night in Haifa I turned toward the Abha Kingdom and laid my head on the pillow.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Have you ever heard of an invalid, whose health is in extreme upheaval, writing a letter to someone in the middle of the ocean during sleep? Yet 'Abdu'l-Baha does this while all the people on the ship are resting comfortably in their beds and sleeping peacefully, while this sick one, captivated by love for the friends, has been occupied with writing from sunrise until now

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: The beauty of the scenery, the pleasantness of the place, the purity of the water, the charm of the horizon, the softness of the breeze, and the lushness of the mountain have combined to produce an extraordinary sight better than which cannot be imagined. However, 'Abdu'l-Baha is so busied with work and writing that He has no time to look [at the scenery]. But the climate is agreeable.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I have heard the Most Great Branch, who in those days was a child of only eight years of age, recount one of His experiences as He ventured to leave the house in which He was then residing. "We had sought shelter, He told us, "in the house of My uncle, Mirza Isma'il...From that day onward, I was never again molested by any of the boys of the streets, nor did I hear any offensive word fall from their lips."

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: See how much work I have to do! It is more than a week since I received this letter from my sister, the Greatest Holy Leaf [Bahiyyih Khanum], and other members of the household, but I have not had the opportunity to open it yet. I was looking for another letter when I came upon this unopened letter. Then I heard that you were waiting here and I came downstairs to see you because I have no time to see you individually.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: During the lifetime of Baha'u'llah my whole object revolved around the idea of how to become more spiritual, more attracted, more enkindled, how to live in accord with the good-pleasure of the Blessed Perfection, how to become assisted in a worthy service, how to attain to an abstracted state of supplication and prayerfulness. I often was in a meeting but I was so self-occupied that I did not hear their conversations.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Consider that 'Abdu'l-Baha, despite physical weakness and frailty of body, must attend to the settlement of all affairs, both great and small. Surely ten people could not manage it. Moreover, from the East and West of the world, like spring rain, letters pour down. These letters must be read and answers written, which is impossible. Furthermore, some letters are filled with questions. Consider then what a tumult is raised.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Since I had not seen the friends all day, I decided to come to the pilgrim house and visit you. The weather was stormy, and I had the lingering trace of an illness and, therefore, thought best not to leave the house so that my condition would not worsen...It was in accordance with this ordinance [of Baha'u'llah] that I sent Aqa Siyyid Asadu'llah to Istanbul to remedy (the bite of the rabid dog) so that it would serve as an example for the friends.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I swear by the life of the friends that I have no time to speak or sleep or write, for I am occupied with work and heavily burdened. You know this, and from these brief words you can read much. Health is attained but rest is lost. The night is an arena of divine address, the day immersed in replies. The morning brings tumult, the evening brings clamor, noon brings uproar, midnight brings murmuring, and dawn brings commotion. Consider then what news there is!

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: When I visited the dungeon in Teheran, as a child, in order to see BAHA'O'LLAH-when the door was opened there were some steps leading down into the place. They took me as far as midway. I peered through the darkness; I could not find anyone; it was exceedingly gloomy. Then I heard the blessed voice saying, "Take him away." When I heard his voice I tried to see the Blessesd Beauty, but because of the great darkness I could not. Then I was taken out; they seated me.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Baha'u'llah at first refused to discuss the case but they implored so strongly that finally he delegated me to go and settle their case in one day. I went and after reconciling the various factions divided the property etc into two parts. When noon arrived I went out and returned after an hour or two. I observed that the inheritors have divided the two parts into three parts. I inquired the reason. They said that this third part is for you â€" your fee in other words.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: During the first year of our arrival in Bagdad one day Mirza Javad asked me to go out with him to an outlying district...We did not have anything on ourselves but the other man had some money and was grateful to us because we saved him. Addressing Mirza Javad he said:- "I am glad you did not kill them. The way you took your rifle in your hands I thought every moment you will shoot at them." [Here the Master had a hearty laugh and added:] "And all this time our rifle was empty."

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: The Master has borne all the hardships for our comfort and ease. He has become an impregnable fortress and a mighty shield before the world and its peoples, bringing us comfort. For us, they first obtained the Mansion of Mazra'ih where we stayed, and then the Mansion of Bahji. He has arisen to serve the Cause in such wise that they do not even have the opportunity to visit Bahji weekly, while we are occupied with [illegible] and the revelation of manifest verses, and they are beset with trouble, hardship and distress, for association with these people is more troublesome than any other hardship.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: This servant's wish and purpose was such that I should have no trace or sign in this ephemeral world - that I should be completely effaced and non-existent and evanescent and without trace. But destiny was such that in early youth by a definitive command from the pure lips I should take a photograph. However it had been forgotten. I know not what happened that it fell into the hands of the friends until it spread throughout all the world and was printed in various forms, even appearing in many newspapers printed and published and famous, and through love of that Kind Beloved I became notorious throughout the horizons.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Therefore the governor and his office and the representative of the Governor of Beirut, Abdul Rahman Hut, who had thought that I would offer them a bribe due to their threats, when they heard my response that the most beloved thing to me was crucifixion, they became cold like cold water poured on fire. After that, when the investigating committee came to 'Akka and requested to meet me, I declined, and even though Hikmat Bey came and pleaded, and even deceitfully wept saying, Even if for a brief time, honor us with your presence, I said, These people have come solely for investigation, and it is best that I do not meet with them at all.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Prolonged [sojourning in foreign lands] and traversing mountains, deserts, valleys and seas for three and a half years has caused weakness and exhaustion in nerves and sinews, for the body has borne more than its capacity. It is as if a person capable of carrying ten thousand mithqals were made to carry a million; however much he may endeavor to lift that heavy load through spiritual strength, the body cannot [endure it] and becomes subject to weakness and exhaustion. This is why Christ - may my spirit be a sacrifice unto Him - says the flesh is sorrowful but the spirit is rejoicing. Now, although 'Abdu'l-Baha's body and faculties are weak, yet through the confirmations of the Abha Kingdom the spirit is in the utmost strength.

Subject: autobiographical account; narrative of Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: One day in the course of His [Baha'u'llah's] talk He eulogized so much the lives and services of the teachers of the Cause and expressed such high appreciation of their unselfish lives, that although I was a prisoner, I said to myself: "Oh! that I might be confirmed in this!" Then I thought I might go to Kashgar, - one of the provinces of China and a place not visited up to that time by any Baha'i teacher. I was going to travel alone, singly and no baggage, only a hand-bag containing a number of Tablets and books and paper and pen. I secured even my passport, the old deceased Mofti stood as my guarantee. When the crafty Motosarraf, Ibrahim Pasha, heard about this, he sent his Secretary to me with the message: 'I have heard your Excellency contemplates taking a long journey. I will not be so disrespectful or discourteous as to thwart your plan or in any way hinder your departure but as I am the Governor of this province, I am responsible to the Central Government for everything that happens here. Therefore it will only be my official duty to send a cable concerning your departure as soon as you set your feet on the steamer.' I was familiar with the fortuitous way of Oriental expressions, so I saw that this was a polite way of saying: "We will not let you go!' hence I deferred it to a more opportune time.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: As soon as they see a trace of violation of The Covenant they must hold aloof from the violators.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: These people are Babis and must be shunned.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: Should you find anyone who showeth the least sign of aversion, turn away from him and shun his company. This is what We have enjoined upon you in all the Tablets.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: Guard thyself against these and their like. Indeed, were We to find thee capable within thyself, We would bid thee not even to pass through their marketplaces nor any city wherein dwelleth one of them

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: However, it is not appropriate for the followers of Yahya to be present in your gatherings, for they have no purpose save casting doubts. Conduct yourselves in such a way that they themselves will not attend.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: As to the matter of our ill-wishers amongst the Yahya'is [i.e. the Azalis], who accuse the Friends [i.e. the Baha'is] of sympathy with the Court [or Government], it is certain that the truth of the case will become plain and evident.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: And shouldst thou see the Satan from whom thou perceivest the odor of polytheism, shun him and be under mighty protection. He appears in human form and speaks of what was revealed in the Bayan, that he might cause confusion among Our weak servants

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: We called it a secure city so that it might remain protected and safeguarded from the arrows of doubt of the Covenant-breakers... Therefore, we beseech God to preserve and protect the nostrils of holy souls from this foul odor, which is like a deadly poison.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: If you are firm and steadfast in the Covenant, maintain strong and firm relations with the Convention, and withdraw from anyone in whom you detect the odor of violation, so that you may remain protected and preserved under the shield of the Covenant and, like a candle, shine with the light of steadfastness.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: Sanctify yourselves from associating with those who have turned away from the Ancient Beauty and who have arisen to practice deception in God's Cause. Purify yourselves from drawing near unto them. By God! That which issueth from their mouths would consume the hearts of them who are nigh unto God. Beware lest ye hasten unto them.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: Is it rational for us to aid him? If a thief wants to enter a house and rob it, should we help him? Judas sold Christ for a trifling thirty coins and Dr. Farid has sold us for four or five dollars. This foundation has been laid through the sufferings and blood of many sacred souls; therefore, is it equitable of us to allow it to be demolished by the treachery of an ill-wisher?

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty in all His Tablets and treatises forbade the faithful and steadfast friends from associating with the violators of the Bab's Covenant, that no one should approach them, for their influence is like the venom of the cobra which kills instantly. Among other passages, in the Hidden Words He states: "Regard the fellowship of the righteous as a gift, and deem freedom from the company of the wicked as a blessing."

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: This servant was absolutely unwilling to meet with him and wrote to Haji Mahmud that this person's intention was like that of Aqa Khan in the Blessed Days who came to Akka with deceit and insisted on attaining the Blessed Presence, showing the utmost helplessness and lamentation. When some arose to intercede, it was said that this person's intention was to meet Us and then slander Us - and so it happened. And now this person's purpose is the same.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: Should ye find from anyone the slightest trace of aversion, turn away from him and shun him. This is what We have enjoined upon you in all the Tablets, and to this testifieth all things, both seen and unseen, and beyond them the Beauty of transcendent, glorious newness. For they are the manifestations of Satan in this day. By God, the True One! The name of God floweth not from their tongues save to turn the servants of the All-Merciful away from the shore of luminous glory. Beware, O loved ones of God! Draw not nigh unto these people, nor gather with them in any place.

Subject: avoidance of Covenant-Breakers
Quotation: Therefore inhale with a spiritual power, unquestionably you will distinguish between the two smells. For in this irrefutable utterance and blessed writing He has most emphatically commanded all the nakezeens to obey (the center of the Covenant.) All the nakezeens whom you observe know this fact but self-interest having crept in they are following the violation. There are letters preserved with the handwriting of Keirullah in which he clearly writes: 'I testify that thou art the Christ, the son of God;' but I did not accept this from him and wrote back that I am Abdul Baha. Now on account of some interest he is following the Nakezeens, but this interest will not remain, it will disappear. This century will pass and in the next century there will remain not one Nakez.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: On the morning of the blessed Friday We proceeded from the Mansion and entered the Garden...Upon Our being seated, Radiyih, upon her be My glory, attained Our presence on thy behalf, laid the table of God's bounty and in thy name extended hospitality to all present.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Concerning what thou didst mention about the gathering of the loved ones in a special council for the conduct of affairs, this hath been accepted. In truth it is necessary. At the beginning of the entry of the Wronged One into the military barracks in the city of Akka, the establishment of a council was decided upon. However, due to changes of location and variations in movement and rest, it was postponed.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: When we were imprisoned in the Military barrack of Acca there was a small, primitive bath in which the Blessed Perfection took occasional bath. When the time arrived for our departure from the barrack we rented a very small house in the town. It was a two story house, having two rooms on the lower and four rooms on the upper floor but they were very small indeed. On the other hand or party was composed of many people and we wondered how could all these souls be accommodated in this small house. Finally 13 of us agreed to live in one room. they lived and slept and worked in this one small room. We lived in this house well-nigh for 20 years. It so happened that although the house was small yet it contained some sort of bath and so the Blessed Perfection could use it as often as he wished. At the end of 20 years we rented a much larger house but it had no bath. I went to Baha'u'llah and asked permission to build one. The more I begged the stronger was his refusal. I said only with fifty pounds a little, comfortable bath can be build but he did not give his consent. Finally a month passed and I was quite worried. At last I went to an Arab friend of mine and borrowed from him £20 at 2 per cent. This money I took to a merchant who was in former time a grain-dealer but now out of work. I told him We will enter into a partnership, the Capital from me, the labor from you. With this fund you will deal four months in grain. After paying off all the expenses of rent etc; and receiving your monthly salary, we will divide the net profit; one third for you and two third for me. We entered into this agreement and he engaged in business. After four months we cleared our accounts. I payed the debt with its two per cent; the merchant received his one third of the net profit, all the other expenses defrayed and 80 pounds left in the balance for me. With that sum, then I built a bath in the house which is kept intact up to the present day.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: The Blessed Perfection always loved this specie of roses. Large bowls containing the same, decorated the table of his room all the time... Baha'u'llah loved perfumery very much and he always used the attar of the rose.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: One day I went to the Holy Presence of the Blessed Beauty and said: 'The palace at Mazra'ih is ready for you, and a carriage to drive you there.'...I took the carriage the next day and drove with Him to the palace.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: When we reached the gate of Akka, He said: "How quiet it is. No one is to be found."

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: The consuls of that city (Adrianople) gathered in the presence of this Youth at the hour of His departure and expressed their desire to aid Him. They, verily, evinced towards Us manifest affection.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: God desired your departure from the Land of Mystery lest you hear the great terror in the days when the polytheists seized the gates of the House and the Ancient Beauty departed from it due to what the hands of those who disbelieved in God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting, had wrought.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: That which was present at that moment before His face was but a piece of bread and a small amount of cheese...Days passed over Us when nothing was present before Us with which to feed ourselves...Once We wore silk after it was presented before Us, and once We found no garment to change into

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: On the morning of the blessed Friday We proceeded from the Mansion and entered the Garden. Every tree uttered a word, and every leaf sang a melody...Upon Our being seated, Radiyih, upon her be My glory, attained Our presence on thy behalf, laid the table of God's bounty and in thy name extended hospitality to all present.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: In those days, all Tablets were revealed and sent down in the blessed handwriting, or He would be engaged in writing, or during the time individuals attained His presence, the blessed time was spent in speaking. And when He would become very tired, He would take a brief walk before noon or sunset, either mounted or on foot.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: He lived very simply and economically regarding his own welfare. He had no return from his property at that time. His property was confined to half the village of Adasieh. It was in ruins and yielded no revenues. Now it is restored and we get some revenues. Baha'u'llah owned vast properties in Persia which were confiscated; also in Baghdad, but they were taken from Him toward the end of our stay. All were sacked and confiscated by the Turkish Government.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: One day while he was walking in the house in the course of his conversation he said 'It is now nine years that my eyes have not beheld one blade of grass.' He loved the green pastures, verdant plaines blossoming trees and flowering spots; especially the prairie of Acca which was wonderfully green and carpeted with wild flowers during the months of spring. For this reason he often remarked: 'the city is the world of bodies; the country is the world of spirits.'

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: When the time arrived for our departure from the barrack we rented a very small house in the town. It was a two story house, having two rooms on the lower and four rooms on the upper floor but they were very small indeed. On the other hand our party was composed of many people and we wondered how could all these souls be accommodated in this small house. Finally 13 of us agreed to live in one room. They lived and slept and worked in this one small room. We lived in this house well-nigh for 20 years.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: One day I went to His Holy Presence and said: 'The palace is ready and also the carriage to drive you there.' At that time there was no carriage in 'Akka or Haifa. He replied: 'I will not go. I am a prisoner.' Later on I requested again. Again He refused. I went so far as to beg Him a third time. He said: 'No.'...The following day he rode in the carriage. I was also in His Holy Presence. We left the city. No one objected. We went to that green spot. From that time on He was either there, in 'Akka in Haifa, or at Bahji.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Association of ideas is a deep psychological phenomenon. Nowhere does my heart truly rest save in this room where the Blessed Beauty spent His days and nights for many years. When I sit there alone how vividly the living picture is brought before my mind! In the evenings, after I go to bed I lay awake for hours, thinking rapidly over the miraculous events of this Cause, how we were at first brought to Acca and imprisoned in the Barrack, how the breast of Baha'u'llah became the target for the arrows of oppression, how He suffered all these ignominies for our sake, how His Celestial Faith shone bright and luminous through untold miseries and trials and how He conquered the hearts of men!

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: At the beginning of arrival in the Most Great Prison in the military barracks, His blessed word, exalted be He: "The River Jordan has joined with the Most Great Sea" etc. Although for this blessed verse which was sent down from the heaven of divine will there are many meanings, yet one manifestation from the sun of its meanings dawned after the acquisition of this land, for this new land was adorned with the ornament of God's Name and is near to the River Jordan - and this is the river that was recorded and mentioned in the divine Books of old, and perhaps it will join [with the Sea] in the future as well.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Then they sent Him to the prison of Akka but to no avail, rather in the prison of Akka He raised the banner of His teachings in all regions.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Thou wert with the Truth and didst migrate with Him until thou didst enter this Prison - this station concerning which the sects have differed.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: the fortress which Thou hast made a prison for the Manifestation of Thyself... Thy most sweet call which hath been raised from the direction of Thy prison

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Then they turned with blackened faces toward radiant faces and drove us from the Land of Mystery and brought us to Akka, which is the most ruined of all cities.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: They sent the Blessed Beauty from Constantinople. His cause became elevated and when they sent him to the prison for murderers and highway robbers in Akka, in that prison he raised his banner.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: After arriving at the garden and renowned palace, which afforded some relief, news arrived from the prison-land that on several occasions the very prison itself had been dearer and more precious than what came after

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: "In the days of the Blessed Perfection this [the garden of Ridvan in 'Akka] was a place of recreation. He used to sit there (pointing) and the friends used to sit around on those seats. Words and prayers used to be revealed and they were all in the utmost of humility and submissiveness. One day I came here with the Motesareff (Governor). His holiness Baha'u'llah was here and the friends were here. He did not receive the Motesareff. He did not meet him. He did not meet me, either. He said, 'Return with the Motasereff,' and I returned."

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Therefore he requested the local government to cast this person into a place of abasement and humiliation, to send Him to a prison of murderers, thieves and brigands, to consort with criminals, that He might fall into loss and ruin. Thus it was that He was confined to the prison of Akka, so that in a short time He and His household would be destroyed and vanish without trace.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: and to an even greater and better extent in Akka. For in Baghdad we were not outwardly imprisoned and confined, and the Cause of God had not yet attained even one-hundredth of its present fame, nor did it face even one-hundredth of its present opponents, adversaries and enemies. In the Most Great Prison we have met with no one and have completely closed the doors of association.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: This is a city that was once the most desolate of lands. God hath adorned it with this Name through which the Ancient Beauty was established upon the Most Great Throne and the mention of God was exalted between the heavens and the earth. God hath made this city the mother of cities in these regions by virtue of the dawning of the Sun of Manifestation from its horizon with this perspicuous Name.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: If you desire news of this land: Our Lord, the All-Merciful, hath fulfilled what He promised in the Holy Books and Tablets. He hath emerged from the Most Great Prison despite the opposition of His enemies, and hath established the seat of His throne first in the Ridvan Garden, then in a palace whose very atoms proclaim: Sovereignty, power, majesty and authority belong to God, the One, the Chosen One!

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Know thou that the heedless banished us from the City of God with such manifest injustice that the voice of weeping was raised betwixt earth and heaven, and the dwellers of the Realm above cried out in lamentation. Then did the ship continue on its way by the leave of God, the Almighty, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, until we arrived before the city in which hath been imprisoned He through Whose appearance the eyes of God's Messengers were gladdened.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: For nine consecutive years the Blessed Perfection did not put his feet outside of the gate of Acca. He was either imprisoned in the barrack of closely watched and guarded in the house. According to the strict royal firman of Abdul Aziz, he was to be jailed in a cell all alone, not even one of us was to be allowed to see or talk to him, and to leave the town of Acca was a matter strictly forbidden. In brief he was to be a life prisoner with these deadly restrictions.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: The court of the barracks had a most gloomy aspect. There were three or four fig trees on the branches of which several ominous owls screeched all night. Every one got sick, and there were neither provisions nor medicine. At the entrance of the barracks there was a morgue. It was a horrible looking room. No one can imagine a worse place than the barracks of Acca. The surroundings were filthy and dirty, the treatment of the officials was unbearable, and we were looked upon as the enemies of religion and corruptors of morals.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Erelong shall the exponents of wealth and power banish Us from the land of Adrianople to the city of 'Akka. According to what they say, it is the most desolate of the cities of the world, the most unsightly of them in appearance, the most detestable in climate, and the foulest in water. It is as though it were the metropolis of the owl, within whose precincts naught can be heard save the echo of its cry. Therein have they resolved to imprison this Youth, to shut against our faces the doors of ease and comfort, and to deprive us of every worldly benefit throughout the remainder of our days.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Upon Our arrival We were welcomed with banners of light, whereupon the Voice of the Spirit cried out saying: 'Soon will all that dwell on earth be enlisted under these banners.'

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Near the army barracks in 'Akka there existed a public bath which was in a state of ruin. For the sake of the Blessed Beauty, I had it repaired. But after leaving the barracks, the simple matter of bathing became increasingly difficult for the Blessed Beauty until I borrowed a sum of money and repaired the bath in the House of 'Abbud.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: Having repaired and furnished all the rooms I ordered the carpenters to make for me a carriage with cover which was done in due time. A good mansion is made ready for you outside of Acca. It is wonderfully situated and is very charming. From one side the lovely mountains and undulating valleys are seen; from another side there are large orange and mandarine orchards, the oranges like unto the red-lanterns shine and glove through the green boughs; from another side verdant gardens and prairies full of narcissus and tulips are seen; the Mediterranean glistens in the distance; a stream of cool water flows in the Center. Then there was another palace belonging to Abboud and his family. This was the palace of Bahajee. Finally I rented if from him at $150.00 a year and Baha'u'llah and the members of the Holy Family moved into it.

Subject: banishment to; life in 'Akka
Quotation: At last the authorities imprisoned Baha'u'llah in the Fortress of Akka, in Syria. Even in prison, while under surveillance, he was able to promulgate his teachings and to write his messages to the world. He remained in the prison-city of Akka until His ascension in 1892, yet His teachings had by then reached far beyond the confines of His prison walls, touching hearts and transforming lives throughout the East and beginning to influence the West.

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: The consuls of that city (Adrianople) gathered in the presence of this Youth at the hour of His departure and expressed their desire to aid Him. They, verily, evinced towards Us manifest affection.

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: The departure of the Most Beauteous One from among the people occurred at noon on Friday, the twenty-second day of the month of Shawwal. For some time there had been talk of departure, and the will of the Pre-existent Sovereign had been fixed and firm upon the command to depart, but owing to the distress of these few servants it had been postponed until that mentioned day. But such lamentation and outcry arose from the beloved ones that a second resurrection was raised up--indeed, it was far greater than the resurrection in Iraq at the time of departure, and the cries of the servants were more intense.

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: The beauty of God departed from the mosque. It so happened that the store of the aforementioned Hasan Aqa was on Baha'u'llah's route. When he arrived at the store, the tongue of God said, "Based on the decision that the gentleman had announced in his proclamation, the countenance of the All-Merciful presented himself, whereas the idolaters repudiated their own agreement."

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: When we were living in Adrianople there was a Bahktashi who lived close by to us. Professionally he was a wood-chopper, socially he was a wit. Once he got severely sick and was on the eve of departure from this world. Becoming acquainted with this fact I called on him. He was lying on a low, uncomfortable cot and his old wife sitting beside it with the marks of solicitude and care on her wrinkled face. Suddenly she started to speak addressing her husband: 'Thou art going to get well real soon. This sickness shall pass away soon and thou wilt be strong. Oh! my beloved! I am praying to Allah for thy speedy recovery. May Allah hear my prayers!' The sick man as though pulling himself out of a heavy drowsiness half opened his eyes and said: 'What can I do even if I get well! I am tired of this world and I want to leave it my dear! Oh! I am so weary, so weary' and he closed his eyes. The wife with much agitation in her mien declared:- Oh no, no! May Allah never bring that black day! My darling! Thou wilt gain back thy health! Together we will go into the garden and thee eat all kinds of fruits. Hand in hand we will walk through the woods and listen to the songs of the birds! Yes, yes, I will nurse thee with the apple of my eyes.' The sick man without opening his eyes, and seemingly with much struggle answered her back. 'Oh my wife! Be silent! Nothing shall happen if I get well. Only this: I have to chop ten or twenty or thirty more loads of wood. That's all. Have I not cut enough wood? Oh! Let me die!' In this world we are all more or less wood-choppers. If we are attacked with a sickness and survive it we have to work a little more, to chop a few more loads of wood and the world will go on perennially.

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: There are two types of pictures of the Blessed Beauty, each one depicting a different pose, and both were taken in Adrianople.  They are distinct and clear and absolutely unmistakable.  You should announce this to all the friends and let them see it and become acquainted with it, because people who seek material gains might be tempted to give currency to some unknown picture as that of the Blessed Beauty, and this would of course perturb the minds of the friends

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: In our days in Baghdad, we would go to the coffeehouse and sit there, meeting with outsiders and insiders, strangers and friends, those far and near. We would bring the distant near, make the stranger a friend, bring the outsider in, serve the Cause of God, aid the Word of God, and exalt the Name of God. Those same services, troubles, hardships, trials and tribulations of those days were endured to a far greater degree by the Most Great Branch in Adrianople, and to an even greater and better extent in Akka. For in Baghdad we were not outwardly imprisoned and confined, and the Cause of God had not yet attained even one-hundredth of its present fame, nor did it face even one-hundredth of its present opponents, adversaries and enemies. In the Land of Mystery too, we would meet with some and grant audience to others. But in the Most Great Prison we have met with no one and have completely closed the doors of association. The Master has borne all the hardships for our comfort and ease. He has become an impregnable fortress and a mighty shield before the world and its peoples, bringing us comfort. For us, they first obtained the Mansion of Mazra'ih where we stayed, and then the Mansion of Bahji. He has arisen to serve the Cause in such wise that they do not even have the opportunity to visit Bahji weekly, while we are occupied with [illegible] and the revelation of manifest verses, and they are beset with trouble, hardship and distress, for association with these people is more troublesome than any other hardship.

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: Six years ago we were invited at the Ottoman suggestion and we have accepted.  Later, without having committed any fault and at the request of Persia we were sent from Baghdad to Constantinople.  After a stay of 4 months, we were exiled to Adrianople. Now, once again, we are being exiled from Adrianople without the knowledge of where we are destined and without any reason, all our possessions were disposed of.  If the Turkish government does not welcome us any more, and as we are not of this country let us be free to go into a country of another power.  It is to the sovereigns of Europe who like to help the oppressed that we plead, supplicating them to release us from this bondage.

Subject: banishment to; life in Adrianople
Quotation: When we were exiled again from Bagdad in our company there was a Baha'i by the name Mirza Ahmad Kashani. He accompanied Baha'u'llah to Constantinople and later on to Adrianople. One night we were invited to a feast. The guests were divided into twos and when the supper time came each company was served with a dish of rice and one chicken. It so happened that I was made the partner of Mirza Ahmad. As we sat around the table to each, my partner humorously remarked to get a wing from that friend, a piece of breast from a second, a leg from a third and so on. I did so, thinking that he will divide our chicken amongst the believers; instead of doing this, he ate both and everybody was most amused. He ate also my share. He was your namesake (the Master turned to me laughing.). I had given him the title of "geometrician," because he like to get the first of every thing and in order to gain his aim, he would devise many humorous plans, calculated to make anybody laugh. When he entered a meeting he would look all around and then sit a place where "huble-bubble" would be served first. When the tea was prepared by one of the believers he would go to him in a hurried fashion. "I have a most important affair to attend to. I must go out now. I cannot wait any longer. Please give me one glass of tea." All these innocent plans, he would resort to, in order to drink a cup of tea before anybody else; because he believed all the aroma of the tea is the first cup.... The first winter we spent in Adrianople was severely cold and this Mirza Ahmad Kashani not being accustomed to hard climate suffered very much. In fact all of us endured the most difficult hardship. Having lived all our lives in moderate and warm climate, the rigorous air of Adrianople was unendurable. The weather was so cold that the water was frozen in copper jars and vases and as a result, they were broken in pieces. My fingers were congealed to the bar of iron and when I tried to push them back the skin was torn off. As the home where the women lived was a little far, whenever I wanted to call on them, I would cover all my head and face with the "Aba," leaving only a small hole for one of my eyes to see my way. Notwithstanding this, the cold was so bitter, the wind was so biting that it was as though some one drove a sword or a dagger or an arrow through my eye. Although we had several rooms in the house, we decided that twelve of us stay in one room to get warmer. We did not have any heavy clothing and the one who had a light overcoat was considered most fortunate. In this one room we had a tin-plate oven and we made fire to keep us warm. The oven would get as red as fire. Near it we would put two or three bottles of water to be kept warm for drinking. When we got up after midnight to drink, the fire of the oven had naturally gone out and therefore the water in the bottles was frozen. We had to make fire, thaw the ice and drink a glass of water. That winter one whole flock of sheep with their shepherd were frozen to death in the country. All the inhabitants said, they had never seen such a winter in their lives. In short, through the assistance of Baha'u'llah we lived through it and when the spring came around the country became verdant and the hearts were made glad.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: When the Blessed Beauty was residing in Baghdad, there was a Shi'i Muslim by the name of Shaykh 'Abdu'l-Hamid who had a tremendous love and affection for Baha'u'llah. At the time of His departure from Baghdad, this man ran a distance of ten miles, escorting Baha'u'llah out of the city.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: Vast amounts of jewellery and many precious objects were in our possession, but all of them were lost. Despite all this material wealth, we arrived in Baghdad with nothing.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: In the days we spent in the Abode of Peace, we would sit in the coffee-house and meet with souls both familiar and strange, from within and without.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: He [Abdu'l-Baha] spoke of the Blessed Beauty's visit to Kirmanshah [on His way to Baghdad]. He remarked:  "How bitterly cold was that winter! We arrived at a caravansary located by a moat. The journey was full of sufferings and difficulties, but since it was in the path of God, it was filled with joy and delight, and we were so happy. In Asadabad it was particularly cold. The temperature was 38 degrees below zero. My socks were wet which caused my feet to be frostbitten. That evening we were to eat some halvah. By mistake, however, pepper was added in place of sugar, which severely burned our mouths and throats. That night we did not sleep and constantly drank water. From the blessings of those adversities, those banishments, now the banner of the Divine Faith is hoisted most high!"

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: When we arrived in Bagdad we were in the utmost poverty, because the secular and religious authorities had exiled us from Teheran after confiscating and pillaging all our belongings, yet the straightened circumstances did not affect us at all. When we were travelling, we passed by the village, Asad Abab, in the vicinity of Hamadan. The coldness of the climate of this place is proverbial, and as it was in the heart of the Winter my feet were frost-bitten.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty (may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones) traveled directly from Tehran to Hamadan, from Hamadan to Kermanshah, and from Kermanshah directly to Baghdad.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: In this time, when the bird of eternity has flown from the land of Iraq and the people of longing and yearning burn with the fire of separation, this letter is being sent by this ephemeral ant to the friends of God....  Now that moment has passed, and that day has slipped out of your grasp. That breeze shall not blow again in this land, that rose shall not again flower here, and that door shall never again open.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: At the time of our exile the most noteworthy man, the first man of Persia, was Mirza Aqa Khan, the prime minister...What a pity it is that such a noteworthy family should be annihilated because of the acceptance of such a faith!

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: Give praise unto God for having chosen you specially for Himself, inasmuch as when the Sun of Pre-existence withdrew from its native land, it rose from the horizon of Iraq, your land. This is of His bounty unto you, wherewith nothing in the heavens and earth can compare.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: Perchance, God willing, Iran may become the envy of all other nations of the world. Though this noble purpose - namely the sacred glory of the government and the prosperity of the country - may not be fully achieved at present, yet through the justice of the just sovereign, the endeavor of the accomplished minister, and the sincerity of the subjects, the foundation of this mighty edifice shall be laid.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: Among the matters that outwardly caused great sorrow, making the friends weep blood, yet inwardly brought joy upon joy, was the banishment of the Blessed Beauty from Iran. The enemies were in the utmost joy and gladness while the friends were in complete despair and disappointment. All were convinced that with the Blessed Beauty's departure from Iran, the Cause would be completely forgotten and obliterated, for there remained but a handful of believers-most had been martyred, their pure blood had stained the earth, and if any believers remained they were in complete hiding. From Tehran to Baghdad, we did not meet a single believer on the road; in thirty stages of the journey, not one soul. Yet it was the Blessed Beauty's departure that caused the exaltation of God's Word in Baghdad. And if there were any among the friends, they were extremely hidden. From Tehran to Baghdad we came, and there was not a single believer along the way. Throughout the journey, not a single soul was there. Now it was the departure of the Blessed Beauty that caused the Word of God to be exalted in Baghdad and the fame of God's Cause to be spread abroad. The hearts of the enemies were troubled, the hearts of the friends became hopeful, souls were gladdened, and all the friends were filled with joy and delight. This was because they remained steadfast, as new souls entered beneath the shadow of the Cause, and throughout all regions of Iran new believers appeared. Had this exile not occurred, this joy and glory would not have been attained. Had He not graced Baghdad with His presence, the Cause would have been obliterated. The blessed presence in Baghdad was a second breath that bestowed new life upon the friends.

Subject: banishment to; life in Baghdad
Quotation: When the Blessed Beauty returned from Kurdistan, the friends in Iran were few in number, and Iraq was frozen and lifeless - no sound, no call. And if there was anyone in the surroundings, they were in utmost despair, fear and caution. But upon arrival in Baghdad, the Most Great Name opened the door, issued a universal call, raised the divine summons, and the fame of God's Cause spread far and wide. The leaders and clergy of all religions would attend His presence day and night, with continuous questions and answers, all acknowledging satisfaction with the responses.

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: When the Blessed Perfection was exiled from Bagdad the large number of believers who went with him divided the work of the party among them. For example, Darveesh Sedk Ali and Haji Ebrahim acted as equerries, Ostad Mohammed Ali looked after the baggage, Mirza Mohammed Goli supervised the pitching of the tents and I was, if we may here use a military term, a commissary officer and had to supply the party, including horses, etc., with food and the daily necessities. Often, by day or by night we covered a distance of from twenty-five to thirty miles. No sooner would we reach a caravanserai than from sheer fatigue everyone would lie down and go to sleep: utter exhaustion having overtaken everybody they would be unable even to move.

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: Later, without having committed any fault and at the request of Persia we were sent from Baghdad to Constantinople. After a stay of 4 months, we were exiled to Adrianople.

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: Then they exiled Him to Constantinople so He would be very far from Iran and the power of His word would have no influence but the opposite occurred - the power of His word became more penetrating.

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: Thus they took the Ancient Beauty from the realm of the East to the country of the West. But this migration and absence became the cause of exalting the Word of God and diffusing the divine fragrances

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: After twelve days the blessed procession departed from Iraq toward Istanbul. All people gathered outside the city for farewell. After the Blessed Beauty mounted, several from outside called the adhan Allahu Akbar! Allahu Akbar!

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: Then two monarchs united and exiled him from Baghdad to Constantinople. 'If he goes further from Persia,' they said, he will be uprooted sooner.' But instead of that his cause was elevated. He paid no heed to the Ottoman power.

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: When the Blessed Perfection was exiled from Bagdad, the large number of the believers who followed him, divided the work of the party amongst themselves. From Bagdad to Samson they served with such rare faithfulness and loyalty.

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: The government of Persia said: "As long as Baha'o'llah is in Persia the country will not be at peace. When Baha'o'llah is exiled from Persia the country will then find peace. He shall no longer be connected with this country; all communications with him shall be suspended." So the Shah of Persia endeavored until he succeeded in expelling the Blessed Perfection to Constantinople to Roumelia.

Subject: banishment to; life in Constantinople
Quotation: At this hour when the Nightingale of the Garden of Eternity has taken wing to the nest of faithfulness, and the Beauty of the assembly of lovers has resolved to journey to the realm of Constantinople - that He might fly from the bower of the Abode of Peace, Baghdad, to the nest of the Abode of Islam, Istanbul, and hasten from this land and region to the territory and realm of Rum, there to warble with holy, celestial melodies, that perchance earthly souls might take flight from their mortal abode to dwell beneath the shade of the True Phoenix, and like birds of the Divine Throne soar to the eternal rose garden... And as to what prompted this move and was the cause of this journey - it was that the Persian government has, for three years until now, pursued this servant with sword and spear, never neglecting even an atom's weight in their efforts. Rather, they have engaged in this with all earnestness and striving, especially during the past year or more when they exerted efforts beyond their capacity. In brief, at first they petitioned and strived with the Ottoman government to have them seize Us and all Our companions and hand Us over bound. The Roman (Ottoman) government refused. Then they involved other powers as intermediaries, and foreign powers advocated and mediated on behalf of the Persian government. However, the Roman government categorically refused, saying that the Persian government should not make such requests as they were impossible and unattainable.

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: During the time Baha'o'llah resided in Mesopotamia he displayed marvelous grandeur and power, notwithstanding the enmity and opposition of the Shah and the noblemen of Persia. Learned men of all nations sought him and were humble in his presence. They received from his holy tongue answers to their questions, and not a single soul left his blessed presence unsatisfied. When the ulama saw that Baha'o'llah exercised such influence in Bagdad they caused him to be exiled to Constantinople. However, he was sent, not as other exiles, but with honorable escort, and the officials en route, including the governor general, showed him great respect. He remained four months in Constantinople. When it was discovered that he was gaining converts he was sent to Adrianople, where he spent five years. Then, at the instigation of the Shah of Persia, he was banished to the fortress of Acca.

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty - may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones - was exiled from Iran to Iraq, from Iraq to Constantinople, thence to Rumelia, the Land of Mystery, and from there to the Most Great Prison

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: One day He was hurried barefoot in chains from Shimiran to Tehran, spending four months in prison with fetters and shackles, every moment under threat of sword and arrow. Sometimes He was exiled to Iraq, sometimes He wandered Kurdistan, finding companionship with wild beasts and birds of the wilderness. For a long time and many years in Baghdad He was surrounded by hostile forces and in severest trials and tribulations. Every day brought a new affliction and every night a grievous calamity. He found not a moment's ease or rest. Then He was exiled to the great city and became the target of grave calumnies. The most prominent and distinguished men all sought to humiliate Him and the pillars of nations thought to destroy Him. Then they banished Him to the Land of Mystery where He was immersed in great hardships and painful torment. One who had been nurtured from the beginning in the embrace of His loving-kindness and shown every kind of tender care rose up with utmost hatred and, like a host of calamities, attacked. He intended to shed His pure blood and like a serpent bit that sacred form, then began to wail and lament, raised cries of being wronged, claimed to be oppressed and victimized, let out moans and cries, began to sob and wail. Like Joseph's envious brothers he cast that Joseph of the Egypt of existence into the dark pit of the well, then raised cries and laments, wept and wailed, and "came to their father in the evening, weeping." Then he became intimate with strangers and friendly with enemies, attributed sedition and corruption to the Peerless Beauty and placed forged documents in the hands of the malicious, so that the candle of the Concourse on High would be extinguished and the ways of the Supreme Concourse forgotten, the Sun of Unity would set and the Sun of Truth decline, the verse of guidance be abrogated and the festival of the Day of the Covenant be annulled. As a result, the means for the Most Great Prison were arranged and grievous calamity occurred. The Wronged One of the horizons fell captive to the people of discord and every hour brought new trials and tribulations. All doors were shut and all paths cut off. Arrows of cruelty rained down unceasingly from all countries of the world like rain, and swords of malice from the hosts of humanity struck that defenseless Form.

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: From the wildernesses of Iraq He was banished to the city and again after more years to the land of mystery Adrianople where He was the object of hatred from both sides. Eventually in utter humility bearing unnumbered hardships He was banished to the Most Great Prison.

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: Then they perceived that the Cause spread more and more rapidly. The fame became more widely circulated. The Teachings of the Blessed Perfection became more pronounced. Then the Chief of Persia determined to expel Baha'u'llah from Baghdad. He arrived in Constantinople. Then the Persian ministers succeeded in having Him banished from Constantinople. A fourth time was He banished, from Roumelia to the Most Great Prison.

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: The departure of the Most Beauteous One from among the people occurred at noon on Friday, the twenty-second day of the month of Shawwal. For some time there had been talk of departure, and the will of the Pre-existent Sovereign had been fixed and firm upon the command to depart, but owing to the distress of these few servants it had been postponed until that mentioned day. But such lamentation and outcry arose from the beloved ones that a second resurrection was raised up--indeed, it was far greater than the resurrection in Iraq at the time of departure, and the cries of the servants were more intense.

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: He was put in chains and thrown into a subterranean dungeon. His extensive hereditary possessions were entirely plundered, He was four times exiled from land to land, and in the end He came to abide in the Most Great Prison.... At last they said, "So long as this man is in Persia there will be no peace or tranquillity. He should be banished, that Persia might again find rest." They subjected Baha'u'llah, therefore, to severe hardships so that He would be forced to seek permission to leave Persia, and they imagined that the lamp of the Cause would be thereby extinguished. But this persecution produced the contrary effect: The Cause grew in stature and its flame waxed brighter. It had until then spread only within Persia; this caused it to spread to other regions. Later they said, "Iraq is too close to Persia; we must dispatch Him to distant lands." Thus the Persian government persisted until Baha'u'llah was exiled from Iraq to Constantinople. But again they saw that He did not falter in the least. They said, "Constantinople is a crossroads for divers peoples and nations, and there are many Persians there." Hence they took further steps and had Him exiled to Adrianople. But that flame gathered still more intensity and the Cause grew even greater in stature. Finally the Persians said, "None of these locations was a place of humiliation: He must be sent to a place where He will be disgraced and subjected to trials and persecutions, and where His kindred and followers will suffer the direst afflictions." Thus they chose the prison city of 'Akka, which was reserved for rebels, murderers, thieves, and highway robbers, and in this wise they made Him associate with such people.

Subject: banishments of Baha'u'llah
Quotation:
When they exiled us from Persia, from Teheran, to Baghdad, there are thirty stages -- in these thirty stages we did not find one Bahai. We did not meet one. And now in every one of these stages there are great numbers of Bahai friends.   ABU0236
First He was banished to Baghdad, then to Constantinople, then to Adrianople, and finally to the prison-city of Akka in Palestine. The government then strove against Baha'u'llah; they banished him to Baghdad, and then to Constantinople and then to Roumania.

Subject: begging; mendicancy; idleness and sloth
Quotation: Verily, We love not idleness and neglect, as doth testify unto this the Self-Sufficient, the Most High.

Subject: begging; mendicancy; idleness and sloth
Quotation: God has created man noble, how can he degrade this station of divine nobility by begging? He has made him of the pure essence of spiritual wealth, how does he dare to alloy it by the base metal of mendicancy?

Subject: begging; mendicancy; idleness and sloth
Quotation: Some of the friends who have now made the pretext of assuming the character of dervishes are engaged in praising the Ancient Beauty through hints and allusions in corners and streets and marketplaces, and are accustomed to encouraging people by singing ghazals and spiritual songs. These souls should abandon this practice henceforth, but for now it is causing encouragement among the people and no one should interfere with them. However, if anyone should engage in wandering about, this is highly reprehensible and contrary to the religion of God and incompatible with detachment and causes the humiliation of the Cause of God.

Quotation: "He was questioned as to the reality of a story related by a young Episcopal clergyman, that on one occasion he saw Mirza Abul Fazl surrounded by a halo, as he taught the people at Green Acre, Maine." This is the Supreme Light, the conscious Reality which comprehends mysteries."

Subject: being a source of light; guidance
Quotation:
When you make a friend, or associate with one, try to be the cause of joy and happiness to him. If he should come to you sad, make him joyful. Now your home should be in such a condition, your actions so harmonious, your love so evident, that if, perchance, a cold or unworthy one should enter, you must treat such a one in such a way that he or she will go away aflame with the Love of GOD. If one enters your home as an extinguished candle, you must kindle him and set his heart aglow, so that he will leave a radiant candle. Should they enter sad, they must go away happy; should they come hopeless, they must leave in great hope. In fact, briefly, if they come as dead, they should go away as alive.   ABU0811
In any case, I hope that you will become the cause of illuminating souls so they may acquire divine qualities, and that your good character will influence multitudes of souls.

Quotation: The second question is about Mary's conception by the Holy Spirit. This is proven and accepted, though some European philosophers doubted it and considered a birth without father impossible, arguing that procreation requires the meeting of male and female elements. Yet these same European philosophers consider the Earth to be created, saying it was originally fire that gradually cooled, forming a crust that thickened and stabilized, allowing plants, animals and humans to develop. Subject: bringing forth results; fruit
Quotation: What is spread abroad and apparent and manifest among people are His words and His loved ones. Yet from His loved ones who are known by His name and attributed with His love, none has inhaled the fragrance of sanctity and detachment, as most engage in deeds that are displeasing and commit reprehensible acts. People judge by analogy - what they observe from this group they attribute to the Manifestation of the lights of Oneness. This is why divine wrath has not yet seized the polytheists. I swear by the Ancient Beauty that if the loved ones of Truth had appeared among creation with sanctity, detachment, deeds and character like unto His, to the extent of their capacity, you would today find most people believers and turned toward God. Consider for example a tree - before its fruits appear, if it is described, some people will acknowledge it while others will waver between acceptance and denial until the fruits appear. And after the fruit appears, if it is bitter, they will surely reject the descriptions of that describer and all will arise in denial, both those who wavered and those who accepted. Thus the tree of human existence becomes known and proven by the fruits of deeds, and all observe its acts and deeds. If they find them good and pleasant they will surely accept, and without this they will surely turn away. Now from the divine loved ones who are counted as fruits of the tree of the All-Merciful, people have perceived naught but unpleasant deeds, therefore all remain turned away and veiled. God willing, in this springtime season may the sweet fragrances of the divine holy Ridvan be inhaled from those who seek the sanctuary of the August King, so that through breathing in the fragrances of those sanctified souls, the servants may return to the original Ridvan. In any case, some of the loved ones have caused the robe of holy glory to be soiled with the dust of people's vain imaginings, and the beauty of the Cause has remained hidden behind veils of suspicion.
