Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Deal with the loved ones of God with the utmost kindness and strive to bring them joy to the extent possible.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: teach all the peoples of the world the mores of love, and show everyone kindliness and friendship, sympathy and courtesy

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Be kind to all peoples of the world and wish well for all nations. Serve and show love to the world of humanity and be the cause of human happiness.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Praise be to God that during these years of war, the friends in Baku were at peace with all peoples and, following divine teachings, were kind to all.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Man must associate with all mankind with joy and fragrance. He must not turn away his face from any soul. He must treat with kindness both the friend and the stranger.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: For we are all lovers of the face of the Beloved...and that is the love of the Lord God and fellowship with all the peoples of the world and kindness to all created beings

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Consort with all the people in love and fragrance. Fellowship is the cause of unity, and unity is the source of order in the world. Blessed are they who are kind and serve with love.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: The people of Baha who have drunk the pure wine of reality must associate with all the world with a perfect spirit of joy and fragrance and remind them of that which is for the benefit of all.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: As far as thou art able, show kindness to all people and manifest love. Choose the path of friendship, truthfulness and reconciliation, that thou mayest become the very soul of the friends and thy radiant love may shine forth.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Be kind and deal with bad people not harshly but leave them alone. Do not mix with them. There are many bad people in the world - have nothing to do with them - do not gossip about them. It must be so that your very silence should be blame itself. Do not spoil your tongue with the mention of evil people.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: O dear maid-servant of the Truth! Deal with all people with utmost love and do not fall short in whatever lies within your power. Be a loving mother to children, a faithful daughter to the elderly, a dear sister to your peers, a shelter and support to the helpless, and strive to guide all to the extent possible.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: For one another must ye give up even life itself. To every human being must ye be infinitely kind. Call none a stranger; think none to be your foe. Be ye as if all men were your close kin and honoured friends. Walk ye in such wise that this fleeting world will change into a splendour and this dismal heap of dust become a palace of delights.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: O people of Baha! Associate with the followers of all religions with joy and fragrance. If ye possess a word or gem of which others are deprived, share it with them in a language of utmost kindliness and goodwill. If it be accepted and be effective, the purpose is achieved; if not, leave him to himself and pray for him, but do not molest him.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: [When Abbas Effendi was specifically asked as to the fate of those millions of human beings who would never hear of Beha Ullah - whether they were, for that reason, to be regarded as hopelessly lost - he replied:] "No. The birth of our Lord was for all; those who shall know of Him and those who shall not. The Spirit is the same everywhere. Under whatsoever name men address Him, He will respond to their call."  Asked, further, about the heathen - those devoutly and sincerely kneeling before stone images - he answered: "They too will be heard, and God will protect them."

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Its gates will be flung wide to mankind; prejudice towards none, love for all.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Blessed is the soul who reclines upon his couch while his heart is illumined with love for all the peoples of the world.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Until love appears among men, there can be no full happiness and peace. We must therefore foster brotherhood and universal love.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: In former ages and cycles, the command of love and non-resistance had been revealed. But there was a pretext among the people, - "merit" and "de-merit." They would say this person is contumacious and a hypocrite and that person is blood-thirsty and cruel. And if any one practiced forgiveness that forgiveness was coupled with blame and reproach. But in this dispensation, all these pretexts are dispelled and real love and kindness with all the soul and heart to all the nations of the earth is the absolute law.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: One must show love and compassion to all the peoples of the world with utmost joy, gladness and delight. No distinction or preference should be made. However, in all dealings, trustworthiness, truthfulness, faith, compassion, kindliness and care must be shown equally to all humanity

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: Love is unlimited, boundless, infinite! Material things are limited, circumscribed, finite. You cannot adequately express infinite love by limited means. The great unselfish love for humanity is bounded by none of these imperfect, semi-selfish bonds; this is the one perfect love, possible to all mankind, and can only be achieved by the power of the Divine Spirit. No worldly power can accomplish the universal love.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: It behoveth everyone to show the utmost love, rectitude of conduct, straightforwardness and sincere kindliness unto all the peoples and kindreds of the world, be they friends or strangers. So intense must be the spirit of love and loving-kindness that the stranger may find himself a friend, the enemy a true brother, no difference whatsoever existing between them. For universality is of God and all limitations earthly.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: He must not turn away his face from any soul. He must treat with kindness both the friend and the stranger.

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: If, however you find a person leading a truly good earnest life, who does not reject or receive these Teachings, you are to remember what our Lord Jesus said, "He that is not against me is with Me."

Subject: consorting with all; being kind; loving to all
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/consorting with all; being kind; loving to all.txt
Quotation: When it is revealed, "Consort with all the religions," the intention is association with such people. Although there is no connection between us, I have served him for twenty years. Such people, as this poor Arab, are not believers, and there is no harm in that; let him believe in his own convictions. It is exhorted that if we disfavor someone, it should not be over his religion. For instance, we should not avoid a Christian because of his beliefs.

Subject: constitutional revolution in Iran
Quotation: When Mirza Malkam Khan saw this, he conceived the idea of seizing the monarchy. He had made arrangements and had first proposed that a republic should be established and despotism removed from Iran, and had arranged for the Shah to be killed. Malcolm Khan had gathered around himself several idle princes and had told them that a republic needed forty men. To each one he said, You are one of those forty men.

Subject: constitutional revolution in Iran
Quotation: Today, like other days, he gained admittance to the presence [of 'Abdu'l-Baha] and reported on the news of Iran, the Constitutional Revolt and the present government.

Subject: constitutional revolution in Iran
Quotation: From the beginning of the revolution in Tehran, it was announced to all regions, especially the Land of ?a, that the Party of God has no involvement in political affairs and has no complaint or praise for the governments of the world.

Subject: constitutional revolution in Iran
Quotation: Even at the beginning of the revolution it was explicitly written that until the government and people mix together like honey and milk, success and prosperity is impossible and unattainable. Iran would be ruined and the end result would lead to intervention by neighboring powers.

Subject: constitutional revolution in Iran
Quotation: Regarding your question about Iran, know that this revolution and turmoil will eventually come to an end and in future times Iran will be like a brilliant, shining star. Do not become discouraged by these present difficulties. Pray that God may assist the government and people of Iran and grant them deliverance and salvation from this revolution and turmoil.

Subject: constitutional revolution in Iran
Quotation: References to political reforms and needs in Iran: "Now is the time for all subjects to strive with perfect sincerity, trustworthiness and obedience so that ultimate comfort and ease may be achieved in the center of sovereignty, and the authorities may attend to the administration of internal affairs and external considerations and relationships, and establishing laws for human happiness..."

Quotation: this matter depends upon consultation among yourselves.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: We have left the matter to consultation to see what the divine friends deem advisable and decide.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: The purpose is this: they should consult with thee regarding the manner that thou deemest to be most prudent.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: The text addresses disputes arising from electoral consultation and decision-making processes within the community.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: He may be patient, he may manifest himself, he may hold fast to consultation and act according to what emerges from it.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: They must take counsel together and unitedly resist the onslaught of the stirrers up of strife and the movers of mischief.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: Whenever a spiritual assembly is established in a locality, the teacher must consult with them and carry out whatever they deem advisable.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: consultation must be carried out with complete thoughtfulness, reflection, calmness and dignity...making the execution of any important matter contingent upon several days of consultation

Subject: consultation
Quotation: You should arise with the utmost effort to elect the consultative assembly regarding this matter, for this is the most important foundation, and the foundation is the consultative assembly. This must be firm.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: The greatest cause for the manifestation and emergence of this station has been and is consultation, for through it man perceives benefit and harm, as souls strengthen one another. Thus, first consultation, then action.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: They should consult together in such wise as to win the good pleasure of God and should choose that which is approved...Upon entering, they must, as deputies of all souls, consult concerning matters and interests affecting all.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: The heaven of divine wisdom shines with the twin lights of consultation and compassion. Take counsel together in all matters, for consultation is the lamp of guidance that shows the way and grants understanding.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: Repeatedly have We written and commanded that ye should consult together and ponder upon that which hath transpired, that perchance no harm may occur and that those who are related to Us may be manifest, radiant, resplendent and luminous amongst the people.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: Your duty is to go with the majority and accept its decisions. The delegates must decide. The Board must carry out the decisions of the Conventions. There must be order. It cannot be that everybody has the right of interference; in that case nothing would be accomplished.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: and consult together on all matters, and implement whatever the majority agrees upon. By the truth of Truth, if all together make an incorrect decision it is better than a correct one made alone, for individual opinions cause discord and discord causes destruction of the edifice.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: and additionally some spiritual matters that have no connection to government and politics can be consulted upon and decisions made...once a month the men's assembly and women's assembly can meet together and discuss the matters of disagreement, with the majority vote being decisive

Subject: consultation
Quotation: When differences of opinion arise, they should refer to the majority vote, and all must obey and submit to the majority. It is not permissible thereafter for any of the honored members to object to or criticize the decision, either within or without the assembly, even if it is not correct.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: The first obligation of the members of consultation is purity of motive, illumination of reality, detachment from all else save God, attraction to the divine fragrances, humility and submissiveness among the friends, patience and forbearance in difficulties, and servitude at the sacred divine threshold.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: The object is that all affairs ought to be referred to the Convention, that is the Assembly which is composed of the representatives from different assemblies sent to the Convention, not all the people gathered for the meetings. If all people present in the meetings take part in the discussions it would not do.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: The purpose of consultation is that the opinions of multiple people are surely better than a single opinion, just as the power of many people is surely greater than the power of one person. Therefore consultation is acceptable at the Divine Threshold and is commanded, from ordinary personal matters to general universal affairs.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: A commission must be formed and all matters must be consulted upon and executed with the commission's knowledge. When I was building the Most Exalted Shrine, I formed a commission of seventeen people and undertook the construction with their knowledge and consultation. Otherwise I would not have succeeded, for consultation is among the greatest foundations of this Cause.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: Concerning what thou didst mention about the gathering of the loved ones in a special council for the conduct of affairs, this hath been accepted. In truth it is necessary. At the beginning of the entry of the Wronged One into the military barracks in the city of Akka, the establishment of a council was decided upon. However, due to changes of location and variations in movement and rest, it was postponed.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: In this Cause consultation is of vital importance, but spiritual conference and not the mere voicing of personal views is intended. The purpose is to emphasize the statement that consultation must have for its object the investigation of truth. He who expresses an opinion should not voice it as correct and right but set it forth as a contribution to the consensus of opinion, for the light of reality becomes apparent when two opinions coincide.

Subject: consultation
Quotation: In God's Book all are commanded to consult, and consultation is blessed and auspicious. From this it is evident that the food of such beasts is meat. If they were to attempt to graze, their teeth would not cut the grass, neither could they chew the cud, for they do not have molars. Likewise, God hath given to the four-footed grazing animals such teeth as reap the grass like a sickle, and from this we understand that the food of these species of animal is vegetable. They cannot chase and hunt down other animals. The falcon hath a hooked beak and sharp talons; the hooked beak preventeth him from grazing, therefore his food also is meat. But now coming to man, we see he hath neither hooked teeth nor sharp nails or claws, nor teeth like iron sickles. From this it becometh evident and manifest that the food of man is cereals and fruit. Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt

Consider those who were given the Gospel - how many servants believed in it and acted according to what was revealed therein, yet when God manifested the meaning of the Gospel and what He had intended therein, they became veiled from it.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: Setting all this aside, have they not seen that throughout all days the King of Knowledge was afflicted at the hands of such people who are like cattle, and was exposed to destruction? Which deed could be more exalted in the sight of these base ones than the sacrifice of one's life? By God! They know all this, but envy, rancor and hatred have prevented them from uttering the truth.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt

Should anyone transgress even slightly from these theological limitations, they pronounce him an infidel.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: Glory be to God! For twelve hundred years they counted themselves foremost among the peoples of the world, yet on the Day of Recompense that party was observed to be the most wretched of men, for they issued the decree for the martyrdom of the Lord of the world. Now it is incumbent, nay obligatory, upon all servants to protect the people from the suspicions and vain imaginings of the past.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: Consider the sect that clung to this word and was known as the Imamis. They took that Pure Being, by Whose word the successors and guardians were created, and suspended Him and martyred Him with the bullets of hatred and rancor. The curse of God be upon the wrongdoing people! Those souls who considered themselves the best of all sects ultimately proved to be the basest of all the world's peoples.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: Among the divines are those who write what their idle fancies inspire them, turning aside from the Pen from which have flowed the springs of wisdom and utterance. Among the people are those whom the winds of idle fancies have stirred and held back from the shore of My Name, the Manifest, the Hidden. Among the people is he who claimeth the inner meaning and thereby holdeth back the people from a path which hath been straight in the eternal past.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt

Fie upon those who have turned away from all the signs, who have taken but a single letter from the Book and used it to prove their contentions, who have denied God through Whose command were sent down glorious scriptures and sublime tablets!

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: Those who have followed Our verses aforetime - these are they who are rightly guided. And those who follow their vain desires - naught of their deeds shall be accepted, and these are they who are the losers. Whosoever heareth the innovative decree, none of his deeds shall be recorded unless he believeth in thy Lord's verses and is among those possessed of certitude. What aileth these people that they perceive not aught of God's verses? These are they who are the wrongdoers.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: O servants! What answer will ye give unto the divine Herald? No, by God! Ye have no answer save either to return to the Sun of the horizon of divine power or to acknowledge that ye have disbelieved in the Primal Point in the First, and in the Later Temple in the Last. O people! Beware, then beware lest ye be veiled from the Truth by His creation and His signs, or object to His description by the Sovereign Describer, or close your eyes to His attributes by the King of attributes.

And until that time I commanded no one with any new judgment from Thy presence, and in all wherein people differed they moved only in what pertained to the air.

These servants have pondered and, by God's grace, have emerged from the thickets of interpretation into the spacious meadow of clear declaration. The interpreters are those who discard the manifest and exalted Truth, and with the axe of conjecture carve out idols of fancy, then bow down before their own handiwork in worship and submission, all the while counting themselves among the worshippers of Truth and those detached unto God.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: It is quite evident that the people did not understand the glad tidings, or prophecies, referring to the Christ in the Bible, for in the Old Testament they found this verse--that the coming one will come as a sovereign and will conquer the east as well as the west. His rod will be of iron, He will promote the laws of the Old Testament, and during the time of his reign all the people, even the creatures and the birds, will live in a peaceful day. These people, finding these prophecies were not fulfilled in the time of Christ, nay rather (the reverse), reached to such a state that they even killed Him.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt

O Beloved of my heart! By Thy life! Were they to observe and ponder upon that which hath outwardly appeared from the Dayspring of Revelation, or were they to hear it, they would assuredly perceive a matter transcending the kingdom of earth and heaven. Base desires, reprehensible deeds, envy, heedlessness, and love of position have deprived people of every kind from the true Water of Life.

Subject: corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/corruption; misinterpretation of the Word of God.txt
Quotation: One melody from the melodies of the Dove of the Bayan regarding the criterion is mentioned specifically for those who seek the sanctuary of the All-Merciful, that they might attain to its recognition and become wholly detached from satanic manifestations, rending asunder the veils of idle fancies in such wise that the people of the Supreme Concourse hear the sound of their being rent [...] They rend asunder the veils of vain imaginings in such wise that the people of the Concourse on High hear the sound of their tearing, and witness them above the entire Concourse of the Bayan among those who have disbelieved and associated partners with God, fleeing from branch to branch that they might cast doubt and suspicion into the hearts of those whom the breezes of the All-Merciful have turned from the left of conjecture to the right of certitude.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: Most great minister, most mighty and noble ambassador, may your prosperity endure... We hope that God may increase your excellency's life, prosperity, and glory at all times. I am most ashamed to have put your excellency to such trouble.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: As for the leader, whenever thou meetest him, show courtesy - neither aversion nor attachment, neither familiarity nor estrangement. For if thou seekest friendship, he will say thou art engaging in flattery, and if thou completely avoid him, he will say there is enmity.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: With that person Sayfu'd-Dawlih, if possible, proceed with the utmost patience and kindness, and never become agitated in conversation. Whatever you hear, answer with perfect mildness and pleasant words so that he will never become disturbed and never experience weariness.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: A man must ever be thoughtful of others and be polite and courteous toward his fellow-beings. One's sitting and rising, speech and conversation, social intercourse and communication should be based upon a firm foundation and be conducive to the glory of the world of humanity.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: It behooves ones like yourself to deal with all souls with kindness and consideration...Regarding deeds, give counsel with kindness as 'Abdu'l-Baha has written, not with force, intensity and harshness, for harshness and intensity never yield fruit but rather have the opposite effect.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: O Amin of the Blessed Beauty! Your letter of the 15th of Dhi'l-Qa'dah [1337] was received. A brief reply is being written. Abdul-Baha is aware of all matters, but there is a verse in the Quran: If thou hadst been severe and harsh-hearted, they would have broken away from about thee. This is in consideration of the supreme kindness.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: Make the beauty of what ye wear commensurate with the finest ye can afford, for this is of God's grace and mercy toward you if ye are able; and if not, grieve not in the least, for verily after your death ye shall behold in Paradise what ye have done. Make not your garments too short nor too long, but observe moderation therein according to what ye love best to wear.

Subject: courtesy; culture [adab]
Quotation: Strip not yourselves of the robe of propriety [adab] and fairness [insaf], and speak not that which ye have been forbidden in the Tablets of your Lord, the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting. He who is deprived of propriety is naked, though he be clothed in all the silk of the earth. This hath been sent down in truth in preserved Tablets of glory. He who hath no propriety [adab] hath no faith [iman], as testifieth that which was revealed in the Bayan, if ye would but witness it.

Then above the crust, plants came into being, then animals appeared, then humans came to exist.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: As for what was asked about creation, know that creation hath ever been and shall ever be. No beginning can be imagined for its beginning, nor any end for its ending. The name Creator itself requireth a creation, just as the name Lord necessitates that which is lorded over.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Praise be to God Who hath raised up the heavens by His command and established the throne upon the waters by His revelation. Then He split the atmospheres and rent the air and tore asunder the veils through the word Be! He raised up the leaves with trees, and the earth with mountains, and the seas with rains, and the springs with their like.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Praise be unto Him Who brought forth the first creation with brilliant signs, radiant lights, rising stars, shining suns, luminous moons, rain-laden clouds, surging seas, firm mountains, resplendent realities, infinite forms, countless beings, and substances endowed with power and capacity - these are the brilliant signs of the Lord of earth and heaven.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Thou art He Who hath brought all things into being from nothing, and hath established all things without anything, and hath ordained the stations of all things by Thy power, and hath made known to all things the dawning-places of Thy power, and hast caused all things to witness the settings of Thine eternity, so that nothing might be veiled from Thy countenance.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Thou hast raised up the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them from nothing by Thy command. Then Thou didst create the creation of all things by Thy power, and didst nourish the creation of all things by Thy will, and didst cause all things to die through the sovereignty of Thy oneness, and didst give life to all things through the manifestations of Thy eternality.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Through a wave from the ocean of His endless mercy, He hath adorned all created things with the ornament of existence, and through a breath from His peerless paradise, He hath honored all beings with the robe of His holy grace. Through an overflowing drop from the deep of the sea of His Sovereign Will, He hath brought infinite creation out of utter nothingness into the realm of being.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Glorified be He! There is none other God but Him. How wondrous is His handiwork, how magnificent His creation! He hath brought forth from utter nothingness the vast expanse of being, and with His hand of power hath given existence to the merest atom from naught, endowing it with speech. Through His Own effulgences He hath transformed absolute nothingness into pure existence, bestowing absolute being through His grace.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Through the manifestation of His power and sovereignty, He brought into being all contingent things from nothingness through His Will and its expressions so that all atoms might be illumined by the radiance of His creative light, and become eager to behold the raiment of His Beauty's countenance, and become fearful of His justice, and see naught in anything save His manifestation, which is more evident than all things.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Furthermore, it is a philosophical principle that the existence of phenomena implies composition and that mortality, or nonexistence, is equivalent to decomposition... Then what have we left as a form of composition? It is the voluntary form of composition, which means that composition is effected through a superior will, that there is will expressed in this motive or action. It is thus proved that the existence of phenomena is effected through the eternal Will, the Will of the Living, Eternal and Self-subsistent.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: The truth is that the Cause is the Handiwork of God which He created by Himself for Himself and made it the cause of all His creation, as the Imam indicated: The cause of things is His handiwork, and it hath no cause. This is attested by all the horizonal and personal signs and the verses of the Book, for the One that proceedeth from the One is the One that is known through duality, which necessitates the existence of trinity - and this is clearly false by proof of separation. Nothing can proceed from the One, which is the essence of origination, except the First Mention.

Subject: creation of the world
Quotation: Praise be to God Who created water from His utterance manifest in the Kingdom of immortality. Then He gazed upon it and it trembled within itself, and a portion of it froze. Thus did the dusty earth appear through His decree, established in the realm of origination. When they separated and divided, the Tongue of Grandeur spoke another word. Then that water, brought forth by the Will manifest in contingent being through the essence of possibility, moved upon that earth created by the will of the All-Merciful. And there arose from them both a subtle, spiritual, luminous heat by its power to the highest station, that it might attain that station wherein speaks the tongue of its Most Glorious Lord. When it reached the ultimate of its station, it paused in that most exalted station which is mentioned in creation as the highest sphere. Then the water mixed partially with the earth and another heat arose from them both, but due to its weakness it did not reach the first and paused in another station which is mentioned as the second sphere. And likewise did heat arise from them again and again until the stations mentioned as the spheres were completed. Then the Tongue of Grandeur spoke another word and the stations and spheres revolved, and from the intensity of revolution a light shone forth and formed a dome over the face of heaven. Then brilliant stars and gleaming planets appeared.

Quotation: And because they have performed so many passion plays and dramas about previous Imams and Prophets day and night, and have greatly exaggerated in their dramatic presentations - for instance, showing angels descending from heaven and making extremely exaggerated narrations - drama has become like a plaything and has absolutely no effect.

Subject: critique of Eastern values; culture

Iran is the dawning-place of lights and the dayspring of the Sun of Truth. Despite this, the Iranians are in eclipse while the wise ones in distant climes are illumined and manifest.

Subject: critique of Eastern values; culture
Quotation: Still the Iranians do not awaken, they are afflicted with a rabbit's sleep, and these mindless leaders have so dominated them like a nightmare that they have not had a moment's relief from their stupor. Especially since "another tune was added to the tambour" - namely the interference of the shameless people in all affairs. The Iranians still have not understood that these calamities were brought upon Iran by this losing party.

Quotation: Yet ironically, the Iranians take axe and hatchet to their own roots, for the Baha'is have so glorified Iran in the eyes of others that today vast multitudes from all seven climes pay homage to Iran, since the Sun of Truth dawned from that horizon and it is the holy homeland of Baha'u'llah. Reflect upon these servants and what befell them. We have ever been occupied with goodly counsel and have spoken that which benefits the servants. Nevertheless, that which occurred caused every fair-minded one to lament and wail. The eye of the world has shed tears because of what befell the friends of God from various parties and peoples.

Subject: definitions of a Baha'i; qualities of a Baha'i

Quotation: To be a Baha'i is to be the embodiment of all human virtues.

Subject: definitions of a Baha'i; qualities of a Baha'i
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/definitions of a Baha'i; qualities of a Baha'i.txt
Quotation: He is a true Bahá’í who striveth by day and by night to progress and advance along the path of human endeavour, whose most cherished desire is so to live and act as to enrich and illuminate the world, whose source of inspiration is the essence of Divine virtue, whose conduct and behaviour is the cause of infinite progress. He should, to the best of his ability, become a source of mercy to all people and of bounty to the whole world. Only when he attaineth unto such perfect gifts can it be said of him that he is a true Bahá’í. For in this holy Dispensation, the crowning glory of bygone ages and cycles, true faith is no mere acknowledgement of the Unity of God, but rather the living of a life that will manifest all the perfections and virtues implied in such belief.

Subject: definitions of a Baha'i; qualities of a Baha'i
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/definitions of a Baha'i; qualities of a Baha'i.txt

In that sense the Baha'i movement is not a new religion.

One may call one's self a Baha'i and in no way live the life, on the other hand one may live the life and never be known as a Baha'i.

Subject: degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence.txt
Quotation: As to the question concerning the soul, know thou, verily, that "soul" is a term applied to numerous realities, according to the exigencies of the following relations with respect to development in the world of existence: (1) In the mineral kingdom, soul is called "latent force," silently working for the disintegration of the substance of the mineral. (2) In the vegetable kingdom it is called "virtue augmentative" or the power of growth, which attracts and absorbs the delicate materials of inorganic substance found in the mineral kingdom of matter, and transforms them into the condition of growth.... (3) In the animal kingdom it is called "sense perception" or instinct. This term soul, as applied to the animal kingdom, is also a natural quality resulting from the mixture of the elements, and it appears from their mingling and combination, for it is a quality which results from the composition of bodies (organisms), and is dispersed at their decomposition.... (4) In the human world, soul signifies the "rational being" or mind. This has a potential existence before its appearance in human life. It is like unto the existence of a tree within the seed. The existence of the tree within the seed is potential; but when the seed is sown and watered, the signs thereof, its roots and branches, and all of its different qualities, appear. Likewise the "rational soul" has a potential existence before its appearance in the human body, and through the mixture of elements and a wonderful combination, according to the natural order, law, conception and birth, it appears with its identity.... (5) If the angelic aspect becomes more powerful, and the divine power and brightness surround man, then the second birth takes place, and eternal life is found at this point. Man becomes then the noblest among creatures.

These three powers are called by different names, according to different interpretations, signifying powers. One signifies spirit, soul - the growing soul - the sensitive soul - and the intellectual soul.

Quotation: It was previously explained that all spirits are divided into five categories: the vegetable spirit, the animal spirit, the human spirit, the spirit of faith, and the Holy Spirit. The vegetable spirit is the power of growth which results from the interaction of other created things with the seed. The animal spirit is a comprehensive power of the senses that comes into being through the composition and combination of elements, and when this composition dissolves, that power also vanishes and disappears.

Subject: degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence

Quotation: In the world of existence -- that which is comprehensible -- there are stages of mortality: the first stage is the mineral world, next is the vegetable world. In the latter world the mineral doth exist but with a distinctive feature which is the vegetable characteristic. Likewise in the animal world, the mineral and vegetable characteristics are present and in addition the characteristics of the animal world are to be found, which are the faculties of hearing and of sight. In the human world the characteristics of the mineral, vegetable and animal worlds are found and in addition that of the human kind, namely the intellectual characteristic, which discovereth the realities of things and comprehendeth universal principles.

Subject: degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence.txt
Quotation: The glory and eminence of every created thing depends upon certain conditions and is related to specific qualities. The excellence, beauty and perfection of the earth lie in its becoming verdant and luxuriant through the bounty of the vernal rain, in plants sprouting forth, in flowers and herbs blooming, in trees becoming fruitful and laden with fresh and tender fruit, in gardens being formed, in meadows becoming adorned, in fields and mountains donning garments of green, and in gardens, plains, cities and villages becoming beautified. This is the happiness of the mineral world. The highest eminence and perfection of the vegetable world, however, consists in a tree growing by the water's edge beside a gentle stream, caressed by gentle breezes and warmed by the sun, tended by a gardener's care, growing day by day, yielding fruit. The glory of the animal world lies in possessing perfect members, organs and powers, with all needs met and provided for - this is the ultimate dignity, honor and elevation possible to it.

Subject: degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence.txt
Quotation: Know that in general there are five kinds of spirit. First is the vegetable spirit, which is the power that results from the composition and combination of the elements according to the wisdom and decree of the Most High, and from their mutual arrangement, their influence upon and their interconnection with other created things. When these parts and elements are separated, the associated power of growth likewise ceases to exist. After this is the animal spirit, which also results from the combination of elements that are brought together in a single composition. But this composition is more complete, and when by the decree of the almighty Lord it reaches a fuller degree of combination, the animal spirit, which consists in the power of the senses, comes to exist. This power perceives sensible realities--that which can be seen, heard, tasted, smelled or touched. As to the human spirit, its likeness is that of a glass and the bounty of the sun. That is, the body of man, which is composed of the elements, is the most perfect form of composition and combination, the soundest arrangement, the noblest composition, and the most perfect of all existing things.
