Quotation: Pass beyond both separation and union,/That thou mayest attain the highest heaven, O son./While thou art in separation, thou art surely in flames;/And in union too art feverish and unwell./Set foot in the pure realm of immortality,/Where all save Him is nothingness.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: And verily, were the names to free themselves from the limitations of creation, they would all become the Most Great Name, if thou be of them that know. For the Ancient Beauty hath, in these hallowed, mighty and inaccessible days, shone forth upon all things with all names.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Whatsoever God willeth; there is no power except through God, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of all worlds. Say: Whatsoever God willeth; there is no glory except for God, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of all worlds.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: He is He, and there is naught except Him. There is no essence except His Essence, no attributes except His attributes, no virtues except His virtues, no beauty except His beauty, no tongue except His tongue, no light except His light, and no manifestation except His manifestation.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Religion consisteth of two letters - one letter is that there is none other God but He, the Lord of all things, and the other letter is that all besides Him is His creation. Between them there is no third letter, nor beneath them a fourth letter, nor besides them a fifth letter.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Therefore praise be unto Thee for having taught me Thy oneness and caused to flow from my tongue the word of Thy glorification. I bear witness that there is no God but Thee, even as Thou hast testified to Thine own Self, though none of Thy creation can comprehend the knowledge thereof.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: For verily, he who is unable to annihilate negation except through His Word - that is the most exalted path in establishing Your unity by negating negation from the court of Your holiness, the seat of Your glory, the sovereignty of Your self-subsistence, and the dominion of Your lordship.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: He is the Subduer over His servants and the Manifest in the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and whatsoever lieth between them by His command. And verily He is the Guardian, the Inaccessible, the Most Exalted, the Compelling. He judgeth with truth and He is the One, the All-Compelling.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: The Supreme Pen hath testified that there is none other God but Him, and that He is the One Who hath revealed Himself unto all things through His most beautiful names on the Day wherein the horizon of Divine Unity was illumined by the Sun of His Name, the All-Subduing Lord of all possibility.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Consider the term Divine Unity, which the Manifestations of God have uttered in every Dispensation, a goodly term which all the divers peoples and kindreds of the world have spoken. Nevertheless, in each Dispensation, it hath been made new and hath in no wise been divested of its novel character.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: I shall ever glorify Thee, for this is what Thou hast ordained until the Day of Resurrection. Blessed art Thou, O my God! I shall ever love to praise Thee in a manner befitting the sublimity of Thy praise, and I have not sanctified Thee in a way worthy of Thine Essence from the holy court of Thy oneness.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: The Eternal Essence, exalted and glorified be He, hath ever unified, and will forever continue to unify, His Essence through His Essence, His attributes through His attributes, and His deeds through His deeds, and praiseth His own Self with that which befitteth His eternal exaltation and His primordial supremacy.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: There is no God but God, to the number of all that He hath created and shall create...There is no God but God, from the beginning that hath no beginning, to the number of all numbers. There is no God but God, unto the end that hath no end, to the number of all that the Sun of Truth hath risen upon or shall rise upon.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Until now the true meaning of Divine Unity hath not been made manifest. Were the Most Exalted Pen to unveil but a little thereof, all would testify to their own polytheism. However, the Name the Concealer hath not withdrawn the hem of grace, and the Name the All-Bountiful hath not permitted justice to reach this station.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: I bear witness that Thou art God, the Single, the One, the Subsisting, the Unique, the Eternal, the Ever-Living, Whom no description can describe and no attribute can qualify, and Whom nothing can know through anything else, for the rule of knowing between two things is forbidden and the word of conjunction after separation is cut off.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: God createth not a single thing but He createth from itself what He willeth through His command, which quickeneth all things. God createth not a single entity but He createth from itself its counterpart, for God, the Lord of all worlds. And God createth not a pair but He createth from itself a single entity, for God, the Lord of all worlds.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: If somewhere mention is made of a station or knowledge of all things, it is due to the greatness of the station of unity, before which all stations are humble and non-existent... Further, regarding the command of the Most Great Name to Satan, I did not understand, for the call was to unity and the ordinances of the Qur'an, no aspect of polytheism was intended.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Lord, cause me to enter the depth of Thy oneness and the ocean of Thy unity." Most people in the station of reality have not truly perceived - were they on the pure path wherein there is no mention of [...] For the speaker hath not beheld God and His works, neither doth he act with pure devotion to God, nor doth he pursue the intention of drawing nigh unto Him.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Verily all things enter into what God loveth, for they are in Paradise and are among His creation which God hath created in the Book of the Exalted Ones, and it is recorded therein. And should it be among that which God loveth not to mention, yet it is among God's creation, His proof hath been perfected concerning it, and God will purify it when He willeth through His command.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Thus doth the Tongue of truth and knowledge inform thee. All names have been transformed, the wailing of all things hath been raised up, and every soul hath been shaken, except those who have been quickened by the breathings of the All-Glorious that have wafted from the direction of your Lord, the All-Merciful, and awakened them from slumber and purified them from the defilement of the idolaters.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: He is the One manifest above His creation, and He is the Mighty, the Beloved. He is the One Who createth whatsoever He willeth through His command Be! and it is. Such is the Creator of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever lieth between them, the Mighty, the Beloved. He is the One before Whom bow down in adoration all who are in the heavens and who are on earth; unto God shall all return.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: This is His Day and His Cause. Blessed is the soul that hath attained unto true divine unity. The people of the past never attained the fragrance of unity, much less its station. Each day they would ascribe a partner unto God, and yet deemed themselves to be believers in His unity... True unity is to turn unto the horizon of the one Manifestation; to exceed this is accounted as polytheism in the Book of God.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: And verily all the worlds are confined to those eight, for the first determination of the Primal K is the station of Muhammadanness, which is the Paradise of Eternity, wherein through manifestation He hath never departed, and whereunto He hath never entered from without. Then verily that Paradise is the portion of the Family of God, who are the Imams of Justice, and no one among creation hath any share therein.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: None has established what God has decreed in the Book, for all food is that which the All-Merciful detailed in the Qur'an aforetime. He defined what He wished and forbade what He wished, and He forbade naught save what Israel forbade for himself. Verily all that is unlawful for mankind is that which the Will beareth, magnifying the Manifestation of the Divine Purpose and exalting the dawning of the sovereignty of Oneness.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: I testify, O my God, that Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be. At no time can there be separated from Thee what befitteth Thy creation or beseemeth Thy handiwork. Thy dominion in Thy kingdom and the manifestations of Thy creation in Thy dominion have ever existed and will ever endure. Were I to say at any time that Thou art Thou and hadst no creation, I would negate my knowledge of Thy power and certainty of Thy Lordship.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: The primary Oneness is a divine reality, abstracted from every attribute, sign, and indication. Could multiplicity, plurality, or distinction be conceived therein from the viewpoint of the perfections of the Essence, its relationship to attributes, and its all-comprehensiveness of divine and lordly names which necessitate the existence of contingent beings? God forbid! Blessed be the name of thy Lord, possessed of majesty and bounty!

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Know then that this connection is not what the servants understand, for He, exalted and mighty be He, is never joined to anything nor connected to any soul, and there exists between Him and His servants no similarity, no link, no geometry, and no sign. He is the Self-Sufficient, the Holy, the Luminous. Rather, union, connection and nearness exist only through the Manifestations of His Self and the Dawning-Places of His Cause, if you be of those who attain.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Know that when the lights of Divine Unity and the effulgence of the radiance of Oneness dawned upon the manifestations of creation from the heaven of Will and the atmosphere of Purpose, nothing came into being except that it served to guide souls to the Dawning-Place of creation and His bountiful Countenance. In this station may be understood what was mentioned aforetime in the tradition: I have not seen a thing except that I saw God before it, after it, or with it.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: And by these stations their ranks become manifest, if ye would understand. All these are stations in the manifestations of mirrors when the Sun shines forth, yet in these days ye inquire not about the Sun. Then bear witness that It hath ever been one in Its essence, one in Its attributes, and one in Its deeds, and apart from this no verdict of absolute unity can be established for It, nor can the sanctification of Its essence from similitude and limitation be confirmed, if ye would understand.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: I testify, and all things testify, to that which Thou hast testified concerning Thyself, and all things bear witness thereunto, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone, without peer. And no heart can know from anything, for above that there is no victory in affirming Your unity, nor below this is there abasement for one whom You have forsaken by Your power. I testify with my heart, my spirit, my soul, my body, my hearing, my sight, my blood, my skin, my hair, and all that You have caused me to possess, that there is no God but You.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: His beginning hath had no beginning other than His Own firstness and His end knoweth no end save His Own lastness. All the most excellent Names belong to the Will, while the depth of His Essence is sanctified above any Name or praise, the purity (kafur) of His indivisible unity (sadhij) is exalted above any glory or loftiness, and the substance of His transcendence is glorified above any height or sublimity. He is the First, yet not defined by it, and He is the Last, but not described by it. He is the Seen, and not praised by it, and He is Hidden, and not recognized by it.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my Lord and my Beloved! I render thanks unto Thee for the wondrous favors of Thy oneness, which Thou hast caused to flow forth and hast sent down from the heaven of Thy holy Being. By Thy might, O my God! Thy favors have attained such heights that no point can be seen in Thy kingdom but that from it have been detailed the mysteries of the wisdom of the sovereignty of Thy Lordship, and no speck of dust can be found but that it testifies of itself, by itself, to Thy unity through that which hath shone upon it from the effulgences of the lights of Thy oneness.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: Let thy self praise God, thy mind proclaim there is none other God but Him, and thy heart declare God is Most Great. Look not upon these Manifestations with the eye of difference, for this is not the path of those endowed with insight and understanding. Rather, He Who created you is He Who sustains you, and He Who created you is He Who causes you to die, and He Who causes you to die is He Who gives you life. No partner hath He in His work and no rival hath He in His dominion. These are mirrors proclaiming that there is none other God but Him - He creates what He willeth and doeth what He pleaseth.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: And as to what you asked about unity (tawhid), this station has been elaborately explained in numerous tablets from the Divine Authoritative Pen, sufficient for all the peoples of the world. You should endeavor to collect, as much as possible, the Persian and Arabic books that have been revealed from the Divine Source in this Most Great Revelation. There remains no knowledge except that which has been mentioned in the tablets of my Lord and your Lord, and no station except that which has been detailed therein. In one of the Persian tablets He says, exalted be His glory and sublime be His praise: The purpose of unity is not to consider two as one, rather its purpose is to consider the One as sanctified above all, for He is not associated with His creation nor is He known through any other than Himself. And one should observe the lights of His manifestations in all things, that is, to see all things sustained by Him and dependent upon Him. This is the station wherein He says "God was, and there was nothing else besides Him." He has ever been, in the heights of inaccessibility and in the summit of exaltation, sanctified above all things and ever shall be. Some who count themselves among the people of unity are walking on the shore of polytheism and wandering in the wilderness of multiplicity, yet they do not perceive it. In another place He says, exalted be His remembrance: "Through My Name were raised the banners of unity and were planted the standards of detachment" to the end of His holy utterance, exalted be His remembrance. And these stations depend upon acceptance of the Truth, for if a person should practice unity his entire life, yet if from the Pen of the Cause a word of negation is revealed concerning him, he would be counted among the people of polytheism. As you observe, most nations today utter the blessed words "There is no God but God," yet in the sight of God they were not and will not be considered among the people of unity, as the Supreme Pen has testified in most tablets to the polytheism of those souls. Today it is incumbent upon the one who turns to God not to look to what he or others possess. He must purify his ears from all that the people possess to hear the divine utterances, that he might attain to what God has intended. In brief, whosoever is accepted today is counted among the people of unity, and without this he is deprived and forbidden.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: As for his state of anger, it was due to God's manifestation to him, whereby his inner and outer being were drawn to God at the station of His manifestation. In this station, his identity and overwhelming power tell of none save God alone. Thus he attributed the unseen to God alone, metaphorically indicating that his knowledge of the unseen is God's knowledge, and there is no account save of God. None knows the unseen save God, for he was in the station of manifesting his knowledge of Divine Unity, and that station is one of pure oneness and absolute obscurity, wherein there is no mention of self save of God's signs alone

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: How many there are who glorify and unify Him throughout all days and nights, yet are among the most heedless of servants, for they recognize not Him Whom they unify at morn and eventide. And how many a believer in divine unity is today a polytheist before God, though he perceiveth it not within himself and is numbered among the idolaters. Consider, for example, the philosophers and the leading figures among the Shaykhis - they established four degrees of divine unity: unity of Essence, then of Attributes, of Actions, and of Worship. They bid people to believe in their doctrines and have written numerous books to prove these four degrees. Yet they remain veiled from Him Whose knowledge they sought to prove to themselves.

Subject: divine unity [tawhid] and degrees of unity
Quotation: I bear witness before Thee and before all things that there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and the dominion, Thine the might and the sovereignty, Thine the power and divinity, Thine the strength and majesty, Thine the dominion and the realm, Thine the glory and grandeur, Thine the countenance and beauty, Thine the face and perfection, Thine the might and deeds, Thine the similitude and parables, Thine the mercy and grace, Thine the authority and justice, Thine the greatness and sublimity, Thine the bounty and favor, Thine the loftiness and elevation, Thine the power and invincibility, Thine the joy and gladness, Thine the tribulation and detachment, Thine the grandeur and majesty, Thine is all that is seen and unseen from the highest heights to the first speck of dust.

This is a Manifestation that revealeth Himself but once in every five hundred thousand years. Thus have We lifted the veil and removed the coverings. Blessed is he who hath recognized the purpose of God - whoso knoweth it, his heart rejoiceth and he remaineth steadfast in the Cause in such wise that all creation cannot deflect him therefrom. We have disclosed in this Tablet one of the mysteries of this Revelation, and have concealed that which is hidden lest the clamor of the ungodly be raised.

Should God will, He could decree for each nine nineteen ten moments like unto a thousand thousand years, or that which none can reckon save God. However, what God hath mentioned regarding fifty [thousand] years was what was previously revealed in the Qur'an, that ye may be mindful.

We pray God that He may graciously assist him to retract and repent. Should he repent, God will, no doubt, forgive him. If he persisteth in his error, God will, assuredly, send down one who will deal mercilessly with him.

Whoso layeth claim to a Revelation before the completion of a full thousand years, such a one is assuredly a lying impostor. And whosoever interpreteth this verse is one who hath turned away from the All-Merciful and is counted among the losers. Although for those possessed of insight, mention was made aforetime of the dominion of Husayn lasting eighty thousand years, yet the people of Baha must at least hold to a thousand years.

As to the cycle of the Blessed Beauty--the times of the Greatest Name--this is not limited to a thousand or two thousand years.… When it is said that the period of a thousand years beginneth with the Manifestation of the Blessed Beauty and every day thereof is a thousand years, the intent is a reference to the cycle of the Blessed Beauty, which in this context will extend over many ages into the unborn reaches of time.

The outward spring, which is charged with the nurturing of all visible things by the command of the Creator of Names, appeareth but once a year, and likewise the spiritual spring, which traineth spirits and illumined hearts and bestoweth eternal and everlasting life, doth appear but once in a thousand years or more, conferring upon all things, both seen and unseen, the garment of existence and the revelation of divine lordship.

Subject: early years; early ministry of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: Outside of Teheran We had a great park planted by the Father of the Beloved Perfection. This was a wonderful garden. It contained our gates, Eastern, Western, Northern and Southern. As you entered the Eastern gate, the Western gate was visible, similarly form the Northern you can see the Southern gate, In the Center of the garden a great throne was built and four straight avenues branching off toward the gates,- so that you could see all the four gates as you sat on that throne. On both sides of these avenues, poplar trees were planted to the number of ten thousand. These trees rising erect and majestic toward the sky. Under these trees thousands of rose bushes were planted, the fragrance of which filled the air. Often we used to sleep at night on this throne. The moon clear, full, silvery stone upon us, the galaxies of the stars shedding their rays, now faintly and again with a lustrous twinkle over the calm and mystic scene of the garden. Long before sunrise, I would open my eyes admiring with wonder this infinite universe of God. Then all at once the nightingales, in sweet melodies break into sweet concert of divine music, the gentle murmur of the rills flowing on all rides reached to the ears and the zephyr passing through the leaves making the noise of a soft sweeping handclap and applause. In the early morning the blessed Perfection would rise and prepare tea for all of us and while the sun was dawning from the Eastern horizon we were gathered around him, drinking tea and enjoying the heavenly scene all around us.

Subject: early years; early ministry of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: Mirza Taqi became very frightened, for if the Blessed Beauty were killed, there would be bloodshed between two tribes. Therefore, he arranged for them to remove the bricks from behind the platform, and when they reached the last layer, to suddenly collapse it and thus extricate the Blessed Beauty from among the crowd, so that the people could not reach Him. He brought the Blessed Beauty to his own house, and the people rushed to the governor's residence. Thus the Blessed Beauty proceeded to Darreh-Gaz, and during this time Muhammad Shah sent a messenger with orders to kill the Blessed Beauty wherever He might be found.

Subject: early years; early ministry of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: In my childhood, this wronged one read in a book by Mulla Baqir Majlisi about the raid on the Banu Qurayzah. From that moment I was distressed and full of sorrow, to the extent that my pen cannot express it -- even though what happened was the decree of God, and its intent was only to foil oppressors. But when the ocean of forgiveness and grace appeared, therefore in those days I beseeched God for that which was the cause of love, fellowship and unity among all who are on earth -- until, on the second of the month of the Birth before the Dawning, all my mental states, my words and thoughts, were turned upside down, an inversion that bore the glad-tidings of the Ascent. This revolution was manifest for twelve days continuously and unremittingly. Afterwards, the waves of the ocean of utterance appeared, and the effulgences of the luminary of tranquillity were radiant. Then the matter eventuated in a time of full revelation (zuhur), when I attained to that which God rendered the basis of the joy of the worlds and the dawn of bestowal on all who dwell in the heavens and the earth. After the Most High Pen [the Bab], We abrogated all that which was the cause of hardship and discomfort and strife by Our decisive decree, and We revealed and implemented all that which was a source of concord and unity.

Subject: early years; early ministry of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: Had the Amir-Nizam been aware of My true position, he would certainly have laid hold on Me. He exerted the utmost effort to discover the real situation, but was unsuccessful. God wished him to be ignorant of it.

Subject: early years; early ministry of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: Since We were renowned among the ministers of Iran, they all expressed friendship toward Us, but they feared lest some dangerous command concerning Us might issue from the government. When the government of Tehran heard about the incident at Badasht, where a group was with Us, they swore an oath, saying: Many times I have heard things about him and overlooked them, but this time I will surely kill him. They had issued orders to the chiefs of Mazandaran to arrest Us and execute Us. However, His Majesty passed away. Later, the Amir-Nizam also said in the assembly of nobles that he had caused much harm to the government, yet he dwells in Tehran in utmost glory. It was a dangerous time, and most of the nobles were urging Me to travel somewhere else.

Subject: early years; early ministry of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: As for the change of air in Shimran in Murgh-Mahallih, it is a gift of the All-Merciful. That place is not a district of birds - it is the nest of the Phoenix of the East and the dwelling of the Simurgh of Mount Qaf, for the Blessed Beauty (may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones) dwelt in that pure and sanctified farm for one summer. In Haji Baqir's garden, which was three stories and overlooked the lake, was the seat of the King of the Kingdom. It was in the beginning of the Cause. In the middle of the lake they had built a large stone platform. In the middle of the platform was a pavilion and around the platform was a garden. Nearly one hundred and fifty of the friends would gather. At night there were songs of glorification that reached the Supreme Concourse. It was a very happy time. The Blessed Beauty would always mention that place.

Subject: early years; early ministry of Baha'u'llah
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty - may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones - made two journeys to Baghdad and Karbala. One journey was after the martyrdom of the Bab - may my spirit be a sacrifice for Him - during the time of Mirza Taqi Khan, the Prime Minister Atabik, and one journey was after the attempt on the Shah's life when He was exiled and banished. When the Blessed Beauty was brought from Niyavaran bareheaded and barefooted in chains and fetters to Tihran, Mirza 'Abdu'l-Vahhab attained His presence in the prison.

Subject: education and the development of capacity
Quotation: Material civilization prevents humans from causing harm through punishment, while divine civilization educates souls to avoid sins without fear of punishment and consider sin itself their greatest chastisement

Subject: education and the development of capacity
Quotation: Man has the power of knowledge which will exalt him to heaven, and the power of ignorance which will debase him to the lowest condition. The more a person advances in Divine matters, the more he will receive the attributes of light; and the more he retrogrades, the more he will receive the qualities of darkness.

Subject: education and the development of capacity
Quotation: For human reality is the dividing line between light and shadow, the confluence of the two seas, and the ultimate point in the arc of descent. Therefore it hath the capacity for all stations: through education it acquireth virtues, and without education it remaineth in the lowest depths of deficiency. Every child may become either a source of illumination for the world or a cause of darkness throughout the horizons.

Subject: education and the development of capacity
Quotation: Clay, however much trained, will not become a brilliant pearl; a black stone will not become a world-illumining gem; and the colocynth and zaqqum trees will not become blessed trees through education and training. That is, education does not transform the human essence, but it has a complete effect and through its penetrating power brings forth whatever perfections and capacities are embedded and inherent in human reality.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Children must be provided with all means of health from the moment of birth... When the child begins to show some sensitivity and understanding, the mother should establish proper conduct and education, and speak of all manner of things, so that in childhood he may learn proper behavior and training, acquire spiritual sensibilities, gain understanding of religious mysteries to the extent possible, and obtain a general knowledge of all physical matters. When the time comes for a teacher, then education regarding knowledge and learning belongs to the teacher at school, and to the father and mother at home.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: They have established schools that are considered gardens of delight for children, furnished with all manner of toys, or in other words, means for children's joy and exercise, whereby their nerves and muscles are strengthened and active, and they avoid [weakness] and lethargy, keeping their mental faculties alert and vigorous. Under the supervision and training of male and female teachers, hundreds of children like flocks of blessed birds spend their days in utmost simplicity and purity in play and joy - but in reality they are becoming accustomed to physical exercise and [not readable] and learning good social manners and fellowship.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: For example, if children remain in the wilderness and receive no education at all, they will certainly remain ignorant, they will certainly remain unaware of the civilized world. No crafts, no commerce, no agriculture - like the peoples of central Africa who are in the utmost savagery. What has distinguished the world of Europe from the world of Africa? Certainly it is education, for the people of Europe are educated while the people of Africa are not educated.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: In this wondrous Cycle, the firm foundation is the establishment of education in sciences and knowledge, and by explicit text all children must acquire sciences to the necessary degree. Therefore, schools and educational institutions must be established in every city and village, and all children must strive to acquire learning to the necessary degree in cities and villages.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Thus it became clear and evident that minds differ in their innate nature, and education also has a mighty influence and powerful effect. Without an educator, all souls would be like beasts, and without a teacher, all children would be like insects. This is why in the Divine Book in this wondrous age, education and training are obligatory, not optional

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The seventh teaching of Baha'o'llah concerns itself and is in accord with this system of universal education; it is that all the children should study and acquire a profession, that there should not remain a single individual without a profession whereby he can earn his livelihood.

Subject: education of children; moral education

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: There can be no improvement unless the girls are brought up in schools and centres of learning, unless they are taught the sciences and other branches of knowledge, and unless they acquire the manifold arts, as necessary, and are divinely trained.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: If the human self is left to its natural state, the character of all children will become reprehensible and satanic... This is what nature requires, and all these corruptions come from nature

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Now it is thus: people quickly form attachments to the caller of desires. Call children to play and frolic, and they will immediately respond with enthusiasm and joy, considering it blissful pleasure. But direct them to school and lessons and teaching, and they will react with aversion and curse it. Human nature inclines toward the life and freedom of wild beasts, but divine education ultimately prevails. When children reach maturity, they themselves abandon play and become independent of foolishness.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Give lessons in divine love to children who are studying, and teach them heavenly teachings, for children and youth require training in character, morals and proper conduct more than they need learning and knowledge. Therefore, train the children in Baha'i schools in divine characteristics and guide them to purity and holiness, so that each one may develop an angelic nature and be adorned with the attributes and character of a true Baha'i.

Subject: education of children; moral education

They must discuses (these affairs) with each other in this manner.

Quotation: Today the spread of beneficial sciences, the discovery of material mysteries of creation, the promotion of useful arts, and the education of children are counted among the greatest gifts of the Lord of Glory

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: I supplicate God that they may become the servants of the Cause of God as their father and mother have, and be trained according to Bahai education, so that they may become two great signs of the love of God.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: It is not permissible even to strike an animal. When an animal is trained properly, it becomes domesticated. Thereby is the crooked branch made straight, and the thorny thicket transformed into a rose-garden.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Today the diffusion of sciences, the training in arts, and the instruction of children - both boys and girls - are amongst the greatest and most fundamental principles of this radiant century and this glorious age.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Through His training these oppressed and downtrodden people, slaves and captives of the Pharaohs, established the splendor of the Solomonic sovereignty. This is an example of a universal Teacher, a universal Educator.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Let us see what the students will do. God willing, may they acquire such proficiency in English that they may succeed in this task. They must attain the utmost proficiency in English, and likewise in Persian and Arabic.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: the greatest means is education of the child. To this must each and all hold fast. We have verily laid this charge upon you in manifold Tablets as well as in My Most Holy Book. Well is it with him who deferreth thereto.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Give great importance to the Ta'yid School. Make every effort through all means that it may make great progress and become distinguished and renowned among the schools of Iran, for it is connected to this momentous Cause.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Therefore you must look upon him with the eye of grace and nurture him in the embrace of education and watch over him day and night so that, God willing, he may become like his father and be born of the element of heart and soul.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: May handmaidens be raised up and nurtured who shall each, with their own voice, sing His praise, and who shall appear and shine forth in the world of creation in such wise as to render obsolete all mention of the women of former times.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Let thyself be reared in the cradle of the loving providence of God and suck the milk of divine knowledge from the breast of His bounty... O Lord! Graciously assist this child to grow and be quickened in the meads of Thy tender affection

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Nurture children from infancy at the breast of education, raise them in the cradle of virtues, and develop them in the embrace of bounty. Make them proficient in every beneficial science and grant them a portion of every wonderful craft.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: teach them the basics of English now and train them in praiseworthy characteristics...You must now strive with complete dedication to teach them morals, good beliefs, and divine education. Endeavor night and day that they may learn English.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: That is to say, seek out such a way and conduct, strive after such a character and disposition, and choose such manners and behavior, that like honey and sugar they may be full of sweetness. Then will the secluded women of Iran follow your example

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The servants must be educated and, with joy and radiance, be made aware of that which profiteth them, that they may become cognizant of the cause and purpose of their own existence and creation, and may see themselves free and detached from all else but God.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The education of children and the nurturing of youth is the noblest of all human accomplishments and attracts the favors and bounties of the All-Merciful Lord, for it is the very foundation of human excellence and the cause of eternal ascent to everlasting glory.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Praise be to God, the Tarbiyat School has become a school of truth, and the young saplings of humanity's garden are acquiring arts and sciences with perfect integrity and uprightness, while the esteemed teachers have arisen to teach the children with utmost capability

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: As to the question about the death of a child at the age of maturity - although a child becomes responsible after reaching maturity, some children in their early years drink from the breast of guidance. Surely these children are manifestations of divine grace and bounty.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Therefore, according to divine commandments, every child must learn reading and writing and acquire necessary and beneficial sciences, as well as learning a craft or trade. These matters require the utmost effort; negligence and laxity in this regard are not permissible.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: These will become very good, because they will receive Baha'i education. They will be reared beneath the shelter of Baha'u'llah. Therefore, they will be very well educated; they will become fruitful trees; they will become very blessed trees; they will become most delectable trees.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Give great importance to the matter of educating children, for this is the foundation of the Law of God and the cornerstone of the edifice of the Religion of God. If you only knew how much joy results from the matter of children, assuredly all the friends would educate children in this way.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Praise be to God that thou hast a kind father and a mother firm in faith and certitude, who desire thy protection, safety, preservation and defence from every direction, and who seek thy lofty station and exalted rank. I beseech God that they may be assisted to raise thee with divine education.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: He hath two dear sons and hopeth they may receive a goodly education, acquire sciences and arts, and become true Baha'is. However, in Rasht the means of education are lacking. Therefore, exert yourselves and request these two children from Rasht and enroll them in the Tarbiyat School without charge.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The Blessed Perfection Baha'u'llah has stressed in all His Holy Writings, in the Kitab-i-Aqdas, in the Ishraqat, in the Kalimat-i-Firdawsiyyih, in the Lawh-i-Bisharat etc, in brief in all His glorious Revelations, the necessity for a well-directed educational system for boys and girls, rich and poor.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Mothers are the first educators of children. They must nurse their infants from the breast of the religion of God and the law of God, so that the love of God may flow with the milk and depart with the soul. Unless mothers educate their children and establish divine principles, education will not yield complete results.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Your services and labors in this most glorious Cause are well-known and renowned, and the honored Tavangar has written of them in detail. But for this service at the Sacred Threshold, great thanksgiving is necessary and ordained, for the education and training of girls leads to servitude at the threshold of the Lord of Verses.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: So too, the education of girls in all the rules of righteous conduct, that they may grow up with a good character and high standards of behavior. For mothers are the first educators of the child, and every child at the beginning of life is like a fresh and tender branch in his parents' hands. His father and mother can train him in any way they choose.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Nurture the tender saplings of the Abha Paradise with the flowing waters of spirit and fragrance, and through the showers of the bounty of the Lord God grant them growth and development. Strive as much as you can that these children may shine forth like peerless trees in the gardens of the All-Glorious with the utmost delicacy, freshness and sweetness.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Children and descendants who, being of noble lineage, are confirmed in goodly character - that is, who are illumined by the effulgences of the Luminary of the horizons - are counted among good deeds that endure. Otherwise, they are detested, subject to wrath, rejected, and the father is addressed with the words "he is not of thy family; his conduct is unrighteous."

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Thou didst make mention of the son of His Honor Hakim Mirza Ayyub, upon him be My Baha and loving-kindness, that he attendeth school, and thou didst likewise seek permission for thine own children. These ordinances have been revealed in the Kitab-i-Aqdas and other Books, and have been inscribed by the Most Exalted Pen; renewed questioning concerning them is not permitted.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: When a mother observes a praiseworthy action from a child, she should praise and commend it and gladden the child's heart. If the slightest useless action occurs, she should counsel the child and rebuke them, employing reasonable means including mild verbal correction if necessary. But hitting and beating is never permitted, for it completely corrupts children's character.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Regarding the schools about which you wrote, certainly give the utmost importance to the Tarbiyat School. The Hands of the Cause must exert such effort in developing this school that it becomes adorned with the finest excellence - in its organization, furnishing, decoration, instruction and education. God willing, may it become a school that shines like a candle throughout all of Iran.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: May your parents educate you spiritually and give you thorough moral training. May you develop so that each one of you shall become imbued with all the virtues of the human world. May you advance in all material and spiritual degrees. May you become learned in sciences, acquire the arts and crafts, prove to be useful members of human society and assist the progress of human civilization.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: About what thou hadst written concerning the attraction and arising of Jinab-i-Shaykh Muhammad-'Ali, in truth, should any soul, like his honor and Jinab-i-Aqa Shaykh Haydar, engage in serving and educating the children of the friends, there is no doubt that they will become the recipients of the Blessed Beauty's glance of favor, and this deed will be adorned with acceptance in the Most Holy Court.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Concerning what you wrote about 'Ata'iyyih, upon her be God's peace, and the gratitude you expressed, all was presented at the Holy Threshold. They said: Praise be to God, the favor of the Truth has encompassed and continues to encompass us, her, and all those associated. Now she is engaged in her studies with the utmost joy and delight. We beseech God to aid her with the hosts of words and knowledge.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: From the very beginning the educators instill the love of music in the hearts and minds of the children. In their common schools they are taught in a concrete manner the laws of harmony and motion. They memorize many songs and sing them quite unconsciously. The parents must see to it that their children are taught the best, classical music, such masterpieces that refine the souls and etherealize the aspirations.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: O sapling of the garden of divine unity! Though thou art but a small child, yet in the Abha Kingdom thou art great, for thou hast drunk the milk of bounty from the breast of guidance, and been nurtured in the cradle of favors, and art being raised in the embrace of the love of God. I hope that through the power of the knowledge of God thou wilt attain to maturity and growth, and become a spiritual youth and a merciful young man.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Very good. Nothing can equal them. Examine that method and you will find it matchless. It is my own creation. With a method of that kind, one year's work is equal to five years by other methods. Try it! From the beginning, give the children pencils so that they may write the letters. They will then learn to read at the same time. The way I have pointed out is an exceedingly easy one, and the children will learn their lessons joyously.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The people of the East were very ignorant. Baha'u'llah announced that all people must acquire knowledge, that all children whether in the cities or in the villages must go to school, that it is the duty of all to teach and educate the children. Should the father and mother be unable to educate the children and have not the means therefor, then society must take care of them and educate them so that not one single soul remains in ignorance.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: These children must be given a good training from their earliest childhood. They must be given a systematic training which will further their development, in order that they may receive greater insight, so that their spiritual receptivity be broadened. Beginning in childhood they must receive instruction. They cannot be taught through books. Many elementary sciences must be made clear to them in the nursery; they must learn them in play, in amusement.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: We are establishing an examination assembly where children are being tested in scientific and technical subjects. This is among the gifts of the Blessed Beauty. We hope this will endure. May examination assemblies be established with the utmost order in all countries and cities where the loved ones reside, and in every examination may the Baha'i children demonstrate such prowess as to earn praise from all, nay, receive commendation from the Concourse on High.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Teaching young children is like unto gardening in the divine gardens. Children must be made to grow and develop like seedlings beside the stream of knowledge and knowledge and wisdom, and with the utmost kindness must be nurtured like pearls within the shell of truth and meaning, so that through the bounty of arts and sciences they may grow and develop, becoming fruitful trees bearing sweet fruits of the mysteries of existence and adorning the rose garden and meadow.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Parents must educate their children and nurture them in the sciences and knowledge. If they show neglect in this matter, they shall be held accountable, condemned and rejected before the watchful Lord. This is an unpardonable sin, for they will have left that helpless child to wander in the wilderness of ignorance, making them wretched, afflicted and tormented. Throughout life, that oppressed child will remain captive to ignorance and pride, unlearned and unconscious.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Schools should be opened, not closed. In all civilized countries, every party, nation and religion has schools, and both the government and people of that country provide the utmost assistance. Only in savage lands, like those of the cannibals who in their extreme savagery eat the slain, do they forcefully prevent the spread of education. Closing schools severs the root of humanity, especially the School of the Oneness of Humanity, whose foundation is fellowship, love and unity among all religions.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Utilize every means to make this School a garden of the All-Merciful, from which the lights of learning will cast their beams, and wherein the children, whether Baha'i or other, will be educated to such a degree as to become God's gifts to man, and the pride of the human race. Let them make the greatest progress in the shortest span of time, let them open wide their eyes and uncover the inner realities of all things, become proficient in every art and skill, and learn to comprehend the secrets of all things even as they are

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The life of men must be productive in some results, otherwise his non-existence is better than existence. As I said before this teaching of the children is a service to the Blessed Perfection. The education of the children is one of the most great services. All these children are mine. If they are educated and illuminated, it is as though my own children are so characterized. They will become the servants and the maid-servants of the Cause of God, the gardeners in the Vineyard of [His] Kingdom and the lights of the assemblage of mankind.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Mothers must educate their children thoroughly from an early age, teach them good character, guide them to human virtues, prevent them from engaging in blameworthy actions, and nurture them in the cradle of Baha'i upbringing. This is so that newborn children may drink the milk of the knowledge of God and love of God from the breast, grow and develop, and learn good conduct, nobility of nature, determination and wisdom in affairs, steadfastness in all things, lofty thoughts, love of progress, high aspiration, chastity and purity. Then they will succeed in whatever they undertake.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: We must be guided entirely by the intelligence and development of the child, as to how soon we should begin to teach it. Many a child of ten is sufficiently developed and advanced to receive some teaching, and some are ready for it at the age of eight or nine. The great thing that is necessary to teach children is to be characterized with the attributes of God, and to be good. Their hearts and minds must be prepared to receive truth as soon as they are old enough to be taught anything--but children should not be taught facts and details which they may not speak of openly to their fellows and companions.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The first educator of the child is the mother, for the child is like unto a fresh and verdant sapling that is at the beginning of its growth, thou shouldst direct it through education. If thou teaches them heavenly virtues, they will grow straight and balanced. It is clear and evident that the mother is the first educator and the establisher of the upright conduct of her child, therefore, do thou know O thou kind mothers, that in the sight of the Omnipotent One, educating children with Divine virtues is among the greatest of all worships that can be rendered and a greater recompense can not be imagined.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Through education the ignorant become learned, the cowardly become courageous, the crooked branch becomes straight, the acrid and bitter fruit of the mountains and woods becomes sweet and succulent, and the five-petaled flower puts forth a hundred petals. Through education barbarous nations become civilized and even animals take on human-like manners. Education must be accorded the greatest importance, for just as diseases are highly communicable in the world of bodies, so is character highly communicable in the realm of hearts and spirits. The differences caused by education are enormous and exert a major influence.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Regarding the girls' school, you wrote that adequate steps have been taken for its establishment and organization, and that through the efforts of true friends a sum has been collected in the gathering, and that the Illustrator of the Merciful has presented the school supplies. As to the letter of the Minister of Education written to the school principal, the occurrence of this matter should cause increased effort and diligence by the members and teachers of the Tarbiyat School, until it reaches such a state that every wise and knowledgeable person, whether stranger or friend, would desire their children to enter that school.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Your child will have extraordinary capacity. It will be a friend of God. Rest assured your child will be assisted by the divine concourse and through this assistance it will exhibit a universal consciousness -- for this cause encompasses the west and the east and children born under these conditions in this day will have the advantages of the universal illumination. Today some children are called prodigies, but the inheritors of this cause will attain to a degree that the others, even though educated in the best schools and with every advantage, know nothing of. Children blessed in this way before they are born are of the new race.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The school for Baha'i children, these flowers of the garden of inner meanings, is most important. Praise be to God that the friends in Hamadan have succeeded in establishing it. Now the teachers must show forth remarkable effort. As for the youth among the friends, they are saplings in the divine garden. They must certainly strive in their study of teaching, so that they may acquire proficiency in establishing divine proofs and evidences, demonstrating the existence of God and His consummate wisdom, proving divine unity, bringing sufficient and satisfying proof for the reality of revelation, and establishing the truth of all the Prophets and Messengers.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Those children who, sheltered by the Blessed Tree, have set foot upon the world, those who are cradled in the Faith and are nurtured at the breast of grace -- such must from the beginning receive spiritual training directly from their mothers. That is, the mother must continually call God to mind and make mention of Him, and tell of His greatness, and instill the fear of Him in the child, and rear the child gently, in the way of tenderness, and in extreme cleanliness. And when the child hath reached the age where he can make distinctions, let him be placed in a Baha'i school, in which at the beginning the Holy Texts are recited and religious concepts are taught. At this school the child is to study reading and writing as well as some fundamentals of the various branches of knowledge, such as can be learned by children.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: In the days of Lycurgus they educated their children according to a special law and order. First, they did not give permission for marriage except to healthy boys and girls. And women would engage in difficult work from the beginning of pregnancy so that the child would be nourished with hardship even in the womb. After birth they would wash it with cold water, and if the mother became ill at that time they would give another's milk to the child. They did not protect them from cold, and from age three they would accustom them to much walking. From age eight they would have them spend half the day studying sciences and half the day in games that strengthened their bodies. And they would arrange strengthening foods for them until at age twenty they would possess strong constitutions and be skilled in sciences and arts. This type of education was special to the children of nobles and notables. Certainly the more children are raised with difficulty and hardship from the beginning of life, and the less they are protected from cold and heat, the better.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: Our hearts must be like the hearts of the children which are without any deceit or dust. The susceptibilities of the children rule over their wills. If the children do not love some one they do not approach him. Of double-dealing they know nothing. They are not hypocritical. Their outward and inward are one. The children must be well educated. These children are like unto the tender plants. If the plant is trained straight by the skilful gardener it will become straight and if it is trained crookedly it will become crooked. From babyhood, the Love of God must be deposited in their hearts. They will, then, be well educated, they will become illumined, they will be imbued with praiseworthy qualities. I love the children very much, because they are near to the Kingdom of God.

Subject: education of children; moral education
Quotation: The great educator of man is woman, for it is the mother who is the first teacher. If the mother be deficient in her attainments, if the teacher be illiterate, how can the pupil be perfect? Therefore the teacher must be well qualified that the pupil may be equally qualified. In the world of humanity the most productive and useful member, after all, is woman, for it is woman who educates man, not the reverse. She rears the children; she cares for the home upon which the body politic is founded; she gives birth to mighty leaders.

Subject: educational curricula
Quotation: Schools and universities should be free from religious and racial prejudices. All schools and colleges should have three foundations: First, they should sincerely train souls, discover nature's mysteries and expand knowledge of art, commerce etc. so ignorance passes away and knowledge shines forth. Second, training in morality is necessary. Third, service to humanity should be obligatory.

Subject: educational curricula
Quotation: Teach lessons in spiritual truths and meanings. Train the children in such wise that each one may become proficient in academic and material sciences and divine meanings

Subject: educational curricula
Quotation: the educator must be a physician--that is, he must teach the children, refine their character, impart knowledge and learning, and nurture them with divine qualities. He must be a physician of character, that he may heal the children of the world from spiritual ills and maladies.

Subject: educational curricula
Quotation: Most ideas must be taught them through speech, not by book-learning. One child must question the other concerning those things and the other child must give the answer. In this way they will make great progress. For example, mathematical problems must also be taught in the form of questions and answers. One of the children asks a question and the other must give the answer. Later the children will on their own accord speak with each other concerning these same subjects.

Subject: educational curricula
Quotation: children's schools must be perfectly organized, teaching and learning firmly established, and the refinement and improvement of character properly systematized, so that in early childhood divine foundations may be laid in the reality of children and a godly structure raised. Consider this matter of education, refinement, improvement, encouragement and stimulation as most important, for it is the very foundation of divine teaching. God willing, from these divine schools may arise illumined children endowed with the noblest human perfections, who may become the cause of the enlightenment of Iran and indeed the entire world. Education and refinement after maturity becomes extremely difficult. Experience has shown that despite utmost effort to change even one trait in someone's character, it proves impossible. If today they become somewhat aware, after a few days they forget and return to their habitual state and accustomed ways. Therefore, this firm foundation must be laid in childhood, for while the branch is fresh and tender, it can easily be made straight and upright.... The teachings for children's schools are extensive, and there is no time now to elaborate, so a brief outline is provided: First, training in manners and character, refinement of qualities, encouragement to acquire perfections, urging adherence to the religion of God and firmness in God's law, complete obedience and submission to just government, truthfulness and trustworthiness toward the present throne, benevolence toward all humanity, kindness to all peoples, learning beneficial arts and foreign languages, good conduct, persistence in offering prayers for the good of kings and subjects, and avoiding the reading of books of materialistic sects and naturalistic peoples, as well as love stories and romantic compositions. The essence of all lessons is confined to the acquisition of human perfections. These are the teachings and arrangements for schools that are briefly recorded here.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Therefore, strive thou to become confirmed and assisted.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: He has called them to striving and seeking that He might bestow upon them that which they desire.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Let him cultivate manners and morals for the betterment of souls; indeed he must strive for years.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Man must seek with his soul and strive with his body and strength and tread the path of the free ones

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Strive that thou mayest be set ablaze by its effulgence and attain complete attraction through its revelation.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Man's duty is to persevere and struggle, and to hope for God's help. Not for him to sit idly by, proud and unconcerned.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: When man discovers the Path of the Heavenly Kingdom, he must strive day and night to develop along the line of spiritual Realities.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: One's efforts should be focussed on the object of one's quest. Many people labored for years to explore the North Pole but Admiral Peary reached it.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: But one must show forth perseverance and self-devotion and consecrate his thoughts, until the tree of hope may give fruit and produce consequences.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Man must rise up with complete effort and striving in every matter so that he may fulfill its conditions and reach the highest degree of perfection.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty often remarked: 'There are four qualities which I love to see manifested in people: fourth, the ability to carry a task, once begun, through to its end.'

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: A person must be rapid in motion and not slow and tortoise-like. When a soul is severed and quick in attending to all his duties, his station is great in the Kingdom of Abha.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Let them not seek rest even for a single moment nor procrastinate for a second. Let them feed the flame of search through their midnight hours and with the sunrise let their faces shine with radiance.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: Striving meaneth this, that ye should live and move according to the divine counsels and admonitions and be filled with zeal and fervour, that ye should seek no rest and be engaged at all times in service.

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: In acquiring the attributes and characteristics of spiritual ones, show forth a manly resolve, that thou mayest attain to the station where "I shall make all my remembrances and prayers but a single prayer, and my condition in Thy service eternal."

Subject: effort; striving
Quotation: How long shall we maintain silence and muteness? How long shall we remain quiet and forgotten? The bright candle - the moths behind the veil are withered and distressed. It is time to surge like the ocean and soar to the Pleiades. If we seek to ascend to the highest horizon we must spread our wings, and if we wish to dive into the ocean's depths we must learn to swim.

Subject: elections
Quotation: the auxiliaries must also be by election of the community, meaning those who receive the majority of votes after the elected members should, with the knowledge of the Spiritual Assembly, be designated as auxiliaries

Subject: elections
Quotation: In the election of the members of the House of Spirituality no political tactics should enter. They must be free from self nor anxious to further their own personal ambitions. The people must be free and untrammelled to choose whomsoever they want.

Subject: elections
Quotation: In a city where the friends of God are few in number, every twenty, thirty, forty or fifty people, depending on whether there are fewer or more friends, should elect one person. These elected individuals are representatives of all and by proxy from all souls should elect the Spiritual Assembly.

Subject: elections
Quotation: It is evident that it is better if the people elect the noble ones among them, and then these elect the president of the republic. That is to say, the president should be the elect of the elect, because the public in general are not as well informed as they should be in regard to political affairs.

Subject: elections
Quotation: Then they should observe which person received the majority of votes from these fifty - that person is the elected one. Those elected should then choose the members of the Spiritual Assembly. Observe how in the West, what great assemblies are elected that are of utmost importance - no clamor, no outcry, no discord, no dispute. Yet now in the election of one Spiritual Assembly, the loved ones of God show such discord, and one or two persons become the cause of such differences.

Subject: elections
Quotation: First, that the election, in the presence of discord, will not take place as it should, and second, it will become a cause of embarrassment for the divine friends before other governments, nations and parties of Iran. However, the election of the friends is good if it takes place in a state of calm and dignity, without creating commotion. Observe how the Parsees conduct their elections - no clamor, no tumult, no noise, no outcry - in perfect peace and composure. If it is done in this manner it is acceptable; otherwise it will cause the attack of other groups and result in calumny, slander, hatred and enmity of the thoughtless ones.

Quotation: the atom is indestructible and subject to coursing and journeyings throughout interminable space

Subject: elementary matter cannot be annihilated
Quotation: The world of elements cannot be annihilated, because pure existence cannot be annihilated; and what we observe are but transformative modifications in the composition of the essence. Complete annihilation cannot take place.

Subject: emanation vs. manifestation
Quotation: Many people think that creation is a manifestation of God, that the divine reality like unto the embryo in a seed, has come forth out of the seed and become a trunk, branches, leaves, flowers. The prophets teach differently. Creation is an emanation from the creator. A tree never becomes a creature: it never acquires sight nor smell; yet both are creations of God - creations in emanation.

Subject: emanation vs. manifestation
Quotation: You had inquired about creation. The mystics believe that the realities of things have appeared from the Truth, and in this regard they give the example and similitude of the seed and tree, saying that the tree is the manifestation of the seed - that single reality which is the seed has appeared in these branches, leaves, blossoms and fruit, thus all are expressions of it. But the people of truth maintain that the appearance of the realities of things from the Truth is through emanation, not manifestation, just as the ray emanates from luminous bodies - all are from Him but are not Him. The luminous rays, infinite bounties, and spiritual impressions and reflections emanated from the Sun of Truth; it is not that they were the manifestation of the Sun of Truth. The difference lies in this point.

Subject: empty learning; false spirituality
Quotation: Therefore if he worships the 'cognition' of his mind as 'God,' he is not worshipping God, he is worshipping the product of his imagination. Then would it not be better to worship 'himself' because he will considered the 'creator' of that thought of God and as such he is greater and more substantial. Thus doth God explain every matter in a clear Book.

Quotation: Then he quoted several of their metaphysical, hair-splitting axioms over each one of which they wrangle and dispute several months in their colleges. Another time a theological poet wrote a book after several years of hardships and privations and took it to a learned man to be read and corrected. He read the book and found out that its contents are very much like the cobwebs of a spider or the phantasmal imaginations of a sickly brain. Therefore he marked the first and the last page; thus conveying the idea that the book is not worth correcting.

Subject: empty learning; false spirituality

For example, Mulla Sadra's ten intellects were derived from the idol-worshipping Greek philosophers. From the first day of Mulla Sadra until this day, what result hath been achieved? Man must strive in matters that give him life. What [use] are matters that cause lethargy and lifelessness?

Whatever thing is deprived of this station is recorded before God as among the most worthless of things. How many souls who day and night, in their own imagination, were occupied with the remembrance of the Lord of all names and were speaking the highest stations of vain mystical utterances, while the Truth was sanctified and exempt from all such souls.

These words changed the affection of the lovers of the Muhammadan Beauty into swords and spears, into injury and enmity. Quotation: It is recorded in the books that one day Abu-Jahl so tightly gripped the throat of His Holiness in the House of Ka'bih that He was near to yielding up His spirit. At that moment Hamzih, the uncle of His Holiness, was returning from a hunt with bow in hand. He rushed upon Abu-Jahl and saved His Holiness from the torment of that wretched one. Then Abu-Jahl said, Have you too become a follower of this person? Until that time Hamzih was not a believer, but his sense of honor was aroused and he replied, Yes, I too have become His follower. This very act of protection caused him to be blessed with the light of faith.

Subject: equality of men and women
Quotation: It must be admitted that in the past woman has not had the same educational opportunities that man has received, but when she is given equal advantages undoubtedly she will become his peer in knowledge and attainments. Brain power is not dependent upon the size of the skull or upon its contents, but upon the character of the convolutions of the brain. The brilliancy of electric light is not dependent upon the lamp, but upon the character of the electric energy.

Subject: equality of men and women
Quotation: In the world of existence there is nothing so important as the investigation of reality, for the illumination of mankind is dependent upon the Sun of Reality. People are divided into two classes concerning this question. Some believe that man is the greater and preferable member of the body politic, that he is created with certain superior virtues, and that woman, however great may be her attainment, can never reach man's level, because she is not endowed with equal faculties. At present the majority is of this class. The other class, now representing the minority, but which ere long may become the majority, is of the opinion that perfect equality already exists.

Quotation: Day and night thou must strive so that the woman world may be adorned with complete culture and refinement, making extraordinary progress in the world of morality and be fully established in the realm of sciences and arts.
