Quotation: Man has free will in matters related to improving qualities and refining character, which lead to ascent to sublime and transcendent stations...However, in universal matters and the law of power, humans cannot interfere and have no choice. For example, one cannot say "Why have I grown old?" and is not able to live forever and never die. In such matters, one is certainly compelled.

Subject: free will and predestination; fate
Quotation: This is one of the most difficult questions... The general opinion is that whatever proceeds from man springs from his own will and has nothing to do with God. Whatever man does is created by man himself and for this reason. This is the opinion of the philosophers. The philosophers of religion on the other hand, say thus: "it is not so. Man is powerless. Of himself, he can do nothing. All is from God."

Subject: free will and predestination; fate
Quotation: The Occidentals see in their Christian God primarily the loving Father of all the children of God. The Muslim honours in the Lord God primarily the Potter Who creates from His clay vessels of honour or dishonour according to His wish. Thus the Islamic Teachings correspond, in accordance with their name, to the total submission of every human being to the inscrutable Will of God. It is true that the Prophet Muhammad taught the foreknowledge of God, but nowhere in the Qur'an has this Messenger of God established the immutable law of absolute predestination; on the contrary, the Prophet knew the narrow limits of human free will. Has not Muhammad, blessed be His words, emphasized that man can possess himself of the grace offered him by God, or can let it escape him? The Lord God can show the spring to a thirsty one, nay can lead him to it, but what if his eyes are bound? If he pushes away the hand that offers him the cup of water, spills the water in his folly?... The serious question arises: 'Has the Lord God foreseen that this human being will not let himself be saved, or has He, for reasons inscrutable to us, let him be ensnared from the begin-ning in folly and delusion?' But as the Lord God is not only the Almighty, but also the All-Merciful - for true might and power are always paired with kind-ness and goodness - and is at the same time the Just and the Avenger, we lowly creatures have to bow to His inscrutable decree and believe that the Potter in His absolute wisdom and goodness, in His justice and truth, creates, changes and completes everything to the best for the individual and for the whole -even where our own understanding and comprehension largely fail. Forget not, O my guest, that the Christian religion expresses itself more in belief than in actions, but Islam concerns itself more with deeds than with belief.

Subject: free will and predestination; fate
Quotation: What is meant by His exalted word decree is the fourth rank of the act wherein no alteration occurs afterwards...When you understand the ruling of Decree in the fourth rank, you will be certain that no good or evil exists in contingent being except through God's Decree and Measure and the five ranks, and all that exists only through the servant's choice. For choice accompanies the existence of the thing, and the manifestations of the act are the existences of things which exist through God, glorified be He.

Subject: free will and predestination; fate
Quotation: And concerning that which thou hast mentioned regarding free will - how can it not be evident to one who gazeth with the eye of insight and witnesseth with the glance of truth? Consider thyself: thou performest an action of thine own free will, yet once done thou canst not reverse it. If thou shouldst act otherwise, would not the same hold true? The celestial spheres move by God's leave according to their own volition, even as He hath decreed man's lifespan which he cannot alter. This returneth to the station of free will, for without knowledge of the reality of the matter, the servant cannot comprehend the truth of the cause.

Subject: free will and predestination; fate
Quotation: As is known among the servants, two terms have been ordained for all things - the first contingent, and the second irrevocable. Yet what they have mentioned regarding these two stations is neither nourishing nor profitable, for they are deprived of the foundation of divine knowledge and the consummate wisdom of the Eternal, save whom thy Lord willeth. Although in one station all that transpires is and shall be irrevocable, and the very act of its execution is proof of its inevitability, yet its mention still abides in the heaven of divine Will, until such time as it descends from the heaven of Will to the kingdom of utterance and is inscribed by the Pen of Destiny.

Subject: free will and predestination; fate
Quotation: This is a station wherein the feet of the mystics have slipped and the steps of the eloquent have faltered, even as one of the holy ones, when questioned about this most manifest station and this greatest of vistas, replied that it was a surging ocean not to be approached, and in another instance a lightless night not to be traversed. He further said that destiny is a mystery of God's mysteries and a treasure of His treasures, sealed with God's seal, folded within God's knowledge.

Subject: freedom of thought and action
Quotation: The point is that a person is free - if they wish they can dedicate their life to the Kingdom of God, or they can serve the Cause of God while engaged in other affairs.

Subject: freedom of thought and action
Quotation: We desire neither absolute despotism, nor unbounded liberty. If in Iran they grant absolute liberty with no opposition against the Faith, it would not be of benefit to us. Nay, freedom makes people lazy. We wish neither the pogroms, the imprisonment, the beatings of the past, nor the complete freedom given in other countries.

Subject: freedom of thought and action
Quotation: Its citizens are enjoying the greatest amount of political and civic freedom. No one is harassed by secret fears, and expresses his thoughts freely and with no compunction. The sphere of the minds is made radiant with dazzling Ideals and the circle for the discussion of progressive and advanced problems of the age as wide as heaven.

Subject: freedom of thought and action
Quotation: There are three types of freedom. The first is divine freedom, which is one of the inherent attributes of the Creator for He is unconstrained in His will, and no one can force Him to change His decree in any matter whatsoever... The second is the political freedom of Europeans, which leaves the individual free to do whatsoever he desires as long as his action does not harm his neighbour. This is natural freedom, and its greatest expression is seen in the animal world. Observe these birds and notice with what freedom they live. However much man may try, he can never be as free as an animal, because the existence of order acts as an impediment to freedom.... The third freedom is that which is born of obedience to the laws and ordinances of the Almighty. This is the freedom of the human world, where man severs his affections from all things. When he does so, he becomes immune to all hardship and sorrow. Wealth or material power will not deflect him from moderation and fairness, neither will poverty or need inhibit him from showing forth happiness and tranquillity. The more the conscience of man develops, the more will his heart be free and his soul attain unto happiness. In the religion of God, there is freedom of thought because God, alone, controls the human conscience, but this freedom should not go beyond courtesy. In the religion of God, there is no freedom of action outside the law of God. Man may not transgress this law, even though no harm is inflicted on one's neighbour. This is because the purpose of Divine law is the education of all -- others as well as oneself -- and, in the sight of God, the harm done to one individual or to his neighbour is the same and is reprehensible in both cases. Hearts must possess the fear of God. Man should endeavour to avoid that which is abhorrent unto God. Therefore, the freedom that the laws of Europe offer to the individual does not exist in the law of God. Freedom of thought should not transgress the bounds of courtesy, and actions, likewise, should be governed by the fear of God and the desire to seek His good pleasure.

Subject: future of Haifa; of the Holy Land
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/future of Haifa; of the Holy Land.txt
Quotation: God willing, a day will come when that region and land will become a divine rose garden and the Most Glorious Kingdom will encompass it. This is the desire of the sincere ones and this is the hope of the unitarians.

Subject: future of Haifa; of the Holy Land
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/future of Haifa; of the Holy Land.txt
Quotation: As for the return of Israel once again to Jerusalem, this is universal and not confined to the divine friends alone. However, after their gathering, they shall ultimately be attracted to the Dawn of Reality and enter beneath the shadow of the Glorious Lord.

Subject: future of Haifa; of the Holy Land
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/future of Haifa; of the Holy Land.txt
Quotation: I now behold the whole of this mountain basking in brilliant lights and the Haifa harbor as the anchor point of thousands of steam ships...Likewise verily I see and behold the future effulgence of hospitals, schools and sanatoriums and the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar established on this mountain.

Subject: future of Haifa; of the Holy Land
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/future of Haifa; of the Holy Land.txt
Quotation: Blessed art thou, O Land of Syria! The Morn of Manifestation hath breathed within thee, and thereby hath the fragrance of God been diffused throughout all else. In this moment the cry of Zion hath been raised and Mount Carmel rejoiceth at the sea of attainment. O Carmel! Thou didst taste the poison of separation through ages and centuries; now the honey of reunion hath come unto thee, inasmuch as the Countenance of the Ancient of Days hath turned toward thee from this direction which was recorded in the Mother Book by the Pen of the All-Merciful.

Subject: future of Haifa; of the Holy Land
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/future of Haifa; of the Holy Land.txt
Quotation: The city of Haifa and the city of Akka will become one city due to extensive development, and the plain between these two cities will be entirely transformed into gardens, groves, and magnificent buildings. A wide, orderly, level, and adorned road, in the utmost elegance, delicacy, and beauty, will be extended from Mount Carmel to the sea, and tall, verdant trees will cast shadows and add to the pleasantness and freshness of the air. Leaders and kings of various peoples will come in groups to visit the Holy Shrine and the Most Exalted Shrine. Akka and Haifa will become a great center of magnificent enterprises and the dawning-place of the lights of sciences and arts.

Subject: generosity [kirama]
Quotation: Adorn your hands with generosity

Subject: generosity [kirama]
Quotation: This esteemed person made such an undertaking and made such a contribution...such an illustrious person would make such a sacrifice

Subject: generosity [kirama]
Quotation: Even in prison thou thinkest of giving. Those who are free should strive to give to the imprisoned, yet this shows to what degree the friends of God are immersed in the sea of detachment and devoted to sacrificing their wealth and lives.

Subject: generosity [kirama]
Quotation: By the life of God! If someone gives even one dinar to a deserving soul for the sake of God, or shows love to another, their mention will never be erased from the ledger of the world. This is a seed that will forever be adorned with the ornament of verdancy. This is a fruit that will forever be visible on the Tree of deeds.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: Deeds are the mirror of the doer, and deeds are a mirror for the doer. We beseech and implore the Exalted Truth to sanctify the people of the Crimson Ark from whatsoever diminisheth consciousness and robbeth reason.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: Belief is proven by actions following the Commands of God. Only those who prove their faith by their lives are worthy to be called the followers of Christ.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: act in accordance with what hath been commanded... Every deed that appeareth today for the sake of God is recorded as the lord of deeds in His presence

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: Know thou its worth and act in a manner befitting it. Blessed is he who acts, and woe unto the heedless

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: The pictures which are in the ideal world are eternal. Man can paint those ideal pictures upon the tablet of existence with the brush of deeds.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: O servants! The triumph of this Cause hath depended, and will continue to depend, upon the appearance of holy souls, upon the showing forth of goodly deeds, and the revelation of words of consummate wisdom.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: "The good deeds of man are like unto the sweet fragrances emanated from the musk. They perfume the nostrils of everyone more especially the doer. As his deeds have been performed with no reference to the applause and commendation of men he enjoys them more than any one else."

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: God hath distinguished between truth and falsehood. Whoso obeyeth God in what He hath revealed in the Furqan is among the people of faith and the companions of knowledge before our Lord, the Most Merciful. Set aside mere words. Adorn yourselves with goodly deeds and spiritual, luminous character.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: For instance, it is possible that a man performs a good deed with a view to personal interest; such a good deed done is not separated from hypocrisy and insincerity. But when a man cherishes a good intention, it is impossible that it be prompted by any prejudice or be intended for anything but good.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: Be a Baha'i in reality and not in word. Be detached, be spiritual, love thy fellowmen with a motiveless love. Let thy mind be a palace of universal ideals, and thy heart the casket of the jewels of sympathy and affection. Give and not take. Be generous in thought, in act and in feeling. Let thy faith and action correspond with each other.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: One accepted deed today is equivalent to a hundred thousand deeds - nay, I seek God's forgiveness for this limitation. A deed appeared and was adorned with the ornament of acceptance in such wise that from the Dayspring of the utterance of the All-Merciful there appeared that whose fragrance shall never cease throughout the kingdoms of earth and heaven.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: Today the deeds of the friends of the Self-Sufficing, the Exalted, distinguish them from the people of the earth. O My loved ones! Hold fast unto sanctity and detachment. Your deeds must be so holy and pure that they will be even as the sun amidst the works of creation. A pure deed is itself a herald - its fragrance guideth men to the most exalted horizon and directeth them thither.

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: The wise ones who have drunk from the wine of inner meanings have affirmed the embodiment of deeds. How excellent are the words of Him Who said! The All-Glorious One declares, and the Dayspring of the Revelation of the All-Merciful has stated: "People shall be rewarded according to their deeds - good for good, and evil for evil." Thus it becomes evident that deeds shall endure, and every attribute shall have existence, so that by the very attribute and deed itself shall they be recompensed. Therefore, every attribute and every deed that appears from any doer has a form in every world and manifests itself therein

Subject: goodly deeds; actions
Quotation: We enjoin upon all virtuous and pure deeds, and praiseworthy and pleasing character. Blessed is the one who aids the Cause through deeds and character - such assistance transcends all other forms of aid, and such deeds surpass all others.

Subject: grammar and orthography
Quotation: As to the personal pronouns referable to His Holiness Christ, His Holiness Buddha, His Holiness Muhammad, His Holiness the Bab and the Blessed Beauty - and all of the Prophets of God - must without exception be capitalized for this is indicative of their Greatness. There is no doubt that these Souls were all Great; this is not a proof of divinity.

Subject: grammar and orthography
Quotation: It hath been ordained in the Gate of Alif that ye shall create a new script for the Bayan and all your writings after sixty-six years have passed if ye are able, and if not then after two hundred and two years if what is renewed is better than the first, that ye may perchance comprehend the conditions of the hereafter, and ye shall embellish all your writings from the first of what ye learn to the last of what ye comprehend.

Subject: grammar and orthography
Quotation: Thou didst ask concerning grammar. By my life, in my youth I paid no heed to the schools’ canons. Rather, the rule is that which ʿAlí—exalted be His remembrance—decreed in another place: every subject (fāʿil) is in the nominative, by reason of the appearance therein of the Name of God, al-Qābiḍ (the Withholder); every object (mafʿūl) is in the accusative, by reason of the appearance therein of the Name of God, al-Muḥyī (the Quickener); and every genitive (muḍāf ilayh) is in the genitive case, by reason of the appearance therein of the Name of God, al-Ḥayy (the Living), which is the station of the air, by which things are bound together. The root of the verb is the manifestation of the Hidden Name: a created quiescent thing unknown by quiescence; therefore the ordinances of the three disclosures run not upon it. All rules of grammar branch from the decree of these theophanies, for him who knoweth God’s ordinance in the kingdom of the Names and Attributes.

Subject: grammar and orthography
Quotation: The Bab -- may my spirit be sacrificed for Him -- entirely abrogated the rules of language and freed the Arabic tongue. Thus, all the writings of His Holiness -- may my spirit be sacrificed for the dust of His footsteps -- demolished the edifice of Arabic grammar. The Ancient Beauty -- may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones -- likewise, in His early writings, opposed the vain imaginings of grammatical rules. However, in the Most Great Prison, in consideration of certain scholars' objections, the verses and writings were revealed in accordance with the people's rules. Nevertheless, on certain occasions, merely to prevent the Arabic language from becoming fettered again in chains and bonds, words were revealed that broke the people's rules.

Subject: grammar and orthography
Quotation: And then, I have answered thy question concerning the ruling of the origins of letters and their points of articulation. Bear thou witness with certitude that the origin of the science of recitation was taken from him whose nature remained unchanged, for when God created the letters, He created their places and points of articulation in the servant such that he needeth not to learn from any among men. Just as thou seest with thine eyes, so do the letters emerge from their points of articulation which God created in thee, without similitude or comparison. Yea, if thou art certain of the change in thy nature, it is incumbent upon thee to learn from those who possess this knowledge. But beware, beware of the people of innovation whose forms change during recitation, for that is pure sin. The Hijazi recitation and eloquence in true melody is that thy countenance should not change during recitation. Thus hath God created thee, and men have no power to change God's creation.

Subject: grammar and orthography
Quotation: The learned ones say that if it is conditional, then if ye but knew is not permissible. Act according to what We previously commanded and write accordingly. In some instances both forms are permissible, though one is preferred. For example, "associate with religions" is preferable to "associate with the religions". Regarding amma and mimma, act in accordance with the Book of God, that is, the Quran, though both forms have flowed from the Pen.

Subject: grammatical and other discrepancies in the Sacred Writings
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/grammatical and other discrepancies in the Sacred Writings.txt
Quotation: O Zayn, the delay in answering what you asked about the verses has been for the preservation of change, for in the early days there was absolutely no consideration of the people's rules at the time of revelation, while in these days it is observed out of wisdom. Therefore, if a Tablet from before is read in the presence of the Face, it descends in some stations differently than what was revealed before. This refers to the outward expression, but in reality whatever was revealed was and will be correct.... Knowledge is in His grasp; He turns it how He wishes. For example, in some places a verse that according to outward rules should be in the nominative or genitive case is revealed in the accusative case. In this instance, either "kana" is implied, or similar accusative particles and their positions. And if somewhere it is revealed in the genitive while according to common practice it should not be, in this case the genitive particle or the possessive construct that causes the genitive is omitted. Apply this rule universally. Likewise, in some instances it relates to the style of verses - We do not wish to mention rhyme in this station. Similarly, according to the leaders of grammar, an intransitive verb appears in transitive form in three ways: through repetition, with "ba", and with "hamza". This is respected among the people, but in divine knowledge, by contextual evidence, an intransitive verb becomes transitive and a transitive verb becomes intransitive. Blessed are those who know, and blessed is he who is certain that all sciences are in the grasp of his Lord's power, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. Similarly, a transitive verb, for example like "rafa'a" is revealed as "arfa'a", and examples of this existed in heavenly books before. This is for emphasis - there is no harm in it. O Zayn of the near ones, the Manifest Beauty is afflicted between two parties. If creation were to become aware in what state the scratching of the Most Exalted Pen is raised, and in what tribulation the Tongue of Grandeur speaks, all would cast off the garment of existence and seek the adornment of non-existence.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: This is the century of the All Merciful! This is the age of spirituality! Every atom of existence is in ecstasy and all things surge with joy and life. The heat of the Sun of Truth has so penetrated the world that the realities of all things are alive with growth and astir with evolution.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: The Cause of Baha'u'llah is incomparable to any other cause; because it is the Collective Center of this age.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Seize, O friends, the chance which this Day offereth you, and deprive not yourselves of the liberal effusions of His grace.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: The Dispensation of the Blessed Beauty is mighty. Ages and cycles must pass ere such a supreme Manifestation should again appear.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: This is a Day wherein if someone misses performing a deed, they will not be able to make up for it even in countless ages to come.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Thou doth behold how the Light of Truth hath illumined both the East and the West! The Candle of Iran hath enlightened every lands.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Soon it will be observed that the native government of the Blessed Beauty will become the most respected government in all the earth.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: The blessed utterance concerned the greatness of the Cause of God, that when it surges, it will submerge all paths and itself ascend.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: This is the Day of God, wherein naught is seen save Him and His signs. This is the Day which past ages and centuries can never rival.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: They were heedless of the power and ascendancy of God's Cause... Observe how the Word of God is confirmed and the Cause of God victorious

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Should anyone reflect upon this very verse, he would become aware of the greatness of the Cause and the majesty of the station of the Day of God.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Although the importance of this divine institution is not so apparent at present, in the future it will become as clear and manifest as the sun.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: the text describes how even opponents acknowledge the greatness of the Cause, and how this dispensation surpasses all previous ages in its effects

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty will be seated upon the throne of celestial sovereignty and the might and majesty of the Cause of God will encompass all regions.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: O Tahir! By the life of God, all days bow down in humility before this day, and all centuries and ages prostrate themselves before this century and age.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: The darkest night hath been illumined as the dawn breathed forth from the horizon of eternity...All things have been stirred by the breezes of revelation

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: The divine banner was raised high and the standards of that blameworthy people were cast down... And the ultimate victory belongs to the God-fearing ones.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: This is the century of lights and the age of mysteries. All created things are astir and in motion, and every existing thing is adorned with its finest ornament.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Today the divine call is raised high. Today the Dayspring of Light is in its dawning and manifestation, and likewise the Source of Fire is in motion and emergence.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Verily, by Truth, every seed cast in this great and magnificent century will be cultivated by God and produce plants through the abundance of the clouds of His mercy

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Centuries, nay ages, must pass away ere the Day-Star of Truth shineth again in its mid-summer splendor, or appeareth once more in the radiance of its vernal glory...

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: This is the time of happiness; it is the day of cheerfulness and exhilaration. For, praise to God, all the doors are opened through the bounty of the Glorious Beauty.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Consider how powerful is the cause of God! He who pronounces one word of truth now, that word will continue to wave and vibrate without end and will never be annihilated.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Know thou the worth of these divine days and their station, and strive that perchance thou mayest be assisted to do what God loveth and attain unto that which He desireth.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: Obviously the Western friends will witness grave tests, but the tests of the Persian friends were a different thing. I await the emergence of those few; they will soon appear.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
Quotation: A Cause has appeared that has had and has no likeness or parallel...Great indeed is this Day - all the pens of the world are powerless to describe and incapable of reckoning it.

Subject: greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/greatness and influence of the Cause; of this Day.txt
