Why all this commotion?' you would find that they know nothing at all of their origin or their end, and that they look for no other good except eating and sleeping and assiduously pandering to their sensual desires.

Subject: materialism; material vs. spiritual civilization
Quotation: In New York I find the people more endowed with spiritual susceptibilities. They are not mere captives of nature's control; they are rising out of the bonds and burden of captivity. Paris is most beautiful in outward appearance. The evidences of material civilization there are very great, but the spiritual civilization is far behind. I found the people of that city submerged and drowning in a sea of materialism. Their conversations and discussions were limited to natural and physical phenomena, without mention of God.

Subject: meaning; importance of dreams and visions
Quotation: According to the prophets, vision is one of the types of revelation. Especially among the prophets of the Children of Israel, the matter of visions is very significant.

Subject: meaning; importance of dreams and visions
Quotation: Dreams are of three kinds. One is a true vision, which is exactly like the morning light and needs no interpretation. Exactly what is seen occurs in the same way...The second kind is the interpretive dream...Another kind is confused dreams.

Subject: meaning; importance of dreams and visions
Quotation: O brother! When you yourself have experienced dreams and seen therein things that had one name and attribute there, but have another name and attribute here, then likewise affirm this difference of forms in the world after death. Know with certainty that the reality, essence, oneness, form and attributes differ. And if you have not witnessed this station with your own eyes, then turn to the interpretations of the mystics among the interpreters, who have interpreted every deed and word, and explained every thing.

Subject: meaning; importance of dreams and visions
Quotation: Know of a certainty that the dream world is equivalent to the spirit and like unto the sun in its station; nothing hath departed from the body. Nay rather, by its light whatever is in the heavens and the earth may be witnessed. Verily, God hath created the dream in His servants that they may be assured of the existence of the worlds hereafter and the life everlasting. As the life of this world becometh transformed after death, in the same manner regard what is seen in the dream: when thou ariseth nothing more of it is seen, save the effect of its interpretation.

Subject: meaning; importance of dreams and visions
Quotation: The other mode of the spirit's operation and influence is without these physical instruments and organs. Thus in sleep it sees without eyes, hears without ears, speaks without a tongue, and moves without feet--in brief, all these powers are exercised without bodily instrumentality. How often does it happen that the spirit has a dream during sleep whose meaning is precisely realized two years hence! Similarly, how frequently does the spirit solve in the dream state a problem that had proved insoluble in waking hours. In the waking state, the eye sees but a short distance, yet in dreams one who is in the East may behold the West. Awake, one perceives only the present; in sleep, one sees the future.

Subject: meaning; importance of dreams and visions
Quotation: As to the matter of dreams and visions: At times they are a manifestation of divine inspiration, a gateway and path, a sublime paradise of graceful trees and sweet fruits. At other times they are confused dreams, a mirage rather than water, a winding alley, nay rather a ruined house, a narrow path of mountain crags and stones. Sometimes they show a wilderness and the sight of a bird's nest and the course of the shining moon; at times flowing water, and like the hundred-petaled rose in bloom; the song of birds and scenes of flower gardens. Sometimes they involve seeking after companions and receiving guidance from leaders. In any case, diseased imagination presents gold and silver, but not from the bountiful mine. Therefore you must sanctify your thoughts from all these imaginings and content yourself with that which the Lord God has established as an enduring proof. Otherwise no soul will become firm and steadfast through such matters, for the heart will not find assurance. At every moment a doubt will cross the mind, and with every breath a misgiving will arise concerning the divine foundation.

Subject: meaning; importance of dreams and visions
Quotation: As for what thou asked regarding the state of the spirit and its conditions, know with certainty that in sleep, the spirit is like the sun in its position--it does not leave the body, but rather by its light beholds the kingdom of the heavens and earth. Should one be a believer, he beholdeth all things, by God’s decree, according to his station, and there adhereth to him an influence that never leaveth him. But should one be an unbeliever, he beholdeth things as inverted images of unbelief; and unto him likewise—by the requirement of justice—there cleaveth an influence that never departeth from him. God has created sleep in His servants that they might be certain of the worlds of the hereafter and its enduring realm. The life of this world and its pleasures after death are like a dream one sees - when one awakens nothing remains of it except the trace of its interpretation.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: after the year sixty-eight corresponding to the numerical value of "Hin" (a time)

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: There is no God but Him, and verily the Being of the Seven Letters is His servant and His Word. God has chosen for Him names of His Primal Nature equaling the essential numbers of all things, and through them have the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them been filled. Verily, there is no God but Him, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The letters (alphabet) and the numbers (arithmetic) have a mystic correspondence with transcendent reality. The letters and numbers are the elements of the spiritual and material worlds. As words these elements are the source of all things intellectual, as letters they represent the source of matter.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Besides these historied testimonies the word "Music" is Persian. It comes from "Musik" and the word "Musik" comes from the word "Musighar," a sweet singing bird.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The entire prayer is structured around the letters of the Arabic alphabet (Alif, Ba, Ta, etc.) with specific spiritual essences and attributes associated with each letter

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Know that God created in you the luminous and dark letters with fourteen points of articulation. The first is the straight path we hold to, and the second is all other letters.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee, O my God! Destroy every being of alif who believeth not in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest... [Following this pattern through all the letters of the alphabet]

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Therein it was clearly stated that the numerical value of Kull u Shay (all things = 36 indicated the time limit when the Cause of Baha'u'llah would, God forbid, be disbanded or dispersed.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: And regarding what was written about the science of letters and the Hidden, what was revealed was a treatise on the science of the Temple sent down from the heaven of the Lord of Causes specifically for you.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Divinity which is exalted above all things, to punish every being of Alif associated with the Tree of Negation... [continues with systematic prayers invoking the letters Alif, Ba, Jim, etc.]

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Let the temples be written from these or in the manner of the connected temple, for it has the strongest effect therein. And verily from the first descent of the water of His being until the time He spoke the number of Ta and Kaf

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: All infinite letters branch forth from the Ocean of the Primal Point, and unto it do they return and find their end. And whoso knoweth the Point knoweth that whereof the outer letters are composed and that which brancheth forth from them.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The calculation of the word "Bab" is 5 and Baha is 9. If you multiply 9 by 5 you have 45. Now 45 is the Arabic numerical value of the word Adam. Also, 1 plus 2 equals 3; 3 plus 3 equals 6; 6 plus 4 equals 10; 10 plus 5 equals 15; 15 is the number of Eve.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Therefore seek refuge for [him] from the deeds of the people of hypocrisy, then of discord, then what was immersed by that which established the Alif between the two Ba's, then by [it] all letters spoke, then by it filled the heavens and earth from Nun...

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: In any case, I hope to set forth, purely for the sake of God, that which has been permitted in this noble science, for none shall grasp any of His knowledge save as He willeth, and verily He is the Sovereign Who hath encompassed all things with His knowledge.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Establish, O my God, all the Letters in the hearts of men, their spirits, their souls and their bodies. Transform, O my God, all the Letters into those Letters which Thou lovest to mention and permittest to appear before Thee among those who bow down in worship.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: In the school of the family of God this is the circle of manifestation, which is identical to four thousand, which is the Jafr of Ali, peace be upon him, as it is established in the science of Jafr that the book of Ali, peace be upon him, had four thousand at its beginning and four thousand at its end, identical to the circle.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The entire prayer is structured around the letters of the Arabic alphabet (Alif, Ba, Jim, etc.), invoking divine assistance for souls associated with each letter. "I beseech Thee by Thy Divinity which transcendeth all things, that Thou assist every soul with Alif who believeth in Him Whom Thou shalt make manifest on the Day of Resurrection"

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The one addressed is the Letter Kaf, and He Who addressed him is God, the Mighty, the Glorious. He revealed Himself unto him in the Point, and thus attributed to him the station of Oneness. All this is detailed in the degrees of Reality in ten essential ranks, eighteen unchanging ones, and nineteen moving ones in the sphere of cycles and the pole of the circles of regions.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Know thou that for the letter Vav, being the first letter of that verse, there is a direction pure from the six directions which pertain to its simplicity and to the letter of its essence, whereof the people thereof make mention through holy names, glorious manifestations, true revelations, and paradisiacal signs - all of which are recorded beneath its shade and confined within its realm.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: O God! I beseech Thee by Thine Ultimacy, which is exalted above all things, to abase every alif that is attributed to the Tree of Negation, by Thy might before Thyself and before all things. O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Loftiness, which is exalted above all things, to abase every ba that is attributed to the Tree of Negation and whatsoever is related to it, by Thy might before Thyself and before all things. [And continuing through all the letters]

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee, O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy primacy which transcendeth all things, that Thou mayest cause to vanish every essence of alif that is attributed to the tree of negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. O my God! I beseech Thee by Thy sublimity which is manifest above all things, that Thou mayest restore every essence of ba that is attributed to the tree of negation, by Thy power over whatsoever Thou willest. [And continuing through all the letters]

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Should one reflect upon the treasures deposited within the letters and become aware as befitteth their station, in that moment would he testify to the power of God, exalted be His glory, through the reality of existence, the reality of the spirit, the reality of the soul, and the reality of the heart. No more than twenty-eight letters exist in their outward form, yet from the treasury of each hath He made manifest that which those possessed of certain knowledge are powerless to reckon.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: And praise be to God Who brought the existences into being through the embellishment of the mystic Alif, self-subsisting, which was originated through the causation of the Point before it and was brought into being through the essence of the aforementioned Will, in its own rank, through it, by it, unto it. This following the mention of 'Ayn, Lam and Ya - Muhammad - that whoso entereth through him may enter the depths of oneness and whoso departeth from him may depart from the presence of oneness.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Know then that if you were to extract the letters contained within the mysteries of this Alif, as We have previously imparted to you, from its four stations, and write their pronunciations, and thereafter divide them into four divisions, and apply to each division what it requires of ascent, descent, elevation and equivalence, there would be revealed to you mysteries at which minds would be bewildered, and you would discover what you have heard of the comprehensive Jafr, and arrive at the source of all knowledge.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Verily I am God, there is no God but I. I have created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them through My command Be! and it is. And I created the letters and made them the keys to all knowledge from Our presence, for We have power over all things. O all things! Reflect ye, from the mention of the Most High to the lowest atom, that ye all shall witness these things in the twenty-eight letters, even as ye have witnessed all letters within them. Thus shall ye witness all the spirits of the letters within their spirits, for We are cognizant of all things.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: "As for the question regarding the science of letters ('ilm al-huruf): take at the head of every ten the first letter and calculate it by the first element of Fire (nar) around the name of God 'the Constrictor' (al-qabi?); and in the second element of Air (hawa') around the name of God 'the Living' (al-Hayy); and in the third element of Water (ma') around the name of God 'the Revivifier' (al-muHayyi); and in the fourth element of Earth (turab) around the name of God the 'Taker of Life' (al-mumit). Then multiply the ten letters from the first to the fourth and from the third to the second."

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Know that the Letter Joseph corresponds in number to the Qayyumu'l-Asma and refers to the Qa'im of the House of Muhammad, peace be upon Him. Inasmuch as I observed that every morning they would recite "I believe in the Mystery of the Family of Muhammad," etc., I desired that the veil be lifted, that deeds might conform to verbal profession. From the time of the revelation of the Qur'an until the number nineteen was to be manifested - which number must needs appear - were the outward members of Muhammad's Family, each number revolving around one letter of "In the Name of God, the Compassionate,"

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The numerical value of the name of that Temple who reciteth unto you the verses from God is the number of Ra and Ba.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: And when five are added unto it, then it becometh light... And God shall add unto it that five, the number of the Gate, and behold, it shall be light upon light upon light unto light.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The difference between the letter Alif in fire (1) and the letter Waw in light (6) is the numerical value of the Gate (5). Thus does God transform fire into light for those who were prostrating before God their Lord.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Do not forget the tradition "All that is in the Torah, Gospel and Psalms is in the Qur'an, and all that is in the Qur'an is in the Opening Chapter, and all that is in the Opening Chapter is in the Bismillah, and all that is in the Bismillah is in the letter B."

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: The letter Ta of 'talab' (seeking) is in its name, which is evidence that it will attain its goal. Its Alif is the Alif of steadfastness, which stands firm in service, and this indicates your standing firm in service. Its Vav proclaims and says: 'The divine promise is manifest, the Promised One is visible through the name of the All-Loving.'

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Then He created the Letter Sin beneath the Ba and made it the earth of the Throne facing the heaven of the Point, which is itself the heaven of the Throne. Within it resides the reality of transcendence wherein is concealed the Primal Will by which all are created. These are two letters from the letters of the Bismillah which God hath sent down at the beginning of His Book.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: And whatsoever God hath created of anything in the Book and what is therein - He intendeth by the first letter of the first verse and what is therein in the mighty Basmalah and what is therein in the first letter - verily there is no God but I, the Lord of the worlds. Verily all that the Quran containeth is encompassed in the Surih of Praise, and all that it containeth is encompassed in the Basmalah, and all that the Basmalah containeth is encompassed in the letter Ba, and all that is in the Ba is encompassed in the Point, and I am that Point beneath the Ba.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Among the gifts bestowed by the Eternal One upon the Point of the Bayan is the knowledge of all things in a single soul, wherein they behold with the eye of certainty the genesis of all things in the world of letters. This is a perfect proof unto all, like unto verses, and hath been among the treasured mysteries of divine knowledge that until now had not been revealed, being more precious than any other knowledge. Upon this knowledge have all books been revealed and shall be revealed. From this knowledge came the command your God is One God, previously revealed. In brief, nothing existeth outside the twenty-eight letters, and likewise the genesis of all things proceedeth not beyond the meanings of these letters.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: Number nine (9) is the last number and it is the greatest number. Number ten (10) is simply the continuation of the number ( because number 10 is 1 and 100 is 1. Place the units up to 10 and we simply return to the number 1, but they will be ended at 9. One cannot find any number greater than 9 written in one digit, and of all numbers it is the highest. Also, in the tens 90 is the highest, and in the hundreds 900 is the highest. Then see if you can find any number greater than 9 to be written in a digit. All other numbers are simply a repetition. As all digits end in 9, that which comes after 9 is simply a repetition of other digits. So number 9 is the highest, and from it all other numbers are made.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: 9 is the last number and it is the greater number. 10 is simply the continuation of the number 1 because 10 is 1 and 100 is 1. Place the units up to 10 and we simply return to the number 1. The units end at 9. Number 9 is the highest, and from it all other numbers are made.

Subject: meanings of letters and numbers; jafr (gematria)
Quotation: When thou didst inquire about divination (jafr), in truth this is not and hath never been the day for questions, even as the Primal Point, Who gave the people glad tidings of the Lord of the Beginning and the End, forbade all from asking questions in this Most Great Revelation. Some time ago this Most Great Verse was revealed from the Supreme Pen: "This is not the Day of questions. It behooveth every soul, when he heareth the Call from the Kingdom of Creation, to arise and say: 'Here am I, here am I, O God of Names! Here am I, here am I, O Creator of Heaven!'" For these fleeting days were not and are not worthy of such things.... Today the comprehensive book of divination is that Most Exalted Word which hath flowed and will continue to flow from the Supreme Pen. From it can be derived all that lieth concealed within the tabernacle of God's knowledge. Should anyone reflect upon the verses and that which hath been sent down from the heaven of God's Will, he would testify to that which My Pen hath testified at this moment. The divine worlds have been and shall forever be without end. The deeds of the Prophets and Messengers bear witness to this clear pronouncement.

Subject: means of establishment of future civilization
Quotation: "A house is never furnished before the structure is erected. So with the Cause of Baha'o'llah. It must be first built up; afterwards it will be furnished with justice and then it will be called the House of Justice. When this time comes and the universal House of Justice is once established, its commands will be obeyed by all."

Subject: meditation
Quotation: The Prophets and Holy Men always went into the wilderness to pray. Many of them walked upon Mount Carmel and communed with God.

Subject: meditation
Quotation: Today striving is necessary, and likewise meditation on the signs in the horizons and within yourselves. Look ye in the Book of Certitude and ponder.

Subject: meditation
Quotation: Through the grace of the existence of the King of existence, it is hoped that night and day you will be engaged in the remembrance and meditation of that Life of the world, so that the sweet fragrance of that station may perfume the nostrils.

Subject: meditation
Quotation: They also meditate upon the scientific questions of the day, and these are likewise solved. Through the meditative faculty inventions are made possible, colossal undertakings are carried out; through it governments can run smoothly. Through this faculty man enters into the very Kingdom of God.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Never talk to God to a man with an empty stomach. Feed him first.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Therefore, use thy utmost power to sow and cast those pure seeds, the divine teachings, in the hearts which move and cheer by the fragrance of God.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The basis of the Call [i.e., teaching and delivering addresses] must be the Oneness of the world of humanity...This must be the basis of your addresses in public meetings.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The servants must be educated like children - first with gentle nourishment until they progress to meat and its like. Likewise, words that cause flight and denial are not permitted.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: It is the time of sweetness and the time of freshness and grace. That is, one must speak with utmost sweetness in the gatherings for teaching and become like a sugar-breaking parrot.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Speak in public meetings. Deliver talks on universal love, the greatness of the cause of Baha'u'llah, the penetration of the Word of God, and the general principles of the Revelation of Baha'u'llah.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The study of teaching is most essential. The gatherings of the friends should be classes for learning to teach, meaning that in every meeting the focus of discussion should be on proofs and evidences.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: We have enjoined wisdom upon all and forbidden that which causeth souls to be perturbed... The manner and method of teaching have been revealed in the Tablets - all must act accordingly and be watchful.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: In the school, teach those divine newcomers heavenly manners, and in the school of unity become a teacher of love, and teach the children of the merciful friends the ways and customs of the love of God

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: You must certainly give importance to this matter and act according to it, for therein lies complete wisdom. Otherwise, those countries will become difficult, even more severe than Iran. You must exercise great caution - this is necessary and obligatory.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: People must be educated with kindness and forbearance and drawn to the eternal realm. For when someone who has clung to certain beliefs for years suddenly hears their opposite without understanding the reason, it will surely cause them to withdraw and object.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Today all must free themselves from their own will, desire, conjectures, imaginings and fancies, and fix their gaze upon the Will of God. By His very Self, the triumph achieved through one goodly deed is superior and more perfect than a hundred thousand swords.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The Master used the metaphor of flowers to explain spiritual truth: "If you have a bed of lilies-of-the-valley that you love and tenderly care for, they cannot see you, nor can they understand your care, nevertheless, because of that tender care, they flourish. So it is with your husband."

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Therefore, the loved ones of God must undertake this momentous task with wisdom and utterance. Some they must teach through words, some through deeds and actions, and some through character, drawing them to the Divine Court. Goodly deeds and spiritual attributes are themselves teachers of the Cause.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Teaching must be done with wisdom according to people's capacity: "Most people you will observe to be as infants - were they given strong food at first, they would perish and never reach maturity. They must be given the milk of divine knowledge from the breast of wisdom until they attain true maturity"

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: It behoveth the people of God to be forbearing. They should impart the Word of God according to the hearer's particular measure of understanding and capacity, that perchance the children of men may be roused from heedlessness and set their faces towards this Horizon which is immeasurably exalted above every horizon.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: When they observe that the intent is not contention and victory, but rather to uphold the word of truth and sincerity and to manifest humanity and divine mercy, they will surely be fair and the eyes and heart of their original nature will open. By God's grace they will become a new creation with keen vision and fresh hearing.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: However, you must proceed with perfect wisdom. If you tarry in a place and meet some souls who have rent asunder certain veils, this would be most excellent. For were your presence to become known, clamor would arise among the people. Patience, calm and concealment are necessary. One must proceed gradually and with perfect wisdom.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: since people are beginners, I deal with them gently in conversation according to their capacity and their being beginners, for this is the beginning of establishment. Most talks in great gatherings are according to the capacity of those present. The purpose is that no one should object until the Cause of God is firmly established.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Yet, one must teach with the utmost wisdom. Should one succeed in illumining a soul through the light of guidance, one should as far as possible conceal his identity. That soul should in turn teach another and conceal the matter. My meaning is that many souls are most eager to enter the Kingdom, yet they fear exposure and publicity.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The friends should only mention the teachings of the Blessed Beauty to outsiders, not the beliefs. They should absolutely not mention a word about beliefs, and if someone asks what belief they have regarding the Blessed Beauty, they should answer that He is the foremost Teacher and Educator in recent ages and 'Abdu'l-Baha is the Center of His Covenant.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Teaching is through heavenly deeds, merciful qualities, clear and evident speech, and brilliant glad tidings radiating from one's countenance during utterance and exposition. One's deeds and actions must testify to the truth of one's words and statements. This is the way of every diffuser of God's fragrances and attribute of every sincere one in God's Cause.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Rather, confine thy words to glad-tidings of the Kingdom of God, to the influence of the Word of God, to the sanctification of the Cause of God, to eternal happiness, to spiritual joy and delight, to divine attributes, to the explanation of the rising of the Sun of Truth above the horizons, and to the breathing of the spirit of life into the body of creation

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: When you are remedying certain prominent citizens and discern in them a hearing ear, share the Word of God. However, all your teaching must be through deeds. If two or three of the notables of ... embrace the Cause, great results will appear. When men like them accept the Faith, keep it secret and do not introduce them to the believers, as the foolish will be the cause of trouble.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: When the beloved Habib the Carpenter wished to prevent the polytheists from idol worship, he attributed polytheism to himself, saying "Why should I not worship Him Who has created me and to Whom ye shall be brought back?" But his intention was "Why do ye not worship Him Who created you?" He attributed polytheism to himself so it would not be harsh to their ears. This was his method of instruction.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: All must be seen in complete humility and must, in truth, gird up the loins of service firmly. We beseech God to assist them in this. By My life! If they were to become aware of this Manifestation and its sovereignty, they would be thunderstruck, let alone draw near to it. Most are ignorant to this day - none has become aware of the divine Tree and its sovereignty, grandeur, and power, save whom thy Lord willed. Therefore, an expounder is needed.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: In the associations, discuss all the teachings of the Blessed Beauty, for today in the Western regions this has influence. If they ask what belief you hold regarding Baha'u'llah, say that we consider Him the first Teacher of the world and the first Educator of the world in this age, and explain this: that these teachings of universal peace and other teachings issued from the pen of Baha'u'llah fifty years ago and were published in Iran and India and spread throughout the world.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The conditions of wisdom have formerly been sent down in various Tablets from the Most Exalted Pen. Among these conditions is that in whatever city ye enter, deposit ye the signs of God in a secure and safe place - that is, outside your dwelling place - and with the tongue, with perfect wisdom and utterance, remind the seekers. And when receptivity is observed, at that time show forth the waves of the ocean of the Merciful's utterance - that is, call for and recite some of the verses.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: If we possess a word of Truth, we will deliver it to the people; if they accept the aim is attained, if they reject we leave them to themselves and pray for them. We have to do this, however, most kindly, without the least sign of ill-feeling and opposition. We will not engage in dispute and altercation. A Baha'i teacher must keep these facts always before his mind, lest in the course of his lecture he may make a dogmatic assertion which may arouse the combative, prejudicial spirit of the listeners.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Verily utterance is a substance that seeketh penetration and moderation. As to penetration, it is conditional upon refinement, which in turn is dependent upon hearts which are detached and pure. As to moderation, this is to be combined with wisdom, which We have revealed in the Books and Tablets. Whosoever possesseth these twin essentials is indeed possessed of the Greater Elixir, for an active substance hath ever been and shall be endowed with these two stations, and it is this that penetrateth and transformeth.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: First, souls must be made thirsty, then the sweet and flowing water should be offered. If the sacred writings were now translated, published and distributed, everyone who obtained a Tablet would be content with reading it and say, I am now familiar with the foundations of this community and need investigate no further. Yet the Tablets must be expounded by the interpreter - that is, the interpreter must first establish the foundation, and after establishing proofs, then read a Tablet; only then will it have effect.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The friends and strangers must know and realize that all the believers of God have the utmost love for His Majesty the Padeshah of the Ottoman empire and that they are entreating for him protection and confirmation. This matter if it could be delivered in a proper way through American believers like Mr. Remey, Mr. MacNutt, Mr. Wilhelm, Mr. Dodge, Mr. Chase, Mr. Woodcock and others, to the Ambassador or the members of the Legation, it would be very appropriate. But this matter must be taught in an incidental way, not especially for this purpose.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Divine matters are in complete accord with reason and science, but the issue lies in the expression of things, which requires an interpreter. The same matter can be presented in many different ways. For example, in Europe and America, we never said, O people, the Promised One of all has appeared, come and worship! Had we done so, they would have shunned us from the first word and would not have listened. Now if divine matters are expressed pleasantly, they will never cause rejection and aversion, but rather will lead to the guidance of many souls.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Abdul-Baha traveled continuously for four years in the countries of Africa, America and Europe, but in cities and villages where the Call of God had not reached the ears of the inhabitants and the worldwide fame of God had not been heard, he opened his tongue to teach in assemblies, gatherings and churches in a new way that accorded with their capacity and capability. Now you too, in cities and villages where they are heedless and unaware, should first open your tongue with counsels and bring hearts to ecstasy through the sweetness of speech, then deliver the Word.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: One must educate the immature through wisdom and utterance and according to their capacity until they reach maturity. Before the martyrdom of Badi' - upon him be the Glory of God - a number were commanded to speak openly and without concealment among the people. Thus did certain souls become so enkindled with the fire of God's commanding Word that they spoke of Him with the utmost power, might and steadfastness until they quaffed the cup of martyrdom. However, after the martyrdom of Badi' - upon him be the Glory of God - the decree of wisdom was sent down from the heaven of God's Will. Now all are commanded to observe it.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Teaching in a limited way consists of the following, namely: explaining the proofs and evidences in regard to the principles of Baha'u'llah, quoting prophecies from the Old and New Testaments, stating that that Day has come. Moreover the intellectual proofs and evidences are this and this, etc. Teaching in an unlimited sense consists of the following and is very good, very great: the teacher himself (or herself) becomes the standing proof of Baha'u'llah -- that he (or she) may become a miracle of Baha'u'llah with such power and such knowledge and desire, such actions and such words and character, and such heavenly powers, that you may live amongst the people, that you may be a proof, undeniable proof, of Baha'u'llah.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: The friends must not argue with people or clergy, but rather converse with utmost consideration, kindness and good expression, and not allow it to lead to dispute and argument, for conversation with dispute and argument has no effect but rather brings hatred and enmity. Therefore they must speak with perfect kindness, selflessness, humility and submissiveness, and never utter a harsh word. They should say that we have no dispute or argument with any group and we do not look with contempt, but rather consider ourselves and them servants of Truth - we have one burden and count ourselves as fruits of one branch. The only difference is that some investigate truth while others remain silent and occupied with themselves and their own interests.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: To every city he goes he should associate with the eminent people and with the poor. He should neither be a rigid saint nor an irreligious liberal, until all those who associate with him will see that this person is a spiritual, religious, heavenly, perfect, knowledgeable and excellent learned man. He should associate with every sect and should keep abreast and harmonise them until he has an influence amongst them and becomes established and rooted within them. He should be like the breeze of the Holy Spirit wafting over their dead bodies. He should open his eyes and investigate about the souls and see what ideas they have and into which directions they are heading and unto what dogmas they are clinging - then he talks, that they will approach nearer and nearer and accept the Faith

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: A verse was revealed in the Tablet to Nabil of Qa'in - if one attains to the sweetness of that verse, he will understand the meaning of assistance: "Say: Utterance is a substance that seeketh penetration and moderation. As to penetration, it is conditional upon refinement, which in turn is dependent upon hearts that are detached and pure. As to moderation, this is commingled with wisdom as recorded in the Tablets." O My Name! Utterance seeketh penetration, for if it penetrateth not it will not be effective, and its penetration dependeth upon pure breaths and detached hearts. Likewise, it seeketh moderation, for without moderation the hearer will not bear it and will at first turn away. And moderation is the combining of utterance with the wisdom that hath been revealed in the Books and Tablets.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: Indeed a teacher is needed, and the qualifications of teachers that were heard from the Tongue of Grandeur have been mentioned separately in responses to letters from friends. If one were to fully reveal what is concealed, an uproar would arise, for it outwardly conflicts with what is in the hands of the people of outward forms. Yet if one were to conceal everything, no one would attain eternal salvation. The conduct of the Ancient Beauty Himself in Iraq and other lands serves as a complete guide for all. Most of the divines in Iraq would present themselves before the Countenance of the Goal of the worlds night and day - some questioning, some seeking, some investigating, and some searching for truth. He would say that if we were to conduct ourselves otherwise, the greatest separation would become manifest, in which case no one would draw near to hear the Word of God.

Subject: methods of teaching the Cause
Quotation: According to the requirements of the place and time, Peter appeared not to recognize them, and then asked: 'Who are you? Where do you come from?' They answered: 'We are the servants of His Holiness the Spirit of God (Christ), and we come from Jerusalem. Then he asked about his Holiness the Spirit: 'Who is He?' They said He is the Promised One of the Bible and the Desired One of all the servants.' Afterward in a spirit of an antagonist, he asked them the universal and particular questions, and at every step contended with them. Often the very nature of the questions gave them a clue to how to answer. In short, one by one he put the doubts and scruples of the people in the form of questions, and they gave convincing answers. Now and then he would accept a number of their explanations, and anon he would wave aside a set of ethers, bringing forth certain counterpropositions, so that the audience might not find out that he was also one of them.

Subject: microcosm and macrocosm ['alam-i-akbar and 'alam-i-asghar]
Quotation: Man is in truth the preface to the Manifest Book of contingent beings, and a brief summary of the meanings of the Preserved Tablet of this mighty universe, and a concise expression of this unfurled scroll of all ancient and modern times.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: This intelligence of man is the intermediary between his body and his spirit. You perceive how the soul is the intermediary between the body and the spirit.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: We hear the murmur of the sea always continuing. But the waves of the mind of man are far greater than those of the sea; they also are ceaseless. They never stop for one instant.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: The body is the horse, the soul is the rider and sometimes the rider moves without a mount. But people who do not reflect say that when the soul has left the body it can no longer act. Spirit has no body.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: The perceptions of man are of two kinds: tangible, or sensible, and reasonable, whereas the animal perceptions are limited to the senses, the tangible only. The tangible perceptions may be likened to this candle, the reasonable perceptions to the light.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: Thus, among the essential characteristics of humans and the infinite virtues of this noble species is the perception of intelligible, not sensible, realities and the discovery of hidden mysteries rather than preoccupation with known, visible substances.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: Therefore, we know that in the human organism there is a center of intellection, a power of intellectual operation which is the discoverer of the realities of things. This power can unravel the mysteries of phenomena. It can comprehend that which is knowable, not alone the sensible.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: While asleep, this physical body is as dead: it neither sees, nor hears, nor feels, and it has neither consciousness nor perception-its powers are suspended. Yet the spirit is not only alive and enduring but exerts a greater influence, soars to loftier heights and possesses a deeper understanding.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: The mind is a power of the human spirit. The spirit is like the lamp and the mind like the light that shines from it. The spirit is like the tree and the mind is like the fruit. The mind is the perfection of the spirit and its essential quality, like the rays of the sun which are an essential necessity of the sun itself.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: It is generally understood that the seat of thought, consciousness and volition is the brain; it is the organ of intellection and understanding. The heart also displays a part through the central nervous system â€" thus the activities of the brain and the heart by the means of afferent and efferent nerve fibers are connected together.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: This human spirit, which is the same as the rational soul and the faculty of intellect, encompasses all things, and discovers and understands them. It draws forth the secrets of beings from the sphere of the invisible into the sphere of the visible. This is the power that discovers all the arts and crafts and sciences and makes them known to the world.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: Nothing yields results until it is perfected in every aspect. For instance, the powers of thought, imagination, reason, comprehension, and memory must all combine to produce results and enable man to understand meanings. Just as when the powers of sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch are combined, then do they bear fruit. In brief, if one possesses the power of thought but lacks comprehension, no results will be achieved. If one has all powers but lacks memory, it is fruitless.

Subject: mind as intermediary between soul and body
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as intermediary between soul and body.txt
Quotation: The body is like a crystal, while the soul is like the light shining through it. Though the crystal be in the utmost state of purity, the manifestation of its loveliness and perfection depends upon the light's rays. The light does not need the crystal, for it is luminous in itself, but the crystal requires the light in order to become illumined. The soul, in like manner, does not need the body, but the body requires the soul. The soul does not live by reason of the body, rather it is the body which lives by reason of the soul.

Subject: mind as principle emanation; activity of the human spirit
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as principle emanation; activity of the human spirit.txt
Quotation: Though in infancy the signs of mind and spirit are present in man, they are not manifested in their perfection but remain incomplete. Only when man attaineth unto maturity do the mind and spirit manifest themselves in their fullest perfection. From the inception of his formation, the mind and spirit existed, but they were concealed and appeared only subsequently.

Subject: mind as principle emanation; activity of the human spirit
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mind as principle emanation; activity of the human spirit.txt
Quotation: Praise and thanksgiving be unto Providence that out of all the realities in existence He has chosen the reality of man and has honored it with intellect and wisdom, the two most luminous lights in either world. Through the agency of this great endowment, He has in every epoch cast on the mirror of creation new and wonderful configurations. This supreme emblem of God stands first in the order of creation and first in rank, taking precedence over all created things. Witness to it is the Holy Tradition, Before all else, God created the mind. From the dawn of creation, it was made to be revealed in the temple of man.

Subject: mindfulness; concentration; focus
Quotation: The Prophets and Holy Men always went into the wilderness to pray. Many of them walked upon Mount Carmel and communed with God.

Subject: miracles and their interpretation
Quotation: If Christ was the son of God and performed so many miracles even as to quickening the dead, why after 2000 yrs his followers do not even practice these simple Teachings of his?

Subject: miracles and their interpretation
Quotation: As for the miracles that occurred in the wars of the Israelites with the unbelievers mentioned in the Holy Book, these have interpretations and meanings; nevertheless, the Baha'is do not consider the miracles of the Prophets impossible or absurd.

Subject: miracles and their interpretation
Quotation: Miracles have frequently obscured the Teachings which the Divine Messenger has brought. The phenomenal miracles are unimportant, and prove nothing to anybody but the witnesses thereof, and even they will very often explain them away! Therefore miracles have no value in the teaching of religion.

Subject: miracles and their interpretation
Quotation: The Manifestations of God are the sources of wondrous deeds and miraculous signs. For them, all difficult or impossible matters become possible and permissible. They perform extraordinary feats through an extraordinary power, and they influence the natural world through a power that transcends nature itself. From each of them, marvelous things have appeared. However, the sacred scriptures employ a special terminology, and in the sight of God's Manifestations these wonders and miracles hold no importance - so much so that they do not even wish them to be mentioned. For even if these miracles were considered the greatest of proofs, they would serve as clear evidence only for those present at their occurrence, not for those who were absent.... Our meaning is not that the Manifestations of God are unable to perform miracles, for this indeed lies within their power.  But that which is of import and consequence in their eyes is inner sight, spiritual hearing and eternal life.  Thus, wherever it is recorded in the sacred scriptures that such a one was blind and was made to see, the meaning is that he was inwardly blind and gained spiritual insight, or that he was ignorant and found knowledge, or was heedless and became aware, or was earthly and became heavenly.

Subject: miracles and their interpretation
Quotation: Christ healed by the power of his word, because the word of the Messiah was the Holy Spirit purified from all else. Jesus said: "Arise, take up thy bed and walk." He did not use prayers or mental suggestion. He used spiritual authority in the command which was the power of the Holy Spirit manifest in him. Therefore his word was obeyed because it was creative.

Subject: miracles and their interpretation
Quotation: Verily I was - God's mercy be upon him - and claimed not the decree which I was given, and therefore no supernatural occurrences appeared from him, for the matter was obscure to thee. And the absence of supernatural occurrences from His servant was due to the Imam's decree, as people know not its mystery. And verily I, were God to will it, would manifest from me without knowledge thereof, as a grace from Him, as I wrote in two books sent to two scholars the decree before its occurrence by eighty-seven days.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: The appearance of the Manifestations is to bring happiness; that all may reach this great aim of life.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: The Holy Manifestations of God came to deliver souls from the darkness of nature, for without a teacher humanity cannot become learned

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: Christ came in order that he may educate the world of humanity, illumine the realm of morality. He sacrificed his life for the realization of this fact. This is reality.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: The holy, divine Manifestations have been sent and have undergone manifold sufferings, persecutions and trials in order that the world of humanity might be freed from the captivity of nature.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: Two purposes underlay the divine appearance of the Messengers: first, to deliver mankind from the darkness of ignorance and guide them to the light of true understanding; second, their well-being and the knowledge of the ways leading thereunto.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: The holy, divine Manifestations give a new spirit and a new mind to man, are the cause of great progress; they illumine the world

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: And in another station We interpret it as the Prophethood of the Beloved, meaning that God addressed him as Prophet that he might inform the people of that which would guide them to the path of right guidance and prevent them from tyranny and corruption.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: The purpose of the divine Manifestations has been the education of holy souls. Their only motive has been the education of blessed souls and sanctified beings who are the foundation of divine education and promoters of the most great guidance and the supreme favor.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: We say that the purpose of the appearance of the Kingdom is the education of souls, the advancement of the human world, the manifestation of the love of God, the fellowship and unity of all mankind, the appearance of divine perfections, and the realization of the exalted nature of humanity. This is the purpose and result of the appearance of the Kingdom.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: It was to manifest this light that Baha'u'llah was born, and came into the world. He taught Eternal Truth to men, and shed the rays of Divine Light in all lands. Therefore Baha'u'llah established a heavenly kingdom in this transient world, lit the celestial lamp, opened the gates of the Kingdom so that the Sun of Truth might shine and heavenly civilization be established.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: This is the primary purpose and true intention of the raising up of the Prophets and appearance of the holy ones and the dawning of the Sun of Truth in this most mighty cycle of the King of Oneness. And if this glorious purpose and intention of the Lord of Glory does not appear and become manifest in the gathering of the world, the cycle and age will remain fruitless and delayed.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: These holy Manifestations of God come into the world to dispel the darkness of the animal, or physical, nature of man, to purify him from his imperfections in order that his heavenly and spiritual nature may become quickened, his divine qualities awakened, his perfections visible, his potential powers revealed and all the virtues of the world of humanity latent within him may come to life.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: We are commanded to quicken the souls, to train the characters, to illumine the realm of man, to guide all the inhabitants of the earth, to create concord and unity among all men and to lead the world of humanity to the Fountain of the Everlasting Glory. The reformation of one empire is not our aim; nay, rather we invoke from God that all the regions of the world be reformed and cultivated

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: The holy, divine Manifestations are sent into this world as Teachers of mankind. The aim of the Prophets of God who were endued with Celestial power has ever been to deliver the people from the slavery of bestial passions and illumine them with the light of God; in other words: to deliver them from the animal Kingdom and cause them to attain to the height of the perfection of the Kingdom of humanity.

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: Know ye that the Exalted One hath in truth sent forth the Messengers to bid men to righteousness and piety, to forbid them from transgression and wickedness, and to give them glad tidings of the meeting with God on the Day when light shall shine forth from a seat of transcendent glory. Through them hath God made known the paths of guidance and error, and hath clarified by the tongue of His Messengers all that He hath willed for them

Subject: mission of the Manifestation of God in the world
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/mission of the Manifestation of God in the world.txt
Quotation: God has sent forth the Prophets for the purpose of quickening the soul of man into higher and divine recognitions. He has revealed the heavenly Books for this great purpose. For this the breaths of the Holy Spirit have been wafted through the gardens of human hearts, the doors of the divine Kingdom opened to mankind and the invisible inspirations sent forth from on high. The mission of the Prophets of God has been to train the souls of humanity and free them from the thralldom of natural instincts and physical tendencies.

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: In truth, you manage with the utmost frugality.

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: Spiritual education causes protection of existence and moderation in affairs. It is possible to educate children to have moderation in all things

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: This is a plain meal, uniform and the same to all. Simplicity and plainness are good, not only in food, but even in dress, in heart, in temperament.

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: The friends of God must hold fast unto the cord of moderation and, with the utmost kindliness, compassion and love, summon the people to the straight path of God.

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: In all matters moderation must be observed and deeds must manifest according to the requirements of wisdom, in the same manner as was witnessed here and practiced in Iraq.

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: There lived in Esphahan a merchant who was very rich but practiced parsimony to the utmost degree. Because he had many boys and girls, every evening before going home he would buy so many loaves of bread and in the morning he gave to each one loaf and one cent. This was their ration till the next 24 hours. Another merchant who displayed the opposite quality and prepared every means of comfort and enjoyment for the members of his family heard about the stinginess of his neighbor and upbraided him severely. 'Why!' he was answered 'I have six children and every day they receive six cents. With this sum they can buy two pots of Abgousht from the bazaar and eat its broth by day and its meat by night. What else do they want?'

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: Hunger is a hardship for humans, and food removes it - it is not that there is pleasure in food. Thirst is a hardship for humans, and water removes it - it is not that there is pleasure in water. Therefore if one is hungry, any food gives pleasure, and if not, there is no pleasure at all.

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: He was not really a parsimonious fellow but a careful, household economist. He would say the loss of a cargo of wheat is not a thing that will happen often but if one does not watch over his daily expenses sooner or later he will be drained to the bottom and will then have to weep over his own carelessness.

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: What is needed is unity and harmony and wisdom and moderation in all matters. Blessed are they who have held fast to the cord of unity and acted in accordance with what they were commanded by One Who is All-Knowing, All-Wise. In any case, in all circumstances one must hold fast to moderation and to means that cause the attraction and drawing near of hearts

Subject: moderation; frugality; simplicity
Quotation: But the friends had promised that henceforth they would conduct their business with moderation. I prayed on this condition, but after receiving confirmations, the drive for commerce prevailed and again they acted recklessly. Contentment is praiseworthy in all matters, even in commerce. The purpose is to facilitate livelihood, for wealth is temporary and expanding the scope of trade causes distraction and has no good end.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: Tablets have been revealed equal in number to the raindrops, and books to match the number of all knowledge, psalms, scriptures and what lies between them, which none hath comprehended save God, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. The essence of utterance hath reached such a station that every letter thereof is a clear book establishing the Cause of God, the Lord of all worlds.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: Though the dawning-place of this Sun of inner meaning has ever existed, yet its first manifestation occurred in the year nine, and later in the year eighty, after which that Pre-existent Sun rose with utmost radiance and effulgence from the Dayspring of eternity. At every moment, verses of sublime glory streamed forth from the holy divine heaven and the throne of exalted majesty, surging like an ocean and descending like rain, to such extent that none could record them - indeed, the equivalent of a hundred thousand verses remained unrecorded.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: Through such as this doth God expose the deed of the weary lie...As the Balance is established, there flow from my hands a thousand verses every six hours when rendered in proper Arabic - a proof none in the heavens or earth can match...And from the day He manifested His verses, none hath produced a verse, and all denied and were amazed, while some believed and acknowledged their impotence.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: The specimens of writing which they had requested were presented to the Most Great Branch - may my spirit be a sacrifice for the dust of His most pure footsteps. He said: "You yourself are witness and can testify that due to the abundance of divine Tablets to be transcribed, there is absolutely no time or opportunity available." And truly it is as He has stated, for even when He repairs to the outskirts of the city for recreation, the Tablets accompany Him and He remains occupied with them there also. Observe how continually petitions arrive from all cities, lands, and from the various regions of this land. The transcription of the Divine Revelation is specifically assigned to this servant, while the transcription of Tablets is entrusted to the Most Great Branch.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: Your letter sent from M has reached this servant. When I broke its seal, the fragrance of your love for our Most Exalted Lord enveloped me. As I read it, I was consumed by the expressions of your eagerness, yearning and attraction to what was sent to you of the words of our Lord, the All-Possessing, the Self-Subsisting. Weeping overtook me and I presented myself before the Throne, and appeared before His countenance. Then the Tongue of Grandeur and Majesty spoke in such manner that I was unable to record or write it, and remained powerless to set down what the Tongue of Power had uttered. I returned to my place and spent the night remembering and praising you, for I saw you that night sitting with me as we shared stories until morning. I ascended to the Most Exalted Horizon and stood before the Throne. Then the Desired One addressed me and other verses were revealed with the speed of a torrent rushing down from mountains or lightning flashing from clouds - nay, even faster. I was unable to record them. By your life! The wine of verses so intoxicated me that my fingers were prevented from moving and my heart from comprehending what was revealed from the heaven of utterance of our All-Knowing, All-Informed Lord. It was as though I had become a piece of fire as I gazed toward the direction of the Throne like one overcome with bewilderment.... It is submitted that the details were as described.... Now time is short and there is no opportunity for more, otherwise my remembrance of you and description of my condition would never end.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: While divine verses are being revealed like torrential rain, nay even more abundantly, and the letters of divine friends arrive continuously and successively, how could any mortal accomplish this mighty and momentous task except through His grace, His favor, and His kindness?

When I am silent, the All-Powerful causeth me to speak and biddeth me to cry out betwixt earth and heaven. When I sleep, my heart calleth me and addresseth me saying: This is not the time for slumber.

He, verily, hath power over all things. By the life of Him Whom God shall make manifest! My Revelation is more wondrous than the Revelation of Muhammad, the Apostle of God, if ye be of them that ponder in the days of God.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: And whenever We repeat the words, in each one of them We intend a meaning which none has understood save My All-Knowing, All-Informed Self. By thy life! Had We found the people to have attained maturity, We would not have repeated the words. Thou dost witness that whatsoever proceedeth from My Pen at every moment is of a wondrous nature. And verily, whenever We send down from the Kingdom of Glory and Power that which We send down, We do so in a manner suited to this creation.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: This is the station of divine revelation. It is not a sensible, but an intelligible reality. It is sanctified from and transcendent above past, present, and future. It is a comparison and an analogy-a metaphor and not a literal truth. It is not the condition that is commonly understood by the human mind when it is said that someone was asleep and then awoke, but signifies a passage from one state to another. For example, sleeping is the state of repose, and wakefulness is the state of motion. Sleeping is the state of silence, and wakefulness is the state of utterance. Sleeping is the state of concealment, and wakefulness is that of manifestation. Briefly, the Manifestations of God have ever been and will ever be luminous Realities, and no change or alteration ever takes place in Their essence. At most, before Their revelation They are still and silent, like one who is asleep, and after Their revelation They are eloquent and effulgent, like one who is awake.

Subject: modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/modes; manner; speed; size of divine revelation.txt
Quotation: For example, when Moses went up to Mount Sinai to establish the religion of God, He fasted for forty days; and fasting was therefore enjoined upon the Israelites to awaken and admonish them. Likewise Christ, at the beginning of the foundation of His divine religion, the establishment of His teachings, and the formulation of His admonitions, disregarded for forty days all physical necessities and refrained from food and drink. Similarly, the Qur'an was revealed during the month of Ramadan and therefore the fast was enjoined during that period. In the same way, in the beginning of His manifestation, the Bab would be so overcome with emotion at the revelation of the divine verses that for days He would confine himself to drinking tea. Likewise, in the days when He was instituting the divine teachings, and when the divine verses would be sent down continuously, Baha'u'llah would be so overwhelmed with the intensity of their influence and the emotions surging within His heart that He would take but little food.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: Asceticism is not necessary. The extreme asceticism of the saints was superstition. The monasticism of the Christian church was mistaken. St. Paul was responsible for much of this because in one of his epistles he praises those who do not marry and prophesied that sects would arise which would not marry. St. Paul disapproved of marriage. But God did not give us good gifts that we should reject them. He created all these blessings that His servants may bless Him.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: How many souls spent their lives in worship and underwent austerities, yearning to enter the Kingdom but did not succeed! Yet you achieved this without hardship or austerity

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: O people of the earth! Living in seclusion or practicing asceticism is not acceptable in the presence of God. It behooveth them that are endued with insight and understanding to observe that which will cause joy and radiance.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: As for what thou hast asked concerning unity and monasticism, the decree of solitude and seclusion - thou hast no right to this, for in this Faith the principle of monasticism is not beloved of God, nor hath He commanded it to His chosen ones.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: In this Cause there is no monasticism, but a person who wants to dedicate their time to teaching the Cause of God and serving their fellow humans can withdraw from all other affairs. Certainly spending time serving the Kingdom of God is better, but not monasticism.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: In the past, some people would engage in austerities with the thought of abandoning physical pleasures and suppressing anger and passion...Thus the purpose of austerity is abandoning the self and desires while still partaking of blessings, not being deprived of God's bounties.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: Consider these nuns. They are not aware of the teachings of Christ, nor of His ordinances, and indeed are ignorant of everything. But in following their own vain imaginings are in fact performing these sacrificial deeds. They withdraw from society and normal life and live in these convents.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: There is no monasticism in this Cause, but a person who wishes to devote his time exclusively to teaching the Cause of God and serving the human race can still distance himself from the things of this world. It would certainly be preferable for him to spend his time in service to the Kingdom of God, but not to practise monasticism.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: No result is gathered from their lives. They enter the monastery alive and they are taken out when dead. Their entire lives are spent in the dark cells; never speaking with any human being, always praying or subjecting themselves to severe self-tortures. Many cannot endure such life and die within a short while. Although from one standpoint this is the highest degree of severance, yet it is a kind of severance which is not only harmful to the body polity but it is productive of no result what so ever.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: Were anyone to wash the feet of all mankind, and were he to worship God in the forests, valleys, and mountains, upon high hills and lofty peaks, to leave no rock or tree, no clod of earth, but was a witness to his worship--yet, should the fragrance of My good pleasure not be inhaled from him, his works would never be acceptable unto God. How many a man hath secluded himself in the climes of India, denied himself the things that God hath decreed as lawful, imposed upon himself austerities and mortifications, and hath not been remembered by God, the Revealer of Verses.  Make not your deeds as snares wherewith to entrap the object of your aspiration

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: The pious deeds of the monks and priests among the followers of the Spirit-upon Him be the peace of God-are remembered in His presence. In this Day, however, let them give up the life of seclusion and direct their steps towards the open world and busy themselves with that which will profit themselves and others.

Subject: monasticism; asceticism
Quotation: Say: O concourse of monks! Seclude not yourselves in churches and cloisters. Come forth by My leave, and occupy yourselves with that which will profit your souls and the souls of men. Thus biddeth you the King of the Day of Reckoning. Seclude yourselves in the stronghold of My love. This, verily, is a befitting seclusion, were ye of them that perceive it. He that shutteth himself up in a house is indeed as one dead. It behooveth man to show forth that which will profit all created things, and he that bringeth forth no fruit is fit for fire. Thus counseleth you your Lord, and He, verily, is the Almighty, the All-Bounteous. Enter ye into wedlock, that after you someone may fill your place. We have forbidden you perfidious acts, and not that which will demonstrate fidelity. Have ye clung to the standards fixed by your own selves, and cast the standards of God behind your backs? Fear God, and be not of the foolish. But for man, who would make mention of Me on My earth, and how could My attributes and My name have been revealed? Ponder ye, and be not of them that are veiled and fast asleep. He that wedded not [Jesus] found no place wherein to dwell or lay His head, by reason of that which the hands of the treacherous had wrought. His sanctity consisteth not in that which ye believe or fancy, but rather in the things We possess. Ask, that ye may apprehend His station which hath been exalted above the imaginings of all that dwell on earth. Blessed are they who perceive it.
