Quotation: Question: Will you explain the subject of Return? Answer: Baha'u'llah has set forth a lengthy and detailed explanation of this matter in the Book of Certitude. Read it, and the truth of this matter will become clear and manifest. But since you have raised the question, a brief explanation will also be provided here.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: "Already His Holiness the Bab said: According to the doctrine of the Return the Prophets are always the same Man and to this I (the Bab) can testify: 'That which spoke in the Prophets of the past, now speaks in Me and will after Me speak in "Man Yuzhiruhu'llah" (Baha'u'llah), for there is no final end of manifestation'."

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: Therefore, all expressions of this word return unto Muhammad in His next Revelation, which is the manifestation of the Point of the BayÃ¡n, and not in His first Revelation. For in His First Revelation, the Tree of divine Unity, had not yet been exalted in the inmost realities of the created beings, but now that 1270 years have passed, this Tree hath attained the stage of yielding fruits.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: This was that which was known to that illustrious one, when there appeared that Day which had been recorded by the Most Holy Pen in the Tablets of God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting - that another Return would come to pass, and less than the eye of a needle would be revealed of the innermost mystery, and all those of Sinai would return from the reality of eternity to nothingness and non-existence.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: Behold My manifestation in the name of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and My manifestation in the name of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and My manifestation in the name of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and My manifestation in the name of Him Whom God shall make manifest with the eye of truth, and see Him Whom God shall make manifest as He Who has been made manifest, that thou mayest not remain veiled in any Revelation.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: On this, that 'Ali, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world, together with all His faithful, and all who believed in the one other than Him. On this, that Fatimih, the blessings of God rest upon Her, hath returned to the world, together with all Her faithful, and all who believed in the one other than Her. On this, that Hasan, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world, together with all His faithful, and all who believed in the one other than Him.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: Baha'o'llah said that "When I say that I am going to plan this tree again," that it will mean that it will be the identical tree, hence if Baha'u'llah says that He will plant this Tree again, it will be the identical Tree again as its spiritual type only, and there will be a difference in the physical construction of the Tree, as there will also be a difference in the material tree, just as there was in the previous life of that tree, but no difference in the Spirit.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: Now to come to the question of the return which is spoken of in Holy Scriptures. For example His Holiness, the Christ, said that John the Baptist is Elias and when they asked of John he said "No, I am not Elias". Though, outwardly these two contradicted each other, however in reality they did not, because that effulgent reality which is absolute and which appeared in all the prophets of God appeared likewise in John the Baptist. That is: the same virtues which were in the former appeared in the later.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: This is the One who in every Revelation hath been known by a name and hath been manifest in that Revelation, until in the previous Revelation He was the Person of Muhammad - may the blessings of God be upon Him and upon the Manifestations of His Cause. And this is the mystery of the tradition related from the Imams - peace be upon them - concerning Him, that at the time of His appearance He makes mention of all from Adam to the Seal, saying that whosoever wishes to behold them should look upon Him, for verily He is their Reality and none other.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: In brief, return is indeed mentioned in the Divine Scriptures, but what is meant is the return of qualities, conditions, effects, perfections and inner realities of the lights which recur in every dispensation - not specific individuals and particular spirits. For instance, we say this lamp is the same as last night's, or that last year's rose has returned to the garden this year. Here the intent is not the individual reality, the fixed identity, and the specific essence of that other light or flower, but rather those qualities and characteristics that were present in that lamp and rose and are now seen in this lamp and rose - meaning those perfections, bounties and gifts of the previous spring have returned in the following spring.

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: Before the First Point, God did manifest Me in such wise that none besides Him can comprehend, and I was, in every Dispensation, among the foremost of them that worship God, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, of the seen and the unseen, the Lord of all the worlds. From the Manifestation of the First Point until now, God hath manifested Me in every Dispensation by whatever name hath been manifested, and all do follow Me. I was Noah in the day of Noah, and Abraham in the day of Abraham, and Moses in the day of Moses, and Jesus in the day of Jesus, and Muhammad in the day of Muhammad, and the Primal Point in the day of the Primal Point, and I shall be Him Whom God shall make manifest in His day, and Him Whom God shall make manifest after Him in His day, and Him Who shall be manifested after Him Whom God shall make manifest in His day

Subject: return of the Manifestations of God
Quotation: Say: O concourse of Jews! If ye desire to crucify the Spirit once again, by God, this indeed is that Spirit appeared amongst you, so do with Him as ye please, for He hath sacrificed His soul in God's path and feareth no one, even were all who are in the heavens and earth to gather against Him, if ye be of those who are certain. Say: O concourse of the Gospel! If ye desire to slay Muhammad the Messenger of God, by God, this indeed is His very Self appeared with the truth, so do with Him as ye desire, for He yearneth to meet His Beloved in the kingdom of His glory, and thus was the decree, if ye but knew. Say: O people of the Furqan! If you desire to hang the body of 'Ali, through whom the Bayan was sent down, by God, this is His Beloved One Who hath appeared with another name and hath come upon the clouds of inner meaning with a sovereignty from His presence.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Whatever is permissible for publication in these days is given permission to be published, for every time has its requirements. As for the Epistle to the Son of the Wolf, in the blessed days permission was not granted to anyone to make copies, as circumstances required. Now it has been printed and published. If the Kitab-i-Aqdas were to be printed, it would be published and fall into the hands of contemptible fanatics, therefore it is not permitted.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The book containing matters pertaining to the Faith and its history which was sent through Mr. Remey will, God willing, be sent and published. As for the book containing the history of the Cause which you intend to author, it must conform entirely to the article. Likewise, some Tablets containing universal teachings which you had sent with Mr. Remey will, God willing, be reviewed and forwarded.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: This Nuqtatu'l-Kaf is pure fabrication - the late Haji Mirza Jani has no knowledge of this history. The history itself is clear evidence that this is contrived.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: As for the printing of the Book of Teaching Lessons by his honor Sadr al-Sudur, there is no objection to it, and there is no objection to sending one volume of the Book of the Key of Gates to Rafsanjan.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The writings of Mirza Abul-Fazl - may my life be a sacrifice to him - I am sending to you in order that you will, all together, compile books from these writings and immediately print and circulate them.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: discussion of proposed anti-Baha'i book to be published in Egypt

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Send some of the newspapers that were sent to reach him through an intermediary

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The text discusses protocols around handling and reviewing personal correspondence

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The Bab declareth: "Beware lest thou be veiled by what hath been revealed in the Bayan."

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: If Mr. Phelps wants to print the book again, the talk that I had with him during the second journey at Mirza Asadu'llah's house about the immortality of spirits and souls should also be included in the second edition. If he includes this correction, he is permitted.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Send with utmost speed several volumes - that is, one copy of each book - to Haddad in America.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The history of the martyrs of Yazd which Bayda has authored - if it is published it would be very good.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Instructions for transcribing and printing tablets in fine handwriting with utmost precision and elegance

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The reference to Madame Markovitch's comedy needing proper revision, and the criticism of Browne's book.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: You were engaged in service, publishing and distributing books... Send a copy of that book to the Holy Land.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Miss Barney, as you know, would not agree. She wants to collect and translate them first, then have them published

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: service to the Star of the West publication should continue but within practical constraints of maintaining livelihoods

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: As for translating the Eastern and Western letters into Turkish and Russian and publishing them, there is no harm in this.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: I am pleased with the talk you gave at the Parliament of Religions. God willing may you always succeed in giving appropriate talks.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The book you had written about Qurratu'l-Ayn I translated into Arabic, and the translation is very eloquent and fluent, and I read all of it carefully.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: However, from some of the servitude-laden contents joy was obtained while others were corrected...I undertook to correct your poetry so that it may serve as a model

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: As for the history of the Cause, the Narrative of the Traveller has been translated and is being printed in Chicago and will be sent for you to distribute, as it is brief and beneficial.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: When I learned of this I sought the ultimate goal and presented it before His Countenance...The servant read his verse and found it a brilliant star in the heaven of eloquence and rhetoric.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: I have sent the papers of Jinab-i-Mirza Abu'l-Fadl, may my spirit be a sacrifice for him, so that you may collectively extract treatises from them to be immediately published and disseminated.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Your eloquent writing was observed, and your second brief letter was seen. The books of the late Shaykh are missing here. Praise be to God, through the efforts of Hajji Niyaz they are available there.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The translation of the blue pamphlet is quite acceptable. The answer to the letter of Barakatollah has been also well written. Distribute ye Baha'i pamphlets among those souls who are thirsty for them.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Letters arrive and remain with you for several days. Among these, Mirza Jalal had sent a letter, but then he himself arrived. After his arrival his letter was received. Please be attentive in this regard.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Leave the political treatise for now until a second signal is given for its publication. In those days when it was written, its publication was very beneficial, for all subsequent events were mentioned therein.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Madame Isabella has truly shown extraordinary effort in composing the book. Convey to her my utmost satisfaction and pleasure. God willing, she will succeed in illustrating and distinguishing these two matters.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Some friends in London in these days had copied those erroneous Tablets with the intention of publishing them. I immediately prohibited this... Therefore, devote all your efforts to publishing the Divine Sacred Tablets.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Regarding the editing of that Christian person's book - if you are successful in that, it would be a great achievement and is very necessary. And when he writes the book he has in mind, he should bring it himself at that time.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Refer to Nikolai's history. Translate, publish, and circulate any matters similar to the issue of the sacred remains of the Exalted One which are clearly false, so that all the friends may become aware and mention them in gatherings.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: When I understood what was in your letter, I sought the Goal and presented what was therein before the One, the Single. He spoke - and His utterance is most sweet - saying that you should wait until God comes to you with His utterance.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: You have requested to print and distribute the questions of Mr. Mirza Haydar-'Ali - printing and distribution among the friends is permitted but among outsiders is absolutely not permitted, as it would cause universal hatred and enmity.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: She must certainly revise the first book. If she succeeds in this, she will receive the protection of divine favors and it will make her an illumined lamp. Regarding the diagnosis of her book, no effort will be spared as far as possible.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Therefore, proceed now with publishing your treatise. The time for dramatic performance will come. Although the Baha'is are scattered and most are poor, except for a few wealthy ones, they will certainly assist you with publishing the book.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: And as for the book of Letters of this servant, on the back of the book let just this much be written: "Letters of Abdu'l-Baha" and at the end of the book whatever the majority of votes of the Assembly of the friends decides, implement that.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: If thou shouldst edit one magazine every six months--two in a year--then forward it to the Holy Land to be corrected and returned, after due correction, for its publication--it is very acceptable and will be the cause of the penetration of the Word of God.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: As for the matter of Gobineau's book translation - the contents of that book do not conform to reality...it is clearly confused. In some places it is merely the imaginings of opponents with no truth whatsoever. The ignorant related such accounts and he wrote them down.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Now I have decided to read this history as much as possible each midnight. The first section which I read last night was very eloquent and well-written...Therefore, you must certainly send these two pages, and it would be better if you yourself were present for the printing.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Let your composition be according to the best style. Do not go beyond the limit of literary law. Like unto the literary productions of the Cambridge university let the pronouns be with small letters and the Capital letters be for nouns, places etc. Do not publish it in the book.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Your noble letter with its gracious contents brought boundless joy and delight, for it indicated that your health is moderate and the conclusive book is nearing completion...If the book were completed during winter and you could travel to Tehran in spring it would be most suitable

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Thou hast written that the publication of the book of Mirza Abu'l Fazl is commenced. This is very acceptable, for his books are written with the utmost sincerity. Likewise the translation of the Hidden Words that you are just thinking to print another edition, this is also acceptable.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: A letter arrived from the handmaiden of God Isabella Grinevskaya. The original and reply are being sent for you to review and deliver the response. If the esteemed lady wishes to publish her book, should the divine friends provide assistance and support, it would encourage and motivate her.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: The short treatise which thou hast written upon "Service in the Kingdom," forwarding it here and asking permission for its publication, was read. Spread it among the believers. The copy of the pamphlet that thou hast sent before, God willing, in opportune time will be read and forwarded to thee.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: You had requested some books from Baku and Ishqabad to be presented to certain important people. From among those books, the Kitab-i-Aqdas, the Tablet of Tajalliyat, the Tablet of Ishraqat, the Kitab-i-Iqan, the Seven Valleys, the Hidden Words, and the Madaniyyih - their presentation is permissible.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Gather together the Tablets of Ishraqat, Kalimat, Tajalliyat, and Bisharat, along with some of the Persian and Arabic Tablets containing divine counsels and exhortations suited to the present time and circumstances, and either send the compilation or let us select and send them for you to print there.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Whenever anyone wishes to publish something, it must be with the knowledge of the Spiritual Assembly. Without this, order would be disrupted, with everyone writing, publishing and disseminating whatever they wish. Thus, for the sake of orderly affairs, one must first consult the Spiritual Assembly and seek their counsel.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Regarding the letter of recommendation you wrote about for there, it is very good, but if addressed to everyone it would not be appropriate for your dignity and the Cause of God, as America is different from Iran. Rather, specify one suitable person to whom a complete recommendation can be made and he can convey it to others.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: As to the book of Mirza Mahmud-i-Zarqani, there is no objection to its translation into English and its circulation particularly among the friends. And as for the printing of Tablets and letters, this is dependent upon and conditioned on the opinion of the Convention's Executive Committee so that it may not cause confusion of minds.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: And concerning what you wrote concerning the spiritual beloved, Jinab-i-'Andalib, upon him be the Glory of God and His favors, praise be to God that he is confirmed in serving the Cause of the Beloved of hearts. Jinab-i-Samandar, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, has repeatedly mentioned him, and in these days his poetry and prose were presented before His presence.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: That person who published the Kitab-i-Aqdas without the permission and consent of His Imperial Majesty has truly opposed the truth...The definitive divine command is that one must obey the government. This admits of no interpretation and requires no explanation. Among the requirements of obedience is that nothing should be published without the permission and consent of the government.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: In any case, He commanded the Most Great Branch - may my spirit and being be sacrificed for the most precious dust of His footsteps - to write a commentary on these matters. God willing, it will be sent later, but as He is currently occupied, it has been delayed. The treatise which was previously written concerning the governance of cities is with Mulla 'Ali-Akbar - you will observe it.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: This service - namely obtaining and sending books - was important because the pen of oppression of every unjust one galloped in the field of rejection against the One of Hidden Favors, and those numerous books took on written form... And you were the cause of those books reaching where needed, and praise be to God, His Holiness Abul-Fadl is engaged in writing, and soon a clear response will be written.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Mrs. Ella Cooper from California has repeatedly written that photographs of the historical sites of this Cause in Iran are very much needed. Therefore, you should write everywhere requesting that photographs be taken of these sites and sent to the Holy Land, so that they may be forwarded from the Holy Land to California. Similarly, wherever photographs of early believers exist, these should also be sent.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Mr. Dreyfus has written from Paris and insisted with utmost emphasis that certain handwritten treatises from insignificant persons like the followers of Yahya are continuously arriving at the public library in Paris, and their purpose is to prevent the greatness of the Cause of God and the penetration of the Word of God and to promote their own vain imaginings. And since there are no handwritten treatises of this Cause in the public library, and since the scholars give more importance to handwritten treatises, they read these insignificant treatises.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Furthermore, regarding what thou didst write about the blessed verse of inheritance, "Blessed art thou for having comprehended that which was revealed from God" - since Jinab-i-Zaynu'l-Muqarrabin, upon him be the Glory of God, the Lord of all worlds, had inquired about inheritance, by command that which was revealed in the Kitab-i-Aqdas regarding this matter was written specifically for him and sent. Similarly, he had inquired about the law of marriage, and what was revealed regarding this was also written and sent by command. All these passages are revealed in the Kitab-i-Aqdas, and that mighty Book was sent specifically to thee.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Sheikh Farajullah translated Ishraqat here with utmost care; nevertheless, I told him to present this translation to the Spiritual Assembly of Egypt for your review. After the approval of the Spiritual Assembly of Egypt, it should be published. This is for the sake of order and regulation, because if it is not conditional upon the approval of the Spiritual Assembly, any person will translate and publish and distribute a treatise from the Tablets, and it is even possible that outsiders will undertake this task and there will remain no order and regulation. But when it is made conditional upon the approval of the Spiritual Assembly, if someone from among outsiders translates and publishes a Tablet, it will not gain circulation.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: As for the matter of publishing books: those previously published, such as the treatises of Abu'l-Fadl and Mr. Remey's treatises, as well as beneficial treatises and books authored and published by some of the friends, and likewise the translations of the Book of Certitude, Tarazat, Words of Wisdom, Glad-Tidings, Ishraqat, Hidden Words, and Seven Valleys, and also Mr. Remey's new treatise written about the twelve principles - these may be published and distributed whenever necessary. But other treatises besides these, or newly composed works, must be carefully examined and investigated in the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar gathering by blessed souls among the friends. If they unanimously consider its publication appropriate, it may be published and distributed. Otherwise, let it wait until the way opens to send it to the Holy Land for correction.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: O Abu'l-Fada'il!... Whatever information you have regarding the history of Mirza Jani the martyr, please write it down.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: But the calamity is this: in these days the shameless community has newly contrived a deception and set in motion an intrigue and conspiracy. They have fabricated a historical book in the name of Haji Mirza Jani, the martyr, and some time ago sent it to the library in Paris. And Edward Browne, the Englishman, who during his journey to Persia was surrounded by the shameless ones, who showed him the utmost servility, and who were in constant communication with him -- they resorted to every means to encourage and incite him against the Cause of God....  Now it has become evident -- that is, the shameless followers of Yahya have prompted Browne to translate that book which they themselves, with consummate skill, had compiled and put together in the name of Aqa Mirza Jani as a history of the Cause, and had sent to the library in Paris. They have dictated and insinuated to him an introduction, so that he might publish and disseminate that introduction and that fabricated history in Persian and English. Now that book has been published and disseminated. From beginning to end, following the instructions and insinuations of the followers of Yahya, it has been written completely contrary to the facts, so that it might cause a distortion of minds and confusion of thoughts. The passages of the book itself contradict one another, and likewise some of its contents are contrary to his earlier work.... Haji Mirza Jani the martyr had written several historical sections, incomplete, which were with the nephew of the honored Zabih, Aqa Muhammad-Rida. It was apparently in Haji Mirza Jani's own handwriting. By whatever means possible, obtain those sections - if possible the original copy, and if not possible, send a transcript of them. In the text of this introduction from abroad, it is written that only one copy of this history was found, and that in the Paris library. Glory be to God! Despite all the friends at that time being extremely thirsty for the history of this Cause, not one copy was found in Iran. From this alone it is clear that that Paris history is fabricated.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: As for the matter of the Nuqtatu'l-Kaf, they have published this and distributed it throughout the world. If, as Browne suggests, its publication in Chihrinama would yield some benefit to you, I am not willing to prevent the Chihrinama office from gaining that benefit, since repeated publication in newspapers does not result in any new promotion. People are of two kinds: one kind investigates truth - these become more steadfast and firm through such publications. The other kind harbor extreme hatred and enmity without cause - we have shown and continue to show them the utmost kindness, but due to their enmity they have no need to read such papers. Therefore, publishing such papers is redundant. Thus, as Browne has indicated, I will not prevent your office from the benefits. I also state with utmost sincerity that these articles, whether in treatises or newspapers, will ultimately cause disgrace and disappointment to their authors and transmitters. This Nuqtatu'l-Kaf is pure fabrication - the late Haji Mirza Jani has no knowledge of this history. The history itself is clear evidence that this is contrived.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: Thou art not like some of the feeble ones who at first make a great noise but later become shaken by the suggestions of the heedless ones, like Edward Browne. This person wrote a book - though the actual writer was a follower of Yahya - yet it was published in his name; that is, whatever they suggested, he wrote. Similarly, a distorted history under the name of the late Aqa Mirza Jani was printed and published. Now, praise be to God, the friends have found the correct copy and the distortion has become clear and evident. The friends are engaged in writing various responses with clear proofs and evident arguments, not false accounts, and these will soon be published.

Subject: review of publications
Quotation: And regarding refuting the external fabrications and proving the alteration of the book [Nuqtatu'l-Kaf], you must render a distinguished service at the Divine Threshold. Your honor, along with all the capable friends, must unite on this matter. Include Jinab-i-Samandar as a partner in this matter so that everyone's knowledge can be gathered and a healing, sufficient response can be written. This matter must be carried out with utmost speed. Jinab-i-Mirza Abu'l-Fadl is prepared and will soon complete the response. Therefore, quickly convey your complete knowledge about the alteration of Mirza Jani's book to Jinab-i-Mirza Abu'l-Fadl.

Subject: reward and punishment
Quotation: Should the leaders of government and nation manifest spiritual virtues, goodly deeds, and kindly words, the lights of justice would encompass all the earth, and all would dwell in perfect tranquility within the pavilion of security and peace. The foundation of the security and welfare of nations rests upon two pillars: reward and punishment. Every sovereign must implement these two principles; indeed it is essential.

Subject: reward and punishment
Quotation: The Great Being saith: The structure of world stability and order hath been reared upon, and will continue to be sustained by, the twin pillars of reward and punishment. Take heed, O concourse of the rulers of the world! There is no force on earth that can equal in its conquering power the force of justice and wisdom. I, verily, affirm that there is not, and hath never been, a host more mighty than that of justice and wisdom.

Subject: reward and punishment
Quotation: Punishment and recompense are the cause of world order.

Subject: reward and punishment
Quotation: In the book (Kitubal-Akdas) it is specified that such a one shall be killed. If he is sentenced to life imprisonment this is worse than death, for every day he dies... The willful murderer should be killed... They must say that our belief is that the murderer, who willfully kills, must be killed. This is the command of Baha'o'llah. According to the Kitab-ul-Akdas, they must be killed.

Subject: reward and punishment
Quotation: Some maintain that by wisdom is meant the divine laws revealed in the Book. Each group, according to their understanding, has presented proofs and evidence for each of what has been mentioned, which if detailed would add to weariness. Glory be to Him Who spoke this supreme word: "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of God," for the fear and awe of God restraineth man from whatsoever causeth abasement and degradation of human station, and aideth him in that which leadeth to elevation and glory. The wise man avoideth shameful deeds, for he beholdeth punishment in their wake. The pavilion of world order is upheld upon two pillars: Reward and Punishment.

Subject: rights of the eldest son; primogeniture
Quotation: In accordance with Baha'u'llah's Teachings, a Baha'i can give all his property to his eldest son. He may do just as he likes. As long as it is his own property he may do as he wishes. One's property cannot be snatched by another. There is one difference, however; when a Baha'i leaves all to his eldest son, the eldest son in turn may break the line and divide as he wants toâ€"according to Baha'u'llah's method, or as he wishes.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: This is the age of woman... In this age of spiritual awakening, the world has entered upon the path of progress

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In this Bahai dispensation His Holiness Baha'u'llah has set a brilliant crown upon the head of women, whose brilliant jewels will shine and gleam throughout all ages and cycles. Whereas in the former time they were oppressed, now they have attained the greatest station of honor. Whereas formerly they were disappointed, now they are hopeful. While in the past they were deprived, praise be to God, they have taken a goodly portion; having been weak, praise be to God they have become strong; having been ignorant, praise be to God they have become wise.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In the world of phenomena the co-ordinate elements of male and female may be compared to the two eyes of man. Should one eye be defective undoubtedly the sight of the other eye would be affected, because sympathetic co-operation is necessary for complete usefulness. The world of humanity is possessed of two wings. One wing is represented by man, the other by woman. When one wing of a bird is defective its flight is hindered, but when both wings are equal in strength and capability then the flight of the bird is made easy.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: I asked why, given that women and men are equal in this Cause, all the addresses in the Hidden Words are to "Son." In response He [Abdu'l-Baha] said that it includes both, like Bani Israel, Bani Hasham, Bani Umayya, Bani Yafith, Bani Sam, and Bani Abbas - this is an Eastern convention.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: From the beginning of creation until now, in no age or cycle were gatherings of the maidservants of the All-Merciful arranged, nor was the promotion of teaching lessons established among them. This is among the special characteristics of this mighty cycle and blessed century. Surely strive with utmost effort in perfecting this association and increasing knowledge of the realities of meanings and mysteries, so that perhaps, God willing, in a short time women will attain the station of men and become the leaders of the learned ones. They will open eloquent tongues and demonstrate persuasive utterance, and in all regions they will shine forth like the lamps of guidance. In some cases, women have a wonderful capacity - they are quick to be attracted and intense in their enthusiasm.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The establishment of a women's assemblage for the promotion of knowledge is entirely acceptable, but discussions must be confined to educational matters. The individual women should, today, follow a course of action which will be the cause of eternal glory to all womankind, so that all women will be illumined. Now the world of women should be a spiritual world, not a political one, so that it will be radiant. I am endeavouring, with Baha'u'llah's confirmations and assistance, so to improve the world of the handmaidens that all will be astonished. This progress is intended to be in spirituality, in virtues, in human perfections and in divine knowledge.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: From the beginning of existence until the Promised Day men retained superiority over women in every respect. It is revealed in the Qur'an: "Men have superiority over women." But in this wondrous Dispensation, the supreme outpouring of the Glorious Lord became the cause of manifest achievements by women. This is a bounteous characteristic of this wondrous Age which hath granted strength to the weaker sex and hath bestowed masculine might upon womanhood.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In the Law of God, women and men are equal in all rights, except for membership in the Universal House of Justice, since according to the explicit Text of the Book its president and members must be men. However, in all other assemblies, such as the Assembly for the Construction of the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, the Teaching Assembly, and the Spiritual Assembly, as well as philanthropic and scientific gatherings, women and men share equally in all rights.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The sphere of divine knowledge was thus far the arena of the masculine sex and the roaming place of men, but in this glorious Cycle some women have been raised who have become the champions in the field of certitude, and dauntless in the arena of assurance. This is one of the distinguishing characteristics of this great Revelation and one of the bestowals of the glorious Lord.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: They say that women are weaker than men in their creation, nature and virtues. But this servant has the strongest conviction that not every man is strong nor every woman weak. Those women who are firm in God's Covenant and Testament are among the most powerful souls and are reinforced by the hosts of the Kingdom. And vacillating men are weaker than a mosquito or spider.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: When women reach the highest degree of progress, then according to the requirements of the time, place and great capacity of the women of the world, the world of women will gain extraordinary distinctions.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The American women as a whole are better educated, more well-informed on classical as well as current subjects and the spreaders of the right ideals of education. They are endowed with a most wonderful power of assimilation and comprehend quickly the subtleties of philosophy and religion. A woman Principal in any of the high schools of the United States is more intelligent than the President of the University of El-Azhar in Cairo! I talked with some of their wise women and their minds quickly grasped my meaning, although we were discussing the profound subjects of divine philosophy. I have spoken on similar topics with the Professors of El Azhar and they were as far from understanding my talk as the tadpole is from visualizing the condition of man!

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In this great Cycle and wondrous Dispensation some women have been raised up who were the emblems of unity and ensigns of oneness, for the revelation of divine bestowals is received by men and women in equal measure. Verily the most honoured in the sight of God is the most virtuous amongst you is applicable to both men and women, to servants and handmaidens.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: women's gatherings will produce eloquent speakers who will astound East and West; women in West have already surpassed men

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In this divine age the bounties of God have encompassed the world of women. Women have become verses of guidance and manifestations of the favors of the Most Glorious Beauty.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The difference between Baha'i women and others is that other Eastern women are either occupied with household management or with amusement and play, while Baha'i women attend to life's necessities as needed and spend the rest of their time explaining truths and meanings.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: Day and night thou must strive so that the woman world may be adorned with complete culture and refinement, making extraordinary progress in the world of morality and be fully established in the realm of sciences and arts. This is the cause of the sublimity of the realm of woman.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In Persia, many men surpassed Kurrat-al-Ayn in knowledge and eloquence, and were more illumined, but she, being a woman, manifested a greater work. The maidservants in America are good souls and are advancing. Among those supplications from America, there are ten from women to one from men.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: O handmaiden of God and daughter of His handmaiden! I beseech God to make thee a sign of guidance and a holy, pure reality, detached from all save God, and a center for the dawning of the sign of sanctification among the handmaidens - one who is attracted, enkindled, speaking forth and calling to the Cause of God.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: It is my hope that through the bounty of God His handmaidens may all without exception become adorned with such wondrous garments as these and such beauteous robes so that each one of them may hear from the kingdom of holiness the words, "Verily God has purified thee and chosen thee amongst the women of the world."

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The tongue of the Concourse on high uttereth praise of those women who are the pride of men, who have forgotten themselves, forsaken their comfort, attached their hearts to the Kingdom of God, raised the call of God, spread the signs of God, and advanced clear proofs and firm evidences of the manifestation of the Kingdom of God.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: Convey greetings and glory to the Handmaid of God, the morning dove of love, and say: O handmaid of God, offer thanks and praise to the Lord of Command, that you have soared in this atmosphere and become attuned to this melody. Then, with an illumined face, you will shine like a candle in the gathering of the handmaids of the All-Merciful

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In this day women have been raised up who are each a mighty sign and a leaf of the Tree beyond which there is no passing. They have laid an everlasting foundation in this transient world and have kindled such a flame at the pole of the earth that the veils of the peoples were consumed. These women became the pride of men and embodied and personified chastity and virtue.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The first educator of the child is the mother, for the child is like unto a fresh and verdant sapling that is at the beginning of its growth, thou shouldst direct it through education. If thou teaches them heavenly virtues, they will grow straight and balanced. It is clear and evident that the mother is the first educator and the establisher of the upright conduct of her child.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: For the day will come when these girls will become mothers. Mothers are the first educators of children, who establish virtues in the child's inner nature. They encourage the child to acquire perfections and goodly manners, warn him against unbecoming qualities, and encourage him to show forth resolve, firmness, and endurance under hardship, and to advance on the high road to progress.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: After the martyrdom of Christ, to Whom be glory, the disciples were greatly disturbed and disheartened. Even Peter had denied Christ and tried to shun Him. It was a woman, Mary Magdalene, who confirmed the wavering disciples in their faith... In the Cause of Baha'u'llah there have been women who were superior to men in illumination, intellect, divine virtues and devotion to God. Among them was Qurratu'l-'Ayn.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The question of training the children and looking after the orphans is extremely important, but most important of all is the education of girl children, for these girls will one day be mothers, and the mother is the first teacher of the child. And how can a mother, herself ignorant and untrained, educate her child? It is therefore clear that the education of girls is of far greater consequence than that of boys.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: Mothers must give the utmost importance to and make every effort in the education of children, for while a branch is still tender it can be trained in any way. Therefore mothers must nurture young children like saplings that a gardener cultivates. They must strive day and night to establish in children faith and certitude, fear of the Merciful, love for the Beloved of all worlds, moral virtues and goodly characteristics.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The conditions of being a handmaiden of God today are that one must gaze at all times toward the Most Exalted Horizon. This station is not attained except through the greatest sanctification and detachment. Blessed are the handmaidens who have drunk from the Kawthar of love for the Purpose of all worlds and are occupied with His mention and praise.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: As for the Teaching Committee, whose esteemed members are the handmaidens of the All-Merciful - they too are confirmed by the aid and care of the Ancient Beauty. Soon they shall observe that they are assisted by unseen hosts and are blessed with the abundant grace of the Kingdom of the All-Forgiving Lord. They shall kindle such a flame throughout all regions that will set aflame the very heart of contingent being and shake the pillars of the world.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: Among famous women of history was Zenobia, who, as you well know, was queen of Palmyra in the East. Among the heroic women of history was also Catherine of Russia, and had it not been for her the Russian sovereignty would have been entirely effaced and Peter the Great would have been defeated. Another was Cleopatra who by reason of her cunning and cleverness frustrated the plans of a Roman Emperor. Still another was Esther, a woman renowned among the Israelites, a woman of great sagacity, who really restored the glory of Israel.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: Services to the divine Threshold are manifold, but the greatest of all services and the most meritorious deed is the education of the children and of the daughters of the friends of God, and the instruction of the orphans and minors of His chosen ones. Exert the utmost effort and zeal in training the male and female children of the believers in God and use a supreme power and might in this regard, haply that learning place will be the beginning of many other schools, and the daughters of the friends will become handmaidens of the Merciful.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In ancient times and medieval ages woman was completely subordinated to man. The cause of this estimate of her inferiority was her lack of education. A woman's life and intellect were limited to the household. Science is praiseworthy -- whether investigated by the intellect of man or woman. So, little by little, woman advanced, giving increasing evidence of equal capabilities with man -- whether in scientific research, political ability or any other sphere of human activity. The conclusion is evident that woman has been outdistanced through lack of education and intellectual facilities. If given the same educational opportunities or course of study, she would develop the same capacity and abilities.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: The women who have today attained unto recognition and confession and service of the friends of God are, in the sight of God, accounted among men, nay rather among the heroes, inasmuch as neither the censure of the critic, nor the scorn of the scorner, nor the clamor of the heedless hath deterred them or shall ever deter them. Their hearts are strong and their feet are firm. I swear by the Day-Star of the horizon of utterance that the mere nail-paring of one of the believing handmaidens of today is, in the sight of God, more preferred than the divines of Persia who, after thirteen hundred years of expectation, have perpetrated what the Jews had not perpetrated at the appearance of the Spirit [Christ].

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: Zenobia was the wife of the governor-general of Athens. Her husband died, and like the Russian Queen, Catherine, she manifested the highest degree of capability in the administration of public affairs. The Roman government appointed her to succeed her husband. Afterward she conquered Syria, conducted a successful campaign in Egypt and established a memorable sovereignty... Among other noted women of history was Cleopatra, Queen of Egypt, who held her kingdom against the armies of Rome for a long time. Catherine, wife of Peter the Great, displayed courage and military strategy of the very highest order during the war between Russia and Muhammad Pasha... Victoria, Queen of England, was really superior to all the kings of Europe in ability, justness and equitable administration.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: In Christianity, Mary Magdalene was the cause of the steadfastness of the apostles. All the apostles were shaken after Christ, but Mary Magdalene remained firm as a lion. In the time of Muhammad, there were two women who were more learned than other women and became promoters of the Islamic Faith. Thus it is evident that women too have their luminaries. In the realm of politics, you have undoubtedly heard about Zenobia of Palmyra who shook the Roman Empire. When going to battle, she placed a crown upon her head, wore purple garments, let her hair flow freely, and with sword in hand led her army with such skill that she devastated the opposing forces. Finally, the Emperor himself was compelled to appear on the battlefield. For two years he besieged Palmyra but could not prevail through valor.

Subject: role and station of women
Quotation: Consider, how in former ages a number of women became confirmed and assisted in the demonstration of faith and assurance and how in this mortal world they left behind immortal names. In the world of existence, there are no greater women than the queens of empires. Materially they have reached the highest station of womanhood and gained great riches, infinite power and glory. Notwithstanding all these advantages when they die and go under the earth, they disappear and become non-existent. They leave behind no name, no trace, no fruit and no sign. But the maid servants of God who are outwardly in the utmost poverty and imprisoned by the people of oppression, humiliated and scoffed at by the outsiders, ere long, they will crown their heads with the diadem of the everlasting Glory and established upon the eternal throne of majesty. Their signs are eternal and their fame universal.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Therefore, today we must close the doors of dispute and prevent the causes of contention. This is impossible except that all follow the Interpreter and obey the appointed Center of the Covenant, meaning they must hold fast to his explicit utterance and cling to the clarity of his exposition, such that their tongues become translators of his tongue and their pens narrators of his words. They must not speak a word more or less, nor add any interpretation, allusion, or explanation, so that all may be gathered beneath the shade of the Word of Unity and assembled under the banner of Oneness.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Thanks be unto the Most Great Unity that thou hast been gathered beneath the shade of the Tree of the Covenant

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: this ancient covenant and mighty testament has been mentioned, so that the word of unity might shine forth and appear in all ranks and stations in the form of oneness

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: If the preservation of Baha'i unity were possible through any other power, I would summon all to it. But consider: can Baha'i unity be preserved by any power except the power of the Covenant? Therefore, we counsel all to hold fast to the Covenant for the sole purpose of preserving Baha'i unity.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: The Covenant is like an ocean that preserves Baha'i unity, and these souls are like foam - they make temporary movements but like Judas Iscariot and Judas' helpers and those who agreed with Judas, they will soon be forgotten like the foam of the sea. But the ocean of the Covenant remains established, for it preserves Baha'i unity. Today the Lord of Hosts is the protector of the Covenant, the powers of the Kingdom guard the Covenant, heavenly souls serve the Covenant, and celestial angels promote the Covenant.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Today the dynamic power of the world of existence is the power of the Covenant which like unto an artery pulsateth in the body of the contingent world and protecteth Baha'i unity. The purpose of the Blessed Beauty in entering into this Covenant and Testament was to gather all existent beings around one point so that the thoughtless souls, who in every cycle and generation have been the cause of dissension, may not undermine the Cause. He hath, therefore, commanded that whatever emanateth from the Centre of the Covenant is right and is under His protection and favour, while all else is error.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty has shut the door to such differences. He has referred all matters to the House of Justice that everyone may strictly obey whatsoever that Body will prescribe.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Praise be to God, in the Sacred Cause all these doors are closed, for a specific reference point has been designated, and that specific reference point is the solver of all problems and the remover of all differences.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty entered into this Covenant for obedience and not for opposition. Were it not for the removal of vain imaginings and the eradication of differences, I should not have asserted that I am 'the Center of the Covenant'.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Do not let go of Baha'i unity, and Baha'i unity is not possible except through holding fast to the divine Covenant.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Ye have not let the Blessed Beauty slip from your minds, to fade unremembered. Ye have striven to keep the Word whole and one.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Baha'o'llah appointed a Covenant in order to ward off dissensions, so that no one should give his own opinion, but that the Center should be referred to.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: in every age and dispensation, for the sake of preserving the word of unity and protecting the Cause of God from disruption, and for the unity of all souls sheltering beneath the tree of divine mercy, a command was given

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: For by what means can Baha'i unity be preserved? Is it through the nonsensical utterances of some? God forbid! The Book of the Covenant is not a tradition - it is from the Supreme Pen and was revealed solely to preserve Baha'i unity

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: We are all under the shadow of Baha'u'llah and in the shade of His tent of covenant and testament. Therefore separation has no effect. The essence is heart-felt love which is always with us and is eternal. We shall all gather in the divine realm, the Kingdom of Baha'u'llah. That meeting is everlasting.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Now is the time for the field of action and testing of men, for the mighty edifice of God's Cause rests upon the pillar of the Covenant and Testament, and the heaven of God's religion is illumined and radiant through the star of the Covenant. God forbid that if some ungrateful person should assault this pillar, not a single nail would remain to uphold the divine pavilion and the merciful tabernacle, not a single lamp would remain lit in the divine gathering. The House of God would be buried from its very foundation, the Cycle would become futile and the laws nullified.... Therefore in every street and plain that you pass through, cry out: "This Covenant is the Covenant of Alast, and this Testament is the Ancient Testament! The armies of the Kingdom of God assist this Covenant, and the hosts of the Concourse on High protect this foundation. It is the continuous and enduring ray of the Sun of Truth and the brilliant lamp of the gathering of the Divine Unity. It is the strong rope and the manifest light. It is the firm handle and the fruit of the blessed tree. It is the Preserved Tablet and the Written Book and the Outstretched Parchment. It is the Covenant - the Covenant! It is the Testament - the Testament! It is mentioned in all the scriptures and books, and recorded in all the scrolls of the ancients and tablets of the latter ones. It is the ruler of the most great crisis and the balance of the Day of Reckoning. It is the Ark of Salvation and the refuge on the Day of Return. It is the holy fragrances of the Lord God and the life-giving breezes from the gardens of the Creator. It is the mighty fortress and the strong shelter. It is the firm pillar and the essence of all books and scriptures of the Old and New Testament. Blessed is he who holds fast to it, clings to it, stands firm in it, whose heart is strengthened by its verses, and who is gathered beneath its banners."

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: The Blessed Beauty has shut the door to such differences. He has referred all matters to the House of Justice that everyone may strictly obey whatsoever that Body will prescribe. Even if the Baha'is were to split up into two groups, 'Abdu'l-Baha has warned, each forming a House of Justice of its own, one in opposition to the other, both would be false.

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: For the unity of the Baha'i Faith cannot be preserved by anything except through the Covenant. If the unity of the Baha'i Faith could have been preserved by anything else, surely the Blessed Beauty would have commanded it... In brief, the unity of the Baha'i Faith cannot be preserved except through the divine Covenant. Today the motivating force in the body of the world is the Covenant. If the Covenant is neglected, by what power can it move?

Subject: role of the Covenant in preserving unity
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/role of the Covenant in preserving unity.txt
Quotation: Among the distinctive features of this Dispensation of Baha'u'llah, which did not exist in previous dispensations, is that Baha'u'llah left no room for discord, for in His blessed day He took a covenant and testament by the pen of the Most High, designated the reference point for all, explicitly appointed the Interpreter of the Book, and closed the doors of interpretation. All must thank God that in this blessed Dispensation He has given rest to all and left no room for hesitation.

Subject: sacred remains; burial of the Bab
Quotation: During the following week, `Abdu'l-Baha informed us, The good news that I had promised is this: the sacred remains of the Exalted Bab have safely left the soil of Iran and just arrived in the Ottoman land.  They are now completely out of danger. After 50 years, what the Blessed Beauty promised has come to pass.

Subject: sacred remains; burial of the Bab
Quotation: Glorified is He Whom neither prison nor what He has endured from the people of hatred could frighten. He has delivered the messages of God, the Protector, the Self-Subsisting, while He was in the hands of His enemies and surrounded by hosts of polytheists.

Subject: sacred remains; burial of the Bab
Quotation: Similarly, a letter was written in my own hand to the handmaiden of Baha regarding the Most Holy Shrine, stating that on Naw-Ruz Day, with the utmost joy and gladness, the sacred remains were placed in the marble sarcophagus and, with great ceremony and majesty, were laid to rest in the Most Holy Shrine.

Subject: sacred remains; burial of the Bab
Quotation: In these days, through divine decree, the confirmation of the Lord of the highest heavens, and the grace of the invisible Kingdom, the sacred remains of the Bab have been laid to rest in their designated place on Mount Carmel in Haifa...The blessed body of the Martyred One has been entirely laid to rest on Mount Carmel.

Subject: sacred remains; burial of the Bab
Quotation: The friends in India deemed it advisable to send his sanctified remains to Iraq - ostensibly to Najaf but in reality to be interred somewhere in Iraq, in Baghdad and its surroundings. Finally the friends deemed it advisable to take them to the shrine of Salman-i-Farsi, five parasangs from Baghdad in Mada'in, to be buried there. They took them near the Arch of Ctesiphon to a very solid tomb. All the friends maintained vigil and with utmost reverence laid this divine trust to rest.

Subject: sacred remains; burial of the Bab
Quotation: Four years ago, through whatever means, that location was acquired and some minor arrangements were made to prepare it. Then special instructions were sent to Rangoon, multiple letters were written, and a design was drawn for a sarcophagus made of marble from that region which is renowned throughout the world. With great difficulty, an inlaid piece was completed and through various means transported here. You have surely heard what happened when it arrived in certain cities along the way. In short, it arrived some time ago along with a casket made of the finest Indian wood. A year ago, we specifically sent Jinab-i-Aqa Mirza Asadu'llah from here so that with a palanquin he could transport the pure body and holy temple and mighty throne - may my spirit be sacrificed for His dust - from Iran with complete reverence, humility, submission and respect, accompanied by several of the friends, arriving in the Holy Land.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Until the reality of sacrifice is realized and manifested in the essence of being, the lights of guidance will not shine forth from the supreme horizon and the dawning-place of 'or nearer.' That is, until the perishable aspects of contingent existence are consumed by the kindled fire of the Lord, the lights of the Abha Kingdom will not illumine the niche of the heart and the glass of the spirit.  "Kindle thou the fire of love and burn away all existence / Then take a step and enter the path of the lovers."  To sacrifice the body is easy, but to sacrifice the qualities emanating from the realm of existence, which are essential requirements of contingency, is difficult. In any case, we hope that thou wilt become a true sacrifice and offered up in the path of the Divine Beloved. And glory be upon thee and upon all who are firm and steadfast in God's Covenant and Testament.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: "some men sell their very souls" shows the greater excellence of pure devotion.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: that thou mayest sacrifice thyself with heart and soul in the path of the Lord

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Muhammad Taqi Khan and his companions voluntarily descend from safety to face certain death

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: O would that 'Abdu'l-Baha had freedom and could carry the clay for the building of that wall!

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: sacrifice your soul, spirit and peace of mind so that you may become the manifestation of divine grace from all directions

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Therefore, if you seek eternal life, become a martyr, and if you desire endless existence, become self-effacing and evanescent.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: In this day service at the sacred Threshold of the Blessed Beauty and steadfastness in His Cause is the real sacrifice of the self.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: This is just at the start for by the time one reaches the end of one's life one should have sacrificed oneself utterly in His Path.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: In any case, your endurance of these hardships is a sacrifice of life, and assuredly this sacrifice will yield the fruit of eternal joy.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Sacrifice this earthly frame for the Beloved of Heaven, and offer up this contingent temple as an oblation to the Beloved of the Placeless Realm

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Truly, thou didst endure great hardships in the path of God and didst kindle the lamp of the Most Truthful Name of God with the fire of the love of God.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: They sacrificed their souls in the manifest and straight Path... performed such deeds in the path of God as bewildered the hearts of those near unto Him

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Since you have stepped upon this path and drunk from this heavenly spring, you must freely give your life in the path of love for the Beloved of the worlds

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: "endured in Baha's path every hardship and affliction...they left no abuse except that they inflicted it upon your precious body and tortured you severely"

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: The body must be laid down for each step of spiritual progress, just as matter was taken up for each step of material progress. This is the law of sacrifice.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: "the Name of God, the Sacrifice, for he hath sacrificed himself in the path of his Lord in such wise as would be deemed worthy of mention in the straight path."

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: The Bahais should sacrifice life in the path of each other...One of the friends said: 'I am he' so that the Shah might kill him and the other friend might go free.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: so that sincere intention to serve the Cause of God would be kneaded into our nature and we would become helpless in our sacrifice - never resting or seeking comfort.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: "But this pride of men, since she gave her life in the path of the All-Merciful, her effects still endure and her mention continues in the gathering of divine friends."

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Here is my head, here is my heart, strike, strike hard this lifeless lover. This Dervish will gamble away his life in Thy path, 'Though the gift of life ill beseemeth the Beloved.

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Among the things I said, I disavowed any intention of amassing an army to wage wars, and stated that I had, rather, prepared an arena where people may lay down their lives [for this Faith].

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice
Quotation: Ye have borne in God's path that which none else hath borne...In truth, ye have heard taunts and witnessed abasement, and for the sake of God ye have renounced all that pertaineth to the world

Subject: sacrifice of self; mystery of sacrifice

Until the reality of sacrifice is realized and manifested in the essence of being, the lights of guidance will not shine forth from the supreme horizon and the dawning-place of "or nearer." I will give you an example by which to distinguish between the Giver of Bounties and mankind. Take the grain which you put in the earth; when the seed wants to be changed into a tree of course it sacrifices all of itself to the tree in order that it may be produced. Quotation: The Cause of Baha'u'llah is incomparable to any other cause; because it is the Collective Center of this age. This Cause regenerates the souls. Whereas formerly he was morally soiled, he becomes pure. Whereas formerly he was ignorant, he becomes wise. He is transformed entirely into the angelic state. Subject: second birth
Quotation: His Holiness Christ says in the Gospel, the one who is born of the flesh is flesh and the one who is born of the spirit is spirit. The interpretation of this verse is this, that physical things are like the body but the breaths of the Holy Spirit are the spirit (in the body). The body must live by the spirit, and therefore His Holiness Christ spoke of the second birth. What is the second birth? It is this: Man while in the matrix world is deprived of bounties. When ushered into this world from that of the matrix he finds himself the possessor of eyes, ears, physical powers, of intelligence. Although God gave all these bounties to man, in the matrix world they were not yet apparent. Only when born into this world did these divine bounties become manifest. Man then found that eyes had been given to him, that he was possessed of ears, and that powers which could discover all created things had been granted him. He saw the sun, and beheld the moon; he glanced at the sea, and witnessed the plains. A rose garden he saw, green and verdant. Of all these things he was unaware in the matrix world; of them he had no knowledge. In like manner must man be born out of this world of nature that he may enter into the world of the Kingdom. Unless he be born from this world he cannot attain to spiritual susceptibilities nor can he discover the mysteries of the Kingdom nor behold the realm of God. When in the matrix world man could receive no tidings of this world. In that world he was, rather, a denier of this world for had anyone said to him that there was a world other than that of the matrix, a world most vast and spacious, where a sun was shining everywhere, and a moon, where a rose garden grew in utmost beauty-had this been said to him he would have denied such news, saying: there is no world save this (the matrix) world. But when he is born he sees that this world is a different world. It is an infinite world, where stars are shining in the heaven and rivers are flowing toward the sea, where rose gardens are adornments and orchards are as embroidery.  Again, the human world is like the animal world. What does it (the animal world) know of the world of the Kingdom! What does it know of God, of spirituality, of divine bounties! When he is born from the world of nature then will man see the world of the Kingdom, then will he behold the lights of the Sun of Reality and will comprehend the manifestations of divine bounty. He will then be submerged in the sea of the lights of mercy and will understand the secrets of second birth. The holy, divine Manifestations of God had come for this purpose, that man may be informed of the Kingdom of the Lord of Hosts, that he may know divine realities and may attain to the second birth.

Quotation: O people! Subject: self-concealment of the Manifestation of God
Quotation: Until when the Cause reached unto His hallowed, sacred, exalted and luminous Countenance, He then concealed Himself behind a thousand veils, lest anyone should recognize Him thereafter, while verses were being sent down upon Him from every direction in such measure as none can reckon save God, thy Lord and the Lord of all worlds. When the time of concealment was fulfilled, We then revealed from behind a thousand thousand veils of light a light from the lights of the Youth's countenance, less than the eye of a needle, whereupon the people of the Supreme Concourse were thunderstruck, then the faces of them that are nigh fell prostrate.

Subject: self-concealment of the Manifestation of God
Quotation: I do not claim to have knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and earth, or knowledge of what has been or will be, nor do I say a word without what has been revealed in the Book and the text from the Imams of excellence. Turn people away from exaggeration regarding me, for God knows two groups will perish: an excessive lover and a hateful detractor. Their sin is not upon me, for I said before and say now before God, His Messengers and His friends that I am a servant who has believed in God and His signs. God has honored me by His grace as He willed with knowledge from the people of infallibility (God's blessings upon them) - as long as the Sun of Identity has risen with identity and the Sun of Oneness has not set with oneness.

Subject: self-concealment of the Manifestation of God
Quotation: certain people have attributed to this weak servant the station of being the Gate (Bab) of the Imam, peace be upon him, whereas I have never claimed nor do I claim such a thing. It is incumbent upon one who claims such a momentous matter that he be characterized by all perfect attributes, both theoretical and practical, and that he lack not any branch of knowledge or custom, and that he have complete and detailed mastery over all outward and inward sciences, and that there be no matter of divine grace or supernatural occurrence that is praiseworthy in God's sight except that he possess it definitively, not merely potentially - like the potential that God has placed in all things, whether essentially or accidentally - and if he lacks any single matter or branch of knowledge, there is no doubt that he is not the bearer of this mighty station. God Almighty and His holy ones bear witness that I am neither learned in nor capable of a single branch of the customary sciences or any supernatural occurrences. And if any words have flowed from my pen, they have been purely instinctual and entirely contrary to the rules of the people, and they do not constitute proof of anything. And whoever believes concerning this humble one that I hold the station of being the Gate of the Imam, peace be upon him - God is my witness that such a person is in error and will be in the fire in the hereafter. And in this document there is no dissimulation or concealment, rather my outer and inner being testify to what I have written, and God suffices as a witness to what I say.

Subject: self-description of God; God's self-remembrance
Quotation: After ascending to the heavens of inner meanings, the wayfarers attain to three stations, meaning that the manifest Sun shines and becomes revealed in the mirrors of existing things according to these three ranks, although some consider the ranks of determinations to be five and have named them the five presences. Were I to explain in detail, a book would not suffice and I would not be able to fulfill it, just as that divine mystic and knower of divine mysteries, the lordly Imam, mentioned a drop from these stations in defining the world of the heart, which has surely come to your noble attention - that the final rank of these three stations is the journey from God unto God. In this station and rank, existence is effaced from self and subsists through the Truth. All are from God and unto God shall they return, and "Say: All things are from God" is sufficient witness and adequate proof of this point, as the mystic of Rum has said:  "The seeker's attributes are annihilated in His attributes, While his essence remains through the survival of His Essence."  This station certainly has no laws and seeks no customs, meaning all His deeds are pure justice even if outwardly they appear as injustice, and pure knowledge even if in form they appear as ignorance.

Subject: self-description of God; God's self-remembrance
Quotation: From everlasting Thou hast been known to Thyself through Thyself alone, and Thou wilt forever continue to be as Thou wert in the eternal past, with none existing besides Thee.

Subject: self-description of God; God's self-remembrance
Quotation: God hath testified of His own Self by His own Self before the creation of His heaven and His earth that there is none other God but Him, the Single, the One, the Powerful, the All-Choosing.

Subject: self-description of God; God's self-remembrance
Quotation: Thou hast ever been, and shalt ever remain, the One Who uniteth Thy Essence with Thy Essence, Who paireth Thy Being with Thy Being, Who remembereth Thy Self through Thy Self, Who sanctifieth Thine Identity through Thine Identity, and Who magnifieth Thy camphor-like purity through Thy camphor-like purity.

Subject: self-description of God; God's self-remembrance
Quotation: It is a glorification wherewith Thou hast glorified Thine Own Essence, magnified Thine Own Being, exalted Thine Own Self, sanctified Thine Own Identity, and praised Thine Own Greatness. Subject: self-description of God; God's self-remembrance
Quotation: Thou hast ever been, and wilt ever be, sanctifying the pure essence of Thine Own Self through Thine Own Self, and glorifying the pristine reality of Thine Own Being through Thine Own Being, and unifying the essential nature of Thine Own Reality through Thine Own Reality, and magnifying the abstract nature of Thine Own Singleness through Thine Own Singleness.

Subject: self-description of God; God's self-remembrance
Quotation: Ever hast Thou been the Describer of Thine own Self unto Thyself, and the Unifier of Thine own Essence with Thine Essence. None besides Thee can comprehend Thy oneness or bear witness to Thy Self-Sufficiency, for Thou hast never been known through Thy creation nor described through Thy servants. When any besides Thee make mention of Thee, they but mention Thy creation, and when they unify Thee, they but acknowledge Thine invention.

Quotation: O servant of God!
