Subject: the Bab; the Primal Point; station and claims of the Bab
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the Bab; the Primal Point; station and claims of the Bab.txt
Quotation: One day the course of conversation Haji Sayad Javad said to me: 'I was a good friend of Haji Sayad Ali, the maternal uncle of the Bab. During my travellings I reached Bushir and inquired about him. They directed me to his office and to my chagrin I found that he has left for Shiraz but the Bab who was then in the efflorescence of his youth was appointed in his place to manage the business of the office. His mustache was just beginning to grow and the signs of manhood appearing in his whole being. As I looked into his young countenance I was wonder-struck with his spiritual dignity, stateliness of manners and the nobleness of his deportment. At the time his holiness was engaged in the business of indigo. After a short conversation I left him impressed with the loftiness of his ethical standard and the purity of his personal character.  Another day I called on him and while I was sitting in his presence several commission men entered the office. He received them with due courtesy and bade them to be seated. After a few preliminary remarks they broke the news that letters are being received from India that the market value of indigo has dropped one or two points. Other merchants were also present and they refuted strongly the assertion made by the commission agents. Pro and Con the conversation lasted for two hours, each side trying to down the other. While the bitter controversy was raging, the Bab sat silent and still and seemed to be not at all interested in the talk which has been going on with such animation. This was rather a crafty device for they intended to buy indigo from the Bab in the absence of his uncle at a lower price than the market value. When they finished their talk, one of them addressing him said: 'Malek-ottojjar has heard that you have in your office many boxes of indigo and he desires to buy some of them from you at the current price. Will you be kind enough to specify your terms?' Up to this moment the Bab had not said a word but now with the utmost calmness and dignity and with as few words and as simple as possible he told them the price and the terms by which the different installments were going to be paid. Loudly and vociferously they protested against the high price and the terms, as it was their wont stating that there must be a reduction. He listened to their words silently and at last getting exasperated at his serene imperturbability they cried: 'What is your wish?' He answered: 'I have already told you. Have I to repeat again the same propositions?' Now they were indeed exasperated. 'What is this new custom?' they bemoaned. 'We have an inherent right to bargain. This shall never be. Are you going to dictate to us? Do you, a young man, know the commercial laws of the country better than we do? Who has ever heard of such strict adherence to one idea? We will not have it. we warn you that if you want to carry on business amongst us you must change this novel, peculiar custom, otherwise no one will approach your office! The Bab just looked into their faces and did not answer them. When they got tired with their harangues and realized that their words produced not the slightest effect they left the office with disgust and grumblings. In an hour they were back with a message from Malek-Ottojjar that he says the price of this indigo is quite high and he begs him to make at least a slight reduction for his sake. 'I have stated in so many words' he said 'the last fixed price and reduction is an impossibility. You are wasting your precious time uselessly.' The commission men were beside themselves with fury and attributed this one-sidedness to his stubbornness and obstinancy. Seeing how futile would be their rage they betook themselves away but soon returned in a chastened mood that the buyer has surrendered and would like to have so many cases. The full terms were drawn up and the cases of indigo were transferred to the store of Malek-ottojjar. A few days passed and in order to gain their point they turned another leaf of double-dealing and pretended the papers were tampered with and certain conditions were incorporated therein by the force of circumstance. Boisterous and noisy they came to the Bab, shouting for a considerable reduction of price and insisting that it must be done immediately. Without heeding their heated protestations he gently said: 'Are you not satisfied with our former stipulations?' They all answered: "Of course not. We are duped, we are hoodwinked!" "Very well, then, you may send back the goods." "What! Sending back the goods!" Who has ever heard of such a thing! You are insulting the dignity and honor of Malek-ottojjar.' (the King of the merchants.) 'Then you do not intend to send them back.' 'No, indeed. We will be considered worse than fools.' Calmly turning only his face to his servant he said: 'Go and take with thyself a number of porters. Call at the store of Malek-ottojjar and ask, in my name, for the cases of indigo. Do not return till you bring them.' The men were so stupefied at this thunderous command that they could not utter a sound and preferred to sit there and see the result. In an hour they were more than amazed to see the servant back with the goods.  This incident was widely circulated in Bushir that Mirza Ali Mohamad has had the daring and courage to precipitate a commercial altercation with the King of the merchants and that his career will be brought to an end by the secret machinations of the powerful man whose dignity has been so sorely wounded. The intimate friends of Aga Sayad Ali called and begged him to go to the enraged man and beg his apology and pardon, intimating that the result of this injured feeling will probably be ruinous to the trade of his uncle. The Bab listened to their advice and said simply:- 'Do not worry about our business. There [is] a God who will protect it from all outside encroachments.

Quotation: Among the people are those who object that "thou dost claim a different station each day". Say: Yea, by My Lord! I am, at every moment, in a new condition, and I desire not to remain fixed in any station. I beseech God to raise Me at every instant to a station more exalted than before. Without this, the essence of My heart would not be content, were ye but to know. Say: This remembrance is not from Me except according to your capacity. Otherwise, God hath established Me in a station that knoweth neither increase nor decrease. Whatsoever appeareth from Me, God manifesteth it by His command according to a prescribed measure, lest the hearts of the unitarians be disturbed.  Remember, O people, when the Revealer of the Bayan came to you with novel and holy verses, saying: "I am the Gate of Knowledge, and whoso believeth concerning Me more than this hath indeed fabricated a calumny and earned for himself a grievous sin." Then He said: "I am verily the promised Qa'im Whose appearance was promised you in sacred scrolls." Then did He, exalted be His remembrance, declare: "I am the Primal Point, which is indeed Muhammad, the Messenger of God, as ye have heard and witnessed in the Tablets of God, the Sovereign, the All-Wise." When the essence of certain souls had been elevated, He then rent asunder the veil and rose from the Holy Dayspring, proclaiming: "I am God, there is no God but Me, your Lord and the Lord of all worlds. I am He Who, from the beginning that hath no beginning, hath been one God, Single, Unique, Alone, Self-Subsisting. I have taken neither partner, nor likeness, nor vizier, nor peer. I have sent Prophets and Messengers from the beginning of beginnings and shall continue to send them unto the end of endings."

Subject: the Bab; the Primal Point; station and claims of the Bab

Quotation: By thy life, this Cause is more wondrous than the Cause of Muhammad, the Apostle of God, would ye but ponder it. Say: He was raised up at a time when he had attained unto forty years of age, and the Book was revealed unto him over twenty-three years, until God established the truth through His signs. Verily He hath power over all things. He was raised up among those who speak the tongue of the Qur'an and glory therein. But God, my Lord, hath manifested me after I had attained twenty-five years of age, as a mercy from His presence. Verily He hath been gracious unto me. God hath opened unto me the gates of all verses, that I might recite them as I please, by His leave. Verily He is nigh unto me. By thy life, if We willed, We could manifest it in the space of two nights and two days, to the measure of the Qur'an. Thus doth God cause to ascend whomsoever He willeth by His command.

Quotation: I said truly how ignorant people are to praise such a display. Christ suffered all manner of tribulations and calamities, wandering alone and destitute day and night in the wilderness, his food was herbs, thorns on his head, the stars of heaven his lamp, every day wandering in a desert. Now these people in the utmost pomp and glory make merry in great monasteries which are better than palaces and say 'We are the disciples of Christ.' A disciple must follow the teacher so that all his ways and conduct conform to the teachings of the master, but these people have great establishments, many endowments and revenues, and are immersed day and night in all manner of desires. Where are those breathings of detachment of Christ?

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: Prayer praising and seeking blessings for 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, the fourth Imam, including references to "the Imams who came before him and after him"

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: And cause his heart to be well-pleased with Thee, his spirit with Thy Prophet, his soul with his chosen forefathers and then with the Imams after him, the pure ones

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is no God but Him, and that those who are witnesses after Muhammad, these are, after the Primal Point, twelve stars - all are assured of them.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: We drink not from the outward cups except as those who affirm that they who were witnesses after Muhammad - these are the Imams of Truth, and these are they who draw proof from God.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: And as to 'the Spirit' mentioned in His words 'The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter' - this referreth to the Qa'im (the Promised One), while by 'the angels' are meant the Imams.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: And I bear witness that Ali and [the other] successors of the Messenger and proofs of God over all that is in the heavens and earth, all of them together, they are honored servants who speak not before Him and act by His command.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: O Husayn! Consider the eagerness with which certain peoples and nations have anticipated the return of Imam-Husayn, whose coming, after the appearance of the Qa'im, hath been prophesied, in days past, by the chosen ones of God, exalted be His glory.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: I bear witness before God and those with Him that I am content with Ali, Fatima, Hussein, Hassan, Ali ibn Hussein, Muhammad ibn Ali, Jafar ibn Muhammad, Musa ibn Jafar, Ali ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ali, Ali ibn Muhammad, Hassan ibn Ali, and Muhammad ibn Hassan as Imams

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: As for the transmitted tradition that there are twelve Imams from His Holiness the Commander [Ali] to Muhammad ibn Hasan, and the second tradition that there are twelve Imams from the lineage of His Holiness Ali and Her Holiness Fatima - there is contradiction between these two traditions.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: Regarding what you wrote about revelation, the holy Imams were the dawning-places of inspiration and the manifestations of the grace of the All-Merciful. Revelation was specific to the Messenger of God, therefore we do not call the words of the holy Imams the Word of God, rather we consider them divine inspiration.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: And these seven have manifestations in the station of the revelation of the Essence, Attributes, Deeds and Worship, which yield from the Word twenty-eight stations, corresponding to the letters of existence through which all being, both unseen and seen, is established. And none hath any portion therein save as God hath ordained for them.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: Verily the Pillars circle round the body of Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, and the Chiefs circle round the heart of the Pillars, and the Nobles circle round the Chiefs. The Pillars look upon all things yet see naught but God alone. The Chiefs look through all things and see the Lord with them. The Nobles look through all things and see the Lord beyond them.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: O God! Send peace upon the repositories of His knowledge, the vessels of His wisdom, the pillars of His prophethood, and the dwellings of His blessing - Thy servants whom Thou hast chosen for Thy religion, approved for Thy mystery, and selected for Thy knowledge, whom Thou hast described in Thy Book, saying - and Thy word is the truth - "honored servants who speak not until He hath spoken, and who act by His command."

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: Glory be to God! If this station were to be revealed, all would testify that the Truth, exalted be His glory, hath had and hath no partner or likeness. The company of the chosen ones have been and are created by His Word, and the station of man is this most exalted Word: We possess for ourselves neither benefit nor harm, neither life nor resurrection. The abominable Shi'ihs each day diminished from the station of the Truth and added to their own.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: The Imams of religion, through their own selves, demonstrate through wisdom; through their manifestations, demonstrate through counsel; and through their names, demonstrate through disputation in the most excellent manner. And verily the one who beholds the station of the Divine Essence and dwells in the kingdom of Names and Attributes, were he to witness the manifestations of the Universal Guardianship, would be able to prove by every aspect attributed to them their absolute guardianship over all created things.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: Regarding the question of the revered mystic His Holiness Safi 'Ali Shah, may God perpetuate his glory and existence, concerning the wisdom behind the number twelve among the guiding stars, the pure Imams (peace be upon them from the Lord of creation) in the dispensation of His Holiness the Seal of the Prophets (greetings and peace be upon Him), numerous utterances flowed from the blessed tongue which cannot be fully described, for what emerged from His sweet utterance in response to this question transcends comprehension's grasp and reason's explanation.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: The second is the Book of Ali, peace be upon him, wherein God hath ordained the laws of absolute sovereignty pertaining to him, and it is the Paradise of Unity. The fourth is the Book of Hassan, peace be upon him, wherein are written his laws and the laws of his followers. The fifth is the Book of Hussein, peace be upon him - may my soul be sacrificed for him - wherein are the laws concerning himself. The sixth is the Book of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, wherein is written whatsoever God hath willed concerning him. The seventh is the Book of Musa ibn Ja'far, peace be upon them both, wherein is written all that God hath willed concerning him.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: This is the Temple of Ali, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Hasan, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Husayn, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Ali, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Muhammad, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Jafar, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Musa, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Ali, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Muhammad, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Ali, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Hasan, the great and righteous Imam. This is the Temple of Muhammad, the great and righteous Imam.

Subject: the Imamate; the Caliphate
Quotation: On this, that 'Ali, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that Hasan, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that Husayn, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that 'Ali the Son of Husayn, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that Muhammad the Son of 'Ali, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that Ja'far the Son of Muhammad, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that Musi the Son of Ja'far, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that 'Ali the Son of Musa, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that Muhammad the Son of 'Ali, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that 'Ali the Son of Muhammad, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world... On this, that Hasan the Son of 'Ali, peace be upon Him, hath returned to the world...

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: I call people to the Kingdom of God

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Turn day and night to the Kingdom of Abha. Supplicate for boundless favors from that Kingdom.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: that thou mayest witness a goodly life and an eternal existence in the Most Glorious Kingdom and observe manifest signs

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Our real happiness is in the Kingdom. Therefore we must know what happiness exists in the Other world, and not in this.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: He would be so beauteous if the light of God could shine upon him and so wise were he was to seek the knowledge of the Kingdom.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: O thou who art looking for the Kingdom of God! The spacious Kingdom was newly adorned, and like unto paradise, manifested beautiful scenes.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: entrance into the Kingdom of Baha'u'llah. The Glory of man is through the Love of God, entrance into his Kingdom and being imbued with his divine characteristics.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: successful in attaining the gifts of the Kingdom...so that when we ascend to the Kingdom we may attain Your presence and be joyous and glad in the Supreme Concourse

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: They have become weary of the earthly world and seek the pure realm, the luminous kingdom...They have been freed from this world and have taken flight to Your realm

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Know thou that the Kingdom of heaven belongeth to such tender plants of the Abha Paradise, and the grace of the Realm of Might is for these children of the school of Divine love.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: If you open the eye of the soul and gaze upon the Kingdom of the Beloved, you will observe that this is a letter of freedom by which you will gain admittance to the divine Kingdom

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Know thou that the realm of the Kingdom belongeth to the newcomers to the Garden of Abha, and the bounties of the realm of divinity are for the children in the school of divine love.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: We are helpless birds with broken wings, yet we desire to soar in the realm of the Kingdom... Make our tongues eloquent and our eyes seeing, that we may behold the realm of the Kingdom

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: May thine eyes be opened to the Greater Signs, and mayest thou become intimate with the mysteries of the Self-Sufficient Lord, and in all conditions mayest thou ever soar to the Abha Kingdom.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: One must attend to the affairs of this world only to the extent necessary and spend the remaining time on the Kingdom of God, so that eternal illumination may be attained and everlasting permanence secured

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Turn your gaze to the Most Glorious Horizon and fix your eyes on the Supreme Kingdom. Whatever is the ultimate desire of the unitarians will be attained, and whatever is the greatest gift of the Lord of the Worlds will be achieved.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: although thou art living on the face of the earth, yet thou mayest truly be in heaven; that although outwardly thou art composed of material elements, yet spiritually thou mayest become composed of heavenly elements. This is the everlasting glory of man! This is the eternal sublimity in the world of existence!

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Bind thy heart to the Most Glorious Beloved - may my spirit and my very essence be sacrificed for His loved ones - that thou mayest attain attachment to the Supreme Companion and enter the Most Glorious Paradise, the songful Garden, and the verdant orchards, and be seated upon the throne of sovereignty at the very heart of Paradise.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: These are they who rejoice in the meeting with God in their first life, and in the hereafter they shall abide beneath the shadow of His favor. They shall ride upon the lightning of light and journey in the atmosphere of Paradise, enjoying the holy bounties. They shall drink the wine of eternity from hands of luminous glory and shall dwell in the highest pavilion among the concourse of the near ones.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: The nightingale will soar toward the Rose-garden of Eternity and on the branches of the Tree of Life it shall perch, singing sweetly the songs of Freedom and Peace... Within the breast of this nightingale, a hundred thousand heart-rejoicing songs are hidden! Once out of the cage, it shall wing its way toward the Horizon of Everlasting glory and there join its heavenly voice with the celestial choir, ever singing, ever singing, never dreaming of return.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Today the existing souls in the world, despite their outward life, are reckoned as dead in the sight of God, for those possessed of true life are souls who have attained unto the recognition of God. They are the possessors of eternal life and everlasting existence. And those dead who have received their portion from the breezes of revelation and the fragrances of inspiration, and have drunk from the Kawthar of recognition from the hand of bounty - they are alive and enduring in the sight of God.

Subject: the Kingdom of God [Malakut]
Quotation: Make the Abha Kingdom thy perspective and the highest heaven thy destination. Fix thy gaze upon the horizon of glory and turn thy attention to the heaven of bounty. All directions and quarters belong to the realm of place, but the Abha Kingdom is sanctified above directions. All rising points exist in the contingent world, but that eternal kingdom exists in the placeless realm. Every region and kingdom is bounded, but that enduring kingdom is abstract and distinct.

Subject: the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace.txt
Quotation: Praise be to God, signs of awakening have appeared in some people - it is the beginning of the dawn of the Most Great Peace. A Supreme Tribunal will be established, and difficulties arising between nations and peoples will be resolved in that Supreme Tribunal.

Subject: the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace.txt
Quotation: Today the most important of all matters in the human world is the question of universal peace, which is the greatest means for life and happiness of humankind. Without this radiant truth, humanity will never find true rest nor progress, but rather day by day calamity and misfortune will increase.

Subject: the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace.txt
Quotation: Today the greatest service to the Kingdom of God is promoting human unity and serving universal peace...They are the cause of death while you are the cause of life...And among the greatest teachings of Baha'u'llah is universal peace which is the cause of comfort and tranquility for humanity...Today the greatest foundation of the Kingdom of God is promoting universal peace and the unity of the human world.

Subject: the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the Lesser Peace and the Most Great Peace.txt
Quotation: Eventually it will be firmly established through the power of Baha'u'llah. Although the representatives of governments have assembled in Paris to establish the foundation of universal peace and bestow comfort and tranquility upon the human world, yet misunderstanding still prevails and self-interest remains. Therefore, universal peace will not easily manifest and new difficulties will arise, for intentions are not in harmony - rather, desires are different.

Subject: the Twelfth Imam; the Qa'im
Quotation: Say: The appearance of the Qa'im from God on the Day of Resurrection is that Day wherein God will distinguish all things with truth, until no living soul shall remain among men save to the number of the Face.

Subject: the Twelfth Imam; the Qa'im
Quotation: God hath made manifest the Qaim in the true Faith from His presence. Therefore present thyself before the Letters of Truth and strive in the presence of the first to pledge allegiance to the mighty Arabian Muhammad.

Subject: the Twelfth Imam; the Qa'im
Quotation: Say: The appearance of the Qa'im from God on the Day of Resurrection is that wherein God will judge between all things with truth, until there remaineth not among men the spirit of life save in the number of the face.

Subject: the Twelfth Imam; the Qa'im
Quotation: And as to 'the Spirit' mentioned in His words 'The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter' - this referreth to the Qa'im (the Promised One), while by 'the angels' are meant the Imams.

Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the Word of God; influence and centrality of.txt
