Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: The surge and motion of this current is not bound by time or moment at all. In less than the twinkling of an eye it reaches from the lowest realm to the highest realm, and instantly arrives from the highest realm to the lowest realm. Its wire is the knowledge of God and its components are the love of God. Its force and penetration set the worlds in motion and its influence endures forever.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: From it flashed forth the lights of might and fellowship and glory, And the fires appeared on Mount Sinai. Through it were raised all thrones, then they became inaccessible, And the All-Merciful was established upon the throne of the mighty Command. From it were stirred the winds of the Spirit from the dawning-place of eternity, And through it surged the oceans of light and brought forth pearls.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: Its radiance in every mirror appears according to that mirror's color. Thus when it shone forth in the mirrors of the hearts of the philosophers, wisdom became manifest. Likewise when it cast its rays upon the hearts of craftsmen, wondrous and exalted arts appeared. And when it dawned in the hearts of the mystics, the wonders of divine knowledge and the mysteries of heavenly utterance were revealed.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: That concealed Word upon which the souls of all the Messengers of God and His Chosen Ones have ever depended hath manifested itself out of the invisible world into the visible plane. So great was the wondrous grace which pervaded all things that through the utterance of the letters "B" and "E" the gems that lay hid within the repositories of this contingent world were brought forth and made manifest.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: All created things are made manifest through the light of that Sun. Were it not for the Sun's light, no created thing would become manifest - all would remain hidden. Indeed, the very life of earthly creation depends upon the light and heat of the Sun, and all things, even to the smallest particles on earth, benefit from its rays and heat. Yet each created thing receives according to its own capacity and worthiness.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: Through Our bounty were created the heavens and what lieth above them of the Throne and what lieth above it of the Seat, and the angels in the heavens who glorify God with Our remembrance and who praise Us. Through Our bounty were created fire and air, then water and earth - by these are all things created. Through Our bounty were created the earth and the seas, then the mountains and what was created therein of minerals.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: Just as the rays of the sun shine upon all earthly things, yet none of these things is the sun itself--though indeed they exist by virtue of the sun--so also all created things appear through the holy outpourings and the divine effulgences of the First Cause, yet none of them is identical to that Reality. The difference between God and His creation is thus essential and not merely nominal, fundamental and not merely imaginal.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: And so the waters of existence descend from the heaven of Thy Oneness and Thou hast caused the showers of Thine Eternal Bounties to rain down from the clouds of the heaven of Thy Mighty Oneness until, through this most mighty Beneficence, the rivers of Thy most wondrous Grace flowed forth upon the soil of all possible existent realities in Thine act of Creation. All lands and regions were watered by these streaming, heavenly rivers.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: The power of divine bounty is like a flood that no barrier can withstand and no cloud can prevent, for it is an undoubted outpouring descending from the invisible Kingdom - a torrential rain and falling waters. It has caused commotion in all regions and trembling in the pillars of the deprived nations. The pulse of contingent being has quickened, and the divine spirit has so permeated that the body of the world has been thrown into ecstasy and joy.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: Then the breeze of the holy east wind blew from the Sheba of true paradise, bearing a fine, perfumed mist from the locks of that spiritual houri. At that moment, several droplets of luminous wine from the spring of the beauty of the All-Merciful condensed in that mist, and the hand of immortal power became manifest from the hidden treasury of sovereign grace. It kneaded that numinous mist into the sweet water of light, then breathed a pre-existent breath into it.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: Glory be to Him Who originates whatsoever He willeth by His command, and when He desireth a thing, before He saith unto it Be!, it already existeth. Praise be to God Who hath manifested Himself to all essences through the light of His Eternal Countenance, without limitation in His Essence, nor location in His Attributes, nor comparison in His Examples, causing all to be bewildered in the stations of Command and Creation according to what God hath willed and ordained.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: When the self-subsistent Living God manifested Himself with all His Names, Attributes, Perfections and Characteristics to the people of the Universe, and illuminated the Dawning-place of the contingent world with the Lights of the orb of the Placeless and raised fervency and clamour within every component atom of the world of Creation, then the Shower of Mercy began to fall, the rays of the Sun gleamed, the refreshing zephyr blew and the Voice of God reached the ears.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: This is the mercy that gives without being asked and bestows upon all contingent and created things, from their beginning to their end, whether concealed or manifest. This is the mercy that preceded all things that were and will be in the worlds of creation, and through this all-encompassing mercy, the universal lordship of the True Educator is made manifest to all who are in the heavens and earth. Through it, all things are sustained, all things are provided for, and all things are given before they ask or desire or will.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: And praise be to God Who hath sent down from the dark clouds of His Will all that existeth in need of divine ordinances, heavenly verses, signs of sovereignty and dominion, and tokens of the earthly realm, so that none might need another in any matter, and each might behold what God hath intended for him throughout all regions and witness what God hath ordained in the worlds of detachment - like the manifestation of His Self in His Self and His manifestations in His signs, as God hath revealed to each thing according to its station.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: Although outwardly the showers of divine mercy have, according to desert, been withheld from the peoples of the world, yet the true rains from the spiritual heaven are ever pouring down and flowing forth - these are the missives of grace and love that have continuously arrived and continue to arrive from the branches of the Divine Lote-Tree and His loved ones. The rains of love have another heaven, another cloud, and another earth. Its earth is hearts and minds, its heaven the favor of the Beloved, and its cloud the will and purpose of the Sovereign of hearts.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: Then He brought forth the latter creation through an all-encompassing grace and a brilliant ray from the Sun of Truth that shines and illumines the horizons with the light of dawning. He spread the carpet of eternal glory, whereby through His abundant outpouring grace the gardens of signs are adorned and the pools of mysteries overflow. He sent the winds of prosperity bearing glad tidings of His mercy to all souls, and caused the clouds of success to rain upon the valleys and hills in the realm of forms. Thus did the light and warmth that emanated from the Luminary of mysteries influence all regions.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: However, I will fully submit and confirm this when, upon turning my attention to that region, its musk-laden breeze and amber-scented air wafts from the rose garden of the highest paradise, perfuming the nostrils of the soul and the consciousness with ambergris. That sweet fragrance is the diffusion of the divine breaths and the showering of the rain of God's guidance. It is the shining forth of the lights of truth and the manifestation of the mysteries of the Divine Unity. It is the arrival of the waves of the ocean of grace and the tempest of love for the Lord of the House of Divinity. It is the dawning of the Sun of Reality and the manifestation of the signs and tokens of the Lord, the King of Divinity.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: The clouds of divine bounty bestow blessings on all. It is sanctified of exclusivity. Showers of divine bounty and confirmation are always falling; if any spot experiences a suspension or delay, other areas shall receive these effusions.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: He bestowed eternal life and granted everlasting bounties generously and abundantly. Consider what a cup full of nectar He bestowed on His friends and what an effervescent wine He graciously gave. That is from God's grace which He bestows on whom He wishes, and God is possessed of mighty grace.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: This mercy is divided into two kinds: One kind is termed the all-encompassing mercy, the universal mercy, the all-embracing mercy, the treasured mercy, the absolute mercy, the all-surrounding mercy... This is the mercy that giveth without being asked and bestoweth upon all contingent and created things, from beginning to end, whether hidden or manifest, more comprehensive than what is concealed or revealed. The other kind is termed the limited mercy, the restricted mercy, and similar terms, and from this mercy there descendeth from the clouds of justice the rain of bounty after the supplication of servants in the world of existence.

Subject: the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the divine emanation; the all-pervading bounty of God.txt
Quotation: If an ant desired to interpret the Qur'an's inner meaning and the inner meaning of its inner meaning, it would be able to do so, for the impenetrable divine mystery has penetrated into the reality of all created things.

Subject: the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving.txt
Quotation: The Teachings of His Holiness Baha'u'llah declare the oneness of the world of humanity; cause religion to be the foundation of union and accord in the world; become conducive to good fellowship among the children of men; conform religion with science and reason; take away political prejudices and race prejudices; uphold the doctrine of perfect equality between men and women; espouse the cause of an international auxiliary language; foster the universalization of education; readjust and equalize in the most perfect manner the economic relations of the social structure; destroy totally the basis of hostility and ill-will from amongst mankind; constitute the five continents as one continent; suffer the various races of men to become as one race; rend asunder entirely the veils of superstitions; reveal in the assemblage of humanity the light of Truth; illumine the hearts with the rays of guidance; resurrect the spirits with the breaths of the Holy Spirit, and baptize the souls with the water of Life Eternal, the fire of the love of God and the outpouring of the Divine Spirit.

Subject: the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving.txt
Quotation: Among them are (the teachings) concerning the question of economics that all the members of the body politic may enjoy through the working out of this solution the greatest happiness, welfare and comfort without any harm or injury attacking the general order of things...In every village there must be established a general storehouse which will have a number of revenues.

Subject: the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving.txt
Quotation: In solving this problem we must start with the farmer and end with other trades, because there are twice as many farmers, if not more, as there are people engaged in other trades. Thus it is right that we begin with them. The farmer is the primary factor in society. In every village a council of wise men of the village should be established and the whole village should be placed under its jurisdiction. In addition, a public treasury should be established with its own administrator. At harvest time a specific quantity of the general produce of the village should be appropriated for the treasury. This treasury will have seven sources of income, namely: tithes, taxes on livestock, unclaimed inheritance, property that has been found but that has no owner, buried treasure (if found, one third of it should be paid to the council), mines (one-third of the natural resources taken should be levied by the council) and donations. Likewise, there are to be seven categories of expenditure: first, moderate public expenditures such as the expenses of the council and maintenance of public health; second, payment of government taxes; third, payment of taxes on livestock to the government; fourth, care of orphans; fifth, providing for the disabled; sixth, management of schools; and seventh, providing the necessary means of livelihood for the poor.

Subject: the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving.txt
Quotation: The solution of this problem is one of the fundamental principles of his holiness Baha'o'llah. But it must be solved with justice and not with force. If this problem is not solved lovingly it will result in war. Perfect communism and equality are an impossibility because they would upset the affairs and the order of the world. But there is a fair method which will not leave the poor in such need, nor the rich in such wealth.

Subject: the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving.txt
Quotation: For instance, God commands, 'But [they] prefer them [the poor] before themselves, although there be indigence among them.' That is, the believers spend of their substance and share their possessions and prefer others to themselves willingly and with utmost spirituality. Socialists, however, desire to enforce equality and association by compulsion. Although the preference for others which is the exhortation of God is more difficult because the rich are enjoined to prefer others to them-selves, this will become common and will be the cause of tranquillity and an aid to the order of the world, because it depends upon the inclination and willingness of the giver. But socialism and egalitarianism, although easier, as those who have are made equal with others, yet such a system will not become widespread and is the cause of disturbance and tumult because it rests on compulsion and coercion.

Subject: the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving.txt
Quotation: Q: Will the money of the rich ever be divided among the people without revolution or bloodshed? Will some men amass great fortunes in the future while others remain poor? Will the law prevent this condition of affairs?   A:  It will not be possible in the future for men to amass great fortunes by the labor of others. The rich will willingly divide. They will come to this gradually, naturally, by their own volition. It will never be accomplished by war and bloodshed. The ruling power or government cannot treat the rich unjustly. To force them to divide their wealth would be unjust. In the future, proportionately about three-quarters of the profits will go to the workmen and one-quarter to the owner. This condition will prevail in about one century. It will certainly come to pass.

Subject: the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the economic problem and its solution; voluntary giving.txt
Quotation: "Human perfection lies in voluntary good deeds, not in compelled good deeds. And beneficence is voluntary goodness, which means that the wealthy should show beneficence to the poor - that is, give to the poor, but of their own free will, not that the poor should compel the wealthy."

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: Shall a man's wealth endure forever, or protect him from the One Who shall, erelong, seize him by his forelock? Gazing upon those who sleep beneath the gravestones, embosomed in the dust, could one ever distinguish the sovereign's crumbling skull from the subject's mouldering bones? Nay, by Him Who is the King of kings! Could one discern the lord from the vassal, or those that enjoyed wealth and riches from those who possessed neither shoes nor mat? By God! Every distinction hath been erased, save only for those who upheld the right and who ruled with justice. Whither are gone the learned men, the divines and potentates of old? What hath become of their discriminating views, their shrewd perceptions, their subtle insights and sage pronouncements? Where are their hidden coffers, their flaunted ornaments, their gilded couches, their rugs and cushions strewn about? Gone forever is their generation! All have perished, and, by God's decree, naught remaineth of them but scattered dust. Exhausted is the wealth they gathered, dispersed the stores they hoarded, dissipated the treasures they concealed. Naught can now be seen but their deserted haunts, their roofless dwellings, their uprooted tree-trunks, and their faded splendour. No man of insight will let wealth distract his gaze from his ultimate objective, and no man of understanding will allow riches to withhold him from turning unto Him Who is the All-Possessing, the Most High. Where is he who held dominion over all whereon the sun shineth, who lived extravagantly on earth, seeking out the luxuries of the world and of all that hath been created upon it? Where is the commander of the swarthy legion and the upraiser of the golden standard? Where is the ruler of Zawra', and where the tyrant of Fayha'? Where are those before whose munificence the treasure-houses of the earth shrank in shame, and at whose largesse and swelling spirit the very ocean was abashed? Where is he who stretched forth his arm in rebellion, and who turned his hand against the All-Merciful? Where are they who went in quest of earthly pleasures and the fruits of carnal desires? Whither are fled their fair and comely women? Where are their swaying branches, their spreading boughs, their lofty mansions, their trellised gardens? And what of the delights of these gardens--their exquisite grounds and gentle breezes, their purling streams, their soughing winds, their cooing doves and rustling leaves? Where now are their resplendent morns and their brightsome countenances wreathed in smiles? Alas for them! All have perished and are gone to rest beneath a canopy of dust. Of them one heareth neither name nor mention; none knoweth of their affairs, and naught remaineth of their signs.

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: Everything shall perish save His Face. Therefore, strive as much as thou canst to attain unto that which endureth

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: Hasten to eternal life! Hasten to everlasting salvation! Hasten to eternal permanence! Hasten to everlasting life!

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: Contrast between the eternal divine realm and temporal physical world: "The eternal beauty and divine countenance undergo no change or alteration"

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: One must attain eternal life and seek everlasting sovereignty...Even in this transient world his traces remain firm and enduring, his mention continues, and his light spreads.

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: He is not content with temporary life but seeks eternal life. He does not remain in nature's darkness but yearns for the Kingdom of light. Therefore be not content with this fleeting life. Seek a life that has no end. Seek a glory that is eternal.

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: Man must spend his talent in a cause the result of which is eternal. If he breaths one breath in the path of God, it will immortalize him throughout ages and cycles. If he writes a poem or a book on the Cause of God they will bring forth eternal fruits.

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: However, in the City of God he laid one brick, and that brick endured and will not be destroyed. This brick he laid in the City of God, and it will never be destroyed. This trace of his will remain forever in the divine edifice. Every foundation will ultimately be ruined except the divine foundation. This is how it is - every foundation is ruined except the foundation of Truth, except the foundation of the beloved ones of God.

Subject: the ephemeral and the eternal
Quotation: The days of this world, its life and existence, which are altered by a mere yellow wind and return to nothingness - to these have they clung so tenaciously that they have passed by the immortal divine Kingdom and remain occupied with their own desires in the wilderness of heedlessness and the desert of error, until they return to their final resting place. How many kings and dwellers of palaces have in an instant returned to their graves! Well was it said: A crier called out to them after they were buried: Where are the couches, the crowns, and the robes? At every moment, how many possessors of wealth and might go forth in utter abasement and great fear. This divine decree is inscribed in clear script upon the tablet of all existence, high and low: All things are perishing save His face.

Subject: the first and the last; the seen and the hidden
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the first and the last; the seen and the hidden.txt
Quotation: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden.

Subject: the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others.txt
Quotation: and they desire not for anyone save what they would desire for themselves.

Subject: the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others.txt
Quotation: It must be so that each friend should prefer others to himself; the others should be first to him...His Holiness Christ said: 'Do unto others..', but his Holiness Baha'u'llah says--Prefer him to thyself.

Subject: the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others.txt
Quotation: "In all the Books, both past and future, He hath commanded that the unitarians and those who have turned towards Him should prefer others over themselves. They should make their paramount concern the vindication of truth and the elimination of falsehood, and should choose for their brethren what they choose for themselves."

Subject: the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others.txt
Quotation: "Those souls who prefer themselves to others are tied with selfish iron-bonds but those who prefer others to themselves are the benefactors of human race."

Subject: the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the golden rule; regard for one's neighbor; doing unto others.txt
Quotation: The people of the world are thinking of, by, and for themselves. They are promoting their own selfish interests and serving their own small causes. Each soul is attached to his own hobby and beating his own drum and soaring in the atmosphere of his own desire. In brief all their movements are dictated by obedience to self. They live, move and feel like unto the animals, self-centred, self-occupied, seeing nothing, believing in nothing beyond their five senses.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: The human spirit, in other words the rational soul, in the world of existence is the intermediary between things corporeal and delimited worldly things; that is to say, between realities spiritual and things corporeal.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: The human spirit is a divine trust which must traverse every degree, for traversing and passing through the degrees of existence is the means of its acquiring perfections. Moreover, it is necessary that the signs of the perfections of the spirit appear in this world, that the realm of creation may bring forth endless fruits and that this body of the contingent world may receive life and manifest the divine bounties.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: God has created all earthly things under a law of progression in material degrees, but He has created man and endowed him with powers of advancement toward spiritual and transcendental kingdoms. He has brought forth everything necessary for the life of this world, but man is a creation intended for the reflection of divine virtues.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: Consider, just as the rays of the sun illumine the earth, in the same way, the soul illumines bodies. It is the soul which makes man heavenly; it is the soul which enables man to benefit from the outpourings of the Holy Spirit; it is his soul which discovers the realities of things; it is his soul which has manifested all these signs; it is his soul which has established these sciences; it is the soul which bestows eternal life; it is the soul which unifies opposing nations; it is the soul which brings East and West together, and turns the human world into a heavenly world.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: The human spirit is a power which comprehends the realities of things...the human spirit is a comprehensive energy and controls the realities of things and discovers the hidden secrets in the domain of the physical world

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: It cannot be said that the ethereal soul hath entered and penetrated this body, for the former is immaterial while the latter is bound by the restraints of time and space. Egress and regress, ascent and descent, setting and rising, dissolution and composition are properties of the body, not the soul. Despite its visible traces, evident signs, manifest attributes, and clear effects, the soul as it is in itself remaineth invisible and concealed. Its center is hidden and its origin is beyond any indication.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: In regard to the phenomenon of death, know that the soul of man is sanctified and independent from material existence. It hath no need to enter or exit, ascend or descend, penetrate or commingle, for these are the properties of bodies, not of souls. Therefore, the soul of man does not enter into this corporeal frame, but rather hath a connection to it.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: You will retain your individuality and will not be swallowed up in one vast spirit. The essence of the human soul is clarified from material substances and purified from the embodiment of physical things.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: When one leaves this sphere, will he ever return? No: No one ever returns here, for this world is a school were the soul of man learns its first lessons in spirituality, and if he leaves this place without having learned his lessons sufficiently, the time is past and the opportunity lost

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: This power of accomplishment is beyond the range of animal intelligence. Therefore, this power is a distinctive attribute of the human spirit and kingdom. The animal spirit cannot penetrate and discover the mysteries of things. It is a captive of the senses.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: Man is not man because of his body; man is man because of his soul, for in regard to bodily things humans and animals are partners. It is through the soul that he is distinguished from the animal.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: As we have before indicated, this human reality stands between the higher and the lower in man, between the world of the animal and the world of Divinity...Man is selfish; They sever him from self and desire. Man is haughty; They make him meek, humble and friendly. He is earthly; They make him heavenly. Men are material; the Manifestations transform them into divine semblance.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: The spirit in man is the perceiving soul, able to understand the realities of things and predominating over all things else. If the spirit of man, his perceiving soul, be confirmed by the spirit of faith so that it loves and knows God, and if it be guided by the guidance of God, and if the divine attributes be manifested in it, then there is a living soul which attains to eternal life.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: The human spirit, which distinguishes man from animal, is the rational soul, and these two terms - the human spirit and the rational soul - refer to one and the same thing. This spirit, which philosophers call the rational soul, encompasses all other created things and, to the extent of human capacity, discovers the realities of things and gains knowledge of the properties and effects of contingent beings and the characteristics and particulars of physical existence. However, unless it is assisted by the spirit of faith, it will not become aware of divine mysteries and heavenly realities.

Subject: the human soul
Quotation: the reality of the human spirit is detached from physical things and sanctified from embodiment in material elements. It is pure light, has no physical form, is a brilliant ray and a luminous radiance.

Subject: the human soul at midpoint of creation; the isthmus [barzakh]
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the human soul at midpoint of creation; the isthmus [barzakh].txt
Quotation: And human reality is the connecting isthmus and dividing line, meaning it possesses the capacity both to ascend to the highest stations and to fall to the lowest depths of destruction.

Subject: the lower is unable to comprehend the higher
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the lower is unable to comprehend the higher.txt
Quotation: Although the mineral, vegetable, animal and man all have actual being, yet the mineral has no knowledge of the vegetable. It cannot apprehend it. It cannot imagine nor understand it. It is the same with the vegetable. Any progress it may make, however highly it may become developed, it will never apprehend the animal, nor understand it.

Subject: the lower is unable to comprehend the higher
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the lower is unable to comprehend the higher.txt
Quotation: Mineral and vegetable entities are unaware of the human and animal worlds. They cannot absolutely conceive it. Is it possible for a plant or a stone to appreciate the realty of hearing and sight? I ask forgiveness of God! And this although both are in the realm of contingency and so how can a transient being comprehend an eternal reality?

Subject: the lower is unable to comprehend the higher
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the lower is unable to comprehend the higher.txt
Quotation: The mineral being has no knowledge of the plant world - it is completely unaware, rather according to its condition denies it. Similarly, the plant being has no knowledge of the animal world - it is completely heedless and unaware, for the animal rank is above the plant rank, and the plant according to its condition is veiled from and denies the animal world.

Subject: the lower is unable to comprehend the higher
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the lower is unable to comprehend the higher.txt
Quotation: If in this merciful existence that universal spiritual existence remains unknown and unrecognized, let there be no wonder or astonishment, for every lower realm is unaware of the higher realm, just as the fetus in the womb is unaware of this world. When it transfers to the higher world it becomes aware and perceives, but before transfer, conception and comprehension are impossible. Now if the vegetable world is wholly unaware of the human world, does this prove the non-existence of the human world? No, by God! Thus, the denial by human souls of the divine world is like the denial of the mineral which has no knowledge of the vegetable world, and like the denial of the plant which has no knowledge of the animal world, and like the denial of the animal which has no knowledge of the human world.

Subject: the mind's power of discovery
Quotation: All that thou seest, such as arts, inventions, traces and discoveries were once in the realm of the unknown...But the human spirit discovered such hidden mysteries and brought them out of the sphere of the unknown into the world of visibility

Subject: the mind's power of discovery
Quotation: For instance, a cow has no knowledge whatsoever of God, no awareness of intellect and the intelligible, no knowledge of the power of discovery in human reality, no knowledge of the force of gravity, no knowledge of the ethereal matter in which you believe, for it is imperceptible.

Subject: the power of example
Quotation: follow the path of Abdu'l-Baha, taking Him as your excellent example - which means responding to every unkindness with faithfulness

Subject: the power of example
Quotation: By My life! The hosts of deeds are My mightiest armies, and virtuous character is the helper and champion of My Cause. Verily He hath come from the heaven of grace with the banners of loving-kindness and justice.

Subject: the power of example
Quotation: They who exhort others unto justice, while themselves committing iniquity, stand accused of falsehood by the inmates of the Kingdom and by those who circle round the throne of their Lord, the Almighty, the Beneficent, for that which their tongues have uttered.

Subject: the power of example
Quotation: Observe what the Arab poet says: In those who have gone before us in past ages, we find examples. This means those souls who have passed before us, these peoples and nations who preceded us in bygone centuries. Which of these souls became like unto a brilliant lamp and attained the highest pinnacle of eternal glory?

Subject: the power of example
Quotation: We hope that the person in question will become aware and awakened through your good conduct and surpassing respect, and will observe that at such a time and in such circumstances, this kind of respect and consideration clearly springs from sincere intentions and has its source in the essential virtues of the people of God.

Subject: the power of example
Quotation: show by your life you have something different, so that all will see and will say, 'What has this person that I have not?' Show the world that in spite of the utmost suffering, poverty, sickness, you have something which gives you comfort, strength and peace - that you are happy - serene - satisfied with all that is in your life. Then they, too, will want what you possess - and will need no further teaching - after you tell them what it is.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: This is what the Tongue of Grandeur uttered: "He is the Powerful over whatsoever He willeth"

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: women will develop eloquent speech and persuasive expression that will render others speechless

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: They are thinking and waging war, you practice Peace and conciliation... Cry out the word Peace.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Read thou the words of God in thy days... Thus hath the Command been, if thou be of them that know.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: We have revealed therein that whereby the fragrance of utterance hath been wafted throughout all creation

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: When asked by what proof, recite thou this Tablet from whose horizon hath shone the Sun of wisdom and utterance.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Then open thy tongue in utterance, for the Spirit will aid thee from the presence of the Mighty, the Self-Subsisting.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: when it was raised from the human Tree with perfect eloquence and rhetoric in the most wondrous melodies, they denied it

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: If thou hadst built and developed the entire world with thine own hands, verily it would not equal one word of these verses.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Whoever in this day utters a single word of truth, that word will forever be in motion and surge forward and will never perish.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Thou art he who hath been faithful to God's Covenant and His Testament, and hath spoken that which made the back of polytheism to quake.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: You yourself know what that pure water Says to the flowers and saplings You yourself know what the sun in Aries Says to the flowers and thorns

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: "From the radiance of the sun full of light, the blind eye receives nothing but heat." They feel the warmth of the sun but not the effulgence of its rays.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: The scratching of the Most Exalted Pen is raised to such a degree that the tongues of the world and the pens of nations are powerless to make mention of it.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: One word that betokens the love of God is a detailed book, and one melody raised in praise and glorification of the Loving Lord is a matchless and peerless song.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: I swear by the Sovereign of all possibility that this is a Day wherein not a single letter appeareth except that it is recorded by the Pen of Destiny in the Manifest Book

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: This is the Day of vision, that one may behold, and the Day of hearing, that one may hearken, and the Day of utterance, that one may voice the praise of the Beloved of all possibility.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: The lights of the love of God were shining from the lamp of meanings and the glass of words and expressions, and the rays of certitude and assurance were radiant in the niche of phrases

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: References to the transformative power of divine utterance: "Thus have We adorned the horizon of utterance with the light of explanation" and guidance to use "wisdom and utterance" in teaching

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Within the very breath of such souls as are pure and sanctified far-reaching potentialities are hidden. So great are these potentialities that they exercise their influence upon all created things.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: We must watch our tongues. Let no one raise his tongue in intentional or unintentional malice against his brother or sister. Let every man write this sentence 'Watch thy tongue' on the tablet of his heart.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: O Beauty of God, come forth from behind the veil, That the sun may rise from the West! In the depths of despair He causeth the light of hope to appear in such wise as to illumine the realm of heart and soul.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: A thousand times it was written that the interference of the clergy in political matters would result in calamities... with such clear language were warning and counsel given, but ears were deaf and eyes were blind

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: How sweet is His Word! How resplendent His Light! How exalted His dominion! The sweetness of the blessed Word bestowed spirit upon all things, conferred light, and granted awareness. There is nothing save it glorifieth His praise.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: The water of life is the divine utterance, and likewise His evidences. Strive that perchance the people of the world may attain eternal life through this everlasting Kawthar and may illumine creation with the light of wisdom and utterance.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: TODAY, if the soul--who is attracted with the Love of God and burning with the flame of enthusiasm--shall unloose his tongue and deliver his speech in the utmost state of attraction, it will undoubtedly produce the most wonderful effect upon the hearts.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: When thou dost win to My Tablet and find the fragrance of revelation in My utterance, say: My God, my God! Praise be to Thee for showing me Thy signs, causing me to hear the scratching of Thy Pen, and illumining my heart with the light of Thy knowledge.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Teaching must be conducted with wisdom and utterance, and triumph achieved through the hosts of goodly character and deeds. The words of holy souls are so effective and penetrating that they can make a withered tree fresh and adorned with delicate, precious fruits.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: O servants! The triumph of the Cause hath been and shall be through the manifestations of pure souls, goodly deeds and penetrating words. Strive then that ye may perchance attain to that which hath been mentioned and be adorned with the ornament of wisdom and utterance.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: O servant in attendance! A single word can, like the spring breezes, make the world fresh and verdant, adorning it with the ornament of life, while another word can, like autumn winds, cause leaves to fall and strip every created thing of its freshness, as hath been and is now witnessed.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Through them, all created things shall arise to glorify the Lord of names and to bear witness that there is none other God save Me, the All-Powerful, the Most Glorious, the Best-Beloved. Nor shall those who make mention of Me speak aught unless they be inspired by this Tongue from its heavenly garden.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: No mention shall profit you this day [...] Say: No mention among all mentions, nor any name among all names, nor any book among all books shall benefit you this day except through this Book which speaketh with truth and before which the Mother Book hath bowed down, would ye but know with certainty.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: The charm and beauty of the voice of Truth attract the hearts and spiritualize the thoughts. Today whosoever takes the lessons of voice culture in the Celestial Conservatory of Baha'u'llah, he will be endowed with a soul-captivating voice which would move and thrill the hearts of numberless music lovers.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: O Muhammad-Rahim! The Wronged One remembereth thee and commandeth thee to observe that which thou wast commanded in His presence and that which We have commanded all in the Book. Say: O loved ones of God! Be not grieved by what hath befallen [My Name] and My friends through that which the hands of every heedless doubter have wrought.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: those letters are as gifts of God to thee...verily, those letters are as the fragrant breezes of the garden of the knowledge of God, which can be smelled by every one whose sense of smelling is clean and purified from any rheum, because they are glad-tidings proceeding from pure lips which are fluent in explaining the mysteries of God

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: O Most Exalted Pen! We have sent down for thee in every condition that which sufficeth the worlds... Through thee was raised the scratching of every pen and every wise decree was expounded. Through thee were hearts drawn to the Beloved, and the hearts of lovers were set ablaze with the fire of separation, and the Face illumined the horizons.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Then remind the people of that which God hath cast into thy heart, and be not of the silent ones. And though silence be beloved before God, yet remembrance before thy Lord is better than it, if thou be of them that know. For silence is beloved except concerning the remembrance of God and the promotion of His Cause, if ye be of them that are assured.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Through thy scratching every soul that turned to God, the Lord of all worlds, was drawn nigh, and through thy movement were all created things stirred to motion in the days of thy Lord, the Mighty, the All-Praised. Through thee were made manifest the hidden mysteries in the Books of God, and that which was treasured in His all-encompassing knowledge was unveiled.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Glory be to God! How resonant is this soundless pen! It is the source of all the world's sounds. Its scratching gives life to souls. The world of command and creation appears through it and returns to it, for in one station it is the first interpreter and in another the second. How many treasuries of arts and knowledge has this hollow shaft gathered within itself!

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Praise be to God! How great is this bounty, and how evident this generosity, that the trace of a pen and the contents of a letter can have such influence in the spiritual realms - meanings that give life, and concepts that nourish the spirit; a word that causes the bird of the spirit to soar, and a thought that brings the nightingale of the heart into song and melody.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Fear God and be of the God-fearing. Ask ye that which shall profit you in the Cause of God and His dominion, for the door of grace hath been opened unto all who dwell in heaven and on earth. Be thou in no wise saddened about this matter, for He hath repeatedly stated that there are certain questions which people need to ask, therefore there is no blame upon the questioners.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: If the nightingale of a thousand melodies fails to sing a tune, it is as a mute sparrow, and if the nightingale of the rose garden of meanings composes no melody, it is as a wingless, speechless bird. If the dove of the garden of mysteries warbles not, it appears as the raven of the refuse heap, and if the peacock of the eternal paradise displays not its glory, it is as the crow of the ruins of extinction.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Through Thy name the Most Great Ocean was stirred, and through Thy remembrance the mouth of them that are nigh unto God was perfumed. Time hath brought Me low, to such extent that the dumb now speaketh, since the gates of utterance have been opened through this human being who proclaimeth at the midmost heart of creation: "Verily, there is none other God but Me, the Speaking One, the True, the Articulate, the Trustworthy."

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Thus hath the Pen of God moved to make mention of thee, that thou mayest remind the people through this utterance which God hath made the Dayspring of His signs. Were We to will it, We would assuredly give victory to the Cause through but one word from Us. But since Our mercy hath preceded all things, We have ordained complete victory to consist in mention and utterance, that Our servants throughout the earth might thereby attain.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Verily God will surely strengthen thee by the lights shining upon all sides and will make thee of the vibrations of the hidden, kindled and Invisible Fire which penetrates every wall, bar and mountain, casting lights upon the hearts of the pious. And He will suffer thee to be established in the center of the City which has no walls so that thou mayest become a sign of Guidance in the extreme Occident, borrowing light from the Supreme Orient.

Subject: the power of words; of speech
Quotation: Then remind the people of this hidden News, and drink at every moment from the cup of life, though thou didst drink therefrom in the days of thy Lord, to which all things bear witness, yet people hear not. O My Name! Deliver the messages of thy Lord unto those who have been mentioned in this Tablet and unto those who have believed in God, the Most High, the Most Great. Beware lest thou be silent in mentioning thy Lord or grow cold in the warmth of thy love.

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul.txt
Quotation: O thou tree planted in the Vineyard of God!...Therefore, O thou tree, be verdant, blossom, put forth leaves and bear beautiful fruits in this most Supreme Paradise!

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul.txt
Quotation: This faith and certitude, like a seed sown in the field of the heart, will soon sprout forth and yield ears of corn, becoming a bountiful harvest for the free ones.

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul.txt

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul.txt
Quotation: If reason prevails, he is luminous and of the highest heaven, but if the self prevails and nature dominates, he is dark and of the lowest hell, for the heavenly power and the natural animal force are in conflict within man until one emerges victorious

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul.txt
Quotation: I beseech God that the garden of hearts may be so adorned through the gift of the All-Glorious and the grace and mercy of the Supreme Concourse that it may become the envy of the most verdant garden and the object of jealousy of the paradise of refuge.

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul.txt
Quotation: O my God! O my God! This plant has put forth its shoots and stands firm upon its stem. It has astounded the cultivators and enraged the envious. O Lord! Sustain it through the showers of Thy grace and make it into mighty heaps like great hills in Thy dominion.

Subject: the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the soul as soil; cultivation of the soul.txt
Quotation: If he acquire praiseworthy virtues, these strengthen the individuality of man and call forth his hidden forces; but if he acquire defects, the beauty and simplicity of the individuality will be lost to him and its God-given qualities will be stifled in the foul atmosphere of self... A fruitless tree under the influence of a wise gardener becomes fruitful; a slab of marble under the hand of a sculptor becomes a beautiful statue.

Subject: the state of enkindlement in teaching
Quotation: the teacher himself must be infinitely affected at the time of teaching

Subject: the state of enkindlement in teaching
Quotation: Therefore, since thou hast been enkindled with the love of God, thou art radiant and brilliant, resplendent and effulgent.

Subject: the state of enkindlement in teaching
Quotation: "And thou, O thou who art attracted by the verses of God, be thou glad in spirit, enkindled in heart, and stirred in soul by this breeze which wafteth from it the fragrance of the Spirit."

Subject: the state of enkindlement in teaching
Quotation: How are the Believers? Are they enkindled? Are they brilliant stars in the Assembly? Do they serve the Cause of God in Love and Harmony? In the meetings of Believers is there a real quickening, or is it cold? What we wish for the meetings of Believers is that they shall be enkindled and enlightened.

Subject: the state of enkindlement in teaching
Quotation: There were some amongst the believers who were most learned and erudite but because "the Flame of the Spirit" was not burning in their souls they could not teach one person. Whenever he began to speak he himself was so stirred by the 'urge of the spirit' that the listeners were moved profoundly and accepted the Truth before he had come to the end of his talk.

Subject: the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer.txt
Quotation: supplication and prayer is the Water of Life. It is the cause of the vivification of existence and brings glad tidings and joy to the soul.

Subject: the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer.txt
Quotation: Is it necessary to arise to say the midnight prayer, or the prayer of the Dawn, or to wash the hands and face before using these? No, the ablution is only for the obligatory daily prayer which should be said three times a day.

Subject: the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer.txt
Quotation: Prayer is the means of connection between God and creation, and the cause of the heart's attraction and attachment. Never does the grace from on high reach that which is below without the means of attachment and connection. Therefore must the servant supplicate and beseech at the threshold of the One, and offer prayer and devotion.

Subject: the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer.txt
Quotation: "The wisdom of this is that this prayer constitutes a link between the servant and His Lord. In this state of communion man turneth with all his heart and soul to God, seeketh His companionship and showeth Him all his love. The lover has no greater joy than to commune with the Beloved, and the seeker can receive no greater gift than to associate with the One sought by all."

Subject: the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer.txt
Quotation: Thou didst question the necessity for prayer, and the wisdom that might lie behind it. What reason could there be, thou didst ask, considering that God hath perfected His creation, ordering all matters in the best way possible, assigning unto every thing its due measure, and appointing for it, with consummate exactitude and precision, its proper station --what reason could there be to make supplication and entreaty, to pray for needs to be fulfilled, and to beg for succour and assistance? Know thou that it belongeth to the weak to make entreaty to the Source of strength, and that it becometh the petitioner of heavenly grace humbly to supplicate to Him Who is the All-Glorious, the Lord of grace abounding. Whensoever the worshipper communeth with his Lord, turneth wholly unto Him, and supplicateth some portion of His boundless grace, then this very act of supplication is a light unto his heart, a collyrium unto his eye, a source of life unto his soul, and a cause of exaltation unto his being. Observe then how, when thou dost thyself commune with God and recitest "Thy Name is my healing", thy heart is thrilled, thy soul transported with the rapture of the love of God, and thy spirit drawn towards His heavenly Kingdom. Through these sensations, moreover, thy receptive capacity is increased: and the more capacious the container, the more copious its contents; the more vehement one's thirst, the sweeter in one's palate the outpouring bounty of the cloud. This is the mystery of supplication; this is the wisdom of praying for the fulfilment of one's needs.

Subject: the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer.txt
Quotation: When the blessed words of the opening takbir flow from one's tongue, one must see oneself as separate from all created things and as evanescent in God's Will and Purpose, to such extent that one seeth naught in existence save Him - this is the station of them that are nigh unto God and the sincere ones. And if anyone attaineth unto such prayer, he is recorded before God and the Concourse on High as one of the people of prayer.

Subject: the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the state of prayer; dynamics of prayer.txt
Quotation: O friends of God! Say: Do not multiply your devotions by day and by night, nor that which ye recite. For if ye refine your deeds, it will draw you nearer unto God, your Lord. This is of God's grace and mercy, that ye may be thankful. And God sets forth parables unto you that ye may understand. If ye grow weary reciting a verse from the Book of God an hundred times when ye read it, then reduce it by ten and by ten until there remain but nineteen.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: The Baha'i Faith encompasses the principles of all religions, for when one hundred comes, ninety is also with it.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: O people! He hath come with that wherewith came 'Ali [the Bab], then Muhammad, then the Spirit [Jesus], then He Who conversed with God [Moses], and the Friend of God [Abraham]

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: This Cause does not oppose the foundation of Christ, but rather it is the Divine Spirit that is also at work and penetrating hearts outside the churches and Christian nations.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: Do not forget the tradition "All that is in the Torah, Gospel and Psalms is in the Qur'an, and all that is in the Opening Chapter is in the Bismillah, and all that is in the Bismillah is in the letter B."

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: The Books have been sealed by the Most Great Book wherein is detailed the knowledge of what hath been and what shall be...The preamble of this Book hath been adorned with that which was foretold in the Psalms, the Qur'an, the Gospel and what was revealed in the Holy Books

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: Man must be just. After these statements no one can deny the greatness of Christ...The philosophers are also teachers but all they could do was to teach themselves and a few other souls. But the prophets of God taught the whole world.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: The Jews admit that Jesus appeared in the world and taught heavenly principles. If Christ had not appeared after Moses the mention of Moses would have been lost. The foundation of Jesus and the foundation of Moses were the same. The foundation of Baha'o'llah is likewise the same as Moses and Jesus.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: He hath created all contingent beings through His pre-existent knowledge of what was and what shall be, and taught them the ways of righteousness by sending unto them the Messengers of the Cause with a mighty revealed Book wherein He ordained holy laws and determined the destinies of all who dwell in the heavens and on earth according to a fixed measure. Among them was Moses, whom He sent with the truth, with nine clear signs, to herald unto the people a station of glorious dignity.... And among them was Jesus, whom God strengthened with the Spirit and sent with the truth.... His days were fulfilled until Muhammad, the Messenger of God, came with beloved signs.... His days were fulfilled until 'Ali before Muhammad [the Bab] came, whereupon all who were on earth arose and disputed with him without right, and warred against him such that they visited upon him and his companions that which they could not bear to hear.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: It is proven with brilliant evidence that God chose the Prophets as a mercy to the worlds, not as a punishment to humanity. All of them called to guidance and held fast to the sure handle until they rescued the degraded nations from the depths of ignorance and blindness to the heights of virtue and wisdom.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: These great and blessed souls had for their aim the same principle. Their purpose was one, their law was one, their teaching was one. His Holiness Zoroaster was a prophet, precisely according to the Messianic example. There was no difference whatsoever between the spirit of the teachings which Zoroaster gave and those which His Holiness the Christ gave.

Subject: the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/the truth of past religions and sacred scriptures.txt
Quotation: In numerous passages in the divine Tablets, blessed mention is made of Zoroaster with utmost praise, for that blessed being was one of the Manifestations of the Divine Unity and became the cause of guidance for a great nation. Whoever studies the teachings and counsels of that noble One will clearly see that those teachings are heavenly and those counsels are the words of a divine being. And as long as the Parsees acted according to the counsels and admonitions of that noble One, they were cherished in both worlds, but when they became deprived of that conduct and behavior, that eternal glory was transformed. In brief, the purpose is that the exalted station of that noble One has become clear and evident in this Revelation.

Subject: theft; seizing the properties of others
Quotation: O peoples, do not spill blood and do not seize the goods of others.

Subject: theft; seizing the properties of others

Quotation: The inscrutable divine wisdom underlieth such heart-rending occurrences. It is as if a kind gardener transferreth a fresh and tender shrub from a confined place to a wide open area. This transfer is not the cause of the withering, the lessening or the destruction of that shrub; nay, on the contrary, it maketh it to grow and thrive, acquire freshness and delicacy, become green and bear fruit. This hidden secret is well known to the gardener, but those souls who are unaware of this bounty suppose that the gardener, in his anger and wrath, hath uprooted the shrub. Quotation: The servant testifies that there is no God but Him. He has ever been and will ever be sanctified from what the creatures possess, and He is the Single, the One, the Powerful, the All-Choosing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: None can comprehend God's Cause, so be not deceived by what ye do, for on the Day of Resurrection He will efface it from you except that ye shall be brought before God and prostrate yourselves.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp are the kingdoms of eternity of the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them. Thou shalt indeed glorify God in the True Faith with a mighty glorification.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him...But for Him none would have attained to the knowledge of God or comprehended the loftiness of His unity and the sublimity of His singleness.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: At all times and seasons the scratching of the Most Exalted Pen and the rustling of the Lote-Tree of the utmost boundary are raised up, yet the people of the mortal realm are deprived of hearing

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God willing, may the friends of God be enabled to act in accordance with this blessed verse which was revealed in the Quran, His exalted Word: Say: 'Allah' then leave them to their vain discourse.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: God cannot be comprehended by anything, yet He hath associated Me with His Self even as He associated the Kaaba with His Self and made it the Sacred House for those who circle round about it.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! How can I make mention of Thee when Thou art exalted above being mentioned by the mention of Thy creation, and sanctified from being praised by praise other than Thine.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: For this tradition has a subtle meaning... which is that the Pre-existent Essence is an impenetrable mystery... and what appears in the kingdom of heaven is the Command which was created from nothing

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who manifests Himself in the realm of might and majesty, Who is inaccessible in the sovereignty of power and perfection, and Who is exalted in the heights of glory and transcendence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: Look not upon aught besides yourselves save as a handful of ashes in your grasp -- nay, even less than this in the sight of your Lord. Ye are God's creation, and all before God are but creatures.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: None knoweth how to mention Him save He Himself, and He is God, the Mighty, the Wise. Glory be to God, the Most High! This indeed is the mystery sanctified above the description of attributes, severed.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is manifest above His creation, and He is the Almighty, the Well-Beloved. His are all things that dwell in the night and in the day, and He is the Single One, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Compelling.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp lies the Kingdom of the divine realms of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them! Therefore sanctify ye God in the True Faith with a mighty sanctification.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Blessed is He to Whom belongeth the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. He bestoweth as He willeth from His bounty. Verily He is the All-Bountiful, the Most Generous.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Consider, then, how His most glorious Kingdom is an endless treasury, for He says: "And there is not a thing but with Us are the treasuries thereof, and We send it not down except in determined measure."

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp lies the Kingdom of the glorifications of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them! Therefore sanctify ye God in the True Faith with a mighty sanctification.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How great is Thy handiwork in that unseen yet manifest, concealed yet well-known, hidden yet visible luminous world...these invisible Divine worlds that can never be understood save by every man of insight

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I glorify Thee above all that by which contingent things have glorified Thee through their essential reality, and above all that by which existent things have sanctified Thee through their intrinsic nature

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: God cannot be comprehended by anything in the heavens or on earth. Eyes shall not perceive Him, yet He createth vision in whomsoever He willeth among His servants, and these gaze upon the signs of God.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: There is no Beloved except Him, and no One to be remembered save His Own Self, the Mighty, the Beautiful. No praise riseth unto Him save the praise of Him Who is sanctified from the praise of all the worlds

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Descent, ascent, egress, regress, and incarnation all relate to bodies, not to spirits. What then must be the condition of the Divine Reality, the Everlasting Being? Exalted is He above all such ascriptions.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Into the abyss (primal depths) of the aloneness of God sink all duality, plurality and individuality. The Godhead can be designated as Primal Love and therefore as the oneness of perception and the perceived.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp lies the kingdom of the divine realms of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. Therefore, on that Day, praise ye God with exalted praise in the true religion.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: His is whatsoever dwelleth in the night and the day, and He is the Single One, the Inaccessible, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting. He is the Manifest above His creation, and He is the Mighty, the Best Beloved.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: We have expounded the Point and interpreted the Books of God. Nothing whatsoever preventeth Him from anything, nor is anything hidden from His knowledge. To this beareth witness the Mother Book in His presence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose hand is the dominion of all things, and unto Whom all shall return. He it is Who created the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them in six days, then ascended the throne.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the Kingdom of the lights of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Therefore glorify ye God on that Day in the true religion with a mighty glorification.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the One Who creates what He wishes by His command Be! and it is. He is the Subduer over His servants, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting. He is the Manifest above His creation, the Mighty, the Beloved.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou art the Worshipped One Who cannot be known, and Thou art the Sought One Who cannot be attained, and Thou art the Beloved One Who cannot be described, and Thou art the Dreaded One Who cannot be characterized.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him. Within His grasp is the dominion of loftiness in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and God is possessed of mighty and glorious loftiness.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O Thou before Whose recognition of oneness the most devoted monotheists are powerless, and to the summit of Whose command's heaven the most accomplished mystics confess their inability to ascend!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Worship increaseth not His station, nor doth the faith of creation profit Him. He is the Absolute Independent, before Whom the kingdom of wealth is as nothing and non-existent, and the dominion of riches is as naught.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God has no sign in creation that points to His Essence, for His Being separates all beings from knowledge of Him, and His Identity prevents all identities from description. He is as He is, none knoweth Him save Himself.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the First above all things, and the Dominant over all things, and the Exalted above all things, and the Inaccessible unto Whom the hands of all things cannot reach, and the Most High in His Cause above all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou hast ever been independent of all else besides Thee and self-sufficient above all else except Thee. All worship Thee according to their capacity, and all prostrate themselves before Thee according to their ability.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Who is able to describe Him, or mention Him, or ascend to the heaven of His knowledge, or arise to perform what beseemeth His days? Verily, power, might, grandeur, and authority have confessed their impotence and weakness

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The verses of God have been sent down in such wise and His evidences have been revealed in such manner that the realm of utterance is powerless to describe them and the worlds of knowledge fall short of encompassing them.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He, verily, there is none other God besides Him, the Mighty, the Best-Beloved! Before Him bow down in adoration all who are in the heavens and on earth, and unto God do all return. He is the Truth, there is no God but Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: His existence differs from all else as the sun differs from other things. The essential thing is to know Him, and after knowing Him, whatever He commands is to be obeyed and corresponds to the requirements of divine wisdom.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O Mystery of the Cloud of Unknowing, hear the call of this blessed, radiant Leaf which speaketh by God's leave and addresseth you from beyond the veils from the right of the Tree of Life in the Mount of Glory, the Holy Land.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The All-Sanctified, the Most Great, the Most Inaccessible, the Most Glorious! The seas have surged by virtue of that Most Great Name which hath appeared from the horizon of eternity, yet most of the people remain fast asleep.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou above my mentioning Thee through any mention other than Thine own, or my describing Thee through praise of Thee in Thy dominion. Thou art He Who hath no peer, no equal, no likeness, no equivalent, no partner.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O my God! No one hath known Thee and no one can know Thee. The mystics are powerless to comprehend even a single sign of Thy divine reality, and the seekers are humbled before a single expression from the heaven of Thy Lordship.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
