Quotation: Say: God hath created for Him Whom God shall make manifest all the good things of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of all worlds - such as have no equal in His knowledge, no peer, no likeness, no companion, and no similitude.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Know then that God - exalted and glorified be He - doth in no wise manifest His inmost Essence and Reality. From time immemorial He hath been veiled in the eternity of His Essence and concealed in the infinitude of His own Being.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the All-Compelling above His servants, and He is the Self-Subsisting, the Inaccessible, the Most Exalted. He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is the Peerless, the All-Subduing, the Self-Subsisting.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is no God but He, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting. God beareth witness that there is no God but He, the Supreme, the All-Glorious. God beareth witness that there is no God but He, the Supreme, the Holy.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The existence of a thing in itself is proof of its impossibility. How can that which is inherent in Thy loftiness be encompassed within the realities of limitation? Verily this is that which naught in the heavens or on earth can sustain.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: That sweet and kind beloved! The end of this infinite expansion they call the supreme heaven, but truly it is beyond description and measure in its loftiness, for this expansion cannot be contained in thought, and this height has no end

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou! Thy Essential Reality is sanctified above the highest soaring of the birds of hearts and imaginations, and Thy Being is exalted above the loftiest summits of the essences possessed by those endowed with understanding.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, Who createth what He willeth by His command Be! and it is. Such is God, your Lord. His is the creation and the command. There is none other God but Him; say: all shall turn unto Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I declare my separation from all whereupon the name of a thing can fall, for all besides Thee are Thy creation and within Thy grasp. I know no beginning whereby I might mention Thee, nor do I know an end whereby I might describe Thee as two.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them! Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the Kingdom of dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He it is Who created the heavens by His command and the earths by His sovereignty, Who subjected the clouds and brought forth fruits from their sheaths. There is none other God but Him, the Mighty, the Supreme, the Powerful, the All-Knowing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art the God of all gods in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, and Thou art the Lord of all lords in the realms of names and attributes. Thou hast no equal, no likeness, no similitude, no peer and no partner.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O God! Thou art the Most Holy of the holy ones. All within the kingdoms of the heavens and earth and whatsoever is between them glorify Thee, and all within the kingdoms of Command and Creation and whatsoever lies beneath them sanctify Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Guardian, the Self-Subsisting. Say: He is the One manifest above His creation, and He is the Inaccessible, the Most High, the All-Glorious, the Most Mighty, the Most Exalted, the Beloved.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I testify that nothing can comprehend Thee, nothing can befall Thee, and no thing can encompass Thee in knowledge. All that can be named besides Thee is vain and ephemeral, created in Thy grasp and possessed by the right hand of Thy sovereignty.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He before Whom boweth down in worship whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. Glorified be He in Whose grasp are the measures of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: There is no God but Him, and unto Him shall all be turned. Blessed is He to Whom belongeth the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. He bestoweth as He willeth through His grace. Say: All are supplicants before Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Source of Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Omnipotent, the Most High, the Self-Subsisting, the Most Exalted, the Inaccessible, the Most Great.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: There is none other God but He, the King, the Holy. Verily, there is none other God but I, all shall know Me. And verily, I am God, there is none other God but I, from before before at the apex of before, and from after after at the apex of after.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Otherwise, it beseemeth not Him Whom God shall make manifest that any should praise Him among all the worlds. This is the Spirit of God - and who is able to praise God his Lord after having been created by His command and subsisting by His command?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In the Name of God, Transcendent is His Glory, His Grandeur and Power! Thou art the Sovereign Whom the sovereignty of the world neither hindereth nor increaseth Thy station, and the power of nations neither compareth with Thee nor diminisheth Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who has risen through the loftiness of His Essence with such exaltation that all things have fallen below Him, and Who has ascended through the greatness of His Being to the throne of oneness before whose presence all have bowed down.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Exalted is His sovereignty that hath encompassed all existence, both seen and unseen. Exalted is His bounty that hath encompassed the world through His Most Great Name. Exalted is the light of His Cause whereby the earth hath been illumined in His days.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thus doth God teach you to worship none but God, my Lord and your Lord, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of all worlds, Who created all things by His command, and verily He is the Single One, the Inaccessible, the Most Exalted.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He Who hath manifested the Manifestation of His Self... They who deny the beginning of the Cause - these are brutish rabble who have no portion of the Book. Would they deny God after having witnessed His sovereignty encompassing all creation?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp lies the Kingdom of subtleties of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever is between them. Glorified be He in Whose grasp lies the Kingdom of eternities of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever is between them.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Blessed is He before Whom bow down in adoration all who are in the heavens and all who are on earth. We all beseech His grace. He is the One before Whom prostrate themselves all who are in the heavens and all who are on earth, and unto Him shall all return.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the One Whom no vision can comprehend, yet He comprehendeth all vision, and He is the One, the All-Subtle. He is the One from Whose knowledge nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on the earth or between them, and He is the One, the All-Knowing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In the Name of God, the Inaccessible, the All-Protecting! This is a Book from God, the Guardian, the Self-Subsisting... I have neither beginning nor end. Verily, I have been from time immemorial, having neither beginning nor end, and I shall forever remain.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: Verily, He Whom God shall make manifest is the First Veil of God. Beyond that Veil ye shall perceive naught but God, and beneath that Veil shall ye perceive all that appeareth from God. God is the Hidden, the Inaccessible, the Exalted, the Best-Beloved.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: That Ancient Beauty shall remain, single and alone, established upon His throne which is sanctified above place and time, above mention and allusion, above description, above loftiness and lowliness. None knoweth this save every discerning and insightful one.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou art He Whom none of Thy servants hath truly glorified, and Thou art He Whom none of Thy creation hath truly praised in the kingdom of Thy earth and Thy heaven. Thou art He Whom none hath truly unified according to the reality of Thy oneness and exaltation.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: From time immemorial Thou hast been unknown, though more manifest than any manifestation, and Thou shalt ever remain concealed, though more renowned in all things than the things themselves. Such is Thy hiddenness in revelation and Thy manifestation in mysteries.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee, that I should describe Thee through other than Thyself, or that I should describe Thee apart from Thyself... Thou art He Who cannot be known through aught else but Thyself, and Thou art He Who cannot be described through aught else but Thyself.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Omnipotent, the Most High, the Self-Subsisting, the Most Sublime, the Inaccessible, the Most Great, the Most Exalted, the Most High.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The reality of the divine world is purified and sanctified from limits and restriction. It is evident that the divine nearness is an unlimited nearness, be it in this world or the next one. This is a nearness which is sanctified from the comprehension of the minds.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: I know none save God, nor do I desire to know any but Him. He is my Lord Who hath created me, sustained me, caused me to die and brought me back to life, and hath raised me up in such wise that no sorrow touched my heart, as a mercy and grace from His presence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: The greatest utterance upon myself is that I should speak of aught besides God. Therefore constrain me not in any matter, O all ye creatures of God! Unto God boweth down whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth, and unto God shall all return.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the All-Compelling, the Self-Subsisting. He is the Manifest above His creation, and He is the Mighty, the Best-Beloved. Before Him prostrate all who are in the heavens and who are on earth, and unto Him do they bow down.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The Divine Reality is Unthinkable, Limitless, Eternal, Immortal and Invisible. The Infinite Reality cannot be said to ascend or descend. It is beyond the understanding of man, and cannot be described in terms which apply to the phenomenal sphere of the created world.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The Reality of Divinity is not limited. Were it limited, it its not Divinity. How can you bind Divinity with finality?...Divinity means a unity indivisible. Divinity is that which is not subject to descent. Divinity is that which is sanctified above all imperfections.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God is not joined with anything, nor can any thing comprehend Him, nor can any thing know Him, nor can any thing bring Him into being, nor can any thing sanctify Him, nor can any thing glorify Him, nor can any thing magnify Him, nor can any thing bear witness unto Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: And there is none like unto Him. He hath created that creation in the most exalted manner possible from a beginning that hath no beginning unto an end that hath no end...He is the One, not of number, and the Exalted One, too high to be described by any likeness or peer.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: He is the Manifest above His creation, the Subduer over His servants, the All-Protecting over all things, the Exalted above all things, and the Inaccessible before Whom prostrate all who are in the heavens and who are in the earth, and all stand before His presence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: God hath testified that there is no God but Him, all are His worshippers. He is the One Who hath created all things by His command, and unto God shall all return. He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, the Mighty, the Beloved.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the Truth, there is no God but Him; He giveth life and causeth death, and unto Him shall all return. He is the One Who createth what He willeth through His command Be! and it is. He is the All-Compelling above His servants, and verily He is the Mighty, the Beloved.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Man, who has also a real existence, is comprehended by God; therefore, the Divinity which man can understand is partial; it is not complete. Divinity is actual Truth and real existence, and not any representation of it. Divinity itself contains All, and is not contained.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O Thou Who art sanctified above my knowledge and the knowledge of the unitarians who are adorned with the garments of certitude, and Who art exalted above my praise and the praise of the mystics who have awakened to the essence of attributes in the realities of creation!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou hast ever been sanctified above the mention of Thy servants and the comprehension of the dwellers of Thy realm. Before Thy power hath the might of all created things proven impotent, and at the revelation of Thy signs have the necks of all contingent beings bowed down.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who hath risen in His exaltation above all created things, and ascended in His ascension above all existing things, and become inaccessible in His inaccessibility above all atoms, and become supreme in His supremacy above all who are in the kingdom of earth

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He Who hath manifested Himself unto the unitarians among His servants and concealed Himself from the idolaters among His creatures. He is that sanctified Being Whom the tongues of the world are powerless to praise and the hearts of nations fall short of knowing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: This is indeed the Mystery of God within you, Who has come to you with a mighty Cause. When the idolaters imprisoned Us, We revealed the Beauty and removed the veil from a face of mighty glory. Say: By God, all matters have proceeded from Me, and I have power over all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Verily He hath been from time immemorial eternally pre-existent. Say: God is the Most Ancient of all that possess antiquity. None can withstand His ancient dominion, neither in the heavens nor on earth nor whatsoever is between them. Verily He hath been eternally pre-existent.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Verily I am God, there is no God but Me. From the beginning that hath no beginning I have been holy in My essence. Verily I am God, there is no God but Me. Until the end that hath no end I shall be holy in My essence. [continues through passages about God's transcendent essence]

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! Thou art sanctified above my praise and commemoration, and exalted beyond my description and tribute. The tongues of the Concourse on High have fallen silent, unable to render due praise - how then can this bird of broken wing flutter in such heights?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: Ye cannot comprehend the knowledge of how God hath joined the letters in these verses. Verily He is powerful over all things. Say: Ye comprehend not the knowledge of how God joineth the letters in these verses, nor the words, nor the names, nor what God sendeth down from heaven

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Nothing can witness Him, yet He witnesseth all things. He is the Observer, the Almighty, the All-Knowing. No one can see Him, yet He seeth all who are in the heavens and the earth. Vision comprehendeth Him not, yet He comprehendeth all vision, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O God! I beseech Thee by Thine eternity which is exalted above all things, to transform, through Thy power over all things, the essence of every being with an Alif that is attributed to the Tree of Fire into light. Verily, Thou art the All-Knowing, the Most Powerful, the Most Great.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: No thing has ever known Him as He deserves to be known, and no thing has ever praised Him as He deserves to be praised. How transcendent is the holy court of His might, for all praise His oneness! How exalted is the sanctified realm of His elevation, for all testify to His uniqueness!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! How can I make mention of Thee, when I have become certain that the tongues of the mystics falter in Thy remembrance and praise, and the birds of the hearts of those who yearn after Thee are prevented from soaring to the heaven of Thy might and knowledge?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the Truth! There is no God but Him and all bow down before Him. And verily what ought to be manifested is that which is manifest above all things, and hidden beneath all things, and first before all things, and last on the right of all things, and dominant on the left of all things

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: His is the creation and the command. He giveth life and causeth death, then causeth death and giveth life, and He, verily, is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp is the kingdom of all things. He createth what He pleaseth by His command. He, verily, hath power over all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I bear witness before Thee, O my God, and before all things, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thou hast ever been one God, eternal, single, ever-living, self-subsisting, sovereign, supreme, holy, everlasting, eternal, transcendent, inaccessible, exalted.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Verily that which is encompassed cannot know the Encompasser, and that which perceiveth cannot perceive Him Who is beyond perception. Glorified be its Creator above being known through the knowledge of His creation or being described by attributes that were limited by human understanding.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O servant who standeth before the Throne! All praise, sanctified from letters and words, befitteth the Most Holy and Most Glorious Court of that Desired One Who hath gathered together the whole world through one Word, and through another Word hath distinguished between truth and falsehood.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. No thing can know Him, and all are created by His command. God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. No thing can unite with Him, and all sanctify Him by His command. Say: God is more hidden than all things, if ye would but perceive.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise, sanctified beyond thought, remembrance and utterance, forever and eternally befitteth and beseemeth the Most Glorious Court of the All-Possessing Lord. His word, exalted be His majesty: Neither My earth nor My heaven can contain Me, yet the heart of My faithful servant containeth Me.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who has manifested Himself to all created things through the ornament of the Point, which is separate from the ocean of creation... It is neither of the East of eternity nor of the West of nothingness. It came into being through its own essence, not from any creation before it

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: On that Day you shall be presented before God, your Lord, with the most penetrating knowledge and the most truthful utterance, steadfast upon the Path. Place, then, your trust in the Ever-Living God Who dieth not, that God may on that Day preserve you from that which you worship apart from God.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou! How can I call upon Thee when I know myself to be in the uttermost remoteness, and what Thou hast created for me to be in the extremity of my own displeasure with myself? Alas, alas! If such be my condition in relation to myself, what then would be Thy judgment concerning me?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He hath ever been the Subduer above all contingent beings, and the Manifest above all existing things, and the Invincible above all created things, and the Exalted above all atoms, and the Most High above all who dwell in the kingdom of earth and heaven, and the All-Powerful above all particles.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How can I make mention of Thee when my mention of Thee is naught but sheer nothingness?...Never hast Thou desired mention, for none among Thy creation can undertake it, nor can anyone render Thee adequate praise, for other than Thee hath never known Thee and besides Thee shall never describe Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I testify that the knowledge of the Ancient One, exalted be His glory, in His essence is forbidden to all else, and in His reality He cannot be manifest to His creation. No created thing hath known Him as He deserves to be known, nor hath any created thing praised Him as He deserves to be praised.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He before Whom prostrate themselves those who are in the heavens and those who are on earth and what lieth between them. Say: All bow down before Him in adoration. And praise be to God, before Whom all that are in the heavens and all that are on earth and what lieth between them give glory.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify, and all things testify, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thou hast ever existed before all things, and wilt exist after all things, and art the Creator of all things, the Essence above all things, and wilt exist after all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: All directions and quarters belong to the realm of place, but the Abha Kingdom is sanctified above directions. All rising points exist in the contingent world, but that eternal kingdom exists in the placeless realm. Every region and kingdom is bounded, but that enduring kingdom is abstract and distinct.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou beyond being associated with aught else or being remembered through the remembrance of any besides Thee! Thou hast ever been, and there was naught else beside Thee, and Thou wilt ever continue to be even as Thou hast been. No one hath any way to attain unto the knowledge of Thy Essence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be God, my Lord - there is no God but Him - we are all prostrate before Him. Glorified be God, my Lord, above what they describe! Glorified art Thou! Is there any like unto Thee, present before the countenance of Thy penitent ones, while the servants, in their weakness, hurt Him as they please?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Verily shall the vainglorious ones be brought low, and the arrogant ones submit, and the philosophers be confounded, and the corrupt ones weep, for she is indeed divine and inaccessible, heavenly and detached, luminous and resplendent, radiant and effulgent, holy and ethereal, sanctified and celestial...

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Such is God, your Lord. His is the creation and the command. There is none other God but He, the Single One, the Inaccessible, the Most Exalted, the Beloved. His is whatsoever dwelleth in the night and in the day, and verily He is the Single One, the Inaccessible, the Most Exalted, the Mighty, the Beloved.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory and praise rest upon Thee, O Thou the Wondrous Countenance, O Thou the Transcendent Beauty, O Thou the Exalted Mystery, O Thou Protector of the Infant, in Whose Hands are the strengthening and advancement of all, O Thou Whose shadow encompasseth all, O Thou the Rising Sun, O Thou the Culminating Light.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I seek forgiveness from Thee at this time for whatsoever I have committed in this station wherein I have uttered between Thy hands the verses which Thou didst make a proof of Thy Being, an evidence of Thine Own Self, and a testimony unto all who are in Thy heaven and on Thine earth

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be to Thee, O my God! I cannot reckon Thy praise, nor do I love to mention Thee for aught save Thy Face. How then can I describe my state before Thee, when Thy knowledge encompasses what is beyond... O my God! As Thou art, Thou canst not be known except through Thyself, nor described except by Thy countenance.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: That is, they are all Divine Manifestations and the reality of Divinity is eternally sanctified above ascent, descent, incarnation and emergence. Whatever man thinks is from his own imagination, therefore there is no incarnation, no emergence, and no ascent. Incarnation and mixing are properties of physical bodies.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Exalted art Thou above the description of any one save Thyself, and the comprehension of aught else except Thee. Too high art Thou for the praise of those who are nigh unto Thee to ascend unto the heaven of Thy nearness, or for the birds of the hearts of them who are devoted to Thee to attain to the door of Thy gate.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and verily He is the Single One, the Supreme, the Self-Subsisting. He it is Who createth whatsoever He willeth by His command Be! and it is, and He it is before Whom boweth down whosoever is in the heavens and whosoever is on earth, and there is no God but God.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: Look, then remember those days wherein the Sun of Truth shone forth from the horizon of Hijaz. The learned and the literary opposed Him until they spoke of Him that which rent asunder the heaven of knowledge and disturbed the hearts of the righteous, while those who had no standing among the people believed in Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: And should I sanctify Thee above all this and above all that the mystics know - this is an attribute wherewith Thou didst describe from aforetime the Manifestations of Thy Self and the Daysprings of Thy Cause. By Thy glory! I am bewildered before Thee, for this is a mystery that souls cannot bear and minds cannot endure.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: None knows the unseen save God... The loftiness of His station negates knowledge from any other than His own Self, for in mentioning His station of unity, there is no remembrance save the remembrance of God, the Most Mighty, the Most Generous. Verily unity and His station admit no mention of multiplicity in His presence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: Verily God can never be associated with anything, nor can He be contained within anything, nor upon anything, nor in anything, nor unto anything. And whatsoever is designated by the name of a thing apart from God is but His creation, the Lord of all worlds. Say: No vision can grasp Him, but His grasp is over all vision.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who cannot be indicated by any sign nor mentioned by any utterance, for signs and utterances are attributes of His creation and were created by His command. The essences of all mention cannot ascend to the heaven of His holiness, and the quintessence of all descriptions cannot return to the court of His glory.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: And unto God belongeth all majesty in the kingdom of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever lieth between them, and He, verily, is the One, the Inaccessible, the Most High. He is the One Who createth whatsoever He willeth through His command, and He, verily, is the Truth, the Most Exalted, the Inaccessible, the Most High.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: After creating all contingent beings and bringing all things into existence, through the revelation of His Name "the Choose", He selected man from among all peoples and creatures for His own knowledge and love, which was the ultimate purpose and cause of the creation of all beings, as mentioned in the well-known sacred tradition.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God testifies that there is no God but Him. His is the creation and the command. He gives life and causes death, then causes death and gives life, and verily God is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Within His grasp is the dominion of all things. He createth whatsoever He willeth by His command. Verily, He is powerful over all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God, my Lord and my Support! This servant desireth to make mention of Thee and to praise Thee, yet findeth himself prevented from that which he desireth, for I know of a certainty that mention of aught else but Thee reacheth not unto Thee nor ascendeth to the heaven of Thy Cause and the atmosphere of Thy Will.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the One to Whose heaven of knowledge the birds of inner meaning and utterance cannot soar, and in Whose atmosphere of expression the wings of remembrance and exposition cannot fly. He hath ever been sanctified beyond my mention and the mention of all who are in the world, and exalted above my praise and the praise of all peoples.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O my God! How can I call upon Thee when all paths of access to the knowledge of Thy Being are barred? Glory be to Thee and exalted art Thou! I testify that Thy Essence hath cut off all created things from attaining the station of knowing Thee, and that Thy timeless Being hath separated all existence from the capacity to describe Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O God! I beseech Thee by Thine eternity which is exalted above all things... by Thy creative power which is inaccessible above all things... by Thy steadfastness which is transcendent above all things... by Thy bounty which is everlasting above all things... by Thy mercy which encompasseth all things and is exalted above all things...

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In joy I perceive Thy glory, O Thou beside Whom there is none other God but Thee! And in sorrow I discern Thy beauty, O Thou beside Whom there is none other God but Thee! In hunger Thine is justice, O Thou beside Whom there is none other God but Thee! And when replete Thine is bounty, O Thou beside Whom there is none other God but Thee!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God alone knoweth His wisdom - glorified and exalted be He above all that they associate with Him! He is the Unknowable, the Inaccessible, Who cannot be comprehended by those who dwell within the multiplicities of the Command or the signs of creation. God alone knoweth His wisdom - glorified and exalted be He above all that they describe!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: There is no God but He, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of all worlds. He is the Truth, there is no God but He. He giveth life and causeth death, and unto Him shall all return. Glorified be He before Whom prostrate themselves all who are in the heavens and all who are on earth, and unto God shall all be turned.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He has ever been sanctified beyond mention and praise, and will ever remain exalted above what the people of creation utter. Since the path to Him is cut off and the proof to Him is rejected, we describe Him as He has described His Essence to His Essence by His Essence, and remember Him as He has remembered His Self to His Self by His Self.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He Who hath sent down the verses in truth unto a people who understand, Who hath expounded therein the mysteries of knowledge and wisdom, and ordained the measure of all things according to a fixed decree. He hath sent forth the Messengers, testifying that there is none other God but Him, the All-Protecting, the Self-Subsisting.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He Who hath revealed His Own Self unto His Own Self, and Who, in the heights of His transcendent unity, is sanctified above the knowledge of His creatures. Praise be unto God Who describeth His attributes unto His attributes, and Who, in the exaltation of His sublime grandeur, is sanctified above the comprehension of His creation.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: None knoweth how He is save He Himself. The Unity hath indicated the Essence of the Will in its realm, and Divinity hath expressed the station of Providence in its ranks. Whosoever saith "He is He" hath indeed associated with Him His creation, and whosoever saith "None knoweth how He is save He" hath indeed coupled his Lord with His creation.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: From time immemorial Thou hast been supreme over all contingent beings, manifest above all existing things, exalted over all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, inaccessible above all who inhabit the realms of names and attributes, transcendent above all created things, and sovereign over all who dwell in the kingdoms of origin and end

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He before Whom boweth down in adoration whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Say: All are submissive to His bidding. Praise be unto God before Whom prostrateth whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever lieth between them. Say: All bow down in worship before Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the One manifest above His creation, and He is the Guardian, the Self-Subsisting. Before Him boweth down in worship whosoever is in the heavens and whosoever is on earth. God beareth witness that there is none other God but He - say: all are His worshippers. God beareth witness that there is none other God but He - say: all bow down before Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In the name of God! Distinction has no station therein, nor can it be assigned. Rather, Praise is a name, then God is a name, then Lord is a name, then Worlds is a name - unto God, Creator of names and majesty. In that station, elevation, establishment and lowering are all valid, for all directions are His names and all expressions are His attributes.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! How can I call upon Thee when Thou knowest my innermost secret? I cannot reckon Thy praise, for Thou canst not be described by other than Thyself, nor be known by any save Thyself. Indeed I know, O my Lord, that Thine Essence hath severed all from knowledge of Thee, and that Thy Being hath barred all from describing Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise and boundless thanksgiving befit the Most Holy Being, the Sovereign Lord, Who has ever been sanctified through His Own Essence from the description of all else but Him, and will everlastingly remain, through His intrinsic nature, as He is - no being existing in His holy presence, and exalted is He above the description of aught else but Himself.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Let nothing veil you from God, your Lord - neither your sovereignty, nor your dominion, nor your knowledge, nor your endeavors, nor your earthly life, nor your life to come. For He is the Creator of all things, and whatsoever is besides Him is but His creation. Therefore, withhold not from Him anything, for He has more right than all else to possess it.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: None shall ever know Thee as befitteth Thy true knowledge, and none shall ever describe Thee as befitteth Thy true description. All that the holy ones know of Thee is but falsehood before the court of Thy holy bountifulness, and all that the unitarians attribute to Thee is but polytheism in the precincts of intimacy with the Sovereign of Thy omnipotence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O God! I beseech Thee by Thy Divinity which is inaccessible above all things... Glorified art Thou, O my God! From time immemorial Thy Will hath been supreme over all contingent beings, Thy Purpose manifest above all created things, Thy Decree exalted above all atoms, and Thy Permission transcendent above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God, Lord of existence and Ruler of the seen and unseen! How can I ever count Thy praises or by what remembrance can I remember Thee that would be worthy of the court of Thy mighty glory? Thou art far exalted above my description and the description of all created things, and sanctified above my praise and the praise of all beings.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou! I should see anyone besides Thee or exalt any other than Thee? And I testify before Thee that this Manifestation is the manifestation of what Thou hast promised to all Thy creation. Is there any goal apart from Thee or any purpose beyond Thee [...] for Thy verses or draw near through Thy chosen ones? Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How then can anyone attain unto Thee or describe Thy beauty? Therefore do I bear witness before Thee, and call to witness the denizens of the Supreme Concourse and the dwellers of the pavilions of eternity, that Thou hast ever been sanctified above the description of all contingent beings and wilt ever remain hallowed beyond the mention of all created things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of essence of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. Therefore, help ye God in the True Faith with a mighty help. Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. Therefore, help ye God in the True Faith with a mighty help.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I testify at this moment that the mention of aught else but Thee can never reach Thee, and the description of all save Thyself can never attain unto Thee. For Thy knowledge soars above the kingdom of immortality, while the mention of all else but Thee is wingless, stationary in the realm of mortality. How then can mortality ascend unto the heaven of immortality?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Eyes comprehend Him not, but He comprehendeth the eyes, and He is the All-Subtle, the All-Informed. The fruit thereof is that His signs are His proof and His existence His evidence. He cannot be known through aught else, nor can He be described save through Himself, for the realm of contingent being is, by its very nature, severed from its Creator and Originator.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Verily I am God, there is no God but Me, the Last, the Last. I have ever been from time immemorial, and shall ever be from time immemorial. I created what I created from a beginning that hath no beginning, and We were powerful over that which We created. And I shall create what is created unto an end that hath no end, and We were mighty over that which We create.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of the lights of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them! Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them! Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of the rubies of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: This is the Festival wherein the Beauty of the Divine Essence hath appeared without veil or concealment, with such sovereignty as hath humbled the necks of the proud. This is the Festival wherein the Beauty of the All-Glorious hath been exalted above all things, and hath spoken between earth and heaven whatsoever He wished and desired, without veil or concealment.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified and exalted is He above what they describe... I testify that Thou art God, the Beloved, Whom nothing can know and none can find a way unto, for Thy Essence is the Camphor-like Reality which by its very nature severs all substances from expression, and Thy Being is the Simple Reality which by its very nature prevents all material things from knowing Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou art independent of all things, and self-sufficient above all things, while all are poor before Thee in love and knowledge, and are servants unto Thee in obedience and faith. All this is far beneath ascription to Thee, for verily Thou art sanctified above all names and attributes, and exalted above all similitudes and indications.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: That sacred Reality is even as the sun, which appeareth in every mirror yet remaineth exalted above all mirrors. Though its light may appear in the mirrors, it dwelleth ever in its own sanctified heights. Were it otherwise, independent existence would belong to both the mirrors and the sun, and the difference between them would be merely nominal, whereas it is real.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: To God belongs the majesty of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them... To God belongs the beauty of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them... To God belongs the grandeur in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them... To God belongs the light of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In any case, in all things that are attributed to God, whether from the highest height or lowest depth -- and this height and depth are mentioned in relation to creation -- all names and attributes have been and are applicable, so long as they abide beneath the shadow of Truth; otherwise the judgment of existence does not apply to them, much less the exalted stations.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Verily, the highest recognition of those who recognize and the utmost attainiment of those who attain returneth unto His creation which was created by His word Be! and it is. All else besides Him is created by His command, brought into being by His will, prostrate before His countenance, and submissive before His presence, and all are preserved with Him in a guarded tablet.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of the essences of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them! Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them! Glorified be He in Whose grasp is the dominion of everlasting things of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise, sanctified from the understanding of all created things, beseemeth the Beloved of the Worlds, Who through the scratching of the Pen hath attracted the gems of the world and guided them to the Most Great Ocean. Holy and sanctified is His mention above the mentions of the people of the earth; exalted and glorified is His description above the descriptions of creation.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The Most Exalted Pen is bewildered as to what to mention, and the Most Glorious Horizon is deep in thought as to what to declare. Though ears were created for this Day, yet, as a consequence of their deeds, they are debarred from hearkening, and though eyes came from sheer nothingness into the realm of being to behold the divine signs, veils and wrappings have withheld them.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: When the servant looks with the eye of oneness and observes nothing in the reference to the cloud besides God the All-Glorious - for God the All-Glorious has ever been, and there was naught else with Him that could be above all things, or within things, or from things, or upon things - rather, pre-existence is His Self, and the cloud is His Essence, and eternity is His Being.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou hast ever been sanctified above all names and exalted beyond all similitudes. Glorified, glorified art Thou beyond being known through Thy creation, or being exalted through the worship of those Thou hast created or wilt create, or being praised by the praise of those Thou hast brought into being or wilt bring into being, for all these are Thy creation and within Thy grasp.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: What do I have and what right have I to remember Thee? And what is the servant in relation to praising Thee? What is the servant in his standing before Thee? I confess my weakness and bear witness to that which Thou lovest for the people of creation. How can I not, when my very existence and that of my Lord in Thy dominion has no permanence? What can one who is non-existent love?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Should anyone reflect even briefly upon that which hath been manifested, he would, in truth, find himself bewildered and would declare with his outer and inner tongue: No bird of understanding can soar to Thy heights. Glorified, glorified art Thou above my description and the description of all who describe Thee, and above my mention and the mention of all who make mention of Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who is single in His bounty and unique in His beneficence, Who is sanctified above whatsoever the people of creation utter and holy beyond every mention and description... How can this impotent one mention Thee after acknowledging and confessing that all remembrances and descriptions are barred from Thy holy court and forbidden from the carpet of intimacy with Thee?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Though He, exalted and mighty is He, has been described by the tongues of all created things past and future, every possessor of knowledge testifies that He has not been described nor characterized. Exalted be His greatness, elevated His sovereignty, mighty His glory! His Self is sanctified and His Essence is purified from all that has been known or unknown, mentioned or unmentioned.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou hast distinguished Thyself above all things, and through Thy loftiness Thou hast transcended the elevation of all things, and through Thy grandeur Thou hast risen above the exaltation of all things. None of Thy servants shall ever know Thee, nor shall any dweller of Thy earth and heaven describe Thee as befitteth the sublimity of Thy glory and the exaltation of Thy sovereignty.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: By my father and mother and all that my Lord knoweth! Neither I nor anyone else hath any mention before you, for all existing things, in the camphor-like essence of their realities, are as nothing beneath the splendor of your countenance, and all contingent things, in the pure abstraction of their being, are utterly non-existent before the manifestation of a remembrance from your hearts.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him: we are His worshippers. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him: we are prostrate before Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him: we are devoted to Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him: we are thankful unto Him. This is God, your Lord; there is none other God but Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou hast ever been sanctified through might and omnipotence, glorified through grandeur and divinity, exalted through dominion and might, possessed of all things through sovereignty and glory, and elevated above all things through sublime holiness and the manifestations of might and the unseen. All creation is in Thy grasp. Thou wert before all things, and Thou shalt be after all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified and exalted art Thou! Thou hast ever been and wilt ever be. No vision can grasp Thee, and Thou hast no likeness, no equal, no peer. Thy Being in its camphor-like essence cuts off all camphor-like essences; Thy Reality in its pristine nature severs all pristine natures; Thy Substance in its identity severs all substances; and Thy Abstraction in its ipseity severs all abstractions.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who hath ascended in His exaltation above all contingent beings, and risen in His loftiness above all created things, and become inaccessible in His remoteness above all existing things... Vision comprehendeth Him not, nor do the thoughts of minds encompass Him, nor can the hidden glances of contemplation reach Him, nor can the highest expressions of praise ascend unto Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who through His exaltation hath risen above all contingent beings [...] Praise be to God Who hath exalted Himself in His sublimity above all created things, and hath risen in His ascendancy above all existing things, and hath made Himself inaccessible in His inaccessibility above all atoms, and hath manifested His power above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified be He Who moved it, and glorified be He Who gave it speech, and glorified be He Who made it known, and glorified be He Who taught it the knowledge of what hath been and what shall be. He hath ever been sanctified above all names and shall ever remain exalted above whatsoever the people of creation utter. Whosoever claimeth to know Him is gainsaid by the tongues of all created things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O my God! Thou art too exalted to be asked about Thy generosity or bounty, too inaccessible to be questioned about Thy grace and mercy, too elevated to be asked about Thy kindness and care, too sanctified to be questioned about Thy tenderness, mercy and loving-kindness, and too holy to be associated with anything that could be named in the kingdom of Thy heaven and the earth of Thy providence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou! How can I comprehend Thy majesty, O my God, when I behold Thy Beloved and see countless possessors of majesty in His shadow - those endowed with sovereignty, knowledge, loftiness and elevation? Yet all of this, before the majesty of Thy Beloved, is as naught, for He prostrateth Himself before Thee and worshippeth Thy Being. How then can I know Thy majesty or reckon Thy grandeur?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: They acknowledge that "He doeth what He willeth," yet they question His actions with "why" and "wherefore." They recognize that "He ordaineth what He pleaseth," yet they hesitate regarding that which hath appeared from Him. Were He to decree existence for that which hath no existence, or were He to apply the law of evanescence to that which endureth, none hath the right to say "why" or "wherefore."

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: God is the First - no first is mentioned with Him, and He is the Originator of the first ones. Say: God is the Last - no last is mentioned with Him, and He is the Creator of the last ones. Say: God is the Manifest - naught is mentioned with Him, and He is the Revealer of them that manifest. Say: God is the Hidden - naught shall be mentioned with Him, and He is the Concealer of them that are hidden.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee! How can I say Thou art One, when Thou art the Unifier of all who profess oneness? Glory be unto Thee! How can I say Thou art the Adorner, when Thou art the One Who adorneth all adorners? Glory be unto Thee! How can I say Thou art Pure, when Thou art the Source of all purity? Glory be unto Thee! How can I say Thou art Unique, when Thou art the One Who maketh unique all who are unique?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou art exalted above all description through the transcendence of Thy Being, and Thou art sanctified above the attributes of all things through the sublimity of Thy Essence. Thy camphoric nature, as it is, severs all camphoric realities from mention of Names and Attributes, and Thy pristine nature, as it is, severs all pristine realities from what can be realized of Thy praise in the earth and heavens.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou art the One known between them, in the hereafter and in the first life. By Thy might! I have found none known, neither before nor after, none beloved, neither in heaven nor on earth, none described, neither in the kingdom of command nor of creation, none sought after, neither in the heights nor in the depths, and none worshipped besides Thee, neither in the highest kingdom nor in the lowest particle.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thine Essence can only be known through Thine Own Self, and Thy Being can only be described through Thine Eternity. Creation, even at the highest reaches of eloquence and the zenith of detachment, can only judge from the station of names and can only be guided from the realm of attributes - attributes which are in themselves cut off from creation and whose essence is sanctified above the plane of invention.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He, exalted and glorified be He, cannot be known in His essence nor worshipped in His Reality. Whatever appears among contingent beings are but signs of His creation, and whatever comes into existence among all things are but lights of His invention. Exalted, exalted be the glory of His grandeur above all similarity and comparison! Exalted, exalted be the majesty of His oneness above all likeness and forms!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: God cannot be known by anything, and all by His command do know themselves, then unto Him do magnify. Say: God cannot be brought into being by anything, neither in the Kingdom of the heavens and earth and all that lies between them, and He is not associated with His creation, neither in remembrance nor in praise, nor in that which ye glorify and extol, nor in that which ye declare His unity and magnify.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: We, of the Orient, distinguish between the wholly transcendent Primal Deity, in the Christian sense God the Father, and the Logos (Gospel of St. John, chapt. I, verses 1 and , in the Christian sense God the Son, also called Demiurge (in the sense of the Greek philosophers), also called the Primal Will by His Holiness the Bab and designated by the Sufis (religious brotherhood) by the name of taw?id = oneness.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise, sanctified beyond mention and utterance, befitteth the Lord of all possibility, Who from agitation brought forth tranquility, and from tumult created assurance. Thou hast ever been sanctified beyond the remembrance of those who remember, the praise of those who praise, and the description of those who describe. Thou wert hidden from the sight of Thy creation and concealed from the eyes of Thy servants.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is sanctified above all similitude and exalted above all comparison. There is no description other than His Essence and no name other than His Being. All that those who describe Him say regarding the attributes of His Self, and all that those who remember Him say regarding the names of His Essence, returns to themselves. He is more glorious than to be known through His creation or described by His servants.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Through but one letter of His glorious Name did the universe and all within it become manifest and evident. All that exists hath been and shall ever be through the effulgence of His bounty. The heaven is a sign of His loftiness and the seas are tokens of His grandeur. Whatever we may say, the seeing eye beholdeth in but a single leaf among the leaves of the divine Lote-Tree His majesty, power, exaltation and favor.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the First before all things, yet cannot be known through firstness; He is the Last after all things, yet cannot be described through lastness; He is the Outward above all things, yet cannot be characterized through outwardness; He is the Inward beneath all things, yet cannot be comprehended through inwardness. He is the One, not from number nor likeness, and He is the Single, not from similitude nor semblance.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Know then that there hath come before the Divine Throne thy letter wherein thou didst make mention of thyself, and toward which were directed the glances of thy Lord, the Lord of all worlds. Therein didst thou ask that which befitteth neither thy station nor the station of any in the heavens and earth. For the Truth, exalted be His mention, has had and shall have no connection or relationship with any created thing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: As to the station of the Godhead, it is exalted above and sanctified beyond the understanding of all created things, how much more above resolving itself into their realities! The truth, however, is that the reality of that sanctified Essence can in no wise descend into the realm of creation. For Him there is no egress or regress, no descent or dissolution, no composition or commingling; only infinite transcendence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou art far too exalted and glorious, too great and too mighty for eyes to perceive even the least token of Thy sovereignty's manifestations, or for hearts to know aught of the manifestations of Thy power. Thou art He Who existed before all things, and Thou art the Creator of all things, and Thou art He Who shall remain after all things. Thou hast ever been, and wilt ever be. Thou canst not be known, nor described...

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I see that every eloquent one, every articulate one, every speaker and describer - their tongues all fall short in describing a single sign of Thy power and characterizing a single word of Thy creation. The birds of minds have broken their wings in attempting to soar to the holy atmosphere of Thy oneness, and the spiders of imagination are unable to weave their webs in the highest pinnacle of the domes of Thy knowledge.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The essential camphor-like purity of Thy Being hath been sanctified beyond the comprehension of all created things, and the pristine essence of Thy Reality hath been glorified above the praise of all existent things. The quintessential nature of Thy Self hath been exalted beyond description by any beings, and the pure abstraction of Thine Identity hath been elevated beyond characterization by any dwellers of earth and heaven.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: All praise, illimitable and transcendent, befitteth the Most Holy, Most Impregnable, Most Exalted, Most Glorious, Most Great, Most Supreme Beloved, Who hath ever been sanctified beyond the comprehension of His creation's highest faculties - whether they be holy temples, glorifying essences, or exalted letters - and Who shall forever remain, through His sovereign might and majesty, far above the recognition of all else but Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O Thou through Whose will the rivers of inner meanings have flowed in the gardens of utterance, and the hearts of the monotheists were attracted by what the Pen of Thy Cause spoke forth in the wonders of knowledge. The servant beareth witness to Thy unity and the singleness of Thy Being, and recognizeth that which the tongue of Thy grandeur hath spoken in the Kingdom of certitude, that verily Thou art God, there is no God but Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou hast ever been one God, single, eternal, self-subsisting, ever-living, everlasting, eternal, self-dependent. Thou hast not taken unto Thyself any [...] Ever-enduring, eternal, and self-subsisting art Thou! Thou hast never taken unto Thyself either consort or son. Thou dost ever give life and cause to die, then cause to die and give life. Verily, Thou art powerful, mighty, and omnipotent; manifest, inaccessible, and all-knowing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God testifieth that there is none other God but Him, and we bear witness even as He hath testified to His Own Self by His Own Self, and verily we are all turned toward His direction. He hath testified by His Own Self that He Who hath appeared with the truth is indeed His Glory unto all who dwell in the highest Paradise, His Proof unto all who abide in the kingdom of creation, and His Evidence unto all in the unseen and visible worlds.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O God! Send Thy blessings upon Muhammad, Thy chosen servant, whom Thou didst select for Thyself and preferred above all created things, making him the manifestation of Thy sovereignty in all realms and spaces, thus demonstrating the transcendence of Thy Being above creation and the appearance of invention. For verily, Thou art not associated with the making of things, nor art Thou described by the manifestations of the people of glory.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God, Who is sanctified above all mention and glorification and exalted above whatsoever the tongues may utter and the pens of all created things may set in motion. He Who hath caused His most exalted horizon to appear through His Most Glorious Name and hath summoned all unto it through His sweetest call, whereby those endued with understanding and they who are established upon the thrones of the names have been enraptured.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee! No attribute of distinctness, nor of essence, nor of being, nor of splendor, nor of eternality, nor of holiness, nor of sanctity can describe Thee. Thou hast ever been without the qualification of permanence, timelessness, praise, divinity, lordship, or divine laudation. For Thou hast ever been unassociated with the creation of things, nor with the darknesses of praise, nor with the oppositions of beauty and majesty.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God has chosen you from amongst his creatures to be the custodians of the secrets of knowledge. He has appointed you to be the vivifiers of the world of humanity. The essence of God being absolutely incomprehensible, unknowable, unsearchable, unattainable, unrealizable, we must turn our faces to those chosen, pure channels through whom the Grace, the Grandeur, the Knowledge and the Power of the Almighty are distributed amongst mortals.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee, O God, Who liftest grief from our pens and causeth them to enter a garden through praise of Thyself. Unto Thee be praise, O my God, praise that is radiant, gleaming, hallowed, shining, sanctified, glittering, exalted and rolling like thunder, in the way that Thou lovest for Thyself and which Thou alone deservest according to the grace of Thine Own Self unto Thine Own Self, in such wise as none of Thy creation can know.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: O people, fear ye God and make not His Cause limited by the limitations of your own selves. Fear God and be not of the transgressors. Say: Verily He cannot be limited by any limit and cannot be veiled by any veil. He manifesteth as He pleaseth, and verily He is the All-Choosing, the Powerful, the Wise. Nothing can prevent Him from His Command and His sovereignty, and the schemes of the schemers and the might of monarchs cannot frustrate Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: My God, my God! Thy Essence is sanctified above all vision and understanding, and Thy Reality is exalted beyond all unveiling and witnessing. There is no way to know Thy Essence and no proof to comprehend the nature of Thy attributes. How can the birds of thoughts reach the kingdom of mysteries? How can a broken wing and weary bird soar to heights that cannot be attained? The paths to attainment are cut off and the ways to achievement are barred.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou! There is no God but Thee. Thou art the One Who is worshipped, and all else is Thy creation. Thou art the One Who is sought, and all else is Thy servant. Thou art the Beloved, unto Whose presence all do yearn and before Whose sovereignty all wish to stand. Thou art the All-Glorious, Whom no heart's bird can ever praise adequately. Thou art the Most Holy, unto Whose court of oneness no essence stripped of all else can ever ascend.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The source of derivation of all names, deeds and attributes is God, glorified and exalted be He, Who is far above being associated with His creation. Rather, He originated His creation without any prior creation, without modality, and without any subsequent indication, and made it the station of His Self in all the worlds of His Command and creation. For eyes cannot perceive Him, but He perceives all eyes, and He is the All-Subtle, the All-Informed.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: But the Divine Light of God is the light of the heavens and earth. This Divine Light is beyond the limit of time, past, present and future all are the same to it. This is why it is said in the Koran "God is the Light of the Heavens and Earth." In brief this Divine Light is the revealer of things, it is the discoverer of things, and it comprehends them before the existence of things and after the manifestation of them. It is beyond the limits of time.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In the Name of our Lord, the Most High, the Most Exalted! Verily, there is none other God but Him. He hath created all contingent beings through His pre-existent knowledge of what was and what shall be, and taught them the ways of righteousness by sending unto them the Messengers of the Cause with a mighty revealed Book wherein He ordained holy laws and determined the destinies of all who dwell in the heavens and on earth according to a fixed measure.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is none other God but He, and we are all submissive unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but He, and we all prostrate ourselves before Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but He, and we are all obedient unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but He, and we all yearn for Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but He, and unto Him shall we all return.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee! How can I praise Thee after my knowledge that my praise, like my existence, is as nothing before Thee? And how can I remember Thee, O my Lord, after my certitude in what Thou art, that Thou canst not be known through other than Thyself, nor described save through Thyself, nor characterized except by Thyself, nor unified through Thy creation, nor worshipped through anything in Thy kingdom, nor praised through anything in Thy dominion?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Exalted, supremely exalted is His transcendent glory above the ascent of the most elevated essences of the adorned ones, or the rising to His holy atmosphere of the ethereal substances of the manifested ones. He is the Being through the essence of His Own Self, the All-Knowing through the knowledge of His Own Reality, the All-Hearing through His Own hearing, the All-Seeing through His holy vision, and the Most Subtle through the subtlety of His Own identity.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thine is whatsoever Thou hast loved or wilt love in the Kingdom of Thy Command and Creation. Thou hast ever been before all things, existing after all things, transcendent above all things, and the Creator of all things. Thou wilt ever remain one God, Single, Eternal, Individual, Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting, Sovereign, Supreme, Holy, Everlasting, Inaccessible, Exalted, Most High, Ruling, All-Possessing, All-Powerful. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! None can witness a flash from the lightning of the fire of the Tree of Thy pre-existence, nor can anyone behold a light from the lights of the Countenance of Thy crimson glory. The most abstract essences of the Divine Realm are bewildered at the appearance of a gleam from the gleams of the fire of Thy Being, and the most sublime essences of the Realm of Might are intoxicated at a spark from the sparks of the light of Thy distinction.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: For Thou, O my God, in Thy Essence art not joined with anything, and in Thy Reality nothing can comprehend Thee, and in Thy Purity nothing can glorify Thee, and in Thy Simplicity nothing can thank Thee, and in Thy Self nothing can unify Thee, for all else beside Thee hath been clothed with the garment of limitation in creation, and Thou art far exalted above being mentioned with the most sublime mention of invention and the most glorious height of transcendence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Sanctified art Thou in Thy Being above all things, magnified art Thou in Thine Essence above the loftiness of all things, transcended in Thy Self-Subsistence above all things, and glorified Thyself in Thy grandeur above the elevation of all things. Thou hast ever been one God, Single, Unique, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, Ever-Living, Self-Sustaining. Thou hast taken neither consort nor son, and Thou hast had no partner in Thy creation nor any associate in Thy invention.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the One Who created the heavens with a word from His Book and sent forth the Messengers and revealed the Books testifying that there is none other God but Him, and He Whom He hath manifested is the Truth from His presence. All this was inscribed in a Book which God sealed with the seal of protection, wherein He ordained the measures of all things according to the balance of justice that was weighed in the Ridvan of the Divine Essence by the measure of the Spirit.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Blessed art Thou, O Lord of the Covenant, above the comprehension of minds throughout the horizons, and sanctified art Thou, O Lord of Radiance, above the imaginings of the people of dissension and the understanding of the chiefs of concord. All minds are but fetters that prevent the birds from soaring to the zenith of understanding, and all comprehension is but illness, for they traverse not the desert of ignorance until they reach the heights of knowledge and wisdom.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He hath been from the beginning that hath no beginning a sovereign, omnipotent, and will be unto the end that hath no end a sovereign, omnipotent... He hath been from the beginning that hath no beginning the Beloved, the Most High, and will be unto the end that hath no end the Beloved, the Most High... He hath been from the beginning that hath no beginning the All-Desired, the Most Glorious, and will be unto the end that hath no end the All-Desired, the Most Glorious...

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O Word of Faithfulness! Bear thou witness in this station wherein the Divine Identity is established upon the Throne of Eternity, unto this most holy, most inaccessible, most glorious, most mighty, most exalted, most sacred, most sanctified, most manifest, most pure, most sublime, most resplendent Beauty, Who revealed from behind seventy thousand veils, to the measure of a needle's eye, a light from the lights of His Beauty upon the throne of the Unseen and of the Cloud.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be sanctified above all utterance, exposition, and whatsoever pertaineth to the contingent world - praise that befitteth the most holy court of the Best Beloved... How can ink, whose quantity is but an indivisible particle, be capable of mentioning that Ocean before which all other seas appear mean and poor? How can a pen, but a span in length or less, be worthy to describe that Sovereign before Whom all the pens of the world confess their inability and impotence?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who hath raised up His Cause and manifested His sovereignty in such wise that neither the doubts of the skeptics, nor the utterances of the polytheists, nor the pronouncements of those who have denied the Day of Judgment could hinder it. Verily, He is the Single, the One, the All-Powerful, Who hath ever been supreme over all who are in the heavens and the earth, and exalted above the comprehension of those who dwell in the kingdoms of creation and command.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified and exalted is He! He hath forbidden the recognition of the innermost essence of His divine Countenance to the people of allusions, and hath removed from the nearness of His holy dominion all material entities from among the people of the veils. For He is too glorious to be wrathful through His supreme essence, with which nothing can be associated and unto which nothing can ascend. He hath ever been such that nothing comprehendeth Him while He comprehendeth all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He beareth witness, and all His creation beareth witness, that there is no God but Him, the One, the All-Witnessing. He further testifieth, and all His creation testifieth, that there is none other God but Him, the One, the All-Compelling. Again He testifieth, and all His creation testifieth, that there is none other God but Him, the One, the All-Subduing. Yet again He testifieth, and all His creation testifieth, that there is none other God but Him, the One, the All-Conquering.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Neither in the heavens nor on earth nor in what lies between them. He createth what He willeth by His command. Verily, He hath power over all things. Blessed is He to Whom belongeth the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what lieth between them. There is none other God but He, the Mighty, the Beloved. Exalted is He to Whom belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and on earth and what lieth between them. There is none other God but He, the All-Subduing, the Self-Subsisting.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou! Glorified art Thou! How could it be possible in contingent existence to know Thee, when the very existence of a thing in itself is proof of its limitation? Eyes cannot perceive Thy grandeur, nor can any who would describe Thee describe Thy attributes. Thy very essence, as it is in itself, transcends all essence beyond the bounds of mention and utterance, and Thy very nature, as it is in itself, transcends all nature beyond the heights of bounty and knowledge.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the First, and there is no first before Him; He is the Last, and there is no last besides Him; He is the Manifest, and there is none manifest before Him; and He is the Beholder, and there is no beholder besides Him. He hath shown His might through the essence of His sovereign Self-Subsistence, before Whose loftiness all contingent things bow down in submission, and He is unique in the kingdom of His holy eternity, before Whose exaltation all existing things humble themselves.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Him! Nothing is like unto Him. He is the One, the Supreme, the All-Compelling.
