All praise be unto God Who hath exalted Himself through the sublimity of His grandeur above the most elevated essence of abstract realities, and Who hath magnified Himself through His Essential Eternity above the uttermost knowledge of all essential beings. He hath ever been beyond the reach of all names and attributes, and no created thing can attain unto the ultimate understanding of Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who hath risen in the transcendence of His Self-Subsistence above all contingent things, and hath prevailed through His primordial sovereignty over all created things, and hath manifested through the revelation of His oneness above all existing things, and hath exalted Himself through the elevation of His Self-Subsistence above all atoms, and hath remained inaccessible through the inaccessibility of His sanctity above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: But the inner reality of the Essence of the True One (praised be He) is beyond the province of Possible Being. Rather it is the knowledge of the traces and effulgences of that Most Holy and Forbidden Mystery. For however much detached minds and pure souls seek to penetrate the worlds of Inner Knowledge, their understanding will never penetrate more than that station which is a sign pointing towards the Monarch of Primal Oneness which He has placed as a trust within the reality of man.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee! Neither can thoughts of reflection grasp Thy signs through mine ears, nor the most subtle contemplations. Thou art God; there is no God but Thee. I testify that Thy description of Thyself is without change, and no description exists for aught else before Thee, nor any description from Thee unto them. Glorified art Thou! Sanctified is Thy Self from the description of all else, for they know not the truth of Thy attributes, nor can they comprehend the essence of Thy Being.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, and exalted art Thou! Thou lovest to raise up another House and to establish all that Thou hast raised therein. Through this are made manifest the seats of Thy command and prohibition, and the dawning-places of Thy power and might in every Revelation. Otherwise, there would be no Manifest One in the manifestations except Thee, no Hidden One in the concealments save Thee, no Inaccessible One in the essences except Thee, and no Transcendent One in the abstractions but Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The Truth has ever judged among men according to outward appearances, and all the Prophets and Messengers were commanded to judge among creatures according to the outer appearance, and no other way is permitted. All who are in earth and heaven were created by His Word and have come from utter nothingness into the realm of being. How then can a created thing which was brought into being by the Word ascend unto the Ancient Being? O Salman! The way of all to the Ancient Being hath ever been barred.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou, O my God! By Thy might, were I to attempt to describe, throughout the duration of Thy sovereign might and the continuance of Thy pure power, even a drop of what Thou hast created therein of the manifestations of Thy creative act and the holy expressions of Thy divinity, I would be utterly powerless, enfeebled and at a loss, ere I could utter a single letter of the essence of that which Thou hast created therein by Thy power and brought into being by Thy will.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Sanctified art Thou, O Lord of might and glory! None besides Thee, O my God, can be mentioned whereby Thou mightest be mentioned. None besides Thee, O my Beloved, can be described whereby Thou mightest be described. None besides Thee, O my Goal, can be characterized whereby Thou mightest be characterized. None besides Thee, O Thou Who art characterized, can be praised whereby Thou mightest be praised. None besides Thee, O Thou Who art described, can be glorified whereby reference might be made to Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the One, the Unique, the Powerful, the Mighty. He hath ever been a hidden and treasured Mystery, and will forever remain as He hath been - the One, the Unique, the Mighty, the Bestower. Every tongue hath been rendered mute before the waves of His ocean of utterance, and all hearts and minds have been bewildered before the dawning-lights of the Sun of His knowledge. He hath ever been sanctified beyond all praise and mention, and beyond all that the denizens of the kingdom of creation have uttered.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, the Most Holy, the Most High. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, the Lord of all worlds. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, the Knower of the unseen and the seen. Say: He is the All-Merciful, the All-Compassionate. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Faithful, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Omnipotent, the Most High, the Inaccessible, the Most High.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou beyond my power to describe Thee through aught except Thyself, for verily Thou art manifest above all things, mighty over all things, dominant over all things, and subsistent over every soul. From time immemorial Thou hast never been known by the names of Thy kingdom, nor described by what Thou hast created from the manifestations of the kingdom of Thy sovereignty. Thou art He Who cannot be known except through Thyself, and Thou art He Who cannot be described save through Thine Own Self.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I testify that every man of equity hath recognized his unfairness in the face of the revelation of the splendors of the Day-Star of Thy Justice, and the ablest of pens hath confessed its impotence before the movement of Thy most exalted Pen. The minds of the profoundest thinkers are sore perplexed as they contemplate the ocean of Thy knowledge, and the heaven of Thy wisdom, and the Luminary of Thy grace. How can he who is but a creation of Thy will claim to know what is with Thee, or to conceive Thy nature?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Were I to praise Thee through attributes, I would witness that they are Thy creation and within Thy grasp, and it befitteth not their manifestations to stand before the gate of the city of Thy Revelation - how much less the station whereon Thou art established upon the throne of Thy grandeur and might, O Lord of Names and Creator of heaven! All that is adorned with the garment of words is verily created in Thy kingdom and brought into being by Thy will, and is unworthy of Thy presence and unsuited to Thy court.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The Truth, exalted be His mention, has ever been and shall ever be sanctified above manifestation and appearance - an unknowable Mystery, an imperceptible Concealment, an unmanifested Inner Reality, an unhidden Treasure, and an unwitnessed Secret. For the term "mystery" applies only when something is not witnessed; in such case it is not manifest that it might be known. And after witnessing, the term "mystery" no longer exists that it might be understood. Therefore the Mystery has been and shall ever be unknowable.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I shall sanctify Thee, O God, above all that hath sanctified Thee or shall sanctify Thee. I shall exalt Thee, O God, above all that hath exalted Thee or shall exalt Thee. I shall glorify Thee, O God, above all that hath glorified Thee or shall glorify Thee. I shall magnify Thee, O God, above all that hath magnified Thee or shall magnify Thee. I shall extol Thee, O God, above all that hath extolled Thee or shall extol Thee. I shall aggrandize Thee, O God, above all that hath aggrandized Thee or shall aggrandize Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the First of the first. Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the Last of the last. Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the Most Manifest of the manifest. Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the Most Hidden of the hidden. Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the Beloved of all worlds. Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the Worshipped One of all worlds. Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the Desired One of all worlds. Glory be unto Thee, O God! Thou art the Praised One in all worlds.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Sanctified is Thy Being in its essence that none among created things can know it, exalted is Thy pure Reality that none among contingent things can comprehend it, glorified is Thy essential Self that none among created things can find it. Thy pure Being hath dominated in such wise that none in the kingdoms of earth and heaven can magnify it as befitteth the majesty of Thy unique sovereignty and the sanctity of Thy eternal Self-Sufficiency, though all would glorify Thee, praise Thee, proclaim Thy unity and magnify Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: As to the question of Divinity, the reality of Divinity in its fullness cannot be comprehended within human capacity, for that which proceeds from minds and thoughts is limited while the reality of Divinity is unlimited. What is clear and evident are His manifest signs which have set the world of being in motion. But the reality of Divinity is sanctified and exalted above the comprehension of all created things. How can a contingent reality comprehend the Ancient Reality? This is impossible and unattainable. The mineral and vegetable kingdoms are unaware of the human and animal realms and can never conceive of them. Is it possible for mineral and vegetable to comprehend the reality of hearing and sight? God forbid! And yet all these are within the realm of creation. How then can a contingent being comprehend the Ancient Reality? The utmost that man can do is to comprehend the divine signs and traces.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God testifieth that there is no God but Him. His is the Kingdom and the Dominion, then the Might and the Omnipotence, then the Power and the Divine Essence, then the Strength and the Ruby, then the Sovereignty and the Human Realm. He causeth to live and to die, then causeth to die and to live. He, verily, is the Ever-Living Who dieth not, the King Who passeth not away, the Just Who wrongeth not, the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on earth or between them.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He is the Glorious, the All-Glorious, the Most Glorious. Praise that is sanctified beyond the comprehension of all created things and exalted above the understanding of all that can perceive befitteth the matchless King of Glory, Who hath ever been sanctified above the mention of aught else but Him and will forever remain exalted beyond the description of all save Himself. None hath ever ascended to the heaven of His praise as beseemeth Him, and no soul hath ever mounted to the heights of His description as is worthy of Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou art He Who hath never been known in all eternity, and Thou art He Who shall never be described in all that pertaineth unto Thee. Thou art He Who hath never been worshipped as befitteth true worship, neither in the kingdom of earth nor of the heavens. Thou art He Who cannot be characterized with the attributes worthy of Thy sovereignty, neither in the realm of names nor of attributes. Thou art He Who cannot be remembered with the remembrance due unto Thee, neither in the kingdom of the beginning nor of endless eternities.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify, and all things testify, that Thou art God, and that there is no God but Thee, alone without peer. How can I ascend unto the heaven of Thine eternal holiness, or soar into the atmosphere of Thy transcendent Self-Subsistence through praise before Thee and glorification of Thee? Verily that which is possible in creation or conceivable in invention befitteth not the sublime holiness of the King of Thy unity, nor can the glances of nearness to the Sovereign of Thy Self-Subsistence comprehend it.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou! Verily, Thou art God, the Single, the One, the Self-Subsisting, Whom none can know save Thyself. Thou art the Just One. If I say Thou art Thou, then likeness would be compared to likeness, yet Thou canst never be known thereby. And if I say He is Thou, then Oneness would indicate the essence of creation and Unity the reality of invention, which in itself decisively proves and distinctly separates created things through exclusion, for Thou hast never been associated with Thy creation nor described by Thy servants.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: It is clearly evident that the sanctified reality of Godhead is beyond any description and incomparable to any attribute. No matter how exalted human conception may be, it can never aspire to gain a glimpse into that sacred Realm, much less gain an understanding of its reality. The Divine Reality is sanctified from all attributes, descriptions and praise. There is no admittance unto that Court and this world has no relation to that Dominion. "No vision taketh in Him, but He taketh in all vision: and He is the Subtle, the All-informed."

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: There is no God but God from the beginning that had no beginning, He Who hath ever been and ever shall be. And verily all that ye behold in the Bayan or in the Books sent down from heaven are attributed to the Exponents of God as they are attributed to God, that ye may be assured of the Cause of God and may manifest for His sake what ye desire. Otherwise, God is the Unseen, the Inaccessible, the Exalted, the Transcendent. No vision can grasp Him, but He graspeth all things by His command. He is the Sovereign, the Inaccessible, the Most High.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Bear thou witness, O friend, that God, the Lord of might and power and eternity, then the Lord of grandeur and loftiness and radiance, then the Lord of beauty and majesty and supreme glory and splendor, when He revealed the mystery of His Self and the secret of His Being and the essence of His Oneness and the reality of His exaltation and the light of His presence in the year sixty, promised those servants who believed in Him beneath the Tree of the Bayan that He would reveal the mystery of His Beauty in the ninth and then in the eightieth year.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Verily, I am God; there is none other God besides Me, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. I have manifested Myself unto men, and have sent down Him Who is the Day Spring of the signs of My Revelation. Through Him I have caused all creation to testify that there is none other God except Him, the Incomparable, the All-Informed, the All-Wise. He Who is everlastingly hidden from the eyes of men can never be known except through His Manifestation, and His Manifestation can adduce no greater proof of the truth of His Mission than the proof of His own Person.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thou art sanctified above all names and exalted above all similitudes, and holy above whatsoever is in the kingdom of command and creation. Thou art the One Who existed before all things, and Thou art the Being after all things, and Thou art the Creator of all things, and Thou art the Essence apart from all things. Thou hast ever been supreme above all contingent beings, manifest above all existing things, inaccessible above all created things, exalted above all things that exist, transcendent above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He hath ever been sanctified beyond the mention of all created things and exalted above the description of all beings. He hath ever been one in His Essence, one in His attributes, and one in His deeds. Every learned one hath failed to reckon what hath been sent down from the heaven of His grace, and every tongue hath fallen silent before the surging waves of the ocean of His remembrance. Every mystic hath confessed his ignorance before the dawning lights of the Sun of His knowledge, and every sage his inability to ascend unto the heaven of His wisdom.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. His is the Kingdom and the Dominion, then the Might and the Omnipotence, then the Power and the Divine Essence, then the Strength and the Ruby, then the Sovereignty and the Human realm. He causeth to live and to die, then causeth to die and to live, and verily He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not, and the King Who passeth not away, and the Just One Who wrongeth not, and the Sovereign Who changeth not, and the Single One from Whose grasp nothing escapeth, whether in the heavens or on earth or between them.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: All that spirits have known is but a sign in His grasp, and all that souls have witnessed is but a token of His eternity, and all that bodies have uttered is but a manifestation of the exaltation of His sovereignty. Verily He, exalted and glorified be He, has ever been an inaccessible mystery, transcendent, sovereign, omnipotent, possessing all things, manifest, well-pleasing. The thoughts of minds cannot comprehend Him, nor can the essence of sight encompass Him. He is as He has described Himself and above what the possessors of insight and vision say of Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. Within His grasp is the kingdom of glory of the heavens and earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is possessed of mighty glory. God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. Within His grasp is the kingdom of majesty of the heavens and earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is possessed of mighty majesty. God beareth witness that there is no God but Him. Within His grasp is the kingdom of beauty of the heavens and earth and whatsoever lieth between them, and God is possessed of mighty beauty.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He was and naught was with Him. He has ever been and there was nothing besides Him. He was God and there was nothing like unto what He was, nor any likeness of Him, nor did anything emanate from Him, nor did anything ascend unto Him, nor did anything move upon the plane of His Self-Subsistence. He is an Entity, pure and camphor-like, such that the inmost realities of all contingent beings fall short of comprehending Him, and He is God before Whom the abstract realities of all created things are severed from any mention of nearness unto Him. None knoweth Him save Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: All names have been and shall forever remain within the grasp of His power, and all people of diverse nations are clinging to and holding fast unto the divine names, for no soul hath the power to transgress the Kingdom of Names or to step outside His command. If We were to say they clung to names and remained veiled from the recognition of the Essence, all people share this station, for all besides Him have been and shall ever be veiled from recognizing His exalted Essence. The way is barred and the path is impassable. He was, and there was nothing besides Him that could know Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify, and all things testify, that Thou art God, there is no God but Thee. Unto Thee belong all glory and grandeur, all majesty and might, all radiance and splendor, all beauty and perfection, all light and illumination, all mercy and compassion, all completion and fulfillment, all greatness and excellence, all power and authority, all knowledge and wisdom, all might and strength, all love and affection, all honor and nobility, all sovereignty and dominion, all kingship and rule, all exaltation and transcendence, all eternality and everlastingness.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Indeed, God, glorified be He, is manifest to thee through thee, observing thee through thee, and encompassing thee through thee. This station is thy highest paradise and thy farthest mosque, for the people of the paradise of good-pleasure have nothing but the mention of God's greatest name and His mightiest, most generous name. This level cannot be indicated through indication - with the perfection of its nearness it is distant, and with the perfection of its remoteness it is near. No veil can conceal it, and it is above all things, hidden in mystery and veiled in the most secret mystery.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be to God Who hath revealed Himself unto all created things through that Name whereby the Concourse on High rejoiced, the hearts of the Manifestations of Names took flight, and through which the lovers uttered "My soul be a sacrifice unto Thee," and the Dove of Holiness warbled upon the Divine Lote-Tree. Then the Tongue of Grandeur spoke between the heavens: "By God, the Truth! That which hath come is that by which all atoms were attracted, and verily He is the One Who was forever hidden, none being aware of Him save His Own Self, the One Who dominates all who are in the heavens and the earth."

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How can a tongue that calls upon other than Thee be worthy to make mention of Thee, and how can a heart that hath turned to any save Thee be fitting to become a mirror of Thy beauty and be warmed by Thy love? How can an eye that hath beheld aught except Thee and turned toward any direction but Thine be capable of witnessing the wondrous handiwork of Thy creative Oneness or be honored by beholding the glory of Thy eternal majesty? How can an ear that hath perceived the finite words of Thy servants possibly hear the comprehensive verses of Thy divine unity or the sweet melodies of the Dove of Thy reality?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory befitteth Him Who hath no glory - how then can I make mention of Thee through it, since Thou art the Creator of glory for all creation? Majesty is an attribute of him who hath no majesty, for Thou art the Fashioner of majesty for those Thou didst create in the beginning and the end. Beauty is a quality of him who hath no beauty - glory be unto Thee, for Thou art the Shaper of beauty for all who dwell in the holy kingdom of deeds. Greatness is a characteristic of him who hath no greatness - how then can it define Thee, since Thou art He Who hath clothed Thy loved ones in the garments of Thy greatness?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Know thou that the Manifestation hath not emerged from the four elements, but rather is the Mystery of Oneness, the Pre-existent Essence, the Self-Subsisting Reality, and the Hidden Identity. Indeed, He cannot be known through aught else... Were He to be known through any other than Himself, His essence could not be proven free from similitude, nor His being sanctified from likeness, nor His uniqueness from the manifestations of creation. This is an ocean which none can enter... Were He to make Himself known to His servants as He truly is, all would be severed from everything and would abide in His presence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: All praise and glory befitteth the sacred and glorious court of the sovereign Lord, Who from everlasting hath dwelt, and unto everlasting will continue to dwell within the mystery of His Own Inmost Reality, Who from time immemorial hath abided and will forever continue to abide within His transcendent eternity, exalted above the reach and ken of all created beings. The sign of His matchless Revelation as created by Him and imprinted upon the realities of all beings, is none other but their powerlessness to know Him. He Himself hath at all times been immeasurably exalted above any association with His creatures.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In truth, it hath never been, nor shall it ever be, fitting to offer praise and mention unto the Truth--glorified be His majesty and abundant be His favors--for the way to that privacy is barred, and the path to that mystery and mystery of mysteries is forbidden. How far removed is this visible assembly from that hidden sanctuary! Where is the path, and where is the way? To make mention with the Pen of that Ancient Being is like an ant making mention of the Desired One, and for the tongue to offer praise unto the Beloved of all possibility is as a mere atom directing one to the Sun, or a drop pointing to the Ocean.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: No praise of created things can reach Him, and no gratitude of contingent beings can find access to His holy court. The Incomparable One cannot be known through what is comparable, and understanding falls short of His description. The people of knowledge and insight confess their impotence. If we say He is manifest, He is a Manifestation that no hidden thing can approach. If we say He is the Meaning, He is a Meaning that cannot be confined by the limitations of words. Sanctified is He beyond word and meaning, exalted is He above manifestation and concealment. Vision cannot attain Him, knowledge cannot encompass Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be unto Thee! How can I say "Thou art Thou," and how can I apologize for saying "Thou art Thou"? For in both stations I am tormented by Thy fire and am in severe affliction by Thy decree. Alas, alas for him who is pure nothingness before Thee yet saith in Thy presence "I am"! By Thy glory, he deserveth punishment for this, and were Thou to make me a judge over myself, I would surely torment it with all that Thou art able to decree as recompense for its mention when it grew proud beyond its bounds and recognized not its own nonexistence. What right hath absolute nothingness to turn toward Thy pure Living Self?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I bear witness, even as God beareth witness unto Himself, that He is the Truth, there is no God but Him, and the angels and those possessed of knowledge stand firm round about the Remembrance in equity - there is no God but Him, and He is God, the All-Knowing of all things. God is He besides Whom there is no God, and He is God, the All-Seeing of the believers. God is He besides Whom there is no God, and He is God, the Witness over the believers. God is He besides Whom there is no God, and He is God, the All-Knowing of the believers. God is He besides Whom there is no God, and He is God, Who encompasseth all the worlds.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The materialists have availed themselves of this dissension amongst the religions and are constantly attacking them, intending to uproot the tree of divine planting. Is it impossible for us to receive the infinite bounties of God? Is it impossible to attain the virtues of the spiritual world because we are not living in the time of Moses, the period of the prophets or the era of Christ? Those were spiritual cycles. Can we not develop spiritually because we are far from them and are living in a materialistic age? The God of Moses and Jesus is able to bestow the same favors, nay, greater favors upon His people in this day.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: By Him Who holdeth all command and creation in His grasp, were the veil to be lifted by a single word, no being would remain on earth that could behold His beauty or gaze upon His countenance or observe the wondrous signs of His sovereignty. As He hath said in His Book, exalted be He: Were We to emerge from the garment We have donned due to your weakness, all who are in the heavens and earth would sacrifice their souls for My sake, and so forth. Yet due to His abundant grace, generosity, bounty and loving-kindness, when He saw the weakness of humanity, He veiled His beauty and concealed His countenance from the gaze of all else.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: O my God! Thou art the One Who hath manifested Thyself unto those in the realm of divinity through the essences of the effulgences of the cloud of unknowing, and unto those in the heights of might through the appearances of glory, and unto those in the domain of sovereignty through the conditions of splendor, and unto those in the kingdom through the signs of destiny, and unto those on earth through the tokens of accomplishment, and unto those in the beauty of the mortal realm through the reflections of the lights of radiance, and unto those beneath the depths of the names and the vast ocean of attributes through the evidences of creation

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: When the Beauty of the Unseen established Himself at the Point of Sorrow, encompassed by the seas of tribulation from the Temples of a wondrous Cause, He uttered a word in His inmost heart beneath the tongue of His heart, and through this word breathed the spirit of the Cause into the soul of the Cause. Thus did the Cause appear through the Cause, and establish the Cause in its station, while the Cause remained heedless of all these stations in manifest forgetfulness, concealed in the mystery of the Unseen, veiled in the veils of mystery and concealment, and wrapped in the coverings of God, the inscribed, the hidden, the treasured, the exalted.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: By Him Who is single in majesty and grandeur, Who brought forth all things from nothing after His own pattern - certitude itself is abashed to be certain of Him or to prostrate before Him, and evidence is abashed to point to Him [or to any other]. Dost thou think thou canst know Him, or prove His existence through aught else than Him? Know then with the most decisive certainty and the most most conclusive, determined command that He, exalted be His glory, mighty be His might, hallowed be His holiness, magnified be His grandeur, and glorified be His attributes, maketh all things to know Him through His own Self. Who then can know Him through aught else?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: It is a self-evident fact that phenomenal existence can never grasp nor comprehend the ancient and essential Reality. Utter weakness cannot understand absolute strength. Furthermore, that which man can grasp is finite to man, and man to it is as infinite. Is it possible then for the reality of Divinity to be finite and the human creature infinite? On the contrary, the reverse is true; the human is finite while the essence of Divinity is infinite. Whatever comes within the sphere of human comprehension must be limited and finite. As the essence of Divinity transcends the comprehension of man, therefore God brings forth certain Manifestations of the divine Reality

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise of those who praise, thanksgiving of those who give thanks, and glorification of those who glorify - how can these be attributed to Him Who is sanctified and exalted above creation, knowledge and comprehension? The inability of all things to reach Him testifies to His sanctity, and the confession and acknowledgment of both the visible and hidden tongues of all created things and beings bears eloquent witness to His transcendence. Who can describe Him as He deserves to be described? Who can mention Him as He deserves to be mentioned? The remembrances of those who remember are bounded by limitations, and the comprehension of those who comprehend falls short and is veiled.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All shall be brought before Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All are God's hosts and all shall appear at His command. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All are servants of God and all are submissive unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All are servants of God and all are faithful unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. Say: All are servants of God and all shall return unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him. His are the creation and the command. Say: All shall return unto Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise befitteth the most inaccessible, most holy court of the Lord, the Desired One, Who through His Most Exalted Word on the Day of the Covenant hath exposed the dissension concealed in the hearts of the people of discord, and through that same blessed Word hath manifested the harmony of the people of concord. He is the One Who hath power to transform His bounty into retribution for the polytheists and His light into fire. With a single word He hath brought all to account and weighed them in the balance. Neither doth the acceptance of them that turn unto Him add unto His glory, nor doth the rejection of them that turn aside diminish it. He hath ever been independent of mention and utterance, and will continue to be so forever.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I bear witness before God and before whomsoever is in His knowledge that were He to reduce me to atoms to the extent of His knowledge, and each atom to further atoms to the extent of His knowledge, unto Him Who is the All-Encompassing, the All-Powerful, the Originator, the Inventor, then make each of those atoms expand to fill all creation and the spheres of invention [from] the Throne to beneath the earth, then punish me with all His vengeance, His dominion, His might and His power, as recompense for what crossed my mind of Thy praise and what my heart desired of meeting Thee, it would still be as nothingness before the Midian of Thy glory and would be little compared to what is deserved by the intensity of the might of Thy power.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I know not, O my God, by what tongue I should call upon Thee nor by what utterance I should invoke Thee. I know not, O Thou Who art my heart's desire, how Thou wishest me to describe Thee. Shall I describe Thee by Thyself or mention Thee through another? If Thou desirest to hear Thy description from Thyself - and this is worthy of One like Thee - yet none can do this save those whom Thou hast made repositories of Thy knowledge and treasuries of Thy light. And if Thou desirest to witness Thy description from another - this is impossible for One like Thee, for mention of that which cometh not from Thee befitteth Thee not, nor is worthy of Thee, nor can ascend to the heavens of Thine eternity, nor rise to the sanctuaries of Thine oneness.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! Thou art He Who is known through Thy manifestations and described through Thy signs. No one hath known Thee as befitteth Thy recognition, nor can anyone know Thee as befitteth Thy recognition. No one hath praised Thee as befitteth Thy favors, nor can anyone praise Thee as befitteth Thy favors. No one hath unified Thee as befitteth Thy oneness, nor can anyone unify Thee as befitteth Thy oneness. No one hath glorified Thee as befitteth Thy sublimity, nor can anyone glorify Thee as befitteth Thy sublimity. No one hath magnified Thee as befitteth Thy grandeur, nor can anyone magnify Thee as befitteth Thy grandeur. No one hath found Thee as befitteth Thy singleness, nor can anyone find Thee as befitteth Thy singleness.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I and all things bear witness that Thou art God, that there is no God but Thee, the Single, the One, the Self-Subsisting, the Unique, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, the Independent, Who begetteth not and was not begotten, and unto Whom there is none comparable, nor equal, nor similar, nor partner, nor likeness. Thou hast distinguished Thyself through the loftiness of Thine Essence above all things, and hast exalted Thyself in the sublimity of Thy Being over all things, and hast glorified Thyself in the pure simplicity of Thy Reality above all things, and hast sanctified Thyself in the abstraction of Thy Nature over all things, and hast elevated Thyself through the sovereignty of Thy Self-Subsistence above all things.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I bear witness that there is no God but God, alone with no partner, even as His Essence has testified to His Essence that He is the Single One Who has ever been, with no thing existing beside Him, and He will ever be even as He was, with no thing sharing His station. He is sanctified above all likeness and exalted above all comparison. There is no description save His Essence and no name save His Being. All that those who describe attribute to His Self, and all that those who remember mention of His names, returns unto themselves. He is too glorious to be known through His creation or to be described by His servants. Rather, He created names and attributes that all existing things might worship Him through them while declaring His transcendence above them

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: He hath ever been the One God, Single, Eternal, Self-Subsisting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, the Sovereign, the Supreme, the Most Holy, the Everlasting, the Never-Ending, the Self-Dependent, the Most Exalted, the Inaccessible, the Most High, the All-Compelling. He hath taken neither consort nor offspring. All glorify Him in the eternity of the past, and all sanctify Him in the resplendent night. Verily God, exalted be His glory, hath ever been sanctified above all things, associated with no thing, known through no thing, and comprehended by no thing. He is far more exalted, sublime, glorious and mighty than to be comprehended by the highest faculties of abstract realities in their subtlety, or to be described by the loftiest expressions of pure essences in their precision.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! The essences are powerless to describe Thee and the realities fall short of characterizing Thee. Glorified and exalted art Thou! Every possessor of splendor boweth down before Thy splendor, every possessor of majesty is humbled before Thy majesty, every possessor of beauty is attracted by Thy beauty, every possessor of greatness is abased before Thy greatness, every possessor of light is illumined by the lights of Thy countenance, every possessor of mercy draweth nigh unto Thee through Thy mercy, every possessor of words is rendered mute before the manifestation of Thy Word, every possessor of grandeur is cut off from all else save Thee through Thine exaltation, every possessor of might taketh shelter beneath the shadow of the Tree of Thy Oneness, every possessor of perfection is as utter nothingness before the perfection of Thy unity.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The Truth, exalted be His mention, hath ever been and shall forever remain sanctified above manifestation and appearance - an unknowable Mystery, an unfathomable Concealment, an unrevealed Inner Reality, an unhidden Treasure, and an unwitnessed Secret. For the term mystery holdeth true only when it remaineth unwitnessed; in such case it is not manifest and thus cannot be known. And after it becometh witnessed, the designation mystery no longer existeth whereby it might be known. Therefore, the Mystery hath been and shall ever remain unknowable. That Most Ancient Beauty is too exalted to be known except through Himself, and too sublime to be described save through His own holy Being. For whatsoever the created ones comprehend at the utmost degree of their understanding is but a fancy they have themselves conceived for themselves. Exalted is He above being known by that which is contingent!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I testify before Thee and before all things that Thou art God, and that there is no God but Thee, alone with no partner. Thine is the kingdom and the dominion, Thine the might and the power, Thine the strength and the divinity, Thine the sovereignty and the realm of creation, Thine the glory and the invincibility, Thine the dominance and the transcendence, Thine the joy and the gladness, Thine the bestowal and detachment, Thine the grandeur and the majesty, Thine the attributes and the names, Thine the glory and the sublimity, Thine the countenance and the beauty, Thine the presence and the perfection, Thine the power and the deeds, Thine the might and the independence, Thine the awe and the justice, Thine the mercy and the grace, Thine the likeness and similitudes, Thine the design and the acts, Thine the sovereignty and the exaltation, and Thine is whatsoever Thou lovest from the treasuries of Thy Cause.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Praise be unto Him Who created the heavens and earth and whatsoever lieth between them through His light, and Who hath risen above every exalted one through His manifestation. All who dwell in the kingdom of His invisibility and visibility bear witness that there is none other God but Him, the Lord of might and majesty, the Possessor of beauty and perfection, of grace and bounty, of power and justice, of mercy and generosity, of glory and grandeur, of sovereignty and dominion, of strength and action, of awesomeness and unfailing purpose. His are the most beautiful names, the most exalted attributes, the most glorious splendor, the most evident favors, the greatest trials, the mightiest signs, the ultimate revelations, and the most elevated manifestations. All faces bow before the sovereignty of His might, and all ages submit to the power of His Will. He hath ever been ancient in the eternity of eternities, and everlasting without measure or decline.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Again, unto Him be grace and permanence and might and sublimity, that the lights of guidance have returned to their abode and the sun of unity and uniqueness hath risen from its horizon, and the temple of sanctity hath donned its robe, and the essence of testimony hath testified to its Witnessed One, its Beloved and its Intended, with its secret and its manifest being, its essence and its heart, that He is the One manifest in His manifestation and hidden in His essence, and exalted in His name, and sanctified in His being from the mention of aught else but Him, and the One witnessed in His beauty and speaking in the heaven of His might and majesty, seated upon the throne of His grandeur and established upon the seat of His command, standing through the sovereignty of His might and His greatness, and self-subsisting through the dominion of His power - He is the One to Whom all existence, both seen and unseen, beareth witness that there is none other God but He, the Almighty, the All-Powerful, the All-Choosing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I beseech Thee to witness, and all things witness in this night which Thou hast made great, majestic, excellent, mighty, and honored above all else through Thy bounty, Thy grace, Thy generosity, Thy bestowal, Thy munificence, and Thy mercy. How exalted, O my God, is Thy sublimity, and O my God, O my Beloved, Thy transcendence! Thou hast ever been established over all things, powerful over all things, knowing all things, ruling over all things, witnessing above all things, subduing all contingent beings, [...] over all existing things, mighty over all created things, inaccessible to all in the kingdom of earth and heavens, exalted above all in the kingdom of names and attributes, transcendent above all atoms, sovereign above all similitudes and allusions, supreme above all geometry and indications, manifest above all metaphors and appearances, mighty above all essences, supreme above all identities, compelling above all egos, powerful above all beings, and stern above all that can be mentioned of similitudes and conditions.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all His worshippers. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all prostrate before Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all devoutly obedient unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all submissive unto Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all humble before Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all His praise-givers. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all bowing down before Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all His servants. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all supplicants before Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we all speak through Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we are all beholders of Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we all exalt Him. God beareth witness that there is none other God but Him, and we shall all return unto Him.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: God, singly and alone, abideth in His Own Place, which is holy above space and time, mention and utterance, sign, description and definition, height and depth.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: There is no remembrance for God in the kingdom of His names and attributes except that it is a remembrance from the manifestations of the signs of the kingdom of thy will which hath pointed to God and become established in His shadow

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: If We were to say they clung to names and remained veiled from the recognition of the Essence, all people share this station, for all besides Him have been and shall ever be veiled from recognizing His exalted Essence. Therefore, all recognition from the peoples of the worlds returneth to the ocean of Names, and it is most evident that every nation of the earth calleth upon Him by a name, and none can transgress this station.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be to God, its Creator, Lord of the Throne and the Seat, far above what they describe.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: above all that by which the names and attributes have magnified Thee through their abstractions

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Do not diminish God's greatness, and understand nothing from our verses except the decree of servitude.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Yet how can the scratching of Thy servants' pens or the praise of any of Thy creatures befit Thy presence?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The comparison made in thy Lord's Book is only to make you understand that your grace compared to His grace is as your selves compared to His Self, that ye may be God-fearing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be to Thee! Far be it to imagine knowledge of Thy Essence or description of Thy eternal handiwork. Thou art He Who cannot be limited or touched, Who cannot be described or perceived.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: God is greater than all wherewith ye describe Him. Say: God is more impregnable than that which ye withhold. Say: God cannot be mentioned by anything, for all besides God is His creation

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I yearn for naught but Thine Own Self and seek no one other than Thee. I am conscious that all created things are debarred from Thy sublime Essence and the entire creation is denied access to Thine inmost Being.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The wings of these powerless birds are too weak to soar in the atmosphere of the splendor of Thy oneness, and the understanding of these feeble souls falls short of reaching the heaven of the sublimity of Thy Lordship.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How, O my God, can I make mention of Thee with the pen after Thou hast sanctified Thy Self above the allusions of eternity? And how can I describe Thee through that which appears from nothingness upon this honored Tablet?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: This weak servant and frail countenance knows not by what meaningless and obsolete words to express his thoughts, for whatever is presented before that Presence is mere falsehood, and whatever is mentioned is pure polytheism.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Indeed, Thine Essence is the camphorated Essence which, by its very being, separates material things from the mention of Names and Attributes, and prevents realities from attaining to the station of explanation and the Divine Essence.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I am powerless to mention even a single leaf among the leaves of Thy most exalted Paradise which Thou didst created through Thy Most Glorious Name - how then could I be capable of making mention of Thee or speaking in praise of Thy Self?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Who is able, O my God, to mention Thee, for if he mentions aught else but Thee it is utter nothingness before the court of Thy holiness? And how can Thy creation unite with Thee when their very existence is cut off from knowing Thy Essence?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou, O my God! I have known Thee through Thee, not through aught else, for that is but Thy creation; and I have unified Thee through Thee, not through any other, for that is but what Thou hast brought into being from nothing.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How can I praise Thee when praise itself is but a token of Thy creation, born of Thy Will? How can I glorify Thee when glorification is but a reflection of Thy sovereignty? How can I sanctify Thee when sanctification is but a sign of Thine everlasting dominion?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How can I remember Thee when the very act of remembrance implies permanence, and the reality of praise indicates some vestige of existence? This is hidden polytheism, manifest veiling, and heedlessness beyond which there is no greater sign of utter powerlessness

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: What mention have I to make mention of Thee? What worth have I to praise Thee? He whom Thou hast created from sheer nothingness and established from naught by Himself for Himself - how can he be capable of Thy praise or able to tread the paths of Thy good-pleasure?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Therefore I have no recourse but to confess my powerlessness and inadequacy, and no refuge but in the depths of poverty and languidness. For inability to comprehend is true comprehension, and powerlessness is true attainment, and confession of poverty is true acquisition.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: By Thy might, every essence that hath sought access to Thy holy court, and every abstract description is falsehood before Thy station of nearness, for Thy very essence, as it is, pointeth to God Thy Lord, and it cutteth off all created things from the station of Thy remembrance.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified art Thou above all whereby I have known Thee, and I seek Thy forgiveness for all whereby I have glorified Thee, and I turn unto Thee in repentance for all whereby I have magnified Thee. For all of me and whatsoever is attributed to me is not befitting to be attributed unto Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: For the attributes of might and majesty, and the qualities of power and beauty, are but signs of Thy Will and revelations of Thy Power, and these, by the testimony of their existence, proclaim the barring of the way, and by the evidence of their own reality, declare the closing of the path.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: In the world of phenomena there is no conception of God, because every inferior degree is entirely out of touch with the degree superior thereto. The reality of divinity has never been comprehended by the human mind. Everlastingly has it been in its holy state, sanctified above comprehension.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Thus have all these mysteries become known, and the fire of "except" hath consumed and destroyed all the veils of limitation denoted by "no," and the banner proclaiming that "God hath power over all things" hath been raised upon the mountain of "He doeth what He willeth and ordaineth what He pleaseth."

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: And there is nothing that ye comprehend, or understand, or encompass, or know, but that He is God Who created what God was, none knoweth it save Him, and none can encompass His knowledge save He Himself, and no hearing can hear what God heareth of Himself, for there is no God but He, the Mighty, the Wise.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Should anything be attributed to Thyself, it would but signify the existence of that thing within its own limitations, even as the Kaaba which Thou hast attributed to Thyself is but clay before Thee. How can relationships ascend to the horizon of Thy sanctity when they are but creations brought into being through Thy Will?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The pure essences of the kingdom testify to their poverty, and the realities of creation bear witness to their need and distress. By Thy glory, I have no knowledge, no portion, no limit in knowing Thy Self, and nothing hath any share in loving Thy Being, for the existence of all things hath ever been as nothing in Thy knowledge.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: It is incumbent upon the servant to exalt his Creator and sanctify his Lord above every attribute, whether known or unknown to His creation, for these are utter non-existence and pure falsehood before Him. The same applies to power and similar praised attributes and most beautiful names. Such is the judgment of the people of the Bayan.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I shall not describe Thee by names and attributes, for they have been realized through the reality of the traces of Thy deeds. Nor shall I characterize Thee by the manifestations of Thy most excellent names, nor by what Thou hast created in the kingdom of earth and heaven, for they have been endowed with being through the traces of Thy creation.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Say: All that ye describe is God, your Lord, the All-Merciful, then through His remembrance do ye make mention. This is how God hath described Himself, for were God not to describe Himself and reveal it in the Book, ye would not be able to describe Him. All that ye ascend unto in describing God is the description of that which ye cannot comprehend.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Were I to praise Thee for the power of creation and the essence of invention, I would not have praised Thee sufficiently for even a single letter of Thy signs. Were I to thank Thee for the essence of origination and the reality of bringing into being, I would not have thanked Thee adequately for even the grammatical inflection of one of Thy letters.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: The minds are bewildered in comprehending Him, and thoughts are perplexed in perceiving His waves. He surgeth by Himself and for Himself, and casteth forth the pearls of knowledge, wisdom and utterance by Himself and for Himself. Exalted is He above being comprehended through descriptions, and sanctified is He beyond being characterized by mentions.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I cannot ascribe to Thee any attribute except Thine Own Self, nor do I see for my praise or my being any station before Thee, for all else besides Thee is non-existent before Thee and in need of Thy sustenance. How then can I mention Thee through that which is in need? Nay, by Thy glory, creation hath no path unto Thee, nor have their deeds any wondrous station before Thee.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Every description by which they who adore Thy unity describe Thee, and every praise wherewith they who are devoted unto Thee praise Thee, are but the traces of the pen which the fingers of Thy strength and power have set in motion. Howsoever I describe Thee, whichever of Thy virtues I recount, I cannot but blush and feel ashamed of what my tongue hath uttered or my pen written.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Description befitteth him who is not known through his essence by his essence, and attribute is meet for him who is not recognized by himself through himself. Glorified be God, the Lord of creation, from the vision of the heart and the description of His servants. No attribute can be known save through His Essence, nor can any name indicate aught save from the station of His Identity.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I am well aware that were I to bow myself before a handful of dust, from now until the end that hath no end, in acknowledgement of its relationship to Thy name, the Fashioner, I would still find myself far removed from that dust, and incapable of approaching it, and would discover that such an adoration can in no wise befit it, nor transcend the limitations to which I myself have been subjected.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: If He is mentioned by the letters "He" and "Hu," this is among the wondrous favors He hath bestowed upon His creation, having permitted them this as a token of His generosity and grace. Otherwise, how can mere verbal expressions compare with that station which transcendeth all meaning and utterance? Exalted is the All-Merciful above the mention of every mentioner, the description of every describer, and the praise of every praiser.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glorified, glorified art Thou from being indicated by mention, or described by praise, or by any sign, for all of these are naught but descriptions of Thy creation, raised up by Thy command and invention. Whatsoever those who remember mention, or the mystics ascend unto the atmosphere of Thy knowledge, they return to that Point which hath submitted to Thy sovereignty, prostrated before Thy beauty, and been brought low by a movement of Thy Pen.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: None among contingent beings hath known Thee, and none among created things hath found Thee. Whosoever seeth Thy attributes as the attributes of Thy creation - hath he any portion of knowledge? Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! And whosoever witnesseth Thy deeds as the deeds of Thy servants - hath he any share in recognition? Glorified art Thou, glorified art Thou! How few are they who truly know Thee, and how fewer still are they who truly unify Thee!

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: How then canst Thou be described thus, when Thou hast ever been and will ever be indescribable save by Thyself? How canst Thou be characterized thus, when Thou hast ever been and will ever be uncharacterizable save by Thyself? How canst Thou be known thus, when Thou hast ever been and will ever be unknowable save through Thyself? How canst Thou be mentioned thus, when Thou hast ever been and will ever be unmentionable through Thy creation? How canst Thou be worshipped thus, when Thou hast ever been and will ever be unworshippable through Thy servants?

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: Glory be to Him! He hath ever existed without the existence of anything with Him, without the description of anything at His level, without the name of anything before the city of His might, and He will ever remain as He hath been throughout all eternity, without any state of change or transition. Glory be to Him! Whosoever desireth to describe Him by a name hath made that name a proof of His Essence and a way to His knowledge. Glory be to Him and exalted is He! His Person is sanctified from being known through any other than Himself or being described by any other than Himself.

Subject: transcendence; unknowability of God
Quotation: I will praise Thee, O my God, and I will sanctify Thee from such praise and attributes as have been distinguished by the imaginations of the most discerning mystics. And I will glorify Thee, O my Beloved, above every description and attribute conceived by the minds of men, even should they traverse the realm of utterance with clear proof and authority. For perception is contingent upon existence, and existence dwelleth in the realm of limitation and descent when confronted with the lights of Thy oneness. Praise and attributes are but confused dreams gathered by the hands of minds and imaginations from the gardens of mystical knowledge. How then can such confused dreams enter and flourish within the sanctuary of Thy names and attributes, or encompass Thy mysteries and signs?

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: One must escape the prison of body and soar into the air!

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: Do not let the vicissitudes of this world sadden you, then ascend to the heaven of faithfulness

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: when thou art freed from physical limitations, divested of human conditions, and become a celestial angel

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: Happy are ye that have turned to God and have raised your sight from this material world to the realm above.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: Indeed, the world and the hereafter are two states. If you turn towards God, exalted be He, then you are in paradise and if you regard your self then you are in the fire and in the world.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: Until man becomes free, he cannot fulfill his service at the Divine Threshold. Until he finds deliverance from the abasement of attachment to this world, eternal glory will not be unveiled.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: Observe the world and its affairs, its changes, decline and extinction, and hold fast unto that whereby thy mention shall be exalted throughout the immortality of names and thy deeds shall endure throughout ages which none save God, the Lord of all worlds, hath knowledge of.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: And if it were higher than luminous bodies like the light of a candle or lamp, they do not perceive the things they reveal and see and know. But with all its elevation, the light of mind is limited by conditions and time because it cannot reveal and see and understand things except after their creation and formation.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: The eagle soaring to the heights of glory would never build its nest and dwelling in the branches of this transient, lowly dust-heap. The divine leviathan would never take up residence in a mere stream of contingent being, and the lion of the Lord's springtime would never make its abode in the jungle of vain imaginings and desires.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: If they be birds of the meadow of divine knowledge, they must needs spread their wings and take flight unto the branches of the gardens of oneness, and if they be fish of the ocean of love, they must needs move and swim forth. The wingless bird is but a worm of the earth, and the waterless fish is but dark dust in the lowest depths.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: This is the station of simple radiance which shines forth and makes them separate from all worldly things, and this leads them to such a condition that while they are walking on the earth, they are moving in the supreme Horizon. They have cut themselves off entirely from worldly conditions, and while they are on the earth they never see it, but look to the Horizon.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: Reflect carefully & then you will realize to what extent man is physically a prisoner to the laws of nature - The slightest draught - a little cold will make him ill or some heat will incommode him - A small mosquito -bite may become deadly for him. This is in relation to his physical reality, but his intellectual or his ideal reality is victorious over all phenomena and with that power he conquers the world of nature.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: How shall it ever become happy and joyous, unless it first forgets all save God and turns its gaze from this nether world to that which is in the realms above, beholds the reality of the concourse on high, and earnestly beseeches the assistance of the divine kingdom of Abha? Unless man forgets all save God, withdraws his gaze from this base world and beholds that which exists in the world above, unless he turns his attention to the Concourse on High and derives illumination from the Abha Kingdom.

Subject: transcending the material condition
Quotation: In the view of the earthworms, the sign of intelligence is to delve into the lower strata of the earth. If any creature turns toward the higher strata, the lowly earthworms call it mad, saying it knows not its own good and recognizes not its own benefit. Although in the lower strata there are thousands of loads of earthly filth, it deprives itself of these and hastens to the higher strata where there is neither mire nor clay, neither putrefaction nor moisture - only air and sky and meadow and purity.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Solomon's kingdom is confined to this heap of dust

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Do not rejoice in the world and whatsoever is therein.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: "Is it from the world after you have seen it passing, passing away?"

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This is better for thee than all the glory and dominion of the world.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: so that they may be released from the influence of the ephemeral world

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The times are not to be relied upon - soon we shall all return to dust.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: For all that ye see and hear will ultimately prove to be like a desert mirage.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: They have become weary of the earthly world...They have been freed from this world

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Make me, O God, to turn away from the life of this world, for it is but a brief enjoyment.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Fear God, O people, for the life of this world is vain, and unto God shall they be the losers

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The water of earthly life, compared to the life to come, is but as a dream wherein ye slumber.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This evanescent world is not permanent. It is a mirage, not the water; a shadow, not the sun.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: continuously remind her of God's favors, the greatness of God's Kingdom, the evanescence of the world

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Ere long the world and whatsoever is therein shall perish and become non-existent, as ye can observe.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world and all that ye behold therein shall pass away, and ye shall pass away like a vanishing shadow

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Otherwise what stability or permanence has worldly wealth? The sighs of the free-spirited have a mighty effect.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Ere long the world and its people shall perish, and the people of God shall abide in the pavilions of eternity.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Thou must render thanks that thou hast found thy way to the divine court and hast witnessed this world as a prison.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The carpet of this ephemeral world shall soon be rolled up; therefore one must think of everlasting glory and grandeur

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Verily the days pass by, lives draw to a close, leaves fall, and fruits change. Take ye heed, O people of understanding!

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Such is the way of the world... This is the joy of heart and soul, and this is freedom from the world of water and clay.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This mortal world is not worthy of human attachment. In a short time human life ends and becomes buried beneath the earth.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This is what endures in the Kingdom of your Lord; all else shall perish...This intensity and that ease shall both soon pass away

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: He whose sight is illumined with the light of understanding will assuredly detach himself from the world and the vanities thereof.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: That which ye behold today shall perish, but that which hath been sent down from the Pen of your Lord, the All-Informed, shall endure.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The nobles of the world took the path of nothingness... Whatever pertains to creation is ephemeral and transient, detested and condemned.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: How many queens and princesses became forgotten, how many daughters and sons of kings and nobles of the world became nameless and traceless

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: These tents may be likened to the trappings of this world, which no sooner are they spread out than the time cometh for them to be rolled up.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Life in this mortal world will quickly come to an end, and this earthly glory, wealth, comfort and happiness will soon vanish and be no more.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Both states are not permanent both are transitory. All that is and is not passes away and only that which is permanent and lasting is important

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: They seek only the Abha Kingdom and they see this mortal world as a dark prison. this earthly home seems to them as a dreadful, dark, narrow place.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The conditions of the world and its manifestations shall soon return to nothingness, and that which endureth forever is and shall be the Word of God.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The people of this mortal world, both high and low, spend their days and nights in pursuit of carnal desires and ultimately meet with manifest loss.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All of it was scattered dust. All these edifices, these buildings, these properties - all of them vanished. All of it was ruined, no trace remained.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: "Soon shall pass away all that thou dost witness and behold, and God shall spread another carpet." "All matters and all things return to extinction."

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All that thou seest around thee is the scattering of dust or an empty. It is an empty shadow, a mere phantom, no more than vain and futile imaginings.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The ladies of the world may shine like the moon at first, but in the end they become like lifeless corpses, detestable and repugnant to heart and soul.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: You must never be distressed by worldly affairs, for the world hath no worth or station in the sight of God, and both its hardship and ease are fleeting.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All that thou seest existing will become non-existent and vanish away, and all that thou seest concealed and hearest of will become manifest and evident.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: No soul has found or will find the light of happiness in this narrow and dark world. Joy and gladness belong to the eternal world and the infinite realm.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Whatever thou beholdest in the realm of existence is transient, and whosoever thou findest dwelling beneath the extended shadow is steadfast and enduring.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Be not saddened by the world, for in truth it is a lethal poison and a deadly bane. Its good and evil are as changeful and inconstant as the winds of heaven

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: In this world of nonexistence, in which existence is only an appearance... How long wilt thou remain a captive of water and clay, abased in this shadow world?

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: "Through your intercession, I will be deprived of the bounty of martyrdom, will fall behind my companions, and remain in the clutches of this ephemeral world."

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Soon shall all that is witnessed shall pass away, while that which hath been revealed from the Supreme Pen specially for His loved ones shall remain and endure.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: They must not occupy themselves with these fleeting days more than is necessary. Let them sometimes spend their days preparing for the countless worlds to come.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All the pleasures of this world, compared to the hereafter, are but as something ye behold in a dream. Should the world present itself unto you, this is its limit.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Material men of this world are like poison to the spiritual... But others are like swine, which eat everything they find, and at last they are good only to be eaten

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: so long as a gem of the Most Great Guidance lingereth within the bosom of this world, its brilliance will remain obscured and concealed...this fragile and gloomy frame

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Exalted is God above those who lay all their hopes in this world and dread the abode hereafter and its felicity. This world bringeth me sorrow and its people reject me.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Be not grieved when the world presseth hard upon thee and space groweth strait, for it shall pass away while thou shalt endure throughout the centuries, cycles and ages.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: What troubles they endure for the sake of name and fame! All are transitory and perishable and no trace of them will remain. It will be as though they had never existed.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: In this ephemeral world the end of every wealth is poverty, the end of every gathering is dispersal, and the end of every health and glory is ailment, degradation and poverty

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Say, this earthly life shall come to an end, and everyone shall expire and return unto my Lord God... This mortal life is sure to perish; its pleasures are bound to fade away

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: transience/worthlessness of the physical world - "The world and all that is therein shall perish, and there shall endure for thee what appeareth from thee in service to thy Lord"

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The earthly Presidency returns to dust. The worldly sovereignty is effaced by a handful of dust, but a Divine and Heavenly Sovereignty is everlasting, effective, through the ages.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world is transient and what is with God endures. We beseech the Truth to confirm His friends in such wise that the ephemeral shall not deprive them of the fragrance of the eternal.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Raise thy endeavor and be not content with the ease and comfort of this world. Find eternal glory and felicity in another realm, and through divine favor enter the everlasting Kingdom.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Let not the pomp and riches and majesty and glory of two days prevent you from everlasting glory and abiding bounty and heavenly sustenance. Yesterday is gone and today too shall pass.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: If human aspiration is confined to these numbered days, such a one was not and is not worthy of mention. Beseech the Truth to confirm His loved ones in that which is lasting and eternal.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All that thou seest shall soon vanish like unto a mirage, save service to the Kingdom of God and the proclamation of the appearance of the Lord of Hosts - this alone shall remain and endure

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: "The world is transient. Although some repine at its lack of permanence and faithfulness, these qualities are in reality beloved, for they have been necessitated by God's inscrutable wisdom"
