Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Erelong, the world shall pass away, and all shall return to nothingness. What endureth is that which the Most Exalted Pen hath ordained at the bidding of God, the Self-Subsisting, the Eternal.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The means and effects of the world, its ornaments and events, prevent man from that which beseemeth him and become a barrier between him and the effulgences of the lights of the supreme horizon

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: By God the Truth, this is better for you than a mighty kingdom, a powerful sovereignty, and incomparable wealth, for it is a kingdom that will not perish for as long as God, the Ancient, endures

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Were all the treasures of the earth to be gathered before thee, not one of them would profit thee when the messenger of thy Chosen Lord cometh unto thee. Know thou that this world shall pass away.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The servants are occupied with their vain desires and rejoice in the possession of fleeting ornaments... Do you see any permanence in what they possess, when all things testify to their transience?

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Exchange not this most exalted station for the world and all that is therein. Soon all that is visible shall return to nothingness, and that which endureth are the deeds performed in the divine days.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: he should not seek anything for himself in this ephemeral world, becoming detached - that is, sacrificing himself with all his conditions at the altar of sacrifice upon the manifestation of his Lord

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Endeavor thou as much as thou canst so that thou mayest leave a sign behind thee in this ephemeral world, for this life on this mound of earth is like unto a vanishing shadow or the mirage of the desert.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The kingdom of this world and all that is therein is, in the eyes of them that gaze upon the All-Merciful, less than the eye of a dead ant - nay, less than that. Glory be to God above what they associate!

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: And unto this age which He hath filled with the grace of His mercy - all that was before hath passed away and all that thou witnesseth now shall likewise pass away, and sovereignty shall remain unto His Face.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: "Days pass by - if they pass in pleasure and joy they yield no result. Consider that no joy and pleasure could be greater than the majesty of Na?iri'd-Din Shah. You observed what that joy and pleasure led to."

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All that thou seest in the world of existence is but a mirage not a water, it's a mere mist not a thirst allaying drink, it is veering towards destruction and non existence, it's a mere show, a mere supposition.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Consider how unfaithful this world is! How then can man set his heart upon it and become attached to it, unless his consciousness becomes unconscious - otherwise he will become detached and withdraw to the shore.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: And know thou, verily, that the earthly world is as a prison to the holy souls and these long for the Kingdom of Sanctity, as birds long for their nests in the gardens of beautiful and wonderful trees, flowers and fruits.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Though the Pope had all worldly power and comfort, "even now, though he has been dead but a short time, the world is already busy with the new 'Pope' and he is nearly forgotten, and after a little no one will mention him at all."

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: You observe that the sovereignty of this world was fruitless, let alone other matters, as the poet says: "The glory of Asaf, the horse of wind, the speech of birds - All passed away like wind, and from that master nothing remained"

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The people have become heedless of their abiding-place, in that they have followed every wicked and ignoble one, casting the blessing of God behind their backs and turning unto that which is putrid. They are assuredly among the losers.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: "behold how a hundred thousand mighty kings in Iran and Turan and other realms of the world ruled from their thrones, yet now there remains no trace, mention or sign of any of them. All became utter nothingness and absolute abasement."

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: In the first station, none is seen save he who hath clung to the Most Great Cord, and all else returneth to nothingness. That which thou seest shall pass away, but there shall endure the deeds of those who have arisen to serve the Cause

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: That great overmastering joy which overwhelmed all the outward difficulties and overrode all the visible obstacles of the journey is now lacking. Now what are we doing? We are sitting in this lovely garden, eating, drinking and sleeping.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Will what they possess benefit them and will what they have gathered suffice them? Verily, the world laughs at those who desire it and calls out to them in the loudest voice: "Do you expect faithfulness from me, O heedless and remote one?"

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: When thou observest the hosts of women in the world, how like successive waves they set foot in this world and in troops upon troops take the path to the realm of nothingness, neither fruit nor trace remain of them, neither benefit nor tidings

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world's foundation rests upon wind, and the foundation of worldly existence is utterly ruined for its people at the end. There is no comfort and no adornment, rather it is but tests and calamities and afflictions in the world of creation.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Were there any worth in this world, We would not have left it to its people - and this is a reminder for those who possess understanding. Verily, he who hath believed is the richest among all people, even though he possess none of earth's treasures.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Soon will pass away all that you witness on earth...Consider the world and its hours and days - do you find it remaining in one state? Nay, by your Lord, the Most Merciful! Every person of insight witnesses its changes and transience at every moment.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The generations that have gone on before you - whither are they fled? And those round whom in life circled the fairest and the loveliest of the land, where now are they? Others ere long will lay hands on what ye possess, and enter into your habitations.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All worldly joys and pleasures have an allure from afar, but when approached they are a mirage and an appearance without reality. Whatever one attaches their heart to is ephemeral and ultimately leads to despair, except the love of God and love for humanity.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This world is transient and shall pass in a brief time. True rest and comfort belong to the soul, which are attained in the eternal world. The life of the body inevitably ends in death - so long as physical life continues to pass, what importance can it have?

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: O Hoopoe! Say: By God! The life of this world shall pass away more swiftly than a moment. Ere long all that is visible shall return to nothingness, and that which endureth forever is pure deeds. Through pure deeds, the element of dust transcendeth the heavens.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: But alas! The children recognized not its worth, and the ignorant counted it of no account. They darkened that pure and subtle horizon with the dense clouds of doubts, and obscured that luminous face of the brilliant moon with the blemishes of desires and passions.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Look at the plains, look at the hills: they are defeated armies, they are hosts that fell in heaps and were levelled with the ground; they are the dust of high pavilions, and palace and hall are the hole of owls that feed upon the dead, the roost of carrion crows...

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world, my brother! will abide with none, By the world's Maker let thy heart be won. Rely not, nor repose on this world's gain, For many a son like thee she has reared and slain. What matters when the spirit seeks to fly, If on a throne or on a bare earth we die?

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Consider the pharaohs and tyrants of the earth - from palaces they returned to graves. Love of position and wealth hath made men heedless of the Day of Reckoning. These are their houses which God hath left to the spider. Take heed, O ye that are endued with discernment!

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Whatever brings thee joy in this world, Think thou upon its separation at that time. Many were gladdened by that which gladdens thee, But in the end fled from it like the wind. Therefore flee thou from it ere it flees from thee, Set not thy heart upon it ere it parts from thee.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: How long wilt thou remain remote from the heights of acceptance in the corner of obscurity, and seek patience and delay in this dark and narrow dungeon, becoming captive to scent and color? Build not thy nest and dwelling like ignorant birds in the furnace of the mortal world.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Know thou the value of these days, then gird up thy loins therein for the triumph of My Cause. Let not the world and what occurreth therein sadden thee. Soon shall all thou beholdest perish, while glory and power shall endure unto God, the Omnipotent, the Mighty, the Chosen One.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: For others, they are the cause of awakening, so that they no longer attach their hearts to this evanescent world. In like manner, the loving Lord hath created diseases, tribulations, and afflictions in this evanescent realm so that souls will not be so enamored and captivated by it.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world hath no worth, neither had it any. That Branch, in the prime of youth, laid down his life and sought another station. The world must be left to heedless nations. A station whereof all things have testified to its transience is not, and hath never been, worthy of attachment.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: How foolish the bird that builds its nest in a tree that may perish when it could build its nest in a ever-verdant garden of paradise! How many kings have flourished in luxury and in a brief moment all has disappeared! Their glory and their honor are forgotten. Where are the sovereigns now?

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Consider the generations of old and reflect upon what transpired in those days. Where is their might and their princes, where their power and dominion, where their hosts and their armies? God hath caused them to return to their graves... Ere long all that is seen shall perish and vanish away.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Strive that the conditions and colors of this world may not make you heedless of the Lord of earth and heaven. These lives are observed to be most fleeting; through the grace of the Beloved of all possibility, you must attain a station which neither decline can seize nor change can approach.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: the world's address to its devotees: "By God! The world laughs at those who have denied and occupied themselves with it, addressing them saying: 'Soon will I disavow you. Are you content with that which has never been faithful to anyone like you? ... Soon will I join you with the former ones.'"

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Their riches have deceived them to such degree that they have turned away from the Face through Whose light the earth and heavens were illumined. All that is on earth shall perish, while that which hath been ordained for the loved ones of God shall endure in a Kingdom sanctified above all mention.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Were the veil to be lifted and you were to behold what is ordained for you, you would cast the world and all that is therein behind you. By My life! All that is on earth shall perish, and glory shall remain with those who have turned to the Dayspring of the Cause and were of them that have attained.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: For any wealth and prosperity which is of this world will have as its end loss and deprivation. The only difference is that some wealth and prosperity disappears quickly while others last several years before disappearing. For every assembly there is a dispersal and for every harvest there is separation.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: By the Sun of the horizon of power: if the world had any worth, the Ancient Beauty would not have dwelt for numbered years in the Most Great Prison. Man, so long as he is in this world, has been and is in truth in the throes of death, save for those detached hearts that behold all things with divine vision.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Blessed be the one who comprehendeth Thine enduring reality and the evanescence of all things but Thee, and who acknowledgeth Thy sovereign authority and the powerlessness of all save Thyself. And as the evanescence of all things is established before the surging ocean of Thy remembrance, O King of all names

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This evanescent servant offers thanks with both outer and inner tongue to the True Beloved, for his intention has been crowned with acceptance. All that is witnessed in this world will return to nothingness in numbered days, but such goodly deeds as these will endure as long as God's dominion and kingdom endure.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Although rich women may be brought up in utmost ease and comfort and luxury, yet at last that comfort and ease will be buried in the dust, in the narrow grave, in a dark place. The ease of the day will pass away, and the happiness of the evening be spent... Ere long the world and whatsoever is therein will pass away

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All that can be seen in this mortal world is naught but imagination, a mere symbol, and not the heavenly reality. For this is a world of dust, and this human reality is hopelessly enmeshed in its corrupt desires. Whatever thou beholdest and findest in this mortal world is void of reality and is but illusion, not heavenly truth.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This mortal world deserves not a moment's trust, and this earthly life warrants not an instant's confidence. In every breath there is the possibility of passing, and in every hour great danger lies. Therefore wise souls ever bind their hearts to the divine world and are quickened by the fragrances of the gardens of the All-Merciful.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world was not and is not worthy of mention. Blessed is the soul whom the veils and clouds of the world and all therein have not debarred from the Dayspring of the names and attributes of God, exalted be His glory. Soon shall all that is visible vanish, and sovereignty, might and power shall remain with God, the One, the Chosen One.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Whatsoever existeth in the world and is possessed by the people of the world is perishable, except what God willeth. All are assured with manifest certainty of the transience of the world and its vicissitudes. Nevertheless, they have clung to it in such wise that they remain heedless and veiled from God and from that which is with Him.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Consider those who oppressed aforetime - where are their lofty palaces? Those are their houses, fallen into ruin with their trellises. Say: By my Lord, the Most Glorious! That which was created shall perish even as the kings and palaces perished, and today thou seest not their traces...By God! The world and its riches shall not profit you.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All humanity in this world are wandering aimlessly, without foundation or stability. For the foundation of existence in this dusty plane is based on non-existence and lowliness - how can it find stability and permanence? Observe how the palaces and mansions of the ancients became ruins and disappeared like a desert mirage, leaving no trace.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world is seen to be as a shadow that exists one moment and is gone the next. If one would awaken even slightly and reflect upon the changes in the world, everything that exists therein, even while appearing to exist, testifies to its own transience and extinction. Man's life passes like the winds, and this passing is hidden from sight and heart.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: They have likened man's life in this world to a bird that alights upon the wall of a palace and warbles a melody, and taketh flight. Despite this evident insignificance and swift evanescence, the world hath held mankind back from the Truth, and its affairs have so veiled the people that they have clung to hellfire and passed by the Kingdom of Divine mercy.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: O 'Ali! Where is thy previous day and where is that which appeared in the previous year? The world testifieth to its evanescence, yet most of the people are heedless. Cling ye unto that which shall endure for you throughout the endurance of the Kingdom and the Realm, and abandon that which every truthful and trustworthy one acknowledgeth as perishable.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: What thou beholdest today shall perish, as thou observest and art of them that witness. Say: O people! Consider today where are those who were occupied before you with that wherewith ye are occupied? And where are those who prided themselves in this perishable world? And where is their joy and their vainglory and their palaces? They have returned to their graves.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This is especially true since the prolongation of life has no purpose and length of days yields no fruit. The purpose of life in this transient world is to achieve divine results. If such results are attained, even if life consists of but numbered days, it is praiseworthy and acceptable. Otherwise, even if one lives a thousand years, it is blameworthy and rejected.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Where are they now? They are under the earth, their very bones are turned into ashes. All their wild ambitions and schemes brought to nought. O thou thoughtless King! O thou negligent emperor! Who art thou and what art thou that art priding thyself above thy fellowmen! A few more days will pass and thou shalt also go under the ground, thou with all thy hopes and fears.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Behold the world as a passing shadow - soon it shall fade away, while that which is ordained by God for His servants shall endure and last forever. Where are the peoples of ancient times? Nay, pass beyond these - where are the people of but last year who, with the utmost pride and heedlessness, were occupied with their passions and veiled from the Lord of earth and heaven?

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Soon shall all that thou seest today perish, but there shall endure for thee that which We have adorned with His mention in the Tablets. There is no doubt that these days and all that is witnessed shall return to nothingness. Therefore, to the extent possible, one must attain the good-pleasure of the Beloved. That which appears from Him is everlasting and shall not perish.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The vicissitudes of the world, its changes, and the evanescence of all things are each a manifest counselor for them that possess sight and gaze toward the Most Sublime Vision. Where are the Pharaohs of the earth and its mighty ones? Where are the tyrants of the lands and their men? ... God hath brought them down from palaces to graves. Take heed, O ye who possess vision!

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: This physical world's life is temporary, it must end. The life and pleasures of this world are fleeting. Its comfort ends in hardship, its glory ends in abasement, its life ends in death, its existence ends in non-existence. Whatever has no permanence has no attraction in the sight of the wise, for the wise person does not turn to the transient world but turns to the eternal world.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The days of our life flee away, and the star of our life will set in the occident of nothingness. The throne of every king will be changed to a mat. The honour and glory of every honoured one will be transformed to utter humiliation. The heads of the generals and great ones will eventually be trodden under foot. The lofty mansions of the dignitaries will change in time to their graves.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: O Maryam! Though a tree be laden with a myriad leaves and fruits, a gust of autumnal wind sufficeth to obliterate them all. Abandon these fleeting shadows, O Maryam, and turn towards the Day-Star of unfading splendour. Every shadow oweth its existence and motion to the presence of the sun; for were the latter to withhold its grace for a single moment, all things would sink beneath the veil of non-existence.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Whither are gone the learned men, the divines and potentates of old? What hath become of their discriminating views, their shrewd perceptions, their subtle insights and sage pronouncements? Where are their hidden coffers, their flaunted ornaments, their gilded couches, their rugs and cushions strewn about? Gone forever is their generation! All have perished, and, by God's decree, naught remaineth of them but scattered dust.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Where now are Chosroes and Caesar, and those who advanced and turned away, and those who mocked and denied God, and where are those who cast the Books of God behind their backs in defiance of God, the Lord of humanity? And where are their palaces and their influence and their manifestation and their pride, and where is their power and their might and their wrath and their dominion? They have returned to dust with regret and abasement.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Praise be to God, it hath through experience become evident that life in this world possesseth neither distinction nor sweetness, and that the flower-garden of earthly existence hath neither freshness nor delicacy. Its honey is poison, its sugar deadly venom. Its life is death itself, and its comfort but the sting of the serpent. This fleeting world is unworthy of attachment, nor hath it ever been, nor will it ever be, deserving of affection.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: All these creatures that you see, from king to peasant - all their endeavors are like writing upon water. What they write from one side is erased from the other. Consider in this infinite universe: thousands of millions of kings and queens and famous persons came and strived night and day to obtain some result from life, but in the end they and their traces were obliterated, destroyed, forgotten, and their results were temporary, having no permanence.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The days of life pass with utmost speed like a fleeting shadow, and all humanity shall ultimately face manifest loss, for when the days of life are folded up, there remains neither trace nor fruit, neither blossom nor leaf. They return to the lowest depths of nothingness and are afflicted with eternal perdition in the well of darkness. From the servant to the king of kings, all follow this path, save those souls who have found freedom from all attachments.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world is sorely agitated and enshrouded with dust. Its ordeals have taken precedence over its peace, its wrath hath surpassed its grace, and its afflictions have exceeded its delight. It is the object of desire of the heedless, while the discerning despise it. Peace and security are found therein as rarely as the philosophers' Stone, whilst its calamities continue to mount beyond enumeration. Its glory is abasement, its riches are poverty, and its constancy is ephemeral.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: In truth, how attached man is to this world, how imprisoned he is. Death liberates man from all these sorrows and grief. I pray that a day may come when I will be freed from all these attachments, but I hope that from the Abha Kingdom my spirit may be gladdened through outstanding services to the loved ones of God in the Blessed Cause. It is strange that people flee from death, while they should flee from life. It is life that casts man into these endless calamities and drowns him in tribulations.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Ere long it will be evident that all that thou seest in the theatre of this world is naught but vain imaginings and empty thoughts. Like unto the waves of a mirage it will all disappear and be as nothing, it will be even as an attempt to paint on water - utterly non-existent. Its sweetness will become a deathly poison and its cradle and comfort a rocky bed, its lights will be dimmed and its sights will be befogged, its glory will turn into abiding humiliation and its inebriation will turn into a headache.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Whenever those endowed with insight observe the signs of the mortality of anything that existeth in the world of being, they bear witness, nay, each thing in itself with its inner tongue doth testify, to the evanescence of all things. The royal seat becometh the perch of the owl and the spider replaceth the chamberlain. With its inner tongue it declareth: "O discerning ones! Where have your thrones gone; where are your mighty palaces?" Ruin followeth behind every edifice, as death followeth behind every life.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: "No glory remains, no wealth, no rank, no power, no religious leadership, no religious authority, no ministry, no assistance - all perished and vanished, were obliterated and disappeared." "Whatever exists in the earthly realm is transient and lost, while whatever exists in the realm of the Kingdom endures and persists. World-conquering kings became prisoners of the layers of dust - no name or trace remains, no effect and no sovereignty, no sound or voice, no fame or pride or supplication - all became utter nothingness."

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Regard not the world and its fleeting shadows, but fix your gaze upon God and His signs that have encompassed all creation.... Let not the world and its vileness grieve you. Happy is he whom riches fill not with vainglory, nor poverty with sorrow.... Unfaithful is the world... Were it worthy of regard or acceptable in the sight of God, they that were the Manifestations of Justice would not have fallen victims to the talons of tyranny. What greater proof of the baseness of the world and its degradation in the eyes of the Almighty?

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: What is the end of it all? He leaves behind his accumulated wealth and goes away empty-handed. All that you see is subject to change. Where is the living, fire-breathing, active past generations? Where is Napoleon, the Great with his Austerlitz victory and Moscow Retreat? Where are the unconquerable phalanxes of his Imperial guards? Where are the long line of the French Kings? Where are the many Louises? Where are the children of Orleans? Where are the descendants of Philippe? All all gone! They have walked through the wilderness of oblivion and the valley of the shadow of death.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: The world is troubled and dust-laden. Its tribulation precedeth its comfort, and its punishment precedeth its blessing, and its toil exceedeth its pleasure. It is the beloved of the heedless and the abhorred of the knowing ones. Comfort and fidelity in it are like the philosopher's stone, and its afflictions are beyond reckoning. Where is the splendor of Parviz and his pure gold? Where is the might of the Pharaohs and their lofty palaces? Where is the wealth of the tyrants and their ordered armies? If thou wert to look today at the palace of Khosrow, thou wouldst find it a spider's web and echo.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Look, then remember the generations of old. Where are the great ones and the princes and the learned? And where are the tyrants and the Pharaohs and the Caesars and the Chosroes? Where are their visible traces and their lofty palaces and their adorned houses and their trellised gardens and their spread-out carpets and their elevated thrones and their assembled armies and their adorned maidens and their embroidered garments and their precious things and their bejeweled crowns and their fortified refuges and their elevated strongholds and their visible treasures and their hidden hoards and their valiant tribes

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: As for man, his end is this: that after passing a few days following his desires and passions and his selfish desires in this dust heap, he will then have to face utter loss and perdition, having not obtained any fruit or reward. Consider the Kings of Persia - when the chalice of their existence was emptied at the brink of life, what spiritual refreshing beverage remained in them? That is why it is revealed in the Quran: We made of them naught but fables in history. In other words, only their story remained - not their harvest, nor nests, nor homes, and none of the divine bounties. No drink, no chalice, and no cup. They all perished like the fast-passing mist.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: Verily, the world is turbid and dust-laden. Its tribulation precedes its comfort, and its retribution precedes its blessing. Its weariness exceeds its delight. It is the desire of the heedless and the abhorrence of the knowing ones. Comfort and fidelity therein are as rare as the philosopher's stone, and its afflictions exceed all reckoning. Man sees therein what he wishes not to see, and consorts with those whose company he does not desire. Were it to have any station, thou wouldst see its sovereign seated upon its thrones. Were it to have any worth, its Creator and Lord would not have turned away from it. Let not its sorrows grieve thee, nor its embellishments gladden thee. Its glory is abasement, its wealth is poverty, and its permanence is extinction.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation: In the material world perfect composure and tranquility are not destined for man. Somehow, somewhere he is attacked by the depressing condition of the time. He may be either physically or morally sick, he may have sorrow of grief of he may be enveloped with invisible enemies. In short if you search throughout the East and the West and inquire from each individual soul whether he is entirely happy you will find that every person possesses either a kind of grief or he is ill, or his thought is confused or he has had some financial reverses or he is defeated in some of the struggles of life. A life which is subject to such rise and fall and is guided by such beginning and ending is of no importance at all. The health and sickness of such a life is of the least consequence.

Subject: transience; worthlessness of the physical world
Quotation:
Consider this: that every puny ant concentrates upon its own existence and works hard to maintain its life. Now when a human being looks at the puny ant it is a source of surprise and wonderment for the human that why should the ant exert so much effort for these few days of life which are not really worth it. Why is this ant exert so much effort in order to have some comfort and food and livelihood? In the same way when these mountains and stone and the sand and ancient trees, when these look at the station of man in a sense they are filled with wonderment but why is man subject to all this seeking and striving and effort. Why all this futility and vanity for the life of the human is also so transient what constitutes for man an ocean is just a dewdrop. For these stones have remained for 100,000 years but the maximum life of a human is 100 years. There is a difference between the span of 100,000 and 100.  AB01709
All glory is fleeting, even the glory of kings and queens, but thy connection to the threshold of the Kingdom is an eternal glory and a luminous jewel upon thy brow in the Kingdom of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: The "Blessed Perfection Baha'u'llah" ordained, in the days of His corporeal existence (i.e. during His lifetime), that the Holy Book of Laws and Ordinances (Kitab-i-Aqdas) should not be translated into other languages. The time will come one day when the International House of Justice will decide when and into what western languages the "Holy Book" of the "Most Exalted Pen" (Baha'u'llah) may and should be translated.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Whatever is permissible for publication in these days is given permission to be published, for every time has its requirements. As for the Epistle to the Son of the Wolf, in the blessed days permission was not granted to anyone to make copies, as circumstances required. Now it has been printed and published. If the Kitab-i-Aqdas were to be printed, it would be published and fall into the hands of contemptible fanatics, therefore it is not permitted. Yes, some apostates like Mirza Mehdi Beg, among the waverers, obtained it and published it, but this was included in the writings of apostates. Since their hatred and enmity is well-known to all, their words and accounts are regarded as dubious and unclear. But if the Baha'is were to publish it, it would be quite another matter. The Quran was confined to the scribes of revelation for twenty-six years; it was disseminated during the time of the Caliphs, and even then it was limited to a few copies.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Mr. Ali Quli Khan has translated the Kitab-i-Iqan and it was sent with him so that it can be published and circulated in that land.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: If you translate and publish the Hidden Words into Russian that would be most acceptable, and if you also translate Some Answered Questions that too would be fitting.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: These verses will soon be translated into English poetical form and then this Divine Song will rise from those lands and reach the ABHA Kingdom in utmost joy and happiness.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding translation as well, you exert the utmost effort and I have complete trust in this service of yours. Send a Persian copy of whatever writings are translated into German.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: These, had they known Persian and understood Arabic, would have been greatly moved, but the means have not yet been made available for a proper and complete translation of these Tablets.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: However, if translating the article into Russian and publishing and distributing it has no harm, then carry it out. But if you translate the Letter of the East and West, it would be very appropriate to send it to Tolstoy.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: As to the establishing of a Bureau of Translation, this great matter is an excellent matter and this great service is an excellent service to the Cause of God; until the Divine Tablets may be translated in the most eloquent style and be spread in those remote countries.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: A person is needed who is well versed in Persian, Arabic and English. Then it will become good. A single individual cannot do it satisfactorily. Among those which are translated, the translation of the Iqan is not fair to a certain extent. In future a committee will be formed. They will translate.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding communications between East and West, this is of the utmost importance. You must most assuredly promote this matter. Mirza Amin must exert his utmost effort in translating these letters that go from East to West or from West to East, for this is the greatest service and virtue - better than a hundred thousand doctorates.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: It was written to Bombay to send the article with utmost speed, and it shall be written to Aqa Siyyid Mustafa to translate speedily into Hindi the Tajalliyat, Ishraqat, Tarazat, Kalimat, and Bisharat - these Tablets - and send them to you. Some American publications are being sent so that you may also spread those publications there.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: You have come to assist me by translating His Sacred Writings as well as my letters to the friends in America and elsewhere in the West. Rest assured, the Blessed Perfection will enable you to translate the Arabic into English. Rest assured that as time goes on you will be assisted to translate from the Arabic much more easily than from the Persian.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding what you wrote about translating and publishing the divine Tablets, this is not advisable at present, for it would quench people's thirst. First, souls must be made thirsty, then the sweet and flowing water should be offered. If the sacred writings were now translated, published and distributed, everyone who obtained a Tablet would be content with reading it and say, "I am now familiar with the foundations of this community and need investigate no further." Yet the Tablets must be expounded by an expounder - that is, the expounder must first establish the foundation, and after presenting the proofs, then recite a Tablet; only then will it have effect. Consider how much the Torah and the Gospel have been translated into various languages, published and distributed, yet not one soul has developed love for Christ through reading these books. Thus it is clear that publication and distribution is not advisable.  If it seems absolutely necessary, translate articles and publish those.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Now the important task is the translation of Ishraqat, Kalimat, Tarazat and Bisharat. These four Tablets are very suitable for the Egyptians and will have a great effect. However, the translation must be in the utmost eloquence and excellence. You, along with Sheikh Farajullah and another person whom you deem suitable from among skilled writers, should translate and publish these Tablets.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding the recent letters from Iran that you wrote about - their translation, publication and dissemination, and how they increased the spiritual sentiments of the Western friends toward their Eastern counterparts, such that in every home and dwelling, in gatherings and meetings, they are remembered and their praise and attributes bring joy to hearts and move souls - it is just as you wrote.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Rather, printing and multiplying tablets indiscriminately causes the value of God's verses to be diminished. Observe that when the Qur'an was printed, they used it to wrap medicines in apothecary shops. Likewise observe how much it was printed and published and fell into the hands of other peoples who recited it. Therefore, the divine verses must be given proper dignity and standing. Furthermore, it is not in the interest of the Cause today for divine verses to fall into people's hands.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Concerning the Tablets of the Kings. If they are translated and published it will be very useful, but one person alone cannot do the translation. A committee must be organized the members of which are well-read and erudite in both Arabic and English languages; so that such a committee may engaged in the translation and not a single individual. All the translations up to the present time have been the result of individual endeavor; therefore the results are not obtained in a befitting and behooving manner.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding the printing of the translation of the book's introduction about the interpretation of sacred scriptures that you had written about - this translation requires the utmost care. Mr. Haddad must exert his utmost effort that it may be in the most wonderful expressions and with perfect eloquence and excellence, even if this necessitates consulting with linguists. Then its printing will be necessary. Concerning the translation of the Kitab-i-Aqdas, something was also written to Anton Effendi himself.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Regarding the translation of the Tablets about which thou didst write: God willing, a translation committee will be formed to translate the Tablets with the utmost eloquence and excellence. However, if thou shouldst translate some of the Tablets, such as the Tajalliyat and Ishraqat, and publish them, this would be most suitable. Only the Kitab-i-Aqdas must be translated by a complete committee that is well-versed in the mysteries of its laws. It is difficult for a single person, and God willing, when the foundation for translation is established, it is hoped that thou too wilt be included.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Now, since they are published, circulate them among the people. I hope that it may produce beneficial results. Perchance some of the souls who are truth-seekers may get a little information about this Cause. But afterward, if thou desirest to get the translation of a Tablet from the Blessed Writings, it must be translated by a committee of two Persian translators together with two competent English writers. The Persians should translate, and the writers mould the significance into profound, musical and perfect cast of style in English, and in such wise that the musical sweetness of the original Persian may not be lost. Then the material must be forwarded to me. I will consider the matter and give permission for its publication and circulation.... In brief, translation is one of the most difficult arts. In both Persian and English utmost proficiency is necessary, that the translator be a writer and use as the vehicle of expression great eloquence and fluency of tongue.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Convey my most glorious greetings to your dear sister and tell her that if she were to recite the Hidden Words in Persian and Arabic and comprehend their inner meanings and truths, they would have a different splendor. No matter how eloquent a translation may be, it can never equal the original.

Subject: translation; publication of the Sacred Writings
Quotation: Truly translation is very difficult. One has to have the utmost proficiency in science and religion, in divine wisdom, in the current trends of thought in Europe, and in philosophical and scientific terms.

Subject: travels to Egypt by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Your recent letter was received in Alexandria. Despite extreme weakness and illness, I am writing a response to make up for what was missed. During this journey, I was so occupied day and night that there was absolutely no opportunity to write, hence the shortcoming. Now, despite my illness, as there is an opportunity, I have undertaken to write this reply.

Subject: travels to Egypt by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: For nearly one month 'Abdul-Baha remained in Port Said and the friends of God came from Cairo, in turn, to visit him. One day he called me to accompany him when taking a walk in the streets of the city...The day that he left for Alexandria he did not mention the matter to anyone; nor did this servant know the time of his departure.

Subject: travels to Egypt by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: For several days I have been staying in Ramleh of Alexandria, and day and night I am occupied with thoughts of the divine friends. After arriving in Port Said, some weakness resulted from the fatigue of travel. In any case, I am now writing this letter in a garden in the shade of a tree.

Subject: travels to Egypt by Abdu'l-Baha

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: I am in Paris

Quotation: When friends in the West wished to make contributions, whether small or large, towards these expenses, they were absolutely refused...in view of an all-encompassing wisdom, we have kept this matter silent in the West

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Before coming to America, the believers of God, through Mirza Ahmad Sohrab, offered for my traveling expenses $16,000 but I did not accept one cent.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: We telegraphed our arrival to Aqa Mirza Jalal, and from Marseilles, under the protection of the Blessed Beauty, we arrived in complete comfort to Thonon in France. It is truly a delightful place. The mildness of the weather, the freshness of the grass and fields, the lushness and pleasantness of the hills, as well as the beauty of the scenery are most perfect. From the day I left Iran until now I had not seen such a place. For the time being, together with a group of the friends, we are staying in the Grant Hotel Park in Thonon. The weather is most agreeable.

Quotation: We have reached Paris.

Were it not for the assistance and protection of the Blessed Beauty (Baha'o'llah) I would never have had any hope of returning from such a long journey. I went as far as Los Angeles, which is situated on the western coast of America and directly opposite the land of Acca.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: There were some places I wanted to go but hadn't finished my work - I wanted to go to Berlin and Italy, especially Romania which is the center of the Pope. I left all of these and came to see you... Even the Iranian Consul General in New York invited us... This passed until on our journey toward California we reached the city of Denver.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Once, when I was on my way to speak in a church in New York city, a person from India, a man prominent in that city, met us accidentally. He came to the church and saw me standing on the platform, proving the prophethood of his holiness the Messenger of God. Indeed, he became amazed. When we came out, his face was radiant beyond description.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Your letter was received in Paris at a time when I was extremely fatigued from extensive travels throughout the Western countries. Every day was spent in a different place, every morning in a different plain, and every evening without rest or repose. Due to this, a period of convalescence became necessary, hence the delay in sending this reply.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: The intention was to be present in London in October, but the friends of God from the cities of California raised an extraordinary cry and lamentation that "We have been waiting for this day for many years; how can you be content that we remain deprived?" Therefore I was compelled to travel to California, but my hope is to be in London in November.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Despite severe illness, "suddenly departing from Haifa to sea and heading to desert and mountain and wilderness, he went to all the Western countries. And in a state of severe nervous illness and chest ailments in cold weather, from morning until midnight in gatherings and assemblies he called out and delivered the call of the Kingdom to all ears."

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: This servant is about to depart for the region of Europe...Now it is being sent from London. Consider how little time there was then, and now it is ten times less, for from morning until midnight there are gatherings for teaching, even priests are present in the meetings and in the churches the cry of 'Abdu'l-Baha is raised and the people are astonished.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: "As soon as the Master left America now and then, letters were received that some of the believers thought and felt that the activities of the Persian American Educational Society in Washington are against the desire and consent of the Beloved. In my last address in California and in conversation with the friends I have encouraged them to assist the Society."

Quotation: 'Abdu'l-Baha will be departing for distant lands in these two days... The people of America, both friends and strangers, are all pleading with utmost insistence for 'Abdu'l-Baha's presence. Perhaps more than a thousand letters have arrived from the friends and various assemblies of America, even from some church ministers. Therefore I am compelled to make this journey.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Before leaving Haifa I felt very ill, but as soon as I embarked on the sea of the service of the Cause of God I felt better. That was why I took my first journey to Europe. Returning to Alexandria I stayed in Egypt for the winter and then started on the long voyage for America. We spent fifteen days on the sea and when we reached New York many meetings and Conferences were commenced by night and day.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: But when we were in America, in Europe, in the field of service, it was clearly evident that the hosts of the seen and unseen were lending their support and assistance. In the Jewish synagogue, five thousand Jews were present when an extensive talk was given that opposed their views to an indescribable degree. In the Jewish synagogue, the Word of God status of Christ was proven - that Christ was the Word of God and the Spirit of God, that Muhammad was the Messenger of God.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: Whenever I get tired on the way, I thought of your promised faces, and the fatigue was taken away. Considered from a geographical standpoint, there is no further point than San Francisco. You see, this is just the opposite point of Syria. Half an arc has been covered. The utmost has been that a person might have traveled 100 miles, or 200, or 500 miles, to meet his friends. On the other hand, I have traveled many, many thousands of miles to reach here, and this has been just for the sake of meeting you. This, then, is unique in history.

Subject: travels to the West by Abdu'l-Baha
Quotation: 'Abdu'l-Baha is in these days bound for America and offers his most earnest supplications at the Threshold of the Most Glorious Beauty that during this absence the divine friends may abide under the protection of His Holiness the One True God and arise to promote the manifest Faith. Detailed letters, some adorned with a thousand names, arrive from America, and special correspondence comes from both friend and stranger, and communications arrive continually from the great assemblies of America, all requesting 'Abdu'l-Baha's journey to those regions and showing the utmost eagerness and desire. Therefore am I compelled to undertake this journey.

Subject: true liberty; freedom
Quotation: There are three types of freedom. The first is divine freedom, which is one of the inherent attributes of the Creator for He is unconstrained in His will, and no one can force Him to change His decree in any matter whatsoever.... The second is the political freedom of Europeans, which leaves the individual free to do whatsoever he desires as long as his action does not harm his neighbour. This is natural freedom, and its greatest expression is seen in the animal world. Observe these birds and notice with what freedom they live. However much man may try, he can never be as free as an animal, because the existence of order acts as an impediment to freedom. The third freedom is that which is born of obedience to the laws and ordinances of the Almighty. This is the freedom of the human world, where man severs his affections from all things. When he does so, he becomes immune to all hardship and sorrow. Wealth or material power will not deflect him from moderation and fairness, neither will poverty or need inhibit him from showing forth happiness and tranquillity. The more the conscience of man develops, the more will his heart be free and his soul attain unto happiness. In the religion of God, there is freedom of thought because God, alone, controls the human conscience, but this freedom should not go beyond courtesy. In the religion of God, there is no freedom of action outside the law of God. Man may not transgress this law, even though no harm is inflicted on one's neighbour. This is because the purpose of Divine law is the education of all -- others as well as oneself -- and, in the sight of God, the harm done to one individual or to his neighbour is the same and is reprehensible in both cases. Hearts must possess the fear of God. Man should endeavour to avoid that which is abhorrent unto God. Therefore, the freedom that the laws of Europe offer to the individual does not exist in the law of God. Freedom of thought should not transgress the bounds of courtesy, and actions, likewise, should be governed by the fear of God and the desire to seek His good pleasure.

Subject: true liberty; freedom
Quotation: I learned from thy letter what was mentioned regarding liberty. Therefore, I write what was revealed concerning it in the Most Holy Book, that every heedless and doubtful one may be awakened thereby. His glory be exalted! He saith: "Consider the pettiness of men's minds. They ask for that which injureth them, and cast away the thing that profiteth them. They are, indeed, of those that are far astray. We find some men desiring liberty, and priding themselves therein. Such men are in the depths of ignorance. Liberty must, in the end, lead to sedition, whose flames none can quench. Thus warneth you He Who is the Reckoner, the All-Knowing. Know ye that the embodiment of liberty and its symbol is the animal. That which beseemeth man is submission unto such restraints as will protect him from his own ignorance, and guard him against the harm of the mischief maker. Liberty causeth man to overstep the bounds of propriety, and to infringe on the dignity of his station. It debaseth him to the level of extreme depravity and wickedness. Regard men as a flock of sheep that need a shepherd for their protection. This, verily, is the truth, the certain truth. We approve of liberty in certain circumstances, and refuse to sanction it in others. We, verily, are the All-Knowing. Say: True liberty consisteth in man's submission unto My commandments, little as ye know it. Were men to observe that which We have sent down unto them from the Heaven of Revelation, they would, of a certainty, attain unto perfect liberty. Happy is the man that hath apprehended the Purpose of God in whatever He hath revealed from the Heaven of His Will that pervadeth all created things. Say: The liberty that profiteth you is to be found nowhere except in complete servitude unto God, the Eternal Truth. Whoso hath tasted of its sweetness will refuse to barter it for all the dominion of earth and heaven." By thy life, this helpless man hath not understood the purpose of the liberty of which the people of Europe speak. He should come into My presence that I may teach him and acquaint him with what they say. He hath heard a statement and followed it without comprehending its reality and the intent of its speaker. Everyone who uttereth the freedom mentioned by that man is called a manifestation of the beasts in creation. I marvel not at him, but rather at those who have attained the Water of Life, yet turn to hearken unto his croaking and the bleating of his like. Say: O people of Baha! By the True One! The essential liberty hath submitted to that servitude which hath appeared through the love of God and His Cause. It behooveth you to see yourselves above the world and all therein of creation, and what they possess of conjectures, idle fancies, and statements arising from darkened and heedless hearts.

Quotation: In God have I believed and He, verily, is sufficient unto us. In Him have we placed our trust, and in God let His trusting servants put their trust. Say: In God, our Lord, have we placed our trust and He, verily, is sufficient unto us, and in Him let His trusting servants put their trust. Seek ye refuge, therefore, in God, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of earth, the Lord of all worlds. Place your trust in God, the Ever-Living Who dieth not, and await ye the days of God wherein ye shall be exalted.

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: What is meant in the prophecies by the Lord of hosts, the promised Christ, is the Blessed Perfection (Baha'u'llah) and his holiness the Exalted One (the Bab)

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: The Ancient Beauty (may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones) did not meet in person with the Exalted One (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him).

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: However, O my God, since he believed in Thee through Thy First Beauty...and acknowledge Thy Later Beauty just as he acknowledged Thy majesty in Thy First Beauty

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: In this greatest period there are only two manifestation, the blessed Bab (May my soul be a random to him!) and the Manifestation of the Blessed Perfection (Glory be to Him!).

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: I manifested Myself aforetime under the name of 'Ali...He is My Beloved and I am His Beloved. Whatsoever appeareth from Me is His purpose...He spoke not except in praise of Me, and I speak not except in remembrance of Him

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: In the books of all religions, two Promised Ones were foretold, just as in the Gospel there is the coming of Elijah and Christ, by which is meant the Bab and Baha'u'llah. There will be no third Manifestation until a thousand years.

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: He it was Whom Thou hast determined to be the Herald of Thy Most Great Revelation and the Announcer of Thy Most Ancient Splendor... And when Thy promise came to pass and the set time was fulfilled, He Who is the Possessor of all Names and Attributes was made manifest unto men.

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: "you heard with your heart and soul the life-giving call of the Primal Point, His Holiness the Exalted One (may my spirit and being be sacrificed for Him), and responded with heart and soul "Yea, verily" to the call of "Am I not?" from the Abha Beauty (may my spirit be a sacrifice for His loved ones)"

Subject: twin Manifestations
Quotation: All the peoples of the world are awaiting two Manifestations, Who must be contemporaneous. This is what they all have been promised. In the Torah the Jews are promised the Lord of Hosts and the Messiah. In the Gospel, the return of Christ and Elijah is foretold. In the religion of Muhammad there is the promise of the Mahdi and the Messiah.... Now, one must prove the advent of these twin Manifestations by reference to the sacred scriptures and by inference from the sayings of the Prophets. For our intention now is to provide arguments drawn from the sacred scriptures, since rational arguments establishing the truth of these two Manifestations were presented at table a few days ago.

Subject: twin duties of recognition and obedience
Quotation: Say: O people, the first duty is to recognize the one true God -- magnified be His glory -- the second is to show forth constancy in His Cause

Subject: twin duties of recognition and obedience
Quotation: The beginning of faith in God, exalted be His glory, has been and is [recognition], and its end is steadfastness in it. Blessed is he who has attained unto both the first and the second.

Subject: twin duties of recognition and obedience
Quotation: The supreme cause for creating the world and all that is therein is for man to know God. In this Day whosoever is guided by the fragrance of the raiment of His mercy to gain admittance into the pristine Abode, which is the station of recognizing the Source of divine commandments and the Dayspring of His Revelation, hath everlastingly attained unto all good. Having reached this lofty station a twofold obligation resteth upon every soul. One is to be steadfast in the Cause with such steadfastness that were all the peoples of the world to attempt to prevent him from turning to the Source of Revelation, they would be powerless to do so. The other is observance of the divine ordinances which have streamed forth from the wellspring of His heavenly-propelled Pen. For man’s knowledge of God cannot develop fully and adequately save by observing whatsoever hath been ordained by Him and is set forth in His heavenly Book.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: Man has two natures. One is material or physical. That is the heritage of Adam to man, for it is elemental; it is material; it belongs to earth. He is possessed of another nature, which is spiritual. That is Christ-like. That is born of the Word of God. That is from the Breaths of the Holy Spirit. That nature is radiant. That nature is heavenly, and that nature is divine.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: The natural world is the mine of imperfection and affliction. War and strife are requirements of the natural world, and the struggle for existence is a characteristic of the animal and plant kingdoms. But the human world is pure good and conscious emanation is pure love. When we look at nature we see pride and arrogance, tyranny and evil, imperfection and deficiency, inequity and transgression, ferocity and bloodthirstiness, causing shame and embarrassment. But the divine law abrogates the law of nature and nullifies the vices of base natures, and legislates true virtues so that through divine education the human world may be renewed.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: The state of man's nature is injustice, butchery, tyranny, treachery, lechery, achievement of selfish motives, neglect of God and fulfillment of carnal desires. The sanctified Manifestations of God rescue humanity from this black pit and guide them to the highest stations of spirituality.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: Human beings are of two kinds. Some are of a material inclination...The other kind of human beings are those who seek the sublime world

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: But in man there exist two stations - luminous and dark, divine and natural, merciful and satanic - for he is the dividing line between light and darkness...

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: What is written concerning the "soul which inclines toward evil" is no other than the fermentation of the passionate desires in the breast of man and the complete, unchecked sway of the carnal and natural forces over him.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: Whatsoever God causeth these verses to issue forth from My soul, in like manner doth He bring forth the spirits of these verses through the emergence of their letters, bearing witness that there is no God but Him, the Mighty, the Beloved.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: Man is possessed of two stations: One is that of sleep and one of wakefulness. One is that of infancy, and one of maturity. One is that of utter helplessness and one of great assistance. One is that of utter poverty and one is absolute wealth. These are the two stations of man.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: There exist in man two powers. One power uplifts him - this is divine attraction which causes man's elevation. In all the grades of existence he will develop through this power which belongs to the spirit. The other power causes man to descend; this is the animal nature. The first attracts man to the Kingdom; the second brings him down to the created world.

Subject: two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two aspects of the human soul; the higher and lower natures.txt
Quotation: From one vantage point it possesses spiritual refinement while from the other it exhibits the crassness of carnality, animalistic traits and worldly characteristics. It is neither an absolute abstraction nor is it completely of the world but is the confluence of two seas and a barzakh between two realities. If the spiritual aspect dominates it becometh lofty, luminous, merciful, tranquil, contented and approved. And if it is contaminated with contingent, worldly concerns, it becometh immersed in the ocean of darknessess, reproachful, commanding to evil and residing in the nethermost regions of the world of existence.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: Whereas Western nations have perfected the machinery of natural civilization yet they are far left behind in divine civilization.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: The difference between material civilization that restrains through punishment versus divine civilization that educates souls to naturally avoid evil and be attracted to virtues

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: Without divine civilization the mysteries of the Kingdom are not revealed and the bounties of heaven are not ascertained... These perfections are attained through divine civilization of which the world of man is in need.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: "The teachings, once established there, will unite the East and the West, the North and the South." "Should you become confirmed therein, this world will become another world, the surface of the earth will become the delectable paradise, and eternal Institutions be founded."

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: Materially you are very well off, but you are in need of what I would term "divine" civilization... Material civilization is like a glass chimney. Divine civilization is like the light within the chimney or lantern. However much the chimney may be polished or clear, it is in need of light.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: The human beings in this earthly kingdom have been divided into two parts: One part is like the animals that have their home, their comfort and their joyous garden in this earthly Home and this lowly Hell...But there is another kind of people who are drunk from the Divine Cup and are free from all attachment to this mortal world

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: It is possible for the mother to educate the child in such wise as to become the leader amongst the leaders or to leave him to evil environments as to become the worst criminal amongst men. They should receive a divine education, not like now when mothers from early childhood tell their sons they must become wealthy and millionaires, they have no other words except these, they never say be truthful and trustworthy, serve humanity.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: Material civilization has reached an advanced plane, but now there is need of spiritual civilization. Material civilization alone will not satisfy; it cannot meet the conditions and requirements of the present age; its benefits are limited to the world of matter. There is no limitation to the spirit of man, for spirit in itself is progressive, and if the divine civilization be established, the spirit of man will advance. Material civilization has advanced unmistakably, but because it is not associated with divine civilization, evil and wickedness abound.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: Material civilization is complete, but it needs heavenly illumination; it needs divine civilization. Divine civilization is the lamp and material civilization is the glass. Divine civilization is the spirit and material civilization is the body. Physical civilization alone is not sufficient, and humanity needs divine civilization in many ways. From physical civilization natural perfections are obtained; from divine civilization spiritual perfections are manifested. Physical civilization serves the world of nature; divine civilization serves the world of morals.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: Evil deeds, unacceptable actions, harmful lies and that which proceeds from them appear in creation in the form of fires, hell, the Zaqqum tree, thorny plants, and in the form of all wickedness, abhorrence, illness, sorrows, poisons, swords, arrows and spears... O what longing for spiritual virtues, goodly deeds, truthful and beneficial words, and that which appeareth therefrom of the raised heaven and spread earth and shining suns and gleaming moons and brilliant stars and pure springs and flowing rivers and gentle breezes and lofty palaces and towering trees and gathered fruits and low-hanging clusters and singing birds and reddened leaves and fragrant flowers!

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: In this journey, although it became clear and evident that the Western world has made extraordinary progress in material civilization, divine civilization is nearly wholly forgotten, for all thoughts are immersed in the world of nature. Everything manifests the splendors of the natural world, not divine splendors. And since in the world of nature there are many imperfections, therefore the lights of divine civilization are hidden and nature has become sovereign. Today in the human world, material civilization is like a glass of utmost delicacy, but alas, a thousand times alas, this glass is deprived of the lamp--and that lamp is divine civilization, which the holy Manifestations of God have established.

Subject: two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of civilization; material and spiritual civilization.txt
Quotation: Therefore it became evident that education is absolutely essential in a civilized society. And civilization is of two kinds, material and spiritual. The latter pertaineth to the realm of human conduct and character. Until these two types of civilization blend together within human society, prosperity and salvation can in no wise be attained. Consider the continent of Europe where the tabernacle of material civilization is raised high, yet it is immersed in darkness. All thought is directed toward the struggle for existence. Every day men equip themselves with new weapons and produce large quantities of incendiary bombs and explosives. Peace and tranquillity have altogether ceased to exist, and the people are greatly oppressed with destitution and perplexities, simply because moral civilization, spirituality and attraction to divine fragrances are completely forgotten.

Subject: two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight.txt
Quotation: Though physical sight be deprived, praise be to God that spiritual vision existeth and the grace of the Lord of existence is evident.

Subject: two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight.txt
Quotation: The light of guidance hath dawned from the daybreak of eternity...that thou mayest receive abundantly from the outpourings of thy Praiseworthy Lord

Subject: two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight.txt
Quotation: Know thou that human beings are of two kinds. Some are of a material inclination, enslaved to the world of nature...The other kind of human beings are those who seek the sublime world

Subject: two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight.txt
Quotation: O dervish, know that knowledge is of two kinds: one is error and one is guidance. Error is the portion of the ignorant...Knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge of bodies and knowledge of religions.

Subject: two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight.txt
Quotation: Those possessed of insight see the world illumined by the rays of the Sun of Truth, but the blind ones are deprived of beholding the light. They say the day is night and cry out that the morning is evening.

Subject: two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight.txt
Quotation: The truly learned one is he whose knowledge prevents him from all that My good-pleasure and His good-pleasure abhorreth, and the mature one is he who hath attained unto the dawning-place of My knowledge; and apart from this none is mature, even though he may live [for...] years

Subject: two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight
Source file: subject_extracts/subjects_inv_length_ordered/two kinds of knowledge [ilm and irfan]; sight and insight.txt
Quotation: Christ's teachings were heavenly, and we must have a heavenly mind in order to comprehend them. The mind of Nicodemus bore the same relation to the teachings of Jesus that a child's mind bears to the man's mind which is, in a sense, perfect.
